1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	}
32	
33	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
34	func (a *App) Load() error {
35		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
36		if err != nil {
37			return err
38		}
39		a.Cfg = cfg
40		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
41		if a.Out == nil {
42			a.Out = os.Stdout
43		}
44		if a.Err == nil {
45			a.Err = os.Stderr
46		}
47		return nil
48	}
49	
50	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
51	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
52	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
53		if a.noRuntime {
54			return runtime.None{}
55		}
56		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
57		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
58			backend = a.runtimeOverride
59		}
60		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
61		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
62			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
63		}
64		return rt
65	}
66	
67	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
68	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
69		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
70	}
71	
72	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
73	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
74		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
75	}
76	
77	// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
78	// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
79	// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
80	// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
81	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
82		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
83	}
84	
85	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
86	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
87

18	func newTryCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
19		var (
20			list  bool
21			clone string
22			noGit bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "try [name]",
26			Short: "Make a dated scratch directory for an experiment",
27			Long: `Create (or jump to) a dated experiment directory under paths.tries_root.
28	
29	Experiments need a home that is neither /tmp (where they vanish) nor your
30	projects directory (where they accumulate as clutter you are afraid to delete).
31	A try is date-prefixed, disposable by default, and promotable with
32	"dev graduate" when it turns out to be real.
33	
34	  dev try                    list what is there
35	  dev try redis-streams      jump to a matching try, or create 2026-08-27-redis-streams
36	  dev try --clone <url>      clone a repo into a dated try directory`,
37			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
38			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
39				ctx := ctxOf()
40				root := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot)
41				if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
42					return err
43				}
44	
45				if list || (len(args) == 0 && clone == "") {
46					return listTries(app, root)
47				}
48	
49				name := ""
50				if len(args) == 1 {
51					name = args[0]
52				}
53				if clone != "" && name == "" {
54					name = repoNameFromRef(clone)
55				}
56				slug := config.Slug(strings.ReplaceAll(name, " ", "-"))
57	
58				// An existing try wins over creating a near-duplicate: the whole
59				// point is to stop accumulating test/test2/test-actually.
60				if match := findTry(root, slug); match != "" && clone == "" {
61					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(match))
62					return openOrCD(app, ctx, match, filepath.Base(match))
63				}
64	
65				dir := filepath.Join(root, time.Now().Format("2006-01-02")+"-"+slug)
66				if _, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil {
67					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(dir))
68					return openOrCD(app, ctx, dir, filepath.Base(dir))
69				}
70	
71				if clone != "" {
72					url := clone
73					if k := forge.FromURL(clone); k != forge.Unknown {
74						if f, err := forge.For(k); err == nil {
75							url = f.CloneURL(clone)
76						}
77					}
78					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, root, "clone", url, dir); err != nil {
79						return err
80					}
81				} else {
82					if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
83						return err
84					}
85					if !noGit {
86						// A try with git history can be graduated without losing
87						// the path that got there, which is most of its value.
88						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "init", "-b", "main"); err != nil {
89							app.warnf("could not git init: %v", err)
90						}
91					}
92				}
93				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(dir))
94				return openOrCD(app, ctx, dir, filepath.Base(dir))
95			},
96		}
97		f := cmd.Flags()
98		f.BoolVarP(&list, "list", "l", false, "list existing tries")
99		f.StringVar(&clone, "clone", "", "clone a repository into the new try")
100		f.BoolVar(&noGit, "no-git", false, "do not git init the new directory")
101		return cmd
102	}
103	
104	// tryEntry is one scratch directory with the facts needed to rank it.
105	type tryEntry struct {
106		name     string
107		path     string
108		modified time.Time
109		isRepo   bool
110		dirty    bool
111	}
112	
113	func listTries(app *App, root string) error {
114		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
115		if err != nil {
116			return err
117		}
118		var tries []tryEntry
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			if !e.IsDir() || strings.HasPrefix(e.Name(), ".") {
121				continue
122			}
123			info, err := e.Info()
124			if err != nil {
125				continue
126			}
127			path := filepath.Join(root, e.Name())
128			t := tryEntry{name: e.Name(), path: path, modified: info.ModTime()}
129			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
130				t.isRepo = true
131				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctxOf(), path); err == nil {
132					t.dirty = st.Dirty()
133				}
134			}
135			tries = append(tries, t)
136		}
137		if len(tries) == 0 {
138			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "No tries yet under %s\n", config.Contract(root))
139			return nil
140		}
141		// Most recently touched first: "what was I doing yesterday?" is the
142		// question a list of experiments actually gets asked.
143		sort.Slice(tries, func(i, j int) bool { return tries[i].modified.After(tries[j].modified) })
144	
145		tbl := NewTable("TRY", "AGE", "GIT")
146		for _, t := range tries {
147			gitCol := "—"
148			switch {
149			case t.isRepo && t.dirty:
150				gitCol = "repo ●"
151			case t.isRepo:
152				gitCol = "repo"
153			}
154			tbl.Add(truncate(t.name, 44), humanAge(time.Since(t.modified)), gitCol)
155		}
156		tbl.Render(app.Out)
157		fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\n%d tries under %s — promote one with `dev graduate <try>`\n",
158			len(tries), config.Contract(root))
159		return nil
160	}
161	
162	// findTry locates an existing try whose name contains the slug, preferring the
163	// most recent when several match.
164	func findTry(root, slug string) string {
165		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
166		if err != nil {
167			return ""
168		}
169		var best string
170		var bestTime time.Time
171		for _, e := range entries {
172			if !e.IsDir() || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(e.Name()), strings.ToLower(slug)) {
173				continue
174			}
175			info, err := e.Info()
176			if err != nil {
177				continue
178			}
179			if info.ModTime().After(bestTime) {
180				best, bestTime = filepath.Join(root, e.Name()), info.ModTime()
181			}
182		}
183		return best
184	}
185	
186	func openOrCD(app *App, ctx context.Context, dir, label string) error {
187		rt := app.Runtime()
188		if rt.Name() == "none" {
189			app.cdDirective(dir)
190			return nil
191		}
192		if _, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, dir, label); err != nil {
193			app.warnf("could not open a session: %v", err)
194		}
195		return nil
196	}

34	An experiment that turns out to matter should stop being an experiment, and
35	that transition is where things usually get lost — the directory keeps its date
36	prefix forever, or it gets copied by hand and the history is left behind.
37	
38	graduate moves the directory to <project_root>/<category>/<name>, drops the
39	date prefix, makes sure it has a git repo and a first commit, and optionally
40	creates the remote with gh or glab.
41	
42	With no argument, the try containing the current directory is used.`,

128	// resolveTry finds the try directory to graduate: an explicit reference, or
129	// the try containing the current directory.
130	func resolveTry(app *App, triesRoot string, args []string) (string, error) {

137			if isDir(direct) {
138				return direct, nil
139			}
140			if match := findTry(triesRoot, ref); match != "" {
141				return match, nil
142			}
143			return "", fmt.Errorf("no try matching %q under %s", ref, config.Contract(triesRoot))
144		}
145	
146		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
147		if err != nil {
148			return "", err
149		}
150		if !strings.HasPrefix(cwd, triesRoot+string(filepath.Separator)) {
151			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not inside %s — name the try to graduate",
152				config.Contract(cwd), config.Contract(triesRoot))
153		}
154		// Walk up to the try's own top-level directory, so running this from a
155		// subdirectory still graduates the whole experiment.
156		rel, _ := filepath.Rel(triesRoot, cwd)
157		first := strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator))[0]
158		return filepath.Join(triesRoot, first), nil
159	}
160	
161	func isDir(p string) bool {
162		info, err := os.Stat(p)
163		return err == nil && info.IsDir()
164	}
165	
166	// ensureInitialCommit gives a repository a first commit if it has none,
167	// seeding a README when the tree is otherwise empty. Reports whether it made
168	// one.
169	func ensureInitialCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) (bool, error) {
170		if _, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, dir); err == nil {
171			return false, nil // already has history
172		}
173		if empty, err := isEmptyTree(dir); err != nil {
174			return false, err
175		} else if empty {
176			readme := filepath.Join(dir, "README.md")
177			if err := os.WriteFile(readme, []byte("# "+name+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
178				return false, err
179			}
180		}
181		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
182			return false, err
183		}
184		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "commit", "-m", "chore: graduate experiment into a project"); err != nil {
185			return false, err
186		}
187		return true, nil
188	}
189	
190	// isEmptyTree reports a directory with nothing in it but git's own metadata.
191	func isEmptyTree(dir string) (bool, error) {
192		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
193		if err != nil {
194			return false, err
195		}
196		for _, e := range entries {
197			if e.Name() != ".git" {
198				return false, nil
199			}
200		}
201		return true, nil
202	}
203

2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"

11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64

66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (

73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)

81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {

84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`

91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`

100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`

106		State State `toml:"state"`

131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}

146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}

151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}

3	import (

16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

114		// personal — nvim or helix, lazygit or gitui, and whatever aliases and
115		// scripts you have built up around your own workflow.

117	}

119	// Tool is one external program bound to a key in the dashboard.
120	type Tool struct {
121		// Key launches it. A single character, and not one of the dashboard's own
122		// bindings — dev reports a clash rather than silently shadowing.
123		Key string `toml:"key"`
124		// Name is shown in the footer.
125		Name string `toml:"name"`
126		// Run is a shell command, executed in the selected row's checkout.
127		Run string `toml:"run"`

129		// shell alias or function can be used. Off by default: startup files can
130		// print output and alter environment in ways an ordinary command should
131		// not inherit accidentally.
132		Interactive bool `toml:"interactive"`
133	}

135	// reservedKeys are the dashboard's own bindings. A tool cannot take one,
136	// because losing the ability to quit or move is not a trade anyone wants.
137	var reservedKeys = map[string]string{
138		"q": "quit", "j": "down", "k": "up", "g": "top", "G": "bottom",
139		"h": "previous view", "l": "next view", "tab": "next view",
140		"/": "filter", "r": "refresh", "o": "open", "p": "park",
141		"c": "edit next action", "s": "start a task", "a": "include done",
142		"0": "clear filters", "1": "hot", "2": "warm", "3": "cold",
143		"?": "help", "H": "repo activity heatmap", "e": "edit config",
144	}

146	// ReservedKey reports the dashboard binding a key would collide with.
147	func ReservedKey(key string) (string, bool) {
148		name, ok := reservedKeys[key]

220	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
221	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
222	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
223	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
224		cfg := Default()
225		if path == "" {
226			path = ConfigFile()
227		}
228		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
229		switch {
230		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
231			return cfg, nil
232		case err != nil:
233			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
234		}
235		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
236			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
237			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
238			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
239		}
240		cfg.Source = path
241		return cfg, cfg.Validate()
242	}
243	
244	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a
245	// worktree create, when a directory has already been made.
246	func (c Config) Validate() error {
247		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
248		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "none":
249		default:
250			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
251		}
252		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
253			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
254		}
255		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
256			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
257		}
258		switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
259		case "", "flat", "preserve":
260		default:
261			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
262		}
263		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
264			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
265		}
266		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
267			return fmt.Errorf("forge.remote_limit must be zero (use default) or positive")
268		}
269		validStrategy := func(v string) bool {
270			switch v {
271			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
272				return true
273			}
274			return false
275		}
276		if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
277			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
278		}
279		for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
280			if !validStrategy(strategy) {
281				return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",
282					ecosystem, strategy)
283			}
284		}
285		seen := map[string]string{}
286		for i, t := range c.TUI.Tools {
287			switch {
288			case t.Key == "":
289				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key is required", i)
290			case t.Run == "":
291				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d] (%s): run is required", i, t.Key)
292			}
293			if binding, ok := ReservedKey(t.Key); ok {
294				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is the dashboard's %q binding; pick another",
295					i, t.Key, binding)
296			}
297			if prev, ok := seen[t.Key]; ok {
298				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is already bound to %q", i, t.Key, prev)
299			}
300			seen[t.Key] = t.Name
301		}
302		return nil
303	}

8	// PostCreate accepts either of two TOML shapes, because both read naturally:
9	//
10	//	post_create = "auto"
11	//	post_create = ["uv sync", "npm ci"]
12	type PostCreate struct {
13		Auto     bool
14		Commands []string
15	}
16	
17	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
18	func (p *PostCreate) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
19		switch t := v.(type) {
20		case string:
21			if t != "auto" {
22				return fmt.Errorf("post_create: %q is not a valid string form (use \"auto\" or a list of commands)", t)
23			}
24			*p = PostCreate{Auto: true}
25			return nil
26		case []any:
27			cmds := make([]string, 0, len(t))
28			for i, e := range t {
29				s, ok := e.(string)
30				if !ok {
31					return fmt.Errorf("post_create[%d]: want a command string, got %T", i, e)
32				}
33				cmds = append(cmds, s)
34			}
35			*p = PostCreate{Commands: cmds}
36			return nil
37		default:
38			return fmt.Errorf("post_create: want \"auto\" or a list of command strings, got %T", v)
39		}
40	}
41	
42	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler so a config round-trips.
43	func (p PostCreate) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
44		if p.Auto {
45			return []byte(`"auto"`), nil
46		}
47		out := []byte("[")
48		for i, c := range p.Commands {
49			if i > 0 {
50				out = append(out, ", "...)
51			}
52			out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%q", c)...)
53		}
54		return append(out, ']'), nil
55	}
56	
57	// Duration is a time.Duration written in TOML as a Go duration string
58	// ("10m", "90s"), which is friendlier than a bare number of seconds.
59	type Duration struct{ time.Duration }
60	
61	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
62	func (d *Duration) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
63		switch t := v.(type) {
64		case string:
65			parsed, err := time.ParseDuration(t)
66			if err != nil {
67				return fmt.Errorf("duration %q: %w", t, err)
68			}
69			d.Duration = parsed
70			return nil
71		case int64:
72			d.Duration = time.Duration(t) * time.Second
73			return nil
74		default:
75			return fmt.Errorf("duration: want a string like \"10m\", got %T", v)
76		}
77	}
78	
79	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler.
80	func (d Duration) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
81		return []byte(fmt.Sprintf("%q", d.Duration.String())), nil
82	}

1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"os"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// XDG base directories, resolved the way the spec prescribes: honor the
10	// environment variable when it holds an absolute path, otherwise fall back to
11	// the documented default under $HOME.
12	
13	func xdgDir(envVar, fallback string) string {
14		if v := os.Getenv(envVar); filepath.IsAbs(v) {
15			return v
16		}
17		return filepath.Join(home(), fallback)
18	}
19	
20	func home() string {
21		if h, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil && h != "" {
22			return h
23		}
24		return os.Getenv("HOME")
25	}
26	
27	// ConfigHome is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default ~/.config).
28	func ConfigHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ".config") }
29	
30	// DataHome is $XDG_DATA_HOME (default ~/.local/share).
31	func DataHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_DATA_HOME", ".local/share") }
32	
33	// CacheHome is $XDG_CACHE_HOME (default ~/.cache).
34	func CacheHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CACHE_HOME", ".cache") }
35	
36	// ConfigFile is the path dev loads its TOML configuration from.
37	func ConfigFile() string { return filepath.Join(ConfigHome(), "dev", "config.toml") }
38	
39	// Expand resolves a leading ~ and any environment variables in p, then makes
40	// the result absolute. Paths in config.toml are written by humans, so both
41	// "~/Worktrees" and "$WORK/trees" have to work.
42	func Expand(p string) string {
43		if p == "" {
44			return ""
45		}
46		p = os.ExpandEnv(p)
47		switch {
48		case p == "~":
49			p = home()
50		case strings.HasPrefix(p, "~/"):
51			p = filepath.Join(home(), p[2:])
52		}
53		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(p); err == nil {
54			return abs
55		}
56		return filepath.Clean(p)
57	}
58	
59	// Contract renders p with $HOME collapsed back to ~, for display only.
60	func Contract(p string) string {
61		h := home()
62		if h != "" && p == h {
63			return "~"
64		}
65		if h != "" && strings.HasPrefix(p, h+string(filepath.Separator)) {
66			return "~" + p[len(h):]
67		}
68		return p
69	}

19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	}

33	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
34	func (a *App) Load() error {
35		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
36		if err != nil {
37			return err
38		}
39		a.Cfg = cfg
40		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
41		if a.Out == nil {
42			a.Out = os.Stdout
43		}
44		if a.Err == nil {
45			a.Err = os.Stderr
46		}

49	
50	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
51	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
52	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
53		if a.noRuntime {
54			return runtime.None{}
55		}
56		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
57		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
58			backend = a.runtimeOverride
59		}
60		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
61		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
62			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
63		}
64		return rt
65	}
66	
67	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
68	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
69		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
70	}
71	
72	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
73	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
74		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
75	}
76	
77	// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
78	// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
79	// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
80	// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
81	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
82		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
83	}
84	
85	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
86	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }

359	// collectRepos builds the repository view: what exists, plus how much of it is
360	// in flight.
361	func collectRepos(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime) ([]tui.RepoRow, error) {
362		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
363		if err != nil {
364			return nil, err
365		}
366		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
367		if err != nil {
368			return nil, err
369		}
370		byRepo := map[string][]*task.Task{}
371		for _, t := range tasks {
372			byRepo[t.RepoPath] = append(byRepo[t.RepoPath], t)
373		}
374		sessions, _ := rt.List(ctx)
375	
376		out := make([]tui.RepoRow, 0, len(repos))
377		for _, r := range repos {
378			row := tui.RepoRow{Repo: r, Tasks: byRepo[r.Path]}
379			if !r.Bare {
380				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path); err == nil {
381					row.Status = st
382				}
383				if list, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path); err == nil && len(list) > 0 {
384					row.Worktrees = len(list) - 1
385				}
386				row.RemoteForge, row.RemoteName = forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.Remote(ctx, r.Path, "origin"))
387			}
388			for _, s := range sessions {
389				if s.Covers(r.Path) || (r.RealPath != "" && s.Covers(r.RealPath)) {
390					row.Live = true
391					row.Runtime, row.RuntimeHandle, row.RuntimeStatus = rt.Name(), s.Handle, s.AgentStatus
392					break
393				}
394			}
395			out = append(out, row)
396		}
397		return out, nil
398	}

400	// externalTools resolves the configured tool bindings.
401	//
402	// Configurable rather than fixed because which program you reach for is
403	// personal, and because the useful ones are often your own scripts and
404	// aliases, not just the well-known tools.
405	func externalTools(app *App) []tui.Tool {
406		var out []tui.Tool
407		for _, t := range app.Cfg.EffectiveTools() {
408			run := t.Run
409			name := t.Name
410			if name == "" {
411				name = firstWord(run)
412			}
413			command := []string{shellPath(), "-c", run}
414			if t.Interactive {
415				// The command string passed to shell -lic is parsed before some
416				// shells finish loading aliases. Parse only eval "$1" up front,
417				// then evaluate the configured command after rc loading, so both
418				// aliases (vibe) and functions (claude-plans-here) work.
419				command = []string{shellPath(), "-lic", `eval "$1"`, "dev-tui-tool", run}
420			}
421			out = append(out, tui.Tool{
422				Key: t.Key, Name: name, Command: command,
423				Available: commandRunnable(run, t.Interactive),
424			})
425		}
426		return out
427	}
428	
429	// commandRunnable resolves the command's first word on PATH, expanding a
430	// leading environment variable so "$EDITOR ." checks the editor itself.
431	func commandRunnable(run string, interactive bool) func() bool {
432		// Availability is stable for the lifetime of one dashboard. In particular,
433		// probing an interactive alias starts a login shell; doing that on every
434		// render would turn a 60fps UI into a shell-launch benchmark.
435		var once sync.Once
436		available := false
437		return func() bool {
438			once.Do(func() { available = checkCommandRunnable(run, interactive) })
439			return available
440		}
441	}
442	
443	func checkCommandRunnable(run string, interactive bool) bool {
444		word := firstWord(run)
445		if strings.HasPrefix(word, "$") {
446			word = os.Getenv(strings.TrimPrefix(word, "$"))
447			if word == "" {
448				return false
449			}
450			word = firstWord(word)
451		}
452		if word == "" {
453			return false
454		}
455		if interactive {
456			// Ask the configured shell after it loads its rc files; LookPath
457			// cannot see aliases or functions.
458			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
459			defer cancel()
460			probe := exec.CommandContext(ctx, shellPath(), "-lic",
461				`command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1`, "dev-tool-probe", word)
462			return probe.Run() == nil
463		}
464		if filepath.IsAbs(word) {
465			_, err := os.Stat(word)
466			return err == nil
467		}
468		_, err := exec.LookPath(word)
469		return err == nil
470	}
471	
472	func firstWord(s string) string {
473		f := strings.Fields(s)
474		if len(f) == 0 {
475			return ""
476		}
477		return f[0]
478	}
479	
480	func shellPath() string {
481		if s := os.Getenv("SHELL"); s != "" {
482			return s
483		}
484		return "/bin/sh"
485	}

487	// remoteCachePath is private because the inventory can contain names and URLs
488	// of private repositories.
489	func remoteCachePath() string {
490		return filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "remotes.json")
491	}

493	// cachedRemotesForRepoRows uses the local repo data the dashboard already
494	// collected, avoiding another process-spawning scan on startup.
495	func cachedRemotesForRepoRows(app *App, locals []tui.RepoRow) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool) {
496		cache, ok := forge.LoadCache(remoteCachePath(), app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration)
497		if !ok {
498			return nil, false
499		}
500		byRemote := map[string]tui.RepoRow{}
501		for _, r := range locals {
502			if r.RemoteForge != forge.Unknown && r.RemoteName != "" {
503				byRemote[string(r.RemoteForge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(r.RemoteName)] = r
504			}
505		}
506		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(cache.Repos))
507		for _, rr := range cache.Repos {
508			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
509			if local, ok := byRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
510				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.Repo.Path, local.Repo.Display()
511			}
512			out = append(out, row)
513		}
514		return out, true
515	}

517	// cachedRemotes returns a fresh, already-local-matched cache for instant TUI
518	// navigation. Local paths are recomputed rather than cached because clones can
519	// move independently of the forge inventory.
520	func cachedRemotes(ctx context.Context, app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool) {
521		cache, ok := forge.LoadCache(remoteCachePath(), app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration)
522		if !ok {
523			return nil, false
524		}
525		return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, cache.Repos), true
526	}

528	// collectRemotes aggregates gh and glab, caches the normalised response, then
529	// marks remotes that already have a checkout under the configured scan roots.
530	// Calls run concurrently so one slow forge does not serialise the other.
531	func collectRemotes(ctx context.Context, app *App, limit int) ([]tui.RemoteRow, error) {
532		if limit <= 0 {
533			limit = app.Cfg.Forge.RemoteLimit
534		}
535		type result struct {
536			repos []forge.RemoteRepo
537			err   error
538		}
539		ch := make(chan result, len(forge.All()))
540		var wg sync.WaitGroup
541		available := 0
542		for _, f := range forge.All() {
543			if !f.Available() {
544				continue
545			}
546			available++
547			wg.Add(1)
548			go func(f forge.Forge) {
549				defer wg.Done()
550				r, err := f.ListRepos(ctx, limit)
551				ch <- result{repos: r, err: err}
552			}(f)
553		}
554		wg.Wait()
555		close(ch)
556		if available == 0 {
557			return nil, fmt.Errorf("neither gh nor glab is installed")
558		}
559	
560		var (
561			remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo
562			errs        []error
563		)
564		for res := range ch {
565			if res.err != nil {
566				errs = append(errs, res.err)
567			}
568			remoteRepos = append(remoteRepos, res.repos...)
569		}
570		// Cache partial results too. They are exactly what was observed, and a
571		// partial list is more useful on the next switch than another six-second
572		// wait merely to rediscover the same provider failure.
573		if len(remoteRepos) > 0 && limit >= app.Cfg.Forge.RemoteLimit {
574			_ = forge.SaveCache(remoteCachePath(), remoteRepos)
575		}
576		return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, remoteRepos), errors.Join(errs...)
577	}
578	
579	func matchRemoteLocals(ctx context.Context, app *App, remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo) []tui.RemoteRow {
580		locals, _ := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
581		localByRemote := map[string]repo.Repo{}
582		for _, r := range locals {
583			if r.Bare {
584				continue
585			}
586			kind, name := forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.Remote(ctx, r.Path, "origin"))
587			if kind != forge.Unknown && name != "" {
588				localByRemote[string(kind)+"/"+strings.ToLower(name)] = r
589			}
590		}
591		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(remoteRepos))
592		for _, rr := range remoteRepos {
593			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
594			if local, ok := localByRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
595				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.Path, local.Display()
596			}
597			out = append(out, row)
598		}
599		return out
600	}
601

303	// visibleRepos applies the text query, and sorts repositories with work in
304	// flight to the top — that is what someone opening the dashboard is looking
305	// for, not alphabetical order.
306	func (m Model) visibleRepos() []RepoRow {
307		var out []RepoRow
308		for _, r := range m.repos {
309			if !matches(r.searchText(), m.filter) {
310				continue
311			}
312			out = append(out, r)
313		}
314		sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool {
315			a, b := out[i], out[j]
316			if a.HotTasks() != b.HotTasks() {
317				return a.HotTasks() > b.HotTasks()
318			}
319			if a.Live != b.Live {
320				return a.Live
321			}
322			if len(a.Tasks) != len(b.Tasks) {
323				return len(a.Tasks) > len(b.Tasks)
324			}
325			if a.Status.Dirty() != b.Status.Dirty() {
326				return a.Status.Dirty()
327			}
328			return strings.ToLower(a.Repo.Display()) < strings.ToLower(b.Repo.Display())
329		})
330		return out
331	}

333	// visibleRemotes filters the combined gh/glab inventory. Local clones sort
334	// first, then recently updated repositories.
335	func (m Model) visibleRemotes() []RemoteRow {
336		var out []RemoteRow
337		for _, r := range m.remotes {
338			if matches(r.searchText(), m.filter) {
339				out = append(out, r)
340			}
341		}
342		sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool {
343			if out[i].Cloned() != out[j].Cloned() {
344				return out[i].Cloned()
345			}
346			if !out[i].Repo.UpdatedAt.Equal(out[j].Repo.UpdatedAt) {
347				return out[i].Repo.UpdatedAt.After(out[j].Repo.UpdatedAt)
348			}
349			return out[i].Repo.Label() < out[j].Repo.Label()
350		})
351		return out
352	}

566	func (m Model) updateList(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
567		n := m.count()
568		page := m.listHeight() / 2
569		if page < 1 {
570			page = 1
571		}
572	
573		switch msg.String() {
574		case "q", "ctrl+c":
575			m.quitting = true
576			return m, tea.Quit
577		case "esc":
578			// One escape clears whatever narrowing is in effect before quitting
579			// becomes the meaning of the key.
580			if m.filter != "" || len(m.states) > 0 {
581				m.filter, m.states = "", nil
582				m.setAt(0)
583				return m, nil
584			}
585			m.quitting = true
586			return m, tea.Quit
587	
588		// Vim-style movement, with the arrow equivalents alongside.
589		case "j", "down", "ctrl+n":
590			m.setAt(m.at() + 1)
591		case "k", "up", "ctrl+p":
592			m.setAt(m.at() - 1)
593		case "ctrl+d", "pgdown":
594			m.setAt(m.at() + page)
595		case "ctrl+u", "pgup":
596			m.setAt(m.at() - page)
597		case "g", "home":
598			m.setAt(0)
599		case "G", "end":
600			m.setAt(n - 1)
601	
602		// View switching. h/l double as left/right between views, since a list has
603		// no horizontal axis of its own.
604		case "tab", "l", "right":
605			m.view = Views[(int(m.view)+1)%len(Views)]
606			return m.afterViewSwitch()
607		case "shift+tab", "h", "left":
608			m.view = Views[(int(m.view)+len(Views)-1)%len(Views)]
609			return m.afterViewSwitch()
610	
611		case "/":
612			m.mode = modeFilter
613			m.input.SetValue(m.filter)
614			m.input.Placeholder = "filter"
615			m.input.CursorEnd()
616			m.input.Focus()
617			return m, textinput.Blink
618	
619		case "r":
620			m.status = "reloading config + data…"
621			if m.view == ViewRemote {
622				m.remotesLoading = true
623			}
624			return m, m.reloadConfig(m.view == ViewRemote)
625	
626		case "1":
627			m.states, m.showDone = []task.State{task.Hot}, false
628			m.view = ViewTasks
629			m.setAt(0)
630		case "2":
631			m.states, m.showDone = []task.State{task.Warm}, false
632			m.view = ViewTasks

807	func (m Model) submit(md mode, value string) tea.Cmd {
808		switch md {
809		case modeEditNext:
810			row, ok := m.currentTask()
811			if !ok {
812				return nil
813			}
814			t := row.Task
815			return func() tea.Msg {
816				if err := m.actions.SetNext(context.Background(), t, value); err != nil {
817					return actionMsg{err: err}
818				}
819				return actionMsg{status: "next action recorded for " + t.Title()}
820			}
821	
822		case modeConfirmPark:
823			row, ok := m.currentTask()
824			if !ok {
825				return nil
826			}
827			t := row.Task
828			return func() tea.Msg {
829				status, err := m.actions.Park(context.Background(), t, value)
830				return actionMsg{status: status, err: err}
831			}
832	
833		case modeStartTask:
834			r, ok := m.currentRepo()
835			if !ok {
836				return nil
837			}
838			if value == "" {
839				return func() tea.Msg { return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("a task needs a name")} }
840			}
841			return func() tea.Msg {
842				status, err := m.actions.Start(context.Background(), r, value)
843				return actionMsg{status: status, err: err}
844			}
845	
846		case modeConfirmClone:
847			r, ok := m.currentRemote()
848			if !ok {
849				return nil
850			}
851			return func() tea.Msg {
852				status, path, err := m.actions.CloneRemote(context.Background(), r)
853				return actionMsg{
854					status: status, remoteName: r.Repo.FullName, localPath: path, err: err,
855				}
856			}
857		}
858		return nil
859	}

861	func (m Model) openSelected() tea.Cmd {
862		cdWanted := m.actions.Runtime != nil && m.actions.Runtime.Name() == "none"
863	
864		if row, ok := m.currentTask(); ok {
865			t := row.Task
866			dir := row.Checkout
867			return func() tea.Msg {
868				status, err := m.actions.Open(context.Background(), t)
869				cd := ""
870				if err == nil && cdWanted {
871					cd = dir
872				}
873				return actionMsg{status: status, cd: cd, err: err}
874			}
875		}
876		if r, ok := m.currentRepo(); ok {
877			dir := r.Repo.Path
878			return func() tea.Msg {
879				status, err := m.actions.OpenRepo(context.Background(), r)
880				cd := ""
881				if err == nil && cdWanted {
882					cd = dir
883				}
884				return actionMsg{status: status, cd: cd, err: err}
885			}
886		}
887		if r, ok := m.currentRemote(); ok {
888			if !r.Cloned() {
889				return nil // c is the explicit clone action
890			}
891			dir := r.LocalPath
892			return func() tea.Msg {
893				status, err := m.actions.OpenRemote(context.Background(), r)
894				cd := ""
895				if err == nil && cdWanted {
896					cd = dir
897				}
898				return actionMsg{status: status, cd: cd, err: err}
899			}
900		}
901		return nil
902	}

904	// launchTool hands the terminal to an external program running in the selected
905	// row's checkout, then reloads — the tool may well have changed the git state
906	// the dashboard is displaying.
907	func (m Model) launchTool(key string) tea.Cmd {
908		for _, t := range m.actions.Tools {
909			if t.Key != key {
910				continue
911			}
912			if t.Available != nil && !t.Available() {
913				return func() tea.Msg {
914					return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("%s is not installed", t.Command[0])}
915				}
916			}
917			dir := m.currentDir()
918			if dir == "" {
919				return func() tea.Msg {
920					return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("nothing selected with a checkout on disk")}
921				}
922			}
923			c := exec.Command(t.Command[0], t.Command[1:]...)
924			c.Dir = dir
925			return tea.ExecProcess(c, func(err error) tea.Msg {
926				if err != nil {
927					return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", t.Name, err)}
928				}
929				return actionMsg{status: "back from " + t.Name}
930			})
931		}
932		return nil
933	}
934	
935	// Tools lists the external programs available on this machine, so the footer
936	// only advertises bindings that will actually work.
937	func (m Model) Tools() []Tool {
938		var out []Tool
939		for _, t := range m.actions.Tools {
940			if t.Available == nil || t.Available() {
941				out = append(out, t)
942			}
943		}
944		return out
945	}
946	
947	// Summary counts the task states, for the header line.
948	func (m Model) Summary() string {
949		counts := map[task.State]int{}
950		for _, r := range m.rows {
951			counts[r.Task.State]++
952		}
953		var parts []string
954		for _, s := range task.States {
955			if counts[s] > 0 {
956				parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s %d %s", s.Icon(), counts[s], s))
957			}
958		}
959		if len(m.repos) > 0 {
960			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%d repos", len(m.repos)))
961		}
962		if m.remotesLoaded {
963			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%d remote", len(m.remotes)))
964		}
965		if len(parts) == 0 {
966			return "no tasks"
967		}
968		return strings.Join(parts, "   ")
969	}

251	func remoteAge(r RemoteRow) string {
252		if r.Repo.UpdatedAt.IsZero() {
253			return "—"
254		}
255		d := time.Since(r.Repo.UpdatedAt)
256		switch {
257		case d < 24*time.Hour:
258			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh ago", int(d.Hours()))
259		case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
260			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd ago", int(d.Hours()/24))
261		case d < 60*24*time.Hour:
262			return fmt.Sprintf("%dw ago", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
263		default:
264			return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo ago", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
265		}
266	}

286				"  " + styleDim.Render("Press tab for the repository list, then s to start work on one.\n") +
287				"  " + styleDim.Render("Or run `dev adopt` to import worktrees and branches already in flight.\n")

292	func (m Model) columnWidths() (name, branch, next int) {
293		const fixed = 2 + 6 + 16 + 5 + 10
294		avail := m.width - fixed
295		if avail < 40 {
296			avail = 40
297		}
298		name = clamp(avail*30/100, 12, 30)
299		branch = clamp(avail*30/100, 12, 30)
300		next = avail - name - branch
301		if next < 10 {
302			next = 10
303		}
304		return name, branch, next
305	}

435				bindings = append(bindings, "enter open local")

437				bindings = append(bindings, "c clone")

439		default:

441		}

443		for _, t := range m.Tools() {

445		}

456	// wrapBindings lays the key hints out over as many lines as the width needs,
457	// rather than truncating them — a hint you cannot read is not a hint.
458	func wrapBindings(items []string, width int) string {
459		if width < 20 {
460			width = 20
461		}
462		var lines []string
463		cur := ""
464		for _, it := range items {
465			candidate := it
466			if cur != "" {
467				candidate = cur + " · " + it
468			}
469			if lipgloss.Width(candidate) > width && cur != "" {
470				lines = append(lines, cur)
471				cur = it
472				continue
473			}
474			cur = candidate
475		}
476		if cur != "" {
477			lines = append(lines, cur)
478		}
479		return strings.Join(lines, "\n  ")
480	}

483		switch {
484		case r.StatusErr != nil:
485			return "?"
486		case !r.CheckoutExists:
487			return "no dir"
488		}
489		return r.Status.Summary()

499	func shortAge(r inventory.Row) string {
500		d := r.Age()
501		switch {
502		case d <= 0:
503			return "—"
504		case d.Hours() < 24:
505			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
506		case d.Hours() < 24*14:
507			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
508		case d.Hours() < 24*60:
509			return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
510		default:
511			return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
512		}
513	}

515	func colourState(s task.State, line string) string {
516		switch s {
517		case task.Hot:
518			return styleHot.Render(line)
519		case task.Warm:
520			return styleWarm.Render(line)
521		case task.Cold:
522			return styleCold.Render(line)
523		case task.Done:
524			return styleDone.Render(line)
525		}
526		return line
527	}

529	// pad truncates to n display columns, measuring the way lipgloss renders so
530	// CJK repo and task names do not shift the table.
531	func pad(s string, n int) string {
532		if lipgloss.Width(s) <= n {
533			return s
534		}
535		var b strings.Builder
536		used := 0
537		for _, r := range s {
538			w := lipgloss.Width(string(r))
539			if used+w > n-1 {
540				break
541			}
542			b.WriteRune(r)
543			used += w
544		}
545		return b.String() + "…"
546	}
547	
548	func clamp(v, lo, hi int) int {
549		if v < lo {
550			return lo
551		}
552		if v > hi {
553			return hi
554		}
555		return v
556	}

15	// RepoRow is one repository as the dashboard shows it: what it is, plus how
16	// much of it is currently in flight.
17	//
18	// The repository view exists because the task list alone answers only half the
19	// question. On a machine with forty repositories and no tasks recorded yet,
20	// a task-only dashboard is empty — and the honest answer to "what do I have
21	// here?" has to come before "what am I working on?"
22	type RepoRow struct {
23		Repo   repo.Repo
24		Status gitx.Status
25		// Worktrees is the number of linked worktrees, excluding the main checkout.
26		Worktrees int
27		// Tasks are the recorded tasks belonging to this repository.
28		Tasks []*task.Task
29		// Live reports a runtime session sitting in this repository.
30		Live          bool
31		Runtime       string
32		RuntimeHandle string
33		RuntimeStatus string
34		// RemoteForge / RemoteName identify origin for matching the REMOTE view to
35		// this local checkout without rescanning every repo when a cache opens.
36		RemoteForge forge.Kind
37		RemoteName  string
38	}
39	
40	// HotTasks counts the repository's tasks that are currently hot.
41	func (r RepoRow) HotTasks() int {
42		n := 0
43		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
44			if t.State == task.Hot {
45				n++
46			}
47		}
48		return n
49	}
50	
51	// StateSummary renders the repository's tasks as a compact per-state tally,
52	// which is what makes the list scannable at forty repositories.
53	func (r RepoRow) StateSummary() string {
54		if len(r.Tasks) == 0 {
55			return ""
56		}
57		counts := map[task.State]int{}
58		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
59			counts[t.State]++
60		}
61		var parts []string
62		for _, s := range task.States {
63			if counts[s] > 0 {
64				parts = append(parts, s.Icon()+strconv.Itoa(counts[s]))
65			}
66		}
67		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
68	}
69	
70	// searchText is what a filter query matches against.
71	func (r RepoRow) searchText() string {
72		var b strings.Builder
73		b.WriteString(r.Repo.Display())
74		b.WriteString(" ")
75		b.WriteString(r.Status.Branch)
76		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
77			b.WriteString(" ")
78			b.WriteString(t.Title())
79			b.WriteString(" ")
80			b.WriteString(t.Branch)
81		}
82		return strings.ToLower(b.String())
83	}
84	
85	// taskSearchText is what a filter query matches a task row against.
86	func taskSearchText(r inventory.Row) string {
87		t := r.Task
88		return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
89			t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.Next, t.Note, string(t.State),
90		}, " "))
91	}
92	
93	// matches reports whether every whitespace-separated term of the query appears
94	// in the haystack.
95	//
96	// Term-wise rather than substring so "auth api" finds a task named "api token
97	// auth" — the order words come to mind in is rarely the order they appear in.
98	func matches(haystack, query string) bool {
99		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
100		if query == "" {
101			return true
102		}
103		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
104			if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
105				return false
106			}
107		}
108		return true
109	}
110	
111	// RemoteRow is one repository known to GitHub or GitLab, optionally matched to
112	// a local checkout. The REMOTE view is the bridge between "what exists on the
113	// forge" and "what is already on this machine".
114	type RemoteRow struct {
115		Repo forge.RemoteRepo `json:"repo"`
116		// LocalPath is the checkout under the configured scan roots, empty when the
117		// remote has not been cloned here.
118		LocalPath string `json:"local_path,omitempty"`
119		// LocalName is the discovered repo's display name.
120		LocalName string `json:"local_name,omitempty"`
121	}
122	
123	// Cloned reports whether this remote already has a local checkout.
124	func (r RemoteRow) Cloned() bool { return r.LocalPath != "" }
125

129			r.Repo.Visibility, r.Repo.DefaultBranch, r.LocalName,
130		}, " "))

18	func newTryCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
19		var (
20			list  bool
21			clone string
22			noGit bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "try [name]",
26			Short: "Make a dated scratch directory for an experiment",
27			Long: `Create (or jump to) a dated experiment directory under paths.tries_root.
28	
29	Experiments need a home that is neither /tmp (where they vanish) nor your
30	projects directory (where they accumulate as clutter you are afraid to delete).
31	A try is date-prefixed, disposable by default, and promotable with
32	"dev graduate" when it turns out to be real.
33	
34	  dev try                    list what is there
35	  dev try redis-streams      jump to a matching try, or create 2026-08-27-redis-streams
36	  dev try --clone <url>      clone a repo into a dated try directory`,
37			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
38			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
39				ctx := ctxOf()
40				root := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot)
41				if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
42					return err
43				}
44	
45				if list || (len(args) == 0 && clone == "") {
46					return listTries(app, root)
47				}
48	
49				name := ""
50				if len(args) == 1 {
51					name = args[0]
52				}
53				if clone != "" && name == "" {
54					name = repoNameFromRef(clone)
55				}
56				slug := config.Slug(strings.ReplaceAll(name, " ", "-"))
57	
58				// An existing try wins over creating a near-duplicate: the whole
59				// point is to stop accumulating test/test2/test-actually.
60				if match := findTry(root, slug); match != "" && clone == "" {
61					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(match))
62					return openOrCD(app, ctx, match, filepath.Base(match))
63				}
64	
65				dir := filepath.Join(root, time.Now().Format("2006-01-02")+"-"+slug)
66				if _, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil {
67					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(dir))
68					return openOrCD(app, ctx, dir, filepath.Base(dir))
69				}
70	
71				if clone != "" {
72					url := clone
73					if k := forge.FromURL(clone); k != forge.Unknown {
74						if f, err := forge.For(k); err == nil {
75							url = f.CloneURL(clone)
76						}
77					}
78					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, root, "clone", url, dir); err != nil {
79						return err
80					}
81				} else {
82					if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
83						return err
84					}
85					if !noGit {
86						// A try with git history can be graduated without losing
87						// the path that got there, which is most of its value.
88						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "init", "-b", "main"); err != nil {
89							app.warnf("could not git init: %v", err)
90						}
91					}
92				}
93				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(dir))
94				return openOrCD(app, ctx, dir, filepath.Base(dir))
95			},
96		}
97		f := cmd.Flags()
98		f.BoolVarP(&list, "list", "l", false, "list existing tries")

100		f.BoolVar(&noGit, "no-git", false, "do not git init the new directory")
101		return cmd
102	}

104	// tryEntry is one scratch directory with the facts needed to rank it.
105	type tryEntry struct {
106		name     string
107		path     string
108		modified time.Time
109		isRepo   bool
110		dirty    bool
111	}
112	
113	func listTries(app *App, root string) error {
114		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
115		if err != nil {
116			return err
117		}
118		var tries []tryEntry
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			if !e.IsDir() || strings.HasPrefix(e.Name(), ".") {
121				continue
122			}
123			info, err := e.Info()
124			if err != nil {
125				continue
126			}
127			path := filepath.Join(root, e.Name())
128			t := tryEntry{name: e.Name(), path: path, modified: info.ModTime()}
129			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
130				t.isRepo = true
131				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctxOf(), path); err == nil {
132					t.dirty = st.Dirty()
133				}
134			}
135			tries = append(tries, t)
136		}
137		if len(tries) == 0 {
138			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "No tries yet under %s\n", config.Contract(root))
139			return nil
140		}
141		// Most recently touched first: "what was I doing yesterday?" is the
142		// question a list of experiments actually gets asked.
143		sort.Slice(tries, func(i, j int) bool { return tries[i].modified.After(tries[j].modified) })
144	
145		tbl := NewTable("TRY", "AGE", "GIT")
146		for _, t := range tries {
147			gitCol := "—"
148			switch {
149			case t.isRepo && t.dirty:
150				gitCol = "repo ●"
151			case t.isRepo:
152				gitCol = "repo"
153			}
154			tbl.Add(truncate(t.name, 44), humanAge(time.Since(t.modified)), gitCol)
155		}
156		tbl.Render(app.Out)
157		fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\n%d tries under %s — promote one with `dev graduate <try>`\n",
158			len(tries), config.Contract(root))
159		return nil
160	}
161	
162	// findTry locates an existing try whose name contains the slug, preferring the
163	// most recent when several match.
164	func findTry(root, slug string) string {
165		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
166		if err != nil {
167			return ""
168		}
169		var best string
170		var bestTime time.Time
171		for _, e := range entries {
172			if !e.IsDir() || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(e.Name()), strings.ToLower(slug)) {
173				continue
174			}
175			info, err := e.Info()
176			if err != nil {
177				continue
178			}
179			if info.ModTime().After(bestTime) {
180				best, bestTime = filepath.Join(root, e.Name()), info.ModTime()
181			}
182		}
183		return best
184	}
185	
186	func openOrCD(app *App, ctx context.Context, dir, label string) error {
187		rt := app.Runtime()
188		if rt.Name() == "none" {
189			app.cdDirective(dir)
190			return nil
191		}
192		if _, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, dir, label); err != nil {
193			app.warnf("could not open a session: %v", err)
194		}
195		return nil
196	}

79	// send feeds a sequence of key presses through Update, running any command the
80	// model returns so the action callbacks actually fire — that is what makes
81	// these tests exercise the real key bindings rather than the model's fields.
82	func send(m tui.Model, msgs ...tea.Msg) tui.Model {
83		var cur tea.Model = m
84		for _, msg := range msgs {
85			var cmd tea.Cmd
86			cur, cmd = cur.Update(msg)
87			// Follow the command chain, so an action's resulting message (and the
88			// reload it triggers) is applied too. Commands that do not return
89			// promptly are the cursor's blink timers; running those would make the
90			// suite sleep for half a second per keystroke.
91			for i := 0; cmd != nil && i < 8; i++ {
92				out, ok := runQuickly(cmd)
93				if !ok || out == nil {
94					break
95				}
96				if _, isBatch := out.(tea.BatchMsg); isBatch {
97					break
98				}
99				cur, cmd = cur.Update(out)
100			}
101		}
102		return cur.(tui.Model)
103	}
104	
105	// runQuickly executes a command, giving up on anything that blocks — which in
106	// practice means the cursor blink timers.
107	func runQuickly(cmd tea.Cmd) (tea.Msg, bool) {
108		done := make(chan tea.Msg, 1)
109		go func() { done <- cmd() }()
110		select {
111		case msg := <-done:
112			return msg, true
113		case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
114			return nil, false
115		}
116	}
117	
118	func key(s string) tea.KeyMsg {
119		switch s {
120		case "enter":
121			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEnter}
122		case "esc":
123			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEsc}
124		case "down":
125			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyDown}
126		case "up":
127			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyUp}
128		}
129		return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune(s)}
130	}
131	
132	func typeText(s string) []tea.KeyMsg {
133		out := make([]tea.KeyMsg, 0, len(s))
134		for _, r := range s {
135			out = append(out, tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune{r}})
136		}
137		return out
138	}

34	
35	  default        create a branch + linked worktree, provision it, open a
36	                 runtime session, and record the task. Safest for work that
37	                 may be interrupted or run in parallel.
38	  --branch-only  create/switch a branch in the canonical checkout, with no
39	                 worktree. Lighter, but that checkout cannot host another
40	                 branch concurrently.
41	  --direct       track the branch already checked out in the canonical repo —
42	                 usually main — without creating either a branch or worktree.
43	                 Best for one-session ad-hoc changes.
44	
45	For untracked ad-hoc navigation, use "dev repo open" or press Enter in the
46	TUI's REPOS view; that opens the project without creating any task at all.
47	
48	With no repo argument, the repository containing the current directory is used.
49	Always pass --base for an unattended branch/worktree task.`,
50			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
51			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
52				ctx := ctxOf()
53				if direct && (branchOnly || noWorktree) {
54					return errors.New("--direct and --branch-only are different modes; pick one")
55				}
56				branchOnly = branchOnly || noWorktree
57	
58				// Resolve the repository: an explicit argument, else the cwd.
59				var repoPath, repoName, category string
60				if len(args) == 1 {
61					r, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), args[0])
62					if err != nil {
63						return err
64					}
65					repoPath, repoName, category = r.Path, r.Name, r.Category
66				} else {
67					cwd, err := os.Getwd()
68					if err != nil {
69						return err
70					}
71					g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
72					if err != nil {
73						return fmt.Errorf("no repo argument and %s is not a git repository", config.Contract(cwd))
74					}
75					repoPath, repoName = g.MainRoot, g.Name
76				}
77	
78				if name == "" {

80						name = branch

83					}

96					}

98						return fmt.Errorf("--direct tracks the branch already checked out (%s), not --branch %s; "+
99							"omit --branch or use --branch-only", st.Branch, branch)
100					}
101					branch, base = st.Branch, st.Branch
102	
103				case branchOnly:
104					mode = task.ModeBranch
105					if branch == "" {
106						branch = "feat/" + config.Slug(name)
107					}
108					if base == "" {
109						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
110					}
111	
112				default:
113					if branch == "" {
114						branch = "feat/" + config.Slug(name)
115					}
116					if base == "" {
117						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
118					}
119				}
120	
121				id := task.MakeID(repoName, branch)
122				if existing, err := app.Tasks.Get(id); err == nil {
123					return fmt.Errorf("task %s already exists (state %s) — use `dev resume %s`",
124						existing.ID, existing.State, existing.ID)
125				}
126	
127				t := &task.Task{
128					Name: name, Repo: repoName, RepoPath: repoPath,
129					Branch: branch, Base: base, Mode: mode,

131				}

133

136					handle, err := rt.Open(ctx, repoPath, repoName+"/"+name)
137					if err != nil {
138						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
139					} else if rt.Name() != "none" {

141					}

143				case task.ModeBranch:

146							return fmt.Errorf("switch to %s: %w", branch, err)
147						}
148					} else {
149						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "switch", "-c", branch, base); err != nil {
150							return fmt.Errorf("create and switch to %s from %s: %w", branch, base, err)
151						}
152					}

210	// checkoutOf is where a task's code lives right now.
211	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
212		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
213			return t.WorktreePath
214		}
215		return t.RepoPath
216	}
217	
218	// annotate pushes the task's state and next action into the runtime as
219	// display-only metadata, so a sidebar can show why a session is open without
220	// anyone having to ask dev.
221	//
222	// For herdr this lands as workspace metadata tokens. A token only renders if
223	// the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
224	//
225	//	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
226	//	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
227	//
228	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
229	// which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
230	func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
231		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
232			return
233		}
234		kv := map[string]string{
235			"stage": t.State.Label(),
236			"next":  t.Next,
237		}
238		if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
239			app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
240		}
241	}
242	
243	func reportProvision(app *App, res *wt.CreateResult) {
244		p := res.Provision
245		if n := len(p.Copied); n > 0 {
246			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   copied    %d gitignored file(s): %s\n", n, strings.Join(p.Copied, ", "))
247		}
248		if n := len(p.Linked); n > 0 {
249			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   linked    %s\n", strings.Join(p.Linked, ", "))
250		}
251		for _, e := range p.Failures {
252			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   warning   %v\n", e)
253		}
254	}

15	func newParkCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

18			note   string
19			wip    bool
20			push   bool
21			cold   bool
22			keepRT bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "park [task]",
26			Short: "Stop working on a task without losing the thread",
27			Long: `Park the current task (or the one named) so its runtime session can close.
28	
29	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
30	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
31	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
32	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
33	
34	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
35	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstruct
36	                  it anywhere later with dev resume.
37	
38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()
44				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48	
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59	
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124	
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}
136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {
137					// Free the canonical checkout for other work. The branch remains
138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", t.Base); err != nil {
140						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
141							t.Base, err)
142					}
143				}
144	
145				t.State = target
146				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
147				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
148					return err
149				}
150				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
151				if t.Next != "" {
152					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
153				}
154				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
155				return nil
156			},
157		}
158		f := cmd.Flags()
159		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
160		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
161		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
162		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
163		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
164		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
165		return cmd
166	}
167	
168	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
169	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
170		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
171			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
172		}
173		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
174		return nil
175	}
176	
177	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
178	// directory when no argument is given.
179	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
180		if len(args) == 1 {
181			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
182		}
183		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
184		if err != nil {
185			return nil, err
186		}
187		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
188		if err != nil {
189			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
190				config.Contract(cwd))
191		}
192		return t, nil
193	}
