```text
14	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			noProvision bool
17			fetch       bool
18			force       bool
19		)
20		cmd := &cobra.Command{
21			Use:   "resume <task>",
22			Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
23			Long: `Make a parked task hot again.
24	
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29	
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
33			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
34			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
35				ctx := ctxOf()
36				t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				if err != nil {
38					return err
39				}
40	
41				host := config.Hostname()
42				if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
43					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47	
48				if fetch {
49					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin"); err != nil {
50						app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
51					}
52				}
53	
54				rt := app.Runtime()
55				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
56				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
57	
58				switch mode {
59				case task.ModeWorktree:
60					_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
61					// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
63						base := t.Base
64						// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
65						// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
66						if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
67							base = remote
68						}
69						m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
70						res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
71							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, RepoName: t.Repo, Branch: t.Branch,
72							Base: base, Label: t.Title(), NoProvision: noProvision,
73						})
74						if err != nil {
75							var exists *wt.ErrExists
76							if asError(err, &exists) {
77								t.WorktreePath = exists.Path
78							} else {
79								return err
80							}
81						} else {
82							t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
83							reportProvision(app, res)
84							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebuilt    %s\n", config.Contract(res.Path))
85						}
86						checkout = t.WorktreePath
87					}
88	
89				case task.ModeBranch:
90					checkout = t.RepoPath
91					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
92					if err != nil {
93						return err
94					}
95					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
96						if st.Dirty() {
97							return fmt.Errorf("cannot switch the canonical checkout from %s to %s: %s",
98								st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())
99						}
100						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "switch", t.Branch); err != nil {
101							return err
102						}
103					}
104	
105				case task.ModeDirect:
106					checkout = t.RepoPath
107					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
108					if err != nil {
109						return err
110					}
111					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
112						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s tracks %s, but the canonical checkout is on %s; "+
113							"switch back explicitly or start a worktree task", t.Title(), t.Branch, st.Branch)
114					}
115				}
116				if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
117					handle, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, checkout, t.Title())
118					if err != nil {
119						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
120					}
121					if rt.Name() != "none" {
122						t.RuntimeHandle = handle
123					}
124				}
125	
126				t.State = task.Hot
127				t.Owner = host
128				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
129					return err
130				}
131				annotate(app, rt, t)
132	
133				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s  %s on %s (%s)\n",
134					task.Hot.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, mode)
135				if t.Next != "" {
136					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   next      %s\n", t.Next)
137				}
138				if t.AgentSession != "" {
139					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   agent     %s (resumable)\n", t.AgentSession)
140				}
141				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout); err == nil {
142					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   git       %s\n", st.Summary())
143					if st.Behind > 0 {
144						app.warnf("branch is %d behind upstream — `git pull --ff-only` before you start", st.Behind)
145					}
146				}
147				if rt.Name() == "none" {
148					app.cdDirective(checkout)
149				}
150				return nil
151			},

155		f.BoolVar(&fetch, "fetch", true, "fetch from origin first")
156		f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "take ownership of a task owned by another machine")
157		return cmd
158	}
```

```text
16	func newDoneCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
17		var (
18			ff           bool
19			pr           bool
20			deleteBranch bool
21			keepWorktree bool
22			push         bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "done [task]",
26			Short: "Integrate a finished change stream and clean up",
27			Long: `Finish a task: integrate the branch, then remove what it leaves behind.
28	
29	Two integration modes, matching the two shapes a branch's history takes:
30	
31	  --ff    rebase onto the base and fast-forward it. Use when the branch's
32	          commits are worth keeping in the base's history.
33	  --pr    push and open a pull/merge request with gh or glab, leaving the
34	          merge to review and CI. Use when someone (or something) should look
35	          at it first.
36	
37	With neither, dev only reports what it would do.
38	
39	Cleanup is deliberately conservative: the worktree is removed, the task entry
40	is marked done, and the branch is deleted only with --delete-branch. A merged
41	branch that still has unpushed commits is never deleted.`,
42			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
43			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
44				ctx := ctxOf()
45				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
46				if err != nil {
47					return err
48				}
49				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
50				if _, err := os.Stat(checkout); err != nil {
51					return fmt.Errorf("%s no longer exists — resume the task first", config.Contract(checkout))
52				}
53	
54				st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
55				if err != nil {
56					return err
57				}
58				if st.Dirty() {
59					return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes: %s.\n"+
60						"Commit them, or park the task with --wip, before finishing it",
61						config.Contract(checkout), st.Breakdown())
62				}
63	
64				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
65				if mode == task.ModeDirect {
66					if ff || pr || deleteBranch || keepWorktree {
67						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s is already on %s; it has no branch/worktree to integrate. "+
68							"Run `dev done` without --ff/--pr/--delete-branch/--keep-worktree", t.Title(), t.Branch)
69					}
70					if push {
71						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
72							return err
73						}
74					}
75					rt := app.Runtime()
76					if t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
77						if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
78							app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
79						}
80						t.RuntimeHandle = ""
81					}
82					t.State = task.Done
83					if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s completed directly on %s\n", task.Done.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Branch)
87					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   no branch or worktree was created or removed")
88					return nil
89				}
90	
91				base := t.Base
92				if base == "" {
93					base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
94				}
95				if base == "" {
96					return fmt.Errorf("cannot determine the base branch for %s — pass --base when starting a task", t.Repo)
97				}
98	
99				switch {
100				case ff && pr:
101					return fmt.Errorf("--ff and --pr are alternatives; pick one")
102				case pr:
103					if err := openPR(ctx, app, t, checkout, base); err != nil {
104						return err
105					}
106					// A PR hands integration to review; the task is not done yet,
107					// so state and cleanup stay untouched.
108					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nThe branch is under review — run `dev done --ff` or `dev sweep` after it merges.")
109					return nil
110				case ff:
111					if err := fastForward(ctx, app, t, checkout, base); err != nil {
112						return err
113					}
114				default:
115					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s on %s (base %s, %s)\n", t.Title(), t.Branch, base, st.Summary())
116					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing done. Choose an integration mode:")
117					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  dev done --ff    rebase onto "+base+" and fast-forward it")
118					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  dev done --pr    push and open a pull request")
119					return nil
120				}
121	
122				if push {
123					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "push", "origin", base); err != nil {
124						app.warnf("could not push %s: %v", base, err)
125					} else {
126						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", base)
127					}
128				}
129	
130				rt := app.Runtime()
131				if t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
132					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
133						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
134					}
135					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
136				}
137				if t.WorktreePath != "" && !keepWorktree {
138					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
139					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath}); err != nil {
140						app.warnf("could not remove the worktree: %v", err)
141					} else {
142						t.WorktreePath = ""
143					}
144				}
145				if deleteBranch {

151				t.State = task.Done
152				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
153					return err
154				}
155				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s merged into %s\n", task.Done.Icon(), t.Title(), base)
156				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   the task entry stays until `dev sweep --apply` reaps it\n")
157				return nil
158			},
159		}
160		f := cmd.Flags()
161		f.BoolVar(&ff, "ff", false, "rebase onto the base and fast-forward it")
162		f.BoolVar(&pr, "pr", false, "push and open a pull/merge request instead of merging locally")
163		f.BoolVar(&keepWorktree, "keep-worktree", false, "keep the worktree checkout")
164		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the resulting branch (direct mode pushes its current branch)")
165		// Off by default: a branch is cheap to keep and expensive to recreate, and
166		// "merged" is not always "finished" — work often continues on a branch
167		// after its first integration.
168		f.BoolVar(&deleteBranch, "delete-branch", false, "delete the branch once its commits are in the base")
169		return cmd
170	}
171	
172	func directPushHint(push bool) string {
173		if push {
174			return " --push"
175		}
176		return ""
177	}
178	
179	// fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
180	// forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
181	//
182	// merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
183	// branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
184	// a merge commit the user did not ask for.
185	func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
186		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
187		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
188			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
189				"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
190				err, config.Contract(checkout))
191		}
192		// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
193		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
194		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
195			return err
196		}
197		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
198			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
199				"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
200		}
201		return nil
202	}
203	
204	// deleteMergedBranch removes a branch only when git agrees its commits are already
205	// contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
206	func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
207		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
208			return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
209		}
210		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "branch", "-d", branch); err != nil {
211			return fmt.Errorf("could not delete %s: %w", branch, err)
212		}
213		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   deleted    branch %s\n", branch)
214		return nil
215	}
216	
217	// openPR pushes the branch and asks the forge CLI to open a pull/merge
218	// request. When no forge CLI is available dev prints the push result and the
219	// URL to open by hand, rather than failing: the branch being published is the
220	// part that actually matters.
221	func openPR(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
222		if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
223			return err
224		}
225		kind := forge.Detect(ctx, t.RepoPath)
226		f, err := forge.For(kind)
227		if err != nil || !f.Available() {
228			app.warnf("no forge CLI for this remote — the branch is pushed; open the request in your browser")
229			return nil
230		}
231		url, err := f.CreatePR(ctx, checkout, forge.PRRequest{
232			Base: base, Head: t.Branch, Fill: true,
233		})
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		if url != "" {
238			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   opened     %s\n", url)
239		}
240		return nil
241	}
```

```text
20	// suggestion is one proposed change, with the reason and the exact effect.
21	type suggestion struct {
22		row    inventory.Row
23		action string
24		reason string
25		// apply performs the change. nil means "report only".
26		apply func() error
27	}
28	
29	func newSweepCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
30		var (
31			apply     bool
32			staleDays int
33			yes       bool
34		)
35		cmd := &cobra.Command{
36			Use:   "sweep",
37			Short: "Review stale tasks and drifted state, and act on them",
38			Long: `Show which tasks have gone stale or drifted, and what dev would do about it.
39	
40	Cleanup usually fails not because people are unwilling but because there is no
41	trustworthy way to be sure the work is recoverable. So sweep reports first and
42	only changes things with --apply, confirming each one unless you pass --yes.
43	Nothing here ever deletes uncommitted work.`,
44			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
45			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
46				ctx := ctxOf()
47				tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
48				if err != nil {
49					return err
50				}
51				rt := app.Runtime()
52				rows := inventory.Collect(ctx, tasks, rt, inventory.Options{})
53				stale := time.Duration(staleDays) * 24 * time.Hour
54	
55				var sugg []suggestion
56				for _, r := range rows {
57					sugg = append(sugg, suggestFor(app, ctx, rt, r, stale)...)
58				}
59	
60				// Live sessions no task claims: the other half of a crowded sidebar.
61				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
62					if orphans := inventory.Orphans(sessions, rows); len(orphans) > 0 {
63						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d live session(s) with no task recorded:\n", len(orphans))
64						for _, s := range orphans {
65							dir := "—"
66							if len(s.Dirs) > 0 {
67								dir = config.Contract(s.Dirs[0])
68							}
69							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %-24s %s\n", truncate(s.Label, 24), dir)
70						}
71						fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  → `dev start` in one of those directories to track it, or just close it.")
72					}
73				}
74	
75				if len(sugg) == 0 {
76					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nNothing to sweep — every task matches its recorded state.")
77					return nil
78				}
79	
80				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d suggestion(s):\n\n", len(sugg))
81				for _, s := range sugg {
82					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s %-28s %s\n", s.row.Task.State.Icon(),
83						truncate(s.row.Task.Title(), 28), s.reason)
84					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "     → %s\n", s.action)
85				}
86	
87				if !apply {
88					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nRe-run with --apply to act on these (each is confirmed individually).")
89					return nil
90				}
91	
92				in := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
93				for _, s := range sugg {
94					if s.apply == nil {
95						continue
96					}
97					if !yes && !confirm(app, in, s.action) {
98						continue
99					}
100					if err := s.apply(); err != nil {
101						app.warnf("%s: %v", s.row.Task.ID, err)
102						continue
103					}
104					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  done: %s\n", s.action)
105				}
106				return nil
107			},
108		}
109		f := cmd.Flags()
110		f.BoolVar(&apply, "apply", false, "act on the suggestions instead of only reporting")
111		f.IntVar(&staleDays, "stale-days", 14, "days without a commit before a task counts as stale")
112		f.BoolVar(&yes, "yes", false, "with --apply, do not confirm each change")
113		return cmd
114	}
115	
116	func suggestFor(app *App, ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, r inventory.Row, stale time.Duration) []suggestion {
117		t := r.Task
118		var out []suggestion
119	
120		switch {
121		// A hot task with no live session is the commonest drift: the session was
122		// closed (or the machine rebooted) without parking.
123		case t.State == task.Hot && !r.Live():
124			out = append(out, suggestion{
125				row:    r,
126				reason: fmt.Sprintf("hot but no live session, idle %s", humanAge(r.Age())),
127				action: fmt.Sprintf("mark %s warm", t.ID),
128				apply: func() error {
129					t.State = task.Warm
130					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
131				},
132			})
133	
134		// A warm task nobody has touched in weeks is a candidate for cold: keeping
135		// the worktree costs disk and clutters every listing.
136		case t.State == task.Warm && r.Age() > stale:
137			reason := fmt.Sprintf("warm and untouched for %s", humanAge(r.Age()))
138			if r.Status.Dirty() {
139				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but has uncommitted work",
140					action: "commit or `dev park --wip` before going cold — not changed automatically"})
141				break
142			}
143			if !r.Status.Synced() {
144				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + fmt.Sprintf(", not pushed (%s)", r.Status.Summary()),
145					action: fmt.Sprintf("push %s so it can go cold: dev park %s --cold --push", t.Branch, t.ID)})
146				break
147			}
148			out = append(out, suggestion{
149				row:    r,
150				reason: reason + ", clean and pushed",
151				action: fmt.Sprintf("go cold: remove %s (branch and remote keep the work)", config.Contract(r.Checkout)),
152				apply: func() error {
153					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
154					if t.WorktreePath != "" {
155						if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
156							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath, RuntimeHandle: t.RuntimeHandle,
157						}); err != nil {
158							return err
159						}
160						t.WorktreePath = ""
161					}
162					t.State, t.RuntimeHandle = task.Cold, ""
163					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
164				},
165			})
166	
167		// A done task's entry has served its purpose once the branch is gone.
168		case t.State == task.Done:
169			out = append(out, suggestion{
170				row:    r,
171				reason: "merged",
172				action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s", t.ID),
173				apply:  func() error { return app.Tasks.Delete(t.ID) },
174			})
175		}
176	
177		// Drift that is independent of the lifecycle stage.
178		if r.WorktreeMissing && t.WorktreePath != "" {
179			wtPath := t.WorktreePath
180			out = append(out, suggestion{
181				row:    r,
182				reason: "records a worktree that git no longer knows about",
183				action: fmt.Sprintf("clear the stale worktree path %s", config.Contract(wtPath)),
184				apply: func() error {
185					if err := gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, t.RepoPath); err != nil {
186						return err
187					}
188					t.WorktreePath = ""
189					if t.State == task.Hot || t.State == task.Warm {
190						t.State = task.Cold
191					}
192					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
193				},
194			})
195		}
196		return out
197	}
198	
199	func confirm(app *App, in *bufio.Reader, action string) bool {
200		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s? [y/N] ", action)
201		line, err := in.ReadString('\n')
202		if err != nil {
203			return false
204		}
205		answer := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line))
206		return answer == "y" || answer == "yes"
207	}
```

```text
139	// scanRepo collects everything in one repository that looks like work in
140	// flight but is not yet recorded.
141	func scanRepo(ctx context.Context, app *App, r repo.Repo, sessions []runtime.Session,
142		known map[string]bool, target task.State, doWorktrees, doSessions, doBranches bool) []candidate {
143	
144		var out []candidate
145		seen := map[string]bool{}
146	
147		add := func(branch, worktree, reason string, state task.State) {
148			if branch == "" || seen[branch] {
149				return
150			}
151			id := task.MakeID(r.Name, branch)
152			if known[id] {
153				return
154			}
155			seen[branch] = true
156			out = append(out, candidate{
157				Reason: reason,
158				Task: &task.Task{
159					ID:           id,
160					Name:         branch,
161					Repo:         r.Name,
162					RepoPath:     r.Path,
163					Branch:       branch,
164					Base:         gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, r.Path),
165					WorktreePath: worktree,
166					State:        state,
167					Owner:        config.Hostname(),
168				},
169			})
170		}
171	
172		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path)
173		if err != nil {
174			return nil
175		}
176	
177		if doWorktrees {
178			for _, w := range worktrees {
179				if w.Main || w.Branch == "" || w.Prunable {
180					continue
181				}
182				// A harness's turn-scoped worktree is not a change stream a human
183				// tracks; adopting those would fill the inventory with noise that
184				// the harness will delete on its own.
185				if isEphemeralWorktree(w.Path, w.Branch) {
186					continue
187				}
188				state := target
189				reason := "existing worktree"
190				if sessionAt(sessions, w.Path) != nil {
191					state, reason = task.Hot, "worktree with a live session"
192				}
193				add(w.Branch, w.Path, reason, state)
194			}
195		}
196	
197		if doSessions {
198			for i := range sessions {
199				for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
200					if d != r.Path {
201						continue
202					}
203					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
204					if err != nil || st.Branch == "" {
205						continue
206					}
207					add(st.Branch, "", "live session in the main checkout", task.Hot)
208				}
209			}
210		}
211	
212		if doBranches {
213			for _, branch := range unmergedBranches(ctx, r.Path) {
214				add(branch, worktreePathFor(worktrees, branch), "branch ahead of the base", target)
215			}
216		}
217		return out
218	}
219	
220	// isEphemeralWorktree recognises the checkouts an agent harness creates and
221	// cleans up itself.
222	func isEphemeralWorktree(path, branch string) bool {
223		return strings.Contains(path, "/.claude/worktrees/") ||
224			strings.HasPrefix(branch, "worktree-")
225	}
226	
227	func sessionAt(sessions []runtime.Session, dir string) *runtime.Session {
228		for i := range sessions {
229			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
230				if d == dir {
231					return &sessions[i]
232				}
233			}
234		}
235		return nil
236	}
237	
238	func worktreePathFor(worktrees []gitx.Worktree, branch string) string {
239		for _, w := range worktrees {
240			if w.Branch == branch && !w.Main {
241				return w.Path
242			}
243		}
244		return ""
245	}
246	
247	// unmergedBranches lists local branches carrying commits the default branch
248	// does not — unfinished work that would otherwise be invisible to dev.
249	func unmergedBranches(ctx context.Context, repoPath string) []string {
250		base := gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
251		if base == "" {
252			return nil
253		}
254		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:short)", "refs/heads/")
255		if err != nil {
256			return nil
257		}
258		var branches []string
259		for _, b := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
260			b = strings.TrimSpace(b)
261			if b == "" || b == base || isEphemeralWorktree("", b) {
262				continue
263			}
264			// Contained in the base means the work has already landed.
265			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", b, base); err == nil {
266				continue
267			}
268			branches = append(branches, b)
269		}
270		return branches
271	}
```

```text
134	// jsonRow is the stable shape of `dev ls --json`. It is a contract for other
135	// tools (and for the multi-host aggregation `ssh host dev ls --json` enables),
136	// so fields are added but never renamed.
137	type jsonRow struct {
138		ID           string   `json:"id"`
139		Name         string   `json:"name"`
140		Repo         string   `json:"repo"`
141		RepoPath     string   `json:"repo_path"`
142		Branch       string   `json:"branch"`
143		Base         string   `json:"base,omitempty"`
144		WorktreePath string   `json:"worktree_path,omitempty"`
145		Checkout     string   `json:"checkout,omitempty"`
146		State        string   `json:"state"`
147		Mode         string   `json:"mode"`
148		Owner        string   `json:"owner,omitempty"`
149		Next         string   `json:"next,omitempty"`
150		Note         string   `json:"note,omitempty"`
151		Tags         []string `json:"tags,omitempty"`
152	
153		CheckoutExists bool   `json:"checkout_exists"`
154		Dirty          bool   `json:"dirty"`
155		Changed        int    `json:"changed"`
156		Staged         int    `json:"staged"`
157		Unstaged       int    `json:"unstaged"`
158		Untracked      int    `json:"untracked"`
159		Conflicted     int    `json:"conflicted"`
160		Added          int    `json:"added"`
161		Modified       int    `json:"modified"`
162		Deleted        int    `json:"deleted"`
163		Renamed        int    `json:"renamed"`
164		Ahead          int    `json:"ahead"`
165		Behind         int    `json:"behind"`
166		Upstream       string `json:"upstream,omitempty"`
167		GitSummary     string `json:"git_summary"`
168	
169		Live          bool     `json:"live"`
170		Runtime       string   `json:"runtime,omitempty"`
171		RuntimeHandle string   `json:"runtime_handle,omitempty"`
172		AgentStatus   string   `json:"agent_status,omitempty"`
173		AgentSessions []string `json:"agent_sessions,omitempty"`
174	
175		Drift      string `json:"drift,omitempty"`
176		AgeSeconds int64  `json:"age_seconds"`
177		Updated    string `json:"updated,omitempty"`
178	}
179	
180	func emitJSON(app *App, rows []inventory.Row) error {
181		out := make([]jsonRow, 0, len(rows))
182		for _, r := range rows {
183			j := jsonRow{
184				ID:             r.Task.ID,
185				Name:           r.Task.Title(),
186				Repo:           r.Task.Repo,
187				RepoPath:       config.Contract(r.Task.RepoPath),
188				Branch:         r.Task.Branch,
189				Base:           r.Task.Base,
190				WorktreePath:   config.Contract(r.Task.WorktreePath),
191				Checkout:       config.Contract(r.Checkout),
192				State:          string(r.Task.State),
193				Mode:           string(r.Task.EffectiveMode()),
194				Owner:          r.Task.Owner,
195				Next:           r.Task.Next,
196				Note:           r.Task.Note,
197				Tags:           r.Task.Tags,
198				CheckoutExists: r.CheckoutExists,
199				Dirty:          r.Status.Dirty(),
200				Changed:        r.Status.Changed,
201				Staged:         r.Status.Staged,
202				Unstaged:       r.Status.Unstaged,
203				Untracked:      r.Status.Untracked,
204				Conflicted:     r.Status.Conflicted,
205				Added:          r.Status.Added,
206				Modified:       r.Status.Modified,
207				Deleted:        r.Status.Deleted,
208				Renamed:        r.Status.Renamed,
209				Ahead:          r.Status.Ahead,
210				Behind:         r.Status.Behind,
211				Upstream:       r.Status.Upstream,
212				GitSummary:     r.Status.Summary(),
213				Live:           r.Live(),
214				Drift:          r.StateDrift(),
215				AgeSeconds:     int64(r.Age().Seconds()),
216			}
217			if !r.Task.Updated.IsZero() {
218				j.Updated = r.Task.Updated.Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05Z")
219			}
220			if r.Session != nil {
221				j.RuntimeHandle = r.Session.Handle
222				j.AgentStatus = r.Session.AgentStatus
223				j.AgentSessions = r.Session.AgentSessions
224			}
225			if r.Task.WorktreePath == "" {
226				j.WorktreePath = ""
227			}
228			out = append(out, j)
229		}
230		enc := json.NewEncoder(app.Out)
231		enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
232		return enc.Encode(out)
233	}
```

```text
25					return err
26				}
27	
28				g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
29				if err != nil {
30					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "directory  %s\n", config.Contract(cwd))
31					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "repo       — not a git repository")
32					return nil
33				}
34	
35				kind := "main checkout"
36				if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
37					kind = "linked worktree"
38				}
39				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "repo       %s (%s)\n", g.Name, kind)
40				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "checkout   %s\n", config.Contract(g.Root))
41				if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
42					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "main       %s\n", config.Contract(g.MainRoot))
43				}
44	
45				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, g.Root); err == nil {
46					branch := st.Branch
47					if st.Detached {
48						branch = "(detached HEAD)"
49					}
50					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "branch     %s  %s\n", branch, st.Summary())
51					if st.Dirty() {
52						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "changes    %s\n", st.Breakdown())
53						if types := st.TypeBreakdown(); types != "" {
54							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "types      %s\n", types)
55						}
56					}
57					if st.Upstream != "" {
58						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "upstream   %s\n", st.Upstream)
59					} else {
60						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "upstream   — not published\n")
61					}
62					if st.Conflicted > 0 {
63						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "conflicts  %d unmerged path(s) — resolve before anything else\n", st.Conflicted)
64					}
65				}
66				if base := gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, g.MainRoot); base != "" {
67					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "default    %s\n", base)
68				}
69				if k := forge.Detect(ctx, g.MainRoot); k != forge.Unknown {
70					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "forge      %s\n", k)
71				}
72	
73				if list, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, g.MainRoot); err == nil && len(list) > 1 {
74					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "worktrees  %d\n", len(list))
75					for _, w := range list {
76						marker := "  "
77						if w.Path == g.Root {
78							marker = "→ "
79						}
80						name := w.Branch
81						if name == "" {
82							name = "(detached)"
83						}
84						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s%-28s %s\n", marker, name, config.Contract(w.Path))
85					}
86				}
87	
88				t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(g.Root)
89				if err != nil {
90					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "task       — not tracked; `dev start` to record it")
91					return nil
92				}
93				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "task       %s %s (%s)\n", t.State.Icon(), t.Title(), t.ID)
94				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "owner      %s\n", dash(t.Owner))
95				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "next       %s\n", dash(t.Next))
96				if t.Note != "" {

98				}
99				if t.AgentSession != "" {
100					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "agent      %s\n", t.AgentSession)
101				}
102				if host := config.Hostname(); !t.OwnedBy(host) {
103					app.warnf("this task is owned by %s — pushing from here can diverge the branch", t.Owner)
104				}
105				return nil
106			},
107		}
108	}
```

```text
34	Shows exactly what "dev ls" shows, from the same code path, plus the ability
35	to open, park and annotate a task without retyping its name.

37	Three lists, switched with tab:

43	Navigation is vim-style, with arrows alongside:
44

47	  /          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit

49	Actions depend on the list:

314				}
315				defer store.Close()
316				until := time.Now()
317				since := until.AddDate(-1, 0, 0)
318				totals, err := store.DayTotals(stats.Query{

352			if dir := m.Chosen(); dir != "" {
353				app.cdDirective(dir)
354			}
355		}
356		return nil
357	}

359	// collectRepos builds the repository view: what exists, plus how much of it is
360	// in flight.
361	func collectRepos(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime) ([]tui.RepoRow, error) {
362		repos, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
363		if err != nil {
364			return nil, err
365		}
366		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
367		if err != nil {
368			return nil, err
369		}
370		byRepo := map[string][]*task.Task{}
371		for _, t := range tasks {
372			byRepo[t.RepoPath] = append(byRepo[t.RepoPath], t)
373		}
374		sessions, _ := rt.List(ctx)
375	
376		out := make([]tui.RepoRow, 0, len(repos))
377		for _, r := range repos {
378			row := tui.RepoRow{Repo: r, Tasks: byRepo[r.Path]}
379			if !r.Bare {
380				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path); err == nil {
381					row.Status = st
382				}
383				if list, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path); err == nil && len(list) > 0 {
384					row.Worktrees = len(list) - 1
385				}
386				row.RemoteForge, row.RemoteName = forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.Remote(ctx, r.Path, "origin"))
387			}
388			for _, s := range sessions {
389				if s.Covers(r.Path) || (r.RealPath != "" && s.Covers(r.RealPath)) {
390					row.Live = true
391					row.Runtime, row.RuntimeHandle, row.RuntimeStatus = rt.Name(), s.Handle, s.AgentStatus
392					break
393				}
394			}
395			out = append(out, row)
396		}
397		return out, nil
398	}
399	
400	// externalTools resolves the configured tool bindings.
401	//
402	// Configurable rather than fixed because which program you reach for is
403	// personal, and because the useful ones are often your own scripts and
404	// aliases, not just the well-known tools.
405	func externalTools(app *App) []tui.Tool {
406		var out []tui.Tool
407		for _, t := range app.Cfg.EffectiveTools() {
408			run := t.Run
409			name := t.Name
410			if name == "" {
411				name = firstWord(run)
412			}
413			command := []string{shellPath(), "-c", run}
414			if t.Interactive {
415				// The command string passed to shell -lic is parsed before some
416				// shells finish loading aliases. Parse only eval "$1" up front,
417				// then evaluate the configured command after rc loading, so both
418				// aliases (vibe) and functions (claude-plans-here) work.
419				command = []string{shellPath(), "-lic", `eval "$1"`, "dev-tui-tool", run}
420			}
421			out = append(out, tui.Tool{
422				Key: t.Key, Name: name, Command: command,
423				Available: commandRunnable(run, t.Interactive),
424			})
425		}
426		return out
427	}
428	
429	// commandRunnable resolves the command's first word on PATH, expanding a
430	// leading environment variable so "$EDITOR ." checks the editor itself.
431	func commandRunnable(run string, interactive bool) func() bool {
432		// Availability is stable for the lifetime of one dashboard. In particular,
433		// probing an interactive alias starts a login shell; doing that on every
434		// render would turn a 60fps UI into a shell-launch benchmark.
435		var once sync.Once
436		available := false
437		return func() bool {
438			once.Do(func() { available = checkCommandRunnable(run, interactive) })
439			return available
440		}
441	}
442	
443	func checkCommandRunnable(run string, interactive bool) bool {
444		word := firstWord(run)
445		if strings.HasPrefix(word, "$") {
446			word = os.Getenv(strings.TrimPrefix(word, "$"))
447			if word == "" {
448				return false
449			}
450			word = firstWord(word)
451		}
452		if word == "" {
453			return false
454		}
455		if interactive {
456			// Ask the configured shell after it loads its rc files; LookPath
457			// cannot see aliases or functions.
458			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
459			defer cancel()
460			probe := exec.CommandContext(ctx, shellPath(), "-lic",
461				`command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1`, "dev-tool-probe", word)
462			return probe.Run() == nil
463		}
464		if filepath.IsAbs(word) {
465			_, err := os.Stat(word)
466			return err == nil
467		}
468		_, err := exec.LookPath(word)
469		return err == nil
470	}
471	
472	func firstWord(s string) string {
473		f := strings.Fields(s)
474		if len(f) == 0 {
475			return ""
476		}
477		return f[0]
478	}
479	
480	func shellPath() string {
481		if s := os.Getenv("SHELL"); s != "" {
482			return s
483		}
484		return "/bin/sh"
485	}
486	
487	// remoteCachePath is private because the inventory can contain names and URLs
488	// of private repositories.
489	func remoteCachePath() string {
490		return filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "remotes.json")
491	}
492	
493	// cachedRemotesForRepoRows uses the local repo data the dashboard already
494	// collected, avoiding another process-spawning scan on startup.
495	func cachedRemotesForRepoRows(app *App, locals []tui.RepoRow) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool) {
496		cache, ok := forge.LoadCache(remoteCachePath(), app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration)
497		if !ok {
498			return nil, false
499		}
500		byRemote := map[string]tui.RepoRow{}
501		for _, r := range locals {
502			if r.RemoteForge != forge.Unknown && r.RemoteName != "" {
503				byRemote[string(r.RemoteForge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(r.RemoteName)] = r
504			}
505		}
506		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(cache.Repos))
507		for _, rr := range cache.Repos {
508			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
509			if local, ok := byRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
510				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.Repo.Path, local.Repo.Display()
511			}
512			out = append(out, row)
513		}
514		return out, true
515	}
516	
517	// cachedRemotes returns a fresh, already-local-matched cache for instant TUI
518	// navigation. Local paths are recomputed rather than cached because clones can
519	// move independently of the forge inventory.
520	func cachedRemotes(ctx context.Context, app *App) ([]tui.RemoteRow, bool) {
521		cache, ok := forge.LoadCache(remoteCachePath(), app.Cfg.Forge.CacheTTL.Duration)
522		if !ok {
523			return nil, false
524		}
525		return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, cache.Repos), true
526	}
527	
528	// collectRemotes aggregates gh and glab, caches the normalised response, then
529	// marks remotes that already have a checkout under the configured scan roots.
530	// Calls run concurrently so one slow forge does not serialise the other.
531	func collectRemotes(ctx context.Context, app *App, limit int) ([]tui.RemoteRow, error) {
532		if limit <= 0 {
533			limit = app.Cfg.Forge.RemoteLimit
534		}
535		type result struct {
536			repos []forge.RemoteRepo
537			err   error
538		}
539		ch := make(chan result, len(forge.All()))
540		var wg sync.WaitGroup
541		available := 0
542		for _, f := range forge.All() {
543			if !f.Available() {
544				continue
545			}
546			available++
547			wg.Add(1)
548			go func(f forge.Forge) {
549				defer wg.Done()
550				r, err := f.ListRepos(ctx, limit)
551				ch <- result{repos: r, err: err}
552			}(f)
553		}
554		wg.Wait()
555		close(ch)
556		if available == 0 {
557			return nil, fmt.Errorf("neither gh nor glab is installed")
558		}
559	
560		var (
561			remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo
562			errs        []error
563		)
564		for res := range ch {
565			if res.err != nil {
566				errs = append(errs, res.err)
567			}
568			remoteRepos = append(remoteRepos, res.repos...)
569		}
570		// Cache partial results too. They are exactly what was observed, and a
571		// partial list is more useful on the next switch than another six-second
572		// wait merely to rediscover the same provider failure.
573		if len(remoteRepos) > 0 && limit >= app.Cfg.Forge.RemoteLimit {
574			_ = forge.SaveCache(remoteCachePath(), remoteRepos)
575		}
576		return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, remoteRepos), errors.Join(errs...)
577	}
578	
579	func matchRemoteLocals(ctx context.Context, app *App, remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo) []tui.RemoteRow {
580		locals, _ := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
581		localByRemote := map[string]repo.Repo{}
582		for _, r := range locals {
583			if r.Bare {
584				continue
585			}
586			kind, name := forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.Remote(ctx, r.Path, "origin"))
587			if kind != forge.Unknown && name != "" {
588				localByRemote[string(kind)+"/"+strings.ToLower(name)] = r
589			}
590		}
591		out := make([]tui.RemoteRow, 0, len(remoteRepos))
592		for _, rr := range remoteRepos {
593			row := tui.RemoteRow{Repo: rr}
594			if local, ok := localByRemote[string(rr.Forge)+"/"+strings.ToLower(rr.FullName)]; ok {
595				row.LocalPath, row.LocalName = local.Path, local.Display()
596			}
597			out = append(out, row)
598		}
599		return out
600	}
```

```text
1	// Package inventory joins the three sources that describe work in progress:
2	// the task registry (human intent), git (durable code state) and the runtime
3	// (what is live right now). It is the single code path behind `dev ls`,
4	// `dev status`, `dev sweep` and the TUI, so all four can never disagree.
5	package inventory
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"os"
10		"sort"

20	// Row is one task enriched with everything derived live.
21	type Row struct {
22		Task *task.Task
23	
24		// Checkout is where the task's code currently lives: its worktree if it
25		// has one, else the repo. Empty when nothing exists on disk.
26		Checkout string
27		// CheckoutExists reports whether that directory is actually present. A
28		// cold task, or one whose worktree was removed behind dev's back, is not.
29		CheckoutExists bool
30		// WorktreeMissing flags a task that records a worktree path which is no
31		// longer a registered git worktree — the drift `dev sweep` reports.
32		WorktreeMissing bool
33	
34		// Status is the live git status of Checkout. Zero when there is nothing
35		// on disk to inspect.
36		Status    gitx.Status
37		StatusErr error
38	
39		// LastCommit is the author time of HEAD, used to age a task.
40		LastCommit time.Time
41	
42		// Session is the live runtime session hosting this checkout, if any.
43		Session *runtime.Session
44		// sessionsTracked reports whether the runtime can observe sessions at all.
45		// With the "none" backend it cannot, so "hot but nothing live" is not
46		// drift — it is the only state that backend can ever produce.
47		sessionsTracked bool
48	}
49	
50	// Live reports whether a runtime session is currently hosting this task.
51	func (r Row) Live() bool { return r.Session != nil }
52	
53	// StateDrift reports a task whose recorded state disagrees with reality:
54	// hot with no live session, or warm/cold with one. It is what `dev sweep`
55	// turns into suggestions — dev reports drift and never silently rewrites it.
56	func (r Row) StateDrift() string {
57		if r.sessionsTracked {
58			switch r.Task.State {
59			case task.Hot:
60				if !r.Live() {
61					return "no live session"
62				}
63			case task.Warm, task.Cold:
64				if r.Live() {
65					return "session is live"
66				}
67			}
68		}
69		if r.Task.State == task.Cold && r.CheckoutExists && r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
70			return "worktree still on disk"
71		}
72		if r.WorktreeMissing {
73			return "worktree is gone"
74		}
75		return ""
76	}
77	
78	// Age is how long since the task's last commit, falling back to when the entry
79	// was last written for a task with no commits of its own.
80	func (r Row) Age() time.Duration {
81		ref := r.LastCommit
82		if ref.IsZero() || r.Task.Updated.After(ref) {
83			ref = r.Task.Updated
84		}
85		if ref.IsZero() {
86			return 0
87		}
88		return time.Since(ref)
89	}
90	
91	// Options tunes what a Collect call spends time on.
92	type Options struct {
93		// SkipRuntime avoids querying the multiplexer, for callers that only need
94		// git facts (and for tests).
95		SkipRuntime bool
96		// SkipGit avoids running git per task, for a fast listing.
97		SkipGit bool
98	}
99	
100	// Collect builds the enriched inventory. Git probes run concurrently: each is
101	// a handful of process spawns, and a machine with dozens of tasks would
102	// otherwise make `dev ls` feel slow.
103	func Collect(ctx context.Context, tasks []*task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opts Options) []Row {
104		rows := make([]Row, len(tasks))
105	
106		var sessions []runtime.Session
107		tracked := false
108		if !opts.SkipRuntime && rt != nil && rt.Name() != "none" {
109			if s, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
110				sessions, tracked = s, true
111			}
112		}
113	
114		var wg sync.WaitGroup
115		// Bound concurrency: git is process-heavy and an unbounded fan-out over a
116		// large inventory would thrash.
117		sem := make(chan struct{}, 8)
118	
119		for i, t := range tasks {
120			rows[i].Task = t
121			rows[i].Checkout = checkoutOf(t)
122	
123			if opts.SkipGit || rows[i].Checkout == "" {
124				continue
125			}
126			wg.Add(1)
127			go func(i int) {
128				defer wg.Done()
129				sem <- struct{}{}
130				defer func() { <-sem }()
131				enrich(ctx, &rows[i])
132			}(i)
133		}
134		wg.Wait()
135	
136		for i := range rows {
137			rows[i].Session = matchSession(sessions, rows[i])
138			rows[i].sessionsTracked = tracked
139		}
140		return rows
141	}
142	
143	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
144		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
145			return t.WorktreePath
146		}
147		return t.RepoPath
148	}
149	
150	func enrich(ctx context.Context, r *Row) {
151		info, err := os.Stat(r.Checkout)
152		r.CheckoutExists = err == nil && info.IsDir()
153		if !r.CheckoutExists {
154			if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
155				r.WorktreeMissing = true
156			}
157			return
158		}
159		if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Checkout); err != nil {
160			r.StatusErr = err
161		} else {
162			r.Status = st
163		}
164		if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Checkout); err == nil && unix > 0 {
165			r.LastCommit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
166		}
167		// A recorded worktree that git no longer knows about is drift worth
168		// surfacing: the directory may exist while the administrative entry is gone.
169		if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
170			if _, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Task.RepoPath, r.Task.Branch); err == nil && !ok {
171				r.WorktreeMissing = true
172			}
173		}
174	}
175	
176	// matchSession picks the runtime session hosting a row's checkout. An exact
177	// directory match is preferred over a containing one, so a worktree's own
178	// session always wins over the parent repo's.
179	func matchSession(sessions []runtime.Session, r Row) *runtime.Session {
180		if r.Checkout == "" {
181			return nil
182		}
183		var contains *runtime.Session
184		for i := range sessions {
185			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
186				if d == r.Checkout {
187					return &sessions[i]
188				}
189				if strings.HasPrefix(d, r.Checkout+"/") && contains == nil {
190					contains = &sessions[i]
191				}
192			}
193		}
194		return contains
195	}
196	
197	// Filter narrows rows by state and repo. An empty filter matches everything.
198	type Filter struct {
199		States []task.State
200		Repo   string
201		// LiveOnly keeps only tasks with a runtime session.
202		LiveOnly bool
203		// DirtyOnly keeps only tasks with uncommitted work.
204		DirtyOnly bool
205	}
206	
207	// Apply returns the rows matching f.
208	func (f Filter) Apply(rows []Row) []Row {
209		out := rows[:0:0]
210		for _, r := range rows {
211			if len(f.States) > 0 && !containsState(f.States, r.Task.State) {
212				continue
213			}
214			if f.Repo != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Task.Repo), strings.ToLower(f.Repo)) {
215				continue
216			}
217			if f.LiveOnly && !r.Live() {
218				continue
219			}
220			if f.DirtyOnly && !r.Status.Dirty() {
221				continue
222			}
223			out = append(out, r)
224		}
225		return out
226	}
227	
228	func containsState(list []task.State, s task.State) bool {
229		for _, v := range list {
230			if v == s {
231				return true
232			}
233		}
234		return false
235	}

237	// Orphans reports live runtime sessions that no task claims — the "I opened
238	// this and never wrote it down" case that makes a sidebar grow without bound.
239	func Orphans(sessions []runtime.Session, rows []Row) []runtime.Session {
240		claimed := map[string]bool{}
241		for _, r := range rows {
242			if r.Session != nil {
243				claimed[r.Session.Handle] = true
244			}
245		}
246		var out []runtime.Session
247		for _, s := range sessions {
248			if !claimed[s.Handle] {
249				out = append(out, s)
250			}
251		}
252		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Label < out[j].Label })
253		return out
254	}
```

```text
11	// Table renders aligned columns. It measures width in runes rather than bytes
12	// so the CJK repo and branch names in a real inventory line up.
13	type Table struct {
14		head []string
15		rows [][]string
16	}
17	
18	// NewTable starts a table with the given header.
19	func NewTable(header ...string) *Table { return &Table{head: header} }
20	
21	// Add appends a row. Short rows are padded, long ones are truncated to the
22	// header width so a stray field can never shift the whole table.
23	func (t *Table) Add(cells ...string) {
24		row := make([]string, len(t.head))
25		copy(row, cells)
26		t.rows = append(t.rows, row)
27	}
28	
29	// Len reports the number of data rows.
30	func (t *Table) Len() int { return len(t.rows) }
31	
32	// Render writes the table, sizing every column to its widest cell.
33	func (t *Table) Render(w io.Writer) {
34		if len(t.rows) == 0 {
35			return
36		}
37		widths := make([]int, len(t.head))
38		for i, h := range t.head {
39			widths[i] = width(h)
40		}
41		for _, r := range t.rows {
42			for i, c := range r {
43				if n := width(c); n > widths[i] {
44					widths[i] = n
45				}
46			}
47		}
48		writeRow(w, t.head, widths)
49		for _, r := range t.rows {
50			writeRow(w, r, widths)
51		}
52	}
53	
54	func writeRow(w io.Writer, cells []string, widths []int) {
55		var b strings.Builder
56		for i, c := range cells {
57			if i == len(cells)-1 {
58				b.WriteString(c) // never pad the last column
59				break
60			}
61			b.WriteString(c)
62			b.WriteString(strings.Repeat(" ", widths[i]-width(c)+2))
63		}
64		fmt.Fprintln(w, strings.TrimRight(b.String(), " "))
65	}
66	
67	// width counts display columns, treating wide CJK runes as two.
68	func width(s string) int {
69		n := 0
70		for _, r := range s {
71			if isWide(r) {
72				n += 2
73			} else {
74				n++
75			}
76		}
77		return n
78	}
79	
80	func isWide(r rune) bool {
81		switch {
82		case r >= 0x1100 && r <= 0x115F, // Hangul Jamo
83			r >= 0x2E80 && r <= 0xA4CF, // CJK radicals through Yi
84			r >= 0xAC00 && r <= 0xD7A3, // Hangul syllables
85			r >= 0xF900 && r <= 0xFAFF, // CJK compatibility ideographs
86			r >= 0xFE30 && r <= 0xFE6F, // CJK compatibility forms
87			r >= 0xFF00 && r <= 0xFF60, // fullwidth forms
88			r >= 0xFFE0 && r <= 0xFFE6,
89			r >= 0x20000 && r <= 0x3FFFD: // CJK extension planes
90			return true
91		}
92		return false
93	}
94	
95	// truncate shortens s to at most n display columns, marking the cut with "…".
96	func truncate(s string, n int) string {
97		if n <= 0 || width(s) <= n {
98			return s
99		}
100		var b strings.Builder
101		used := 0
102		for _, r := range s {
103			rw := 1
104			if isWide(r) {
105				rw = 2
106			}
107			if used+rw > n-1 {
108				break
109			}
110			b.WriteRune(r)
111			used += rw
112		}
113		return b.String() + "…"
114	}
115	
116	// dash renders an empty value as a visible placeholder, so a blank column is
117	// never mistaken for a rendering bug.
118	func dash(s string) string {
119		if strings.TrimSpace(s) == "" {
120			return "—"
121		}
122		return s
123	}
124	
125	// humanAge renders a duration the way a changelog would: "3d", "2w", "5mo".
126	func humanAge(d time.Duration) string {
127		switch {
128		case d <= 0:
129			return "—"
130		case d < time.Hour:
131			return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", int(d.Minutes()))
132		case d < 24*time.Hour:
133			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
134		case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
135			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
136		case d < 60*24*time.Hour:
137			return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
138		default:
139			return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
140		}
141	}
142	
143	// shellQuote makes a path safe to paste into a POSIX shell command.
144	func shellQuote(s string) string {
145		if s == "" {
146			return "''"
147		}
148		safe := true
149		for _, r := range s {
150			if !(r == '/' || r == '.' || r == '-' || r == '_' || r == '~' ||
151				(r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') || (r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z') || (r >= '0' && r <= '9')) {
152				safe = false
153				break
154			}
155		}
156		if safe && utf8.ValidString(s) {
157			return s
158		}
159		return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'"
160	}
```

```text
module TryCompat
  def self.mkdir_p(path)
    path = File.expand_path(path.to_s)
    return path if Dir.exist?(path)
    stack = []
    dir = path
    while dir && dir != "/" && dir != "." && !Dir.exist?(dir)
      stack.unshift(dir)
      parent = File.dirname(dir)
      break if parent == dir
      dir = parent
    end
    stack.each do |d|
      begin
        Dir.mkdir(d.to_s)
      rescue Errno::EEXIST
      end
    end
    path
  end

  def self.stty_save
    `stty -g 2>/dev/null`.to_s.chomp
  rescue
    ""
  end

  def self.stty_set(state)
    return if state.nil? || state.empty?
    system("stty #{state} 2>/dev/null")
  end

  def self.with_raw_tty
    saved = nil
    if STDIN.tty?
      saved = stty_save
      system("stty raw -echo 2>/dev/null")
    end
    yield
  ensure
    stty_set(saved) if saved && !saved.empty?
  end

  def self.with_cooked_tty
    saved = nil
    if STDIN.tty?
      saved = stty_save
      system("stty cooked echo 2>/dev/null")
    end
    yield
  ensure
    stty_set(saved) if saved && !saved.empty?
  end

  def self.stdin_iflush
    begin
      loop { STDIN.read_nonblock(4096) }
    rescue IO::WaitReadable, EOFError, Errno::EAGAIN, Errno::EWOULDBLOCK, Errno::EINVAL
    end
  end

  def self.win_platform?
    !!(RUBY_PLATFORM.to_s =~ /mswin|mingw|cygwin/i)
  end

    name = File.basename($0.to_s)
    !name.end_with?(".rb")
```

```markdown
# `dev try` TUI 與 repository lifecycle 規劃

## Context

`dev try` 已能列出低負擔的試作目錄，但目前缺少適合「重新撿起舊實驗、判斷價值、整理磁碟空間」的互動式工作流。目標是在不犧牲既有 CLI 可腳本化能力的前提下，讓使用者能於 TUI 中快速建立或開啟臨時實驗、辨識值得保留的項目、將成熟項目 graduate，並對已備份且可恢復的項目安全地 archive／移除本機副本。

規劃必須同時涵蓋：

- `try` 與主 TUI 的整合邊界，避免平行實作或將 domain 邏輯耦合到 view。
- 可組合的分類標記（例如 important、experiment）與互斥 lifecycle 狀態。

- CLI、TUI、測試與文件的一致行為。
```

```text
 	// RelativeLinks makes an index portable when it and the repositories move
 	// together; absolute links are less surprising across mount points.
 	RelativeLinks bool `toml:"relative_links"`
 }
 
 // TUI configures the interactive dashboard.
 type TUI struct {
 	// Tools are the external programs the dashboard can hand the terminal to,
 	// each on its own key. When empty, DefaultTools applies.
 	//
 	// Configurable rather than fixed because which program you reach for is
 	// personal — nvim or helix, lazygit or gitui, and whatever aliases and
 	// scripts you have built up around your own workflow.
 	Tools []Tool `toml:"tools"`
 }
 
 // Tool is one external program bound to a key in the dashboard.
 type Tool struct {
 	// Key launches it. A single character, and not one of the dashboard's own
 	// bindings — dev reports a clash rather than silently shadowing.
 	Key string `toml:"key"`
 	// Name is shown in the footer.
 	Name string `toml:"name"`
 	// Run is a shell command, executed in the selected row's checkout.
 	Run string `toml:"run"`
 	// Interactive runs through $SHELL -lic, loading the user's rc file so a
 	// shell alias or function can be used. Off by default: startup files can
 	// print output and alter environment in ways an ordinary command should
 	// not inherit accidentally.
 	Interactive bool `toml:"interactive"`
 }
 
 // reservedKeys are the dashboard's own bindings. A tool cannot take one,
 // because losing the ability to quit or move is not a trade anyone wants.
 var reservedKeys = map[string]string{
 	"q": "quit", "j": "down", "k": "up", "g": "top", "G": "bottom",
 	"h": "previous view", "l": "next view", "tab": "next view",
 	"/": "filter", "r": "refresh", "o": "open", "p": "park",
 	"c": "edit next action", "s": "start a task", "a": "include done",
 	"0": "clear filters", "1": "hot", "2": "warm", "3": "cold",
-	"?": "help",
+	"?": "help", "H": "repo activity heatmap", "e": "edit config",
 }
 
 // ReservedKey reports the dashboard binding a key would collide with.
 func ReservedKey(key string) (string, bool) {
 	name, ok := reservedKeys[key]
 	return name, ok
 }
 
 // DefaultTools are the programs bound when nothing is configured. They are
 // written out in full by `dev config init` rather than left implicit, so what
 // is bound is visible rather than something to discover by pressing keys.
 func DefaultTools() []Tool {
 	return []Tool{
 		{Key: "L", Name: "lazygit", Run: "lazygit"},
 		{Key: "Y", Name: "yazi", Run: "yazi"},
 		{Key: "E", Name: "editor", Run: "$EDITOR ."},
 		{Key: "S", Name: "shell", Run: "$SHELL"},
 	}
 }
 
 // EffectiveTools returns the configured tools, or the defaults when none are
 // configured. A configured list replaces the defaults entirely — a partial
 // merge would make it unclear which bindings are in effect.
 func (c Config) EffectiveTools() []Tool {
 	if len(c.TUI.Tools) == 0 {
 		return DefaultTools()
 	}
 	return c.TUI.Tools
 }
 
 // Stats configures activity collection for the heatmap.
 type Stats struct {
 	// Sampler enables recording live agent/runtime activity into stats.db.
 	Sampler bool `toml:"sampler"`
 	// WakaTime enables the WakaTime importer as an additional source.
 	WakaTime bool `toml:"wakatime"`
 	// WakaTimeConfig points at the ini file holding the API key.
 	WakaTimeConfig string `toml:"wakatime_config"`
 }

 func newTask(repo, branch string, st task.State) *task.Task {
 	return &task.Task{
 		Repo:     repo,
 		RepoPath: "/src/" + repo,
 		Branch:   branch,
 		Base:     "main",
 		State:    st,
 		Owner:    "test-host",
 	}
 }
 
 func TestMakeID(t *testing.T) {
 	for _, tc := range []struct{ repo, branch, want string }{
 		{"atp-sipui", "fix/gx-security-recovery", "atp-sipui__fix-gx-security-recovery"},
 		{"My Repo", "feat/a/b", "My-Repo__feat-a-b"},
 		{"", "", "repo__branch"},
 	} {
 		if got := task.MakeID(tc.repo, tc.branch); got != tc.want {
 			t.Errorf("MakeID(%q,%q) = %q, want %q", tc.repo, tc.branch, got, tc.want)
 		}
 	}
 }
 
 func TestSaveGetRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
 	s := task.NewStore(t.TempDir())
 	in := newTask("atp-sipui", "fix/gx-security-recovery", task.Warm)
 	in.Next = "finish refresh regression test"
 	in.Tags = []string{"work", "urgent"}
 	in.AgentSession = "claude:2136a917"
+	in.Mode = task.ModeDirect
 
 	if err := s.Save(in); err != nil {
 		t.Fatalf("Save: %v", err)
 	}
 	if in.ID != "atp-sipui__fix-gx-security-recovery" {
 		t.Errorf("Save should derive the ID, got %q", in.ID)
 	}
 	if in.Created.IsZero() || in.Updated.IsZero() {
 		t.Error("Save should stamp Created and Updated")
 	}
 
 	out, err := s.Get(in.ID)
 	if err != nil {
 		t.Fatalf("Get: %v", err)
 	}
 	if out.Next != in.Next || out.Branch != in.Branch || out.State != task.Warm {
 		t.Errorf("round trip mismatch: %+v", out)
 	}
 	if len(out.Tags) != 2 || out.AgentSession != "claude:2136a917" {
 		t.Errorf("tags/session lost: %+v", out)
 	}
+	if out.Mode != task.ModeDirect {
+		t.Errorf("mode lost: saved %q, loaded %q", in.Mode, out.Mode)

 func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
```

```text
+	Added          int    `json:"added"`

+	Deleted        int    `json:"deleted"`

 	AgentStatus   string   `json:"agent_status,omitempty"`
 	AgentSessions []string `json:"agent_sessions,omitempty"`
 
 	Drift      string `json:"drift,omitempty"`
 	AgeSeconds int64  `json:"age_seconds"`
 	Updated    string `json:"updated,omitempty"`
 }
 
 func emitJSON(app *App, rows []inventory.Row) error {
 	out := make([]jsonRow, 0, len(rows))
 	for _, r := range rows {
 		j := jsonRow{
 			ID:             r.Task.ID,
 			Name:           r.Task.Title(),
 			Repo:           r.Task.Repo,
 			RepoPath:       config.Contract(r.Task.RepoPath),
 			Branch:         r.Task.Branch,
 			Base:           r.Task.Base,
 			WorktreePath:   config.Contract(r.Task.WorktreePath),
 			Checkout:       config.Contract(r.Checkout),
 			State:          string(r.Task.State),
+			Mode:           string(r.Task.EffectiveMode()),
 			Owner:          r.Task.Owner,
 			Next:           r.Task.Next,
 			Note:           r.Task.Note,
 			Tags:           r.Task.Tags,
 			CheckoutExists: r.CheckoutExists,
 			Dirty:          r.Status.Dirty(),
+			Changed:        r.Status.Changed,
+			Staged:         r.Status.Staged,
+			Unstaged:       r.Status.Unstaged,
+			Untracked:      r.Status.Untracked,
+			Conflicted:     r.Status.Conflicted,
+			Added:          r.Status.Added,
+			Modified:       r.Status.Modified,
+			Deleted:        r.Status.Deleted,
+			Renamed:        r.Status.Renamed,
 			Ahead:          r.Status.Ahead,
 			Behind:         r.Status.Behind,
 			Upstream:       r.Status.Upstream,
 			GitSummary:     r.Status.Summary(),
 			Live:           r.Live(),
 			Drift:          r.StateDrift(),
 			AgeSeconds:     int64(r.Age().Seconds()),
 		}
 		if !r.Task.Updated.IsZero() {
 			j.Updated = r.Task.Updated.Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05Z")
 		}
 		if r.Session != nil {
 			j.RuntimeHandle = r.Session.Handle
 			j.AgentStatus = r.Session.AgentStatus
 			j.AgentSessions = r.Session.AgentSessions
 		}
 		if r.Task.WorktreePath == "" {
 			j.WorktreePath = ""
 		}
 		out = append(out, j)
 	}
 	enc := json.NewEncoder(app.Out)
 	enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
 	return enc.Encode(out)
 }
```

```text
 func parseBranchHeader(rec string, s *Status) {
 	f := strings.Fields(rec)

 	}
```

```text
+func configEditorProcess(app *App, editor string) (*exec.Cmd, string, bool, error) {
```

```text
1	// Package inventory joins the three sources that describe work in progress:
2	// the task registry (human intent), git (durable code state) and the runtime
3	// (what is live right now). It is the single code path behind `dev ls`,
4	// `dev status`, `dev sweep` and the TUI, so all four can never disagree.
5	package inventory
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"os"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"sync"
13		"time"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
18	)
19	
20	// Row is one task enriched with everything derived live.
21	type Row struct {
22		Task *task.Task
23	
24		// Checkout is where the task's code currently lives: its worktree if it
25		// has one, else the repo. Empty when nothing exists on disk.
26		Checkout string
27		// CheckoutExists reports whether that directory is actually present. A
28		// cold task, or one whose worktree was removed behind dev's back, is not.
29		CheckoutExists bool
30		// WorktreeMissing flags a task that records a worktree path which is no
31		// longer a registered git worktree — the drift `dev sweep` reports.
32		WorktreeMissing bool
33	
34		// Status is the live git status of Checkout. Zero when there is nothing
35		// on disk to inspect.
36		Status    gitx.Status
37		StatusErr error
38	
39		// LastCommit is the author time of HEAD, used to age a task.
40		LastCommit time.Time
41	
42		// Session is the live runtime session hosting this checkout, if any.
43		Session *runtime.Session
44		// sessionsTracked reports whether the runtime can observe sessions at all.
45		// With the "none" backend it cannot, so "hot but nothing live" is not
46		// drift — it is the only state that backend can ever produce.
47		sessionsTracked bool
48	}
49	
50	// Live reports whether a runtime session is currently hosting this task.
51	func (r Row) Live() bool { return r.Session != nil }
52	
53	// StateDrift reports a task whose recorded state disagrees with reality:
54	// hot with no live session, or warm/cold with one. It is what `dev sweep`
55	// turns into suggestions — dev reports drift and never silently rewrites it.
56	func (r Row) StateDrift() string {
57		if r.sessionsTracked {
58			switch r.Task.State {
59			case task.Hot:
60				if !r.Live() {
61					return "no live session"
62				}
63			case task.Warm, task.Cold:
64				if r.Live() {
65					return "session is live"
66				}
67			}
68		}
69		if r.Task.State == task.Cold && r.CheckoutExists && r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
70			return "worktree still on disk"
71		}
72		if r.WorktreeMissing {
73			return "worktree is gone"
74		}
75		return ""
76	}
77	
78	// Age is how long since the task's last commit, falling back to when the entry
79	// was last written for a task with no commits of its own.
80	func (r Row) Age() time.Duration {
81		ref := r.LastCommit
82		if ref.IsZero() || r.Task.Updated.After(ref) {
83			ref = r.Task.Updated
84		}
85		if ref.IsZero() {
86			return 0
87		}
88		return time.Since(ref)
89	}
90	
91	// Options tunes what a Collect call spends time on.
92	type Options struct {
93		// SkipRuntime avoids querying the multiplexer, for callers that only need
94		// git facts (and for tests).
95		SkipRuntime bool
96		// SkipGit avoids running git per task, for a fast listing.
97		SkipGit bool
98	}
99	
100	// Collect builds the enriched inventory. Git probes run concurrently: each is
101	// a handful of process spawns, and a machine with dozens of tasks would
102	// otherwise make `dev ls` feel slow.
103	func Collect(ctx context.Context, tasks []*task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opts Options) []Row {
104		rows := make([]Row, len(tasks))
105	
106		var sessions []runtime.Session
107		tracked := false
108		if !opts.SkipRuntime && rt != nil && rt.Name() != "none" {
109			if s, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
110				sessions, tracked = s, true
111			}
112		}
113	
114		var wg sync.WaitGroup
115		// Bound concurrency: git is process-heavy and an unbounded fan-out over a
116		// large inventory would thrash.
117		sem := make(chan struct{}, 8)
118	
119		for i, t := range tasks {
120			rows[i].Task = t
121			rows[i].Checkout = checkoutOf(t)
122	
123			if opts.SkipGit || rows[i].Checkout == "" {
124				continue
125			}
126			wg.Add(1)
127			go func(i int) {
128				defer wg.Done()
129				sem <- struct{}{}
130				defer func() { <-sem }()
131				enrich(ctx, &rows[i])
132			}(i)
133		}
134		wg.Wait()
135	
136		for i := range rows {
137			rows[i].Session = matchSession(sessions, rows[i])
138			rows[i].sessionsTracked = tracked
139		}
140		return rows
141	}
142	
143	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
144		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
145			return t.WorktreePath
146		}
147		return t.RepoPath
148	}
149	
150	func enrich(ctx context.Context, r *Row) {
151		info, err := os.Stat(r.Checkout)
152		r.CheckoutExists = err == nil && info.IsDir()
153		if !r.CheckoutExists {
154			if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
155				r.WorktreeMissing = true
156			}
157			return
158		}
159		if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Checkout); err != nil {
160			r.StatusErr = err
161		} else {
162			r.Status = st
163		}
164		if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Checkout); err == nil && unix > 0 {
165			r.LastCommit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
166		}
167		// A recorded worktree that git no longer knows about is drift worth
168		// surfacing: the directory may exist while the administrative entry is gone.
169		if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
170			if _, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Task.RepoPath, r.Task.Branch); err == nil && !ok {
171				r.WorktreeMissing = true
172			}
173		}
174	}
175	
176	// matchSession picks the runtime session hosting a row's checkout. An exact
177	// directory match is preferred over a containing one, so a worktree's own
178	// session always wins over the parent repo's.
179	func matchSession(sessions []runtime.Session, r Row) *runtime.Session {
180		if r.Checkout == "" {
181			return nil
182		}
183		var contains *runtime.Session
184		for i := range sessions {
185			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
186				if d == r.Checkout {
187					return &sessions[i]
188				}
189				if strings.HasPrefix(d, r.Checkout+"/") && contains == nil {
190					contains = &sessions[i]
191				}
192			}
193		}
194		return contains
195	}
196	
197	// Filter narrows rows by state and repo. An empty filter matches everything.
198	type Filter struct {
199		States []task.State
200		Repo   string
201		// LiveOnly keeps only tasks with a runtime session.
202		LiveOnly bool
203		// DirtyOnly keeps only tasks with uncommitted work.
204		DirtyOnly bool
205	}
206	
207	// Apply returns the rows matching f.
208	func (f Filter) Apply(rows []Row) []Row {
209		out := rows[:0:0]
210		for _, r := range rows {
211			if len(f.States) > 0 && !containsState(f.States, r.Task.State) {
212				continue
213			}
214			if f.Repo != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Task.Repo), strings.ToLower(f.Repo)) {
215				continue
216			}
217			if f.LiveOnly && !r.Live() {
218				continue
219			}
220			if f.DirtyOnly && !r.Status.Dirty() {
221				continue
222			}
223			out = append(out, r)
224		}
225		return out
226	}
227	
228	func containsState(list []task.State, s task.State) bool {
229		for _, v := range list {
230			if v == s {
231				return true
232			}
233		}
234		return false
235	}
236	
237	// Orphans reports live runtime sessions that no task claims — the "I opened
238	// this and never wrote it down" case that makes a sidebar grow without bound.
239	func Orphans(sessions []runtime.Session, rows []Row) []runtime.Session {
240		claimed := map[string]bool{}
241		for _, r := range rows {
242			if r.Session != nil {
243				claimed[r.Session.Handle] = true
244			}
245		}
246		var out []runtime.Session
247		for _, s := range sessions {
248			if !claimed[s.Handle] {
249				out = append(out, s)
250			}
251		}
252		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Label < out[j].Label })
253		return out
254	}
255
```

```text
1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123	
124		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
125		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
126	}
127	
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141	
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}
```
