1	package task
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"io/fs"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"regexp"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	
14		"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}
241

9	// Status is the live git state of one checkout — everything dev's inventory
10	// shows about a task without persisting any of it.
11	type Status struct {
12		Branch   string `json:"branch,omitempty"`
13		Detached bool   `json:"detached"`
14		// Upstream is the tracking ref (e.g. "origin/feat/auth"), empty when the
15		// branch has never been published.
16		Upstream string `json:"upstream,omitempty"`
17		Ahead    int    `json:"ahead"`
18		Behind   int    `json:"behind"`
19		// Changed counts unique changed paths. Staged and Unstaged are index /
20		// working-tree views and can overlap when one path has both kinds of
21		// changes; Changed does not double-count it.
22		Changed   int `json:"changed"`
23		Staged    int `json:"staged"`
24		Unstaged  int `json:"unstaged"`
25		Untracked int `json:"untracked"`
26		// Added, Modified, Deleted and Renamed classify status letters. One path
27		// can contribute to two when its staged and unstaged states differ.
28		Added    int `json:"added"`
29		Modified int `json:"modified"`
30		Deleted  int `json:"deleted"`
31		Renamed  int `json:"renamed"`
32		// Conflicted counts unmerged paths; a non-zero value means the checkout is
33		// mid-merge or mid-rebase and must not be touched automatically.
34		Conflicted int `json:"conflicted"`
35	}
36	
37	// Dirty reports uncommitted work of any kind.
38	func (s Status) Dirty() bool { return s.Changed > 0 }
39	
40	// Published reports whether the branch has an upstream at all.
41	func (s Status) Published() bool { return s.Upstream != "" }
42	
43	// Synced reports a branch that is published and exactly level with upstream.
44	func (s Status) Synced() bool { return s.Published() && s.Ahead == 0 && s.Behind == 0 }
45	
46	// Summary renders the compact, starship-like column used throughout dev:
47	//
48	//	⇕⇡2⇣1 =1 +3 !2 ?4
49	//
50	// Divergence, conflicts, staged, unstaged and untracked paths remain separate
51	// so "dirty" says how and by how much, rather than collapsing to one ●.
52	func (s Status) Summary() string {
53		var parts []string
54		switch {
55		case s.Ahead > 0 && s.Behind > 0:
56			parts = append(parts, "⇕⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead)+"⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
57		case s.Ahead > 0:
58			parts = append(parts, "⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead))
59		case s.Behind > 0:
60			parts = append(parts, "⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
61		}
62		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
63			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted))
64		}
65		if s.Staged > 0 {
66			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged))
67		}
68		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
69			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged))
70		}
71		if s.Untracked > 0 {
72			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked))
73		}
74		if len(parts) == 0 {
75			if !s.Published() {
76				return "local"
77			}
78			return "clean"
79		}
80		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
81	}
82	
83	// Breakdown renders the detailed change count shown by `dev status` and the
84	// TUI detail pane. Changed is the unique-path total; staged and unstaged may
85	// overlap, which is stated by presenting them as categories rather than a sum.
86	func (s Status) Breakdown() string {
87		if s.Changed == 0 {
88			return "0 changed paths"
89		}
90		var parts []string
91		if s.Staged > 0 {
92			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged)+" staged")
93		}
94		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
95			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged)+" unstaged")
96		}
97		if s.Untracked > 0 {
98			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked)+" untracked")
99		}
100		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
101			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted)+" conflicted")
102		}
103		return strconv.Itoa(s.Changed) + " changed paths (" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")"
104	}
105	
106	// TypeBreakdown classifies the status letters when that detail is available.
107	func (s Status) TypeBreakdown() string {
108		var parts []string
109		for _, item := range []struct {
110			n    int
111			name string
112		}{
113			{s.Added, "added"}, {s.Modified, "modified"}, {s.Deleted, "deleted"},
114			{s.Renamed, "renamed/copied"},
115		} {
116			if item.n > 0 {
117				parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(item.n)+" "+item.name)
118			}
119		}
120		return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
121	}
122	
123	// StatusOf reads the porcelain v2 status of the checkout at dir. Porcelain v2
124	// is the documented machine-readable format: it reports branch, upstream and
125	// ahead/behind in the same pass as the file states, so one process gives dev
126	// everything it needs.
127	func StatusOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Status, error) {
128		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=normal", "-z")
129		if err != nil {
130			return Status{}, err
131		}
132		var s Status
133		for _, rec := range nulLines(out) {
134			if rec == "" {
135				continue
136			}
137			switch rec[0] {
138			case '#':
139				parseBranchHeader(rec, &s)
140			case '1', '2':
141				// "1 XY ..." ordinary change, "2 XY ..." rename/copy. X is
142				// staged, Y unstaged. This record is one unique changed path even
143				// when both sides are non-dot.
144				f := strings.Fields(rec)
145				if len(f) < 2 || len(f[1]) < 2 {
146					continue
147				}
148				s.Changed++
149				x, y := f[1][0], f[1][1]
150				if x != '.' {
151					s.Staged++
152				}
153				if y != '.' {
154					s.Unstaged++
155				}
156				classifyChange(x, &s)
157				classifyChange(y, &s)
158			case 'u':
159				s.Changed++
160				s.Conflicted++
161			case '?':
162				s.Changed++
163				s.Untracked++
164			}
165		}
166		return s, nil
167	}
168	
169	func classifyChange(code byte, s *Status) {
170		switch code {
171		case 'A':
172			s.Added++
173		case 'M', 'T':
174			s.Modified++
175		case 'D':
176			s.Deleted++
177		case 'R', 'C':
178			s.Renamed++
179		}
180	}
181	
182	func parseBranchHeader(rec string, s *Status) {
183		f := strings.Fields(rec)
184		if len(f) < 3 {
185			return
186		}
187		switch f[1] {
188		case "branch.head":
189			if f[2] == "(detached)" {
190				s.Detached = true
191			} else {
192				s.Branch = f[2]
193			}
194		case "branch.upstream":
195			s.Upstream = f[2]
196		case "branch.ab":
197			// "# branch.ab +2 -1"
198			if len(f) < 4 {
199				return
200			}
201			s.Ahead, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[2], "+"))
202			s.Behind, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[3], "-"))
203		}
204	}
205	
206	// LastCommit reports the author timestamp of HEAD as a Unix epoch, and the
207	// subject line. Used to age a task in `dev sweep`.
208	func LastCommit(ctx context.Context, dir string) (unix int64, subject string, err error) {
209		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "log", "-1", "--format=%at%x00%s")
210		if err != nil || out == "" {
211			return 0, "", err
212		}
213		ts, subj, _ := strings.Cut(out, "\x00")
214		unix, _ = strconv.ParseInt(ts, 10, 64)
215		return unix, subj, nil
216	}
217	
218	// WipCommit stages everything and records a checkpoint commit.
219	//
220	// A checkpoint commit is deliberately preferred over `git stash`: a stash is
221	// invisible in the log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never
222	// travel to another machine, which is exactly what parking a task needs.
223	func WipCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, message string) (bool, error) {
224		st, err := StatusOf(ctx, dir)
225		if err != nil {
226			return false, err
227		}
228		if !st.Dirty() {
229			return false, nil
230		}
231		if st.Conflicted > 0 {
232			return false, &Error{Args: []string{"commit"}, Dir: dir,
233				Stderr: "checkout has unmerged paths; resolve the conflict before parking"}
234		}
235		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
236			return false, err
237		}
238		if message == "" {
239			message = "wip: checkpoint"
240		}
241		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", message); err != nil {
242			return false, err
243		}
244		return true, nil
245	}
246

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
38		Bare bool
39		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
40		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
41		// initialise them.
42		HasGit bool
43	}
44	
45	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
46	func (r Repo) Display() string {
47		if r.Category == "" {
48			return r.Name
49		}
50		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
51	}
52	
53	// Options tunes discovery.
54	type Options struct {
55		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
56		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
57		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
58		MaxDepth int
59		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
60		IncludeNonRepos bool
61	}
62	
63	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
64	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
65	
66	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
67	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
68	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
69		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
70		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
71		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
72		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
73	}
74	
75	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
76	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
77	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
78	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
79		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
80			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
81		}
82		seen := map[string]bool{}
83		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
84		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
85		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
86		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
87		identities := map[string]bool{}
88		var out []Repo
89	
90		for _, root := range roots {
91			info, err := os.Stat(root)
92			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
93				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
94			}
95			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
96	
97			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
98				if err != nil {
99					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
100				}
101				if ctx.Err() != nil {
102					return ctx.Err()
103				}
104				if path == rootClean {
105					return nil
106				}
107				name := d.Name()
108				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
109				isDir := d.IsDir()
110				if isLink {
111					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
112					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
113					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
114					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
115						isDir = info.IsDir()
116					}
117				}
118				if !isDir {
119					return nil
120				}
121				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
122					return filepath.SkipDir
123				}
124	
125				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
126				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
127	
128				if isRepoDir(path) {
129					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
130					if real == "" {
131						real = path
132					}
133					bare := isBareDir(path)
134					identity := real
135					if !bare {
136						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
137							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
138							// project in the repo inventory.
139							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
140								return filepath.SkipDir
141							}
142							identity = g.GitCommonDir
143							real = g.MainRoot
144						}
145					}
146					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
147						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
148						out = append(out, Repo{
149							Name:     name,
150							Path:     path,
151							RealPath: real,
152							Symlink:  isLink,
153							Root:     rootClean,
154							Category: filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
155							Bare:     bare,
156							HasGit:   true,
157						})
158					}
159					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
160					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
161					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
162					return filepath.SkipDir
163				}
164				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
165					return filepath.SkipDir
166				}
167				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
168					if !seen[path] {
169						seen[path] = true
170						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
171					}
172				}
173				return nil
174			})
175			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
176				return out, ctx.Err()
177			}
178		}
179	
180		for i := range out {
181			if out[i].Category == "." {
182				out[i].Category = ""
183			}
184		}
185		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
186			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
187				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
188			}
189			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
190		})
191		return out, nil
192	}
193	
194	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
195	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
196	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
197		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
198			return true
199		}
200		return isBareDir(path)
201	}
202	
203	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
204	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
205		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
206			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
207				return false
208			}
209		}
210		return true
211	}
212	
213	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
214	//
215	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
216	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
217	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
218	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
219		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
220		if err != nil {
221			return Repo{}, nil, err
222		}
223		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
224			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
225				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
226				if real == "" {
227					real = g.MainRoot
228				}
229				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
230				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
231				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
232				return Repo{
233					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
234					Symlink: real != abs, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
235				}, nil, nil
236			}
237		}
238		for _, r := range all {
239			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
240				return r, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
244		var hits []Repo
245		for _, r := range all {
246			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
247				hits = append(hits, r)
248			}
249		}
250		switch len(hits) {
251		case 1:
252			return hits[0], nil, nil
253		case 0:
254			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
255		default:
256			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
257		}
258	}
259	
260	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
261	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
262	
263	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
264	
265	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
266	type AmbiguousError struct {
267		Ref        string
268		Candidates []Repo
269	}
270	
271	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
272		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
273		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
274			names[i] = c.Display()
275		}
276		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
277	}
278

1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
18	type Session struct {
19		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
20		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
21		Handle string
22		Label  string
23		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
24		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
25		// value.
26		Dirs []string
27		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
28		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
29		AgentStatus string
30		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
31		AgentSessions []string
32		Focused       bool
33	}
34	
35	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
36	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
37		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
38			if d == dir || strings.HasPrefix(d, dir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(dir, d+"/") {
39				return true
40			}
41		}
42		return false
43	}
44	
45	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
46	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
47	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
48	type Runtime interface {
49		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
50		Name() string
51		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
52		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
53		Available() bool
54		// Open makes dir live and returns a handle. Opening something already open
55		// focuses it rather than duplicating it.
56		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error)
57		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
58		// task entry.
59		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
60		// List enumerates live sessions.
61		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
62		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
63		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
64		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
65	}
66	
67	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
68	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
69	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
70	type WorktreeOpener interface {
71		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error)
72	}
73	
74	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
75	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
76	
77	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
78		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
79	}
80	
81	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
82	//
83	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
84	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then None.
85	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
86	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
87		herdr, tmux, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}
88		switch backend {
89		case "herdr":
90			return herdr
91		case "tmux":
92			return tmux
93		case "none":
94			return none
95		case "", "auto":
96			if herdr.Available() {
97				return herdr
98			}
99			if tmux.Available() {
100				return tmux
101			}
102			return none
103		}
104		return none
105	}
106	
107	// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.
108	func All() []Runtime { return []Runtime{NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}} }
109	
110	// haveBinary reports whether name is on PATH.
111	func haveBinary(name string) bool {
112		_, err := exec.LookPath(name)
113		return err == nil
114	}

1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"time"
6	)
7	
8	// PostCreate accepts either of two TOML shapes, because both read naturally:
9	//
10	//	post_create = "auto"
11	//	post_create = ["uv sync", "npm ci"]
12	type PostCreate struct {
13		Auto     bool
14		Commands []string
15	}
16	
17	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
18	func (p *PostCreate) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
19		switch t := v.(type) {
20		case string:
21			if t != "auto" {
22				return fmt.Errorf("post_create: %q is not a valid string form (use \"auto\" or a list of commands)", t)
23			}
24			*p = PostCreate{Auto: true}
25			return nil
26		case []any:
27			cmds := make([]string, 0, len(t))
28			for i, e := range t {
29				s, ok := e.(string)
30				if !ok {
31					return fmt.Errorf("post_create[%d]: want a command string, got %T", i, e)
32				}
33				cmds = append(cmds, s)
34			}
35			*p = PostCreate{Commands: cmds}
36			return nil
37		default:
38			return fmt.Errorf("post_create: want \"auto\" or a list of command strings, got %T", v)
39		}
40	}
41	
42	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler so a config round-trips.
43	func (p PostCreate) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
44		if p.Auto {
45			return []byte(`"auto"`), nil
46		}
47		out := []byte("[")
48		for i, c := range p.Commands {
49			if i > 0 {
50				out = append(out, ", "...)
51			}
52			out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%q", c)...)
53		}
54		return append(out, ']'), nil
55	}
56	
57	// Duration is a time.Duration written in TOML as a Go duration string
58	// ("10m", "90s"), which is friendlier than a bare number of seconds.
59	type Duration struct{ time.Duration }
60	
61	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
62	func (d *Duration) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
63		switch t := v.(type) {
64		case string:
65			parsed, err := time.ParseDuration(t)
66			if err != nil {
67				return fmt.Errorf("duration %q: %w", t, err)
68			}
69			d.Duration = parsed
70			return nil
71		case int64:
72			d.Duration = time.Duration(t) * time.Second
73			return nil
74		default:
75			return fmt.Errorf("duration: want a string like \"10m\", got %T", v)
76		}
77	}
78	
79	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler.
80	func (d Duration) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
81		return []byte(fmt.Sprintf("%q", d.Duration.String())), nil
82	}
83

220	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
221	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
222	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
223	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
224		cfg := Default()
225		if path == "" {
226			path = ConfigFile()
227		}
228		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
229		switch {
230		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
231			return cfg, nil
232		case err != nil:
233			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
234		}

237			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
238			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)

244	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a

247		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
248		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "none":
249		default:
250			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
251		}
252		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
253			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
254		}
255		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
256			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
257		}

262		}
263		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
264			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
265		}
266		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
267			return fmt.Errorf("forge.remote_limit must be zero (use default) or positive")
268		}

270			switch v {
271			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
272				return true
273			}
274			return false
275		}
276		if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
277			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
278		}
279		for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
280			if !validStrategy(strategy) {
281				return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",
282					ecosystem, strategy)

290			case t.Run == "":
291				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d] (%s): run is required", i, t.Key)
292			}

294				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is the dashboard's %q binding; pick another",
295					i, t.Key, binding)
296			}
297			if prev, ok := seen[t.Key]; ok {
298				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is already bound to %q", i, t.Key, prev)
299			}
300			seen[t.Key] = t.Name

```text
# try - fresh directories for every vibe

**[Website](https://pages.tobi.lutke.com/try/)** · **[RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/try-cli)** · **[GitHub](https://github.com/tobi/try)**

*Your experiments deserve a home.* 🏠

> For everyone who constantly creates new projects for little experiments, a one-file Ruby script to quickly manage and navigate to keep them somewhat organized

Ever find yourself with 50 directories named `test`, `test2`, `new-test`, `actually-working-test`, scattered across your filesystem? Or worse, just coding in `/tmp` and losing everything?

**try** is here for your beautifully chaotic mind.

# What it does 

![Fuzzy Search Demo](assets/try-fuzzy-search-demo.gif)

*[View interactive version on asciinema](https://asciinema.org/a/ve8AXBaPhkKz40YbqPTlVjqgs)*

Instantly navigate through all your experiment directories with:
- **Fuzzy search** that just works
- **Smart sorting** - recently used stuff bubbles to the top
- **Auto-dating** - creates directories like `2025-08-17-redis-experiment`
- **Zero config** - just one Ruby file, no dependencies

## Installation

### RubyGems (Recommended)

```bash
gem install try-cli
```

Then add to your shell:

```bash
# Bash/Zsh - add to .zshrc or .bashrc
eval "$(try init)"

# Fish - add to config.fish
try init | source
```

### Quick Start (Manual)

```bash
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tobi/try/refs/heads/main/try.rb > ~/.local/try.rb

# Make "try" executable so it can be run directly
chmod +x ~/.local/try.rb

# Add to your shell (bash/zsh)
echo 'eval "$(ruby ~/.local/try.rb init ~/src/tries)"' >> ~/.zshrc

# for fish shell users
echo '~/.local/try.rb init ~/src/tries | source' >> ~/.config/fish/config.fish
```

## The Problem

You're learning Redis. You create `/tmp/redis-test`. Then `~/Desktop/redis-actually`. Then `~/projects/testing-redis-again`. Three weeks later you can't find that brilliant connection pooling solution you wrote at 2am.

## The Solution

All your experiments in one place, with instant fuzzy search:

```bash
$ try pool
→ 2025-08-14-redis-connection-pool    2h, 18.5
  2025-08-03-thread-pool              3d, 12.1
  2025-07-22-db-pooling               2w, 8.3
  + Create new: pool
```

Type, arrow down, enter. You're there.

## Features

### 🎯 Smart Fuzzy Search
Not just substring matching - it's smart:
- `rds` matches `redis-server`
- `connpool` matches `connection-pool`
- Recent stuff scores higher
- Shorter names win on equal matches

### ⏰ Time-Aware
- Shows how long ago you touched each project
- Recently accessed directories float to the top
- Perfect for "what was I working on yesterday?"

### 🎨 Pretty TUI
- Clean, minimal interface
- Highlights matches as you type
- Shows scores so you know why things are ranked
- Dark mode by default (because obviously)

### 📁 Organized Chaos
- Everything lives in `~/src/tries` (configurable via `TRY_PATH`)
- Auto-prefixes with dates: `2025-08-17-your-idea`
- Skip the date prompt if you already typed a name

### Shell Integration

- Bash/Zsh:

  ```bash
  # default is ~/src/tries
  eval "$(~/.local/try.rb init)"
  # or pick a path
  eval "$(~/.local/try.rb init ~/src/tries)"
  ```

- Fish:

  ```fish
  ~/.local/try.rb init | source
  # or pick a path
  ~/.local/try.rb init ~/src/tries | source
  ```

Notes:
- The runtime commands printed by `try` are shell-neutral (absolute paths, quoted). Only the small wrapper function differs per shell.

## Usage

```bash
try                                          # Browse all experiments
try redis                                    # Jump to redis experiment or create new
try new api                                  # Start with "2025-08-17-new-api"
try . [name]                                   # Create a dated worktree dir for current repo
try ./path/to/repo [name]                      # Use another repo as the worktree source
try worktree dir [name]                        # Same as above, explicit CLI form
try clone https://github.com/user/repo.git  # Clone repo into date-prefixed directory
try https://github.com/user/repo.git        # Shorthand for clone (same as above)
try --help                                   # See all options
```

Notes on worktrees (`try .` / `try worktree dir`):
- With a custom [name], uses that; otherwise uses cwd’s basename. Both are prefixed with today’s date.
- Inside a Git repo: adds a detached HEAD git worktree to the created directory.
- Outside a repo: simply creates the directory and changes into it.

### Git Repository Cloning

**try** can automatically clone git repositories into properly named experiment directories:

```bash
# Clone with auto-generated directory name
try clone https://github.com/tobi/try.git
# Creates: 2025-08-27-tobi-try

# Clone with custom name
try clone https://github.com/tobi/try.git my-fork
# Creates: my-fork

# Shorthand syntax (no need to type 'clone')
try https://github.com/tobi/try.git
# Creates: 2025-08-27-tobi-try
```

Supported git URI formats:
- `https://github.com/user/repo.git` (HTTPS GitHub)
- `git@github.com:user/repo.git` (SSH GitHub)
- `https://gitlab.com/user/repo.git` (GitLab)
- `git@host.com:user/repo.git` (SSH other hosts)

The `.git` suffix is automatically removed from URLs when generating directory names.

### Keyboard Shortcuts

- `↑/↓` or `Ctrl-P/N/J/K` - Navigate
- `Enter` - Select or create
- `Backspace` - Delete character
- `Ctrl-D` - Delete directory (with confirmation)
- `ESC` - Cancel
- Just type to filter

## Configuration

Set `TRY_PATH` to change where experiments are stored:

```bash
export TRY_PATH=~/code/sketches
```

Default: `~/src/tries`

## Nix

### Quick start

```bash
nix run github:tobi/try
nix run github:tobi/try -- --help
nix run github:tobi/try init ~/my-tries
```

### Home Manager

```nix
{
  inputs.try.url = "github:tobi/try";
  
  imports = [ inputs.try.homeManagerModules.default ];
  
  programs.try = {
    enable = true;
    path = "~/experiments";  # optional, defaults to ~/src/tries
  };
}
```

## Homebrew

### Quick start

```bash
brew tap tobi/try https://github.com/tobi/try
brew install try
```

After installation, add to your shell:

- Bash/Zsh:

  ```bash
  # default is ~/src/tries
  eval "$(try init)"
  # or pick a path
  eval "$(try init ~/src/tries)"
  ```

- Fish:

  ```fish
  try init | source
  # or pick a path
  try init ~/src/tries | source
  ```

## Why Ruby?

- One file, no dependencies
- Works on any system with Ruby (macOS has it built-in)
- Fast enough for thousands of directories
- Easy to hack on

## The Philosophy

Your brain doesn't work in neat folders. You have ideas, you try things, you context-switch like a caffeinated squirrel. This tool embraces that.

Every experiment gets a home. Every home is instantly findable. Your 2am coding sessions are no longer lost to the void.

## FAQ

**Q: Why not just use `cd` and `ls`?**
A: Because you have 200 directories and can't remember if you called it `test-redis`, `redis-test`, or `new-redis-thing`.

**Q: Why not use `fzf`?**
A: fzf is great for files. This is specifically for project directories, with time-awareness and auto-creation built in.

**Q: Can I use this for real projects?**
A: You can, but it's designed for experiments. Real projects deserve real names in real locations.

**Q: What if I have thousands of experiments?**
A: First, welcome to the club. Second, it handles it fine - the scoring algorithm ensures relevant stuff stays on top.

## Installing from Source / Fork

If you've forked `try` or want to run a modified version:

```bash
# Clone your fork
git clone git@github.com:YOUR_USER/try.git
cd try

# Option 1: Build and install as a gem (replaces the official gem)
gem build try-cli.gemspec
gem install ./try-cli-*.gem

# Option 2: Point your shell directly at the repo (no gem needed)
# Add to your ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc:
eval "$(ruby /path/to/your/try/try.rb init ~/src/tries)"
```

After installing a new gem, re-source your shell config (`source ~/.zshrc`) so the wrapper function picks up the new path.

For a full development walkthrough, see [docs/ruby-dev-guide-101.md](docs/ruby-dev-guide-101.md).

## Contributing

It's one file. If you want to change something, just edit it. Send a PR if you think others would like it too.

## License

MIT - Do whatever you want with it.

---

*Built for developers with ADHD by developers with ADHD.*

*Your experiments deserve a home.* 🏠
```

     6	  def collect(path)
     7	    git_path = File.join(path, '.git')

    10	    branch = git(path, "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
    11	    return nil unless branch
    12	    branch = branch.strip
    13	
    14	    # Detached HEAD — show short sha instead
    15	    if branch == "HEAD"
    16	      short = git(path, "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD")
    17	      branch = short ? short.strip : "HEAD"
    18	    end
    19	
    20	    remote_lines = git(path, "remote")
    21	    remote = remote_lines ? remote_lines.strip.split("\n").first : nil
    22	
    23	    remote_url = nil
    24	    if remote && !remote.empty?

    27	    end
    28

    30	    behind = 0
    31	    if remote && !remote.empty?
    32	      counts = git(path, "rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", "HEAD...@{upstream}")
    33	      if counts && counts =~ /\d/
    34	        parts = counts.strip.split(/\s+/)
    35	        ahead  = parts[0].to_i
    36	        behind = parts[1].to_i
    37	      end
    38	    end
    39	
    40	    dirty = false
    41	    status_out = git(path, "status", "--porcelain", "-uno")

    45	      branch: branch,
    46	      remote: remote && !remote.empty? ? remote : nil,

    48	      ahead: ahead,
    49	      behind: behind,
    50	      dirty: dirty
    51	    }

    53	    nil
    54	  end

===== spec/delete_spec.md =====
# Delete Mode Specification

## Overview

Delete mode allows batch deletion of directories with visual feedback and confirmation. This is a multi-step operation designed to prevent accidental deletions.

## Workflow

### Step 1: Mark Items

- Press `Ctrl-D` on any directory entry to mark it for deletion
- Marked entries display with `{strike}` token (dark red background)
- Selection indicator changes to show marked state
- Can continue navigating and marking multiple items
- Pressing `Ctrl-D` on an already-marked item unmarks it (toggle)
- Cannot mark the `[new]` entry

### Step 2: Delete Mode UI

When one or more items are marked:

- Footer changes to show delete mode status
- Format: `DELETE MODE | X marked | Ctrl-D: Toggle | Enter: Confirm | Esc: Cancel`
- Marked items remain visible with strikethrough styling

### Step 3: Confirm or Cancel

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| Enter | Show confirmation dialog |
| Esc | Exit delete mode, clear all marks |
| Ctrl-D | Toggle mark on current item |
| Arrow keys | Continue navigating |

### Step 4: Type YES to Delete

Confirmation dialog shows:

```
Delete X directories?

  - directory-1
  - directory-2
  - ...

Type YES to confirm:
```

- Must type exactly `YES` (case-sensitive) to proceed
- Any other input cancels the operation
- After typing, press Enter to submit

## Script Output Format

In exec mode, delete outputs a shell script that is evaluated by the shell wrapper.

### Script Structure

```sh
cd '/path/to/tries' && \
  test -d 'dir-name-1' ]] && rm -rf 'dir-name-1' && \
  test -d 'dir-name-2' ]] && rm -rf 'dir-name-2' && \
  cd '/original/pwd' 2>/dev/null || cd '/path/to/tries'
```

Each command is on its own line, chained with `&& \` for readability, with 2-space indent on continuation lines.

### Script Components

1. **Change to tries base directory**
   ```sh
   cd '/path/to/tries' && \
   ```
   All deletions happen relative to the tries base path.

...
</persisted-output>
```

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Read tobi try metadata and README

`gh repo view tobi/try --json nameWithOwner,description,defaultBranchRef,url,licenseInfo,updatedAt && gh api 'repos/tobi/try/contents/README.md?ref=main' --jq '.content' | base64 --decode`

```text
{"defaultBranchRef":{"name":"main"},"description":"fresh directories for every vibe","licenseInfo":{"key":"mit","name":"MIT License","nickname":""},"nameWithOwner":"tobi/try","updatedAt":"2026-08-27T08:45:58Z","url":"https://github.com/tobi/try"}
# try - fresh directories for every vibe

**[Website](https://pages.tobi.lutke.com/try/)** · **[RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/try-cli)** · **[GitHub](https://github.com/tobi/try)**

*Your experiments deserve a home.* 🏠

> For everyone who constantly creates new projects for little experiments, a one-file Ruby script to quickly manage and navigate to keep them somewhat organized

Ever find yourself with 50 directories named `test`, `test2`, `new-test`, `actually-working-test`, scattered across your filesystem? Or worse, just coding in `/tmp` and losing everything?

**try** is here for your beautifully chaotic mind.

# What it does

![Fuzzy Search Demo](assets/try-fuzzy-search-demo.gif)

*[View interactive version on asciinema](https://asciinema.org/a/ve8AXBaPhkKz40YbqPTlVjqgs)*

Instantly navigate through all your experiment directories with:
- **Fuzzy search** that just works
- **Smart sorting** - recently used stuff bubbles to the top
- **Auto-dating** - creates directories like `2025-08-17-redis-experiment`
- **Zero config** - just one Ruby file, no dependencies

## Installation

### RubyGems (Recommended)

```bash
gem install try-cli
```

Then add to your shell:

```bash
# Bash/Zsh - add to .zshrc or .bashrc
eval "$(try init)"

# Fish - add to config.fish
try init | source
```

### Quick Start (Manual)

```bash
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tobi/try/refs/heads/main/try.rb > ~/.local/try.rb

# Make "try" executable so it can be run directly
chmod +x ~/.local/try.rb

# Add to your shell (bash/zsh)
echo 'eval "$(ruby ~/.local/try.rb init ~/src/tries)"' >> ~/.zshrc

# for fish shell users
echo '~/.local/try.rb init ~/src/tries | source' >> ~/.config/fish/config.fish
```


### Native binary (optional)

Compile a native `try` with [Spinel](https://github.com/matz/spinel). Build Spinel from source; [PR 3906](https://github.com/matz/spinel/pull/3906) is required so `IO#tty?` / `#winsize` work on handles that are not statically typed IO.

```bash
make native SPINEL=/path/to/spinel   # -O s, then strip
./dist/try --help
eval "$(./dist/try init)"   # wires the shell function to the binary, not MRI
make native-test SPINEL=/path/to/spinel
```

MRI `ruby try.rb` and the gem keep working. `dist/try init` emits the binary path; `ruby try.rb init` still emits `/usr/bin/env ruby '…/try.rb'`.

## The Problem

You're learning Redis. You create `/tmp/redis-test`. Then `~/Desktop/redis-actually`. Then `~/projects/testing-redis-again`. Three weeks later you can't find that brilliant connection pooling solution you wrote at 2am.

## The Solution

All your experiments in one place, with instant fuzzy search:

```bash
$ try pool
→ 2025-08-14-redis-connection-pool    2h, 18.5
  2025-08-03-thread-pool              3d, 12.1
  2025-07-22-db-pooling               2w, 8.3
  + Create new: pool
```

Type, arrow down, enter. You're there.

## Features

### 🎯 Smart Fuzzy Search
Not just substring matching - it's smart:
- `rds` matches `redis-server`
- `connpool` matches `connection-pool`
- Recent stuff scores higher
- Shorter names win on equal matches

### ⏰ Time-Aware
- Shows how long ago you touched each project
- Recently accessed directories float to the top
- Perfect for "what was I working on yesterday?"

### 🎨 Pretty TUI
- Clean, minimal interface
- Highlights matches as you type
- Shows scores so you know why things are ranked
- Dark mode by default (because obviously)

### 📁 Organized Chaos
- Everything lives in `~/src/tries` (configurable via `TRY_PATH`)
- Auto-prefixes with dates: `2025-08-17-your-idea`
- Skip the date prompt if you already typed a name

### Shell Integration

- Bash/Zsh:

  ```bash
  # default is ~/src/tries
  eval "$(~/.local/try.rb init)"
  # or pick a path
  eval "$(~/.local/try.rb init ~/src/tries)"
  ```

- Fish:

  ```fish
  ~/.local/try.rb init | source
  # or pick a path
  ~/.local/try.rb init ~/src/tries | source
  ```

Notes:
- The runtime commands printed by `try` are shell-neutral (absolute paths, quoted). Only the small wrapper function differs per shell.

## Usage

```bash
try                                          # Browse all experiments
try redis                                    # Jump to redis experiment or create new
try new api                                  # Start with "2025-08-17-new-api"
try . [name]                                   # Create a dated worktree dir for current repo
try ./path/to/repo [name]                      # Use another repo as the worktree source
try worktree dir [name]                        # Same as above, explicit CLI form
try clone https://github.com/user/repo.git  # Clone repo into date-prefixed directory
try https://github.com/user/repo.git        # Shorthand for clone (same as above)
try --help                                   # See all options
```

Notes on worktrees (`try .` / `try worktree dir`):
- With a custom [name], uses that; otherwise uses cwd’s basename. Both are prefixed with today’s date.
- Inside a Git repo: adds a detached HEAD git worktree to the created directory.
- Outside a repo: simply creates the directory and changes into it.

### Git Repository Cloning

**try** can automatically clone git repositories into properly named experiment directories:

```bash
# Clone with auto-generated directory name
try clone https://github.com/tobi/try.git
# Creates: 2025-08-27-tobi-try

# Clone with custom name
try clone https://github.com/tobi/try.git my-fork
# Creates: my-fork

# Shorthand syntax (no need to type 'clone')
try https://github.com/tobi/try.git
# Creates: 2025-08-27-tobi-try

# Paste a GitHub pull request URL to clone and check out that PR
try https://github.com/tobi/try/pull/124
# Creates: 2025-08-27-tobi-try
```

Supported git URI formats:
- `https://github.com/user/repo.git` (HTTPS GitHub)
- `git@github.com:user/repo.git` (SSH GitHub)
- `https://gitlab.com/user/repo.git` (GitLab)
- `git@host.com:user/repo.git` (SSH other hosts)
- `ssh://git@host.com:port/user/repo.git` (SSH other hosts with custom port)
- `user@host:path/to/repo.git` (nested SCP-style SSH URLs)
- `https://github.com/user/repo/pull/123` (GitHub pull requests)

A GitHub pull request URL clones the main repository, fetches the PR ref, and
checks it out in detached HEAD state. The directory name is based on the main
repository URL, not the `/pull/<number>` suffix. The `.git` suffix is
automatically removed from URLs when generating directory names.

### Keyboard Shortcuts

- `↑/↓` or `Ctrl-P/N/J/K` - Navigate
- `Enter` - Select or create
- `Backspace` - Delete character
- `Ctrl-D` - Delete directory (with confirmation)
- `ESC` - Cancel
- Just type to filter

## Configuration

Set `TRY_PATH` to change where experiments are stored:

```bash
export TRY_PATH=~/code/sketches
```

Default: `~/src/tries`

## Nix

### Quick start

```bash
nix run github:tobi/try
nix run github:tobi/try -- --help
nix run github:tobi/try init ~/my-tries
```

### Home Manager

```nix
{
  inputs.try.url = "github:tobi/try";

  imports = [ inputs.try.homeManagerModules.default ];

  programs.try = {
    enable = true;
    path = "~/experiments";  # optional, defaults to ~/src/tries
  };
}
```

## Homebrew

### Quick start

```bash
brew tap tobi/try https://github.com/tobi/try
brew install try
```

After installation, add to your shell:

- Bash/Zsh:

  ```bash
  # default is ~/src/tries
  eval "$(try init)"
  # or pick a path
  eval "$(try init ~/src/tries)"
  ```

- Fish:

  ```fish
  try init | source
  # or pick a path
  try init ~/src/tries | source
  ```

## Why Ruby?

- One file, no dependencies
- Works on any system with Ruby (macOS has it built-in)
- Fast enough for thousands of directories
- Easy to hack on

## The Philosophy

Your brain doesn't work in neat folders. You have ideas, you try things, you context-switch like a caffeinated squirrel. This tool embraces that.

Every experiment gets a home. Every home is instantly findable. Your 2am coding sessions are no longer lost to the void.

## FAQ

**Q: Why not just use `cd` and `ls`?**
A: Because you have 200 directories and can't remember if you called it `test-redis`, `redis-test`, or `new-redis-thing`.

**Q: Why not use `fzf`?**
A: fzf is great for files. This is specifically for project directories, with time-awareness and auto-creation built in.

**Q: Can I use this for real projects?**
A: You can, but it's designed for experiments. Real projects deserve real names in real locations.

**Q: What if I have thousands of experiments?**
A: First, welcome to the club. Second, it handles it fine - the scoring algorithm ensures relevant stuff stays on top.

## Contributing

It's one file. If you want to change something, just edit it. Send a PR if you think others would like it too.

## License

MIT - Do whatever you want with it.

---

*Built for developers with ADHD by developers with ADHD.*

*Your experiments deserve a home.* 🏠

54	func runList(app *App, o listOptions) error {
55		ctx := ctxOf()
56		tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
57		if err != nil {
58			return err
59		}
60	
61		filter := inventory.Filter{Repo: o.repo, LiveOnly: o.live, DirtyOnly: o.dirty}
62		for _, s := range o.states {
63			st, err := task.ParseState(s)
64			if err != nil {
65				return err
66			}
67			filter.States = append(filter.States, st)
68		}
69		if len(filter.States) == 0 && !o.showAll {
70			filter.States = []task.State{task.Hot, task.Warm, task.Cold}
71		}
72	
73		rt := app.Runtime()
74		rows := inventory.Collect(ctx, tasks, rt, inventory.Options{SkipRuntime: o.noRuntime})
75		rows = filter.Apply(rows)
76	
77		if o.jsonOut {
78			return emitJSON(app, rows)
79		}
80	
81		if len(rows) == 0 {
82			if len(tasks) == 0 {
83				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No tasks yet. Start one with:  dev start <repo> --task <name>")
84			} else {
85				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No tasks match that filter. Try `dev ls --all`.")
86			}
87			return nil
88		}
89	
90		t := NewTable("", "TASK", "STATE", "REPO", "BRANCH", "GIT", "AGE", "SESSION", "NEXT")
91		for _, r := range rows {
92			session := "—"
93			if r.Live() {
94				session = rt.Name()
95				if r.Session.AgentStatus != "" {
96					session += ":" + r.Session.AgentStatus
97				}
98			}
99			gitCol := r.Status.Summary()
100			switch {
101			case r.StatusErr != nil:
102				gitCol = "?"
103			case !r.CheckoutExists:
104				gitCol = "no checkout"
105			}
106			t.Add(
107				r.Task.State.Icon(),
108				truncate(r.Task.Title(), 28),
109				r.Task.State.Label(),
110				truncate(r.Task.Repo, 20),
111				truncate(r.Task.Branch, 28),
112				gitCol,
113				humanAge(r.Age()),
114				session,
115				truncate(dash(r.Task.Next), 40),
116			)
117		}
118		t.Render(app.Out)
119	
120		// Surface drift as a hint rather than rewriting state behind the user's
121		// back: dev reports, the user decides.
122		var drifted int
123		for _, r := range rows {
124			if r.StateDrift() != "" {
125				drifted++

127		}
128		if drifted > 0 {
129			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\n%d task(s) drifted from their recorded state — run `dev sweep` to review.\n", drifted)

181		out := make([]jsonRow, 0, len(rows))

194				Owner:          r.Task.Owner,

196				Note:           r.Task.Note,

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"io"
6		"strings"
7		"time"
8		"unicode/utf8"
9	)
10	
11	// Table renders aligned columns. It measures width in runes rather than bytes
12	// so the CJK repo and branch names in a real inventory line up.
13	type Table struct {
14		head []string
15		rows [][]string
16	}
17	
18	// NewTable starts a table with the given header.
19	func NewTable(header ...string) *Table { return &Table{head: header} }
20	
21	// Add appends a row. Short rows are padded, long ones are truncated to the
22	// header width so a stray field can never shift the whole table.
23	func (t *Table) Add(cells ...string) {
24		row := make([]string, len(t.head))
25		copy(row, cells)
26		t.rows = append(t.rows, row)
27	}
28	
29	// Len reports the number of data rows.
30	func (t *Table) Len() int { return len(t.rows) }
31	
32	// Render writes the table, sizing every column to its widest cell.
33	func (t *Table) Render(w io.Writer) {
34		if len(t.rows) == 0 {
35			return
36		}
37		widths := make([]int, len(t.head))
38		for i, h := range t.head {
39			widths[i] = width(h)
40		}
41		for _, r := range t.rows {
42			for i, c := range r {
43				if n := width(c); n > widths[i] {
44					widths[i] = n
45				}
46			}
47		}
48		writeRow(w, t.head, widths)
49		for _, r := range t.rows {
50			writeRow(w, r, widths)
51		}
52	}
53	
54	func writeRow(w io.Writer, cells []string, widths []int) {
55		var b strings.Builder
56		for i, c := range cells {
57			if i == len(cells)-1 {
58				b.WriteString(c) // never pad the last column
59				break
60			}
61			b.WriteString(c)
62			b.WriteString(strings.Repeat(" ", widths[i]-width(c)+2))
63		}
64		fmt.Fprintln(w, strings.TrimRight(b.String(), " "))
65	}
66	
67	// width counts display columns, treating wide CJK runes as two.
68	func width(s string) int {
69		n := 0
70		for _, r := range s {
71			if isWide(r) {
72				n += 2
73			} else {
74				n++
75			}
76		}
77		return n
78	}
79	
80	func isWide(r rune) bool {
81		switch {
82		case r >= 0x1100 && r <= 0x115F, // Hangul Jamo
83			r >= 0x2E80 && r <= 0xA4CF, // CJK radicals through Yi
84			r >= 0xAC00 && r <= 0xD7A3, // Hangul syllables
85			r >= 0xF900 && r <= 0xFAFF, // CJK compatibility ideographs
86			r >= 0xFE30 && r <= 0xFE6F, // CJK compatibility forms
87			r >= 0xFF00 && r <= 0xFF60, // fullwidth forms
88			r >= 0xFFE0 && r <= 0xFFE6,
89			r >= 0x20000 && r <= 0x3FFFD: // CJK extension planes
90			return true
91		}
92		return false
93	}
94	
95	// truncate shortens s to at most n display columns, marking the cut with "…".
96	func truncate(s string, n int) string {
97		if n <= 0 || width(s) <= n {
98			return s
99		}
100		var b strings.Builder
101		used := 0
102		for _, r := range s {
103			rw := 1
104			if isWide(r) {
105				rw = 2
106			}
107			if used+rw > n-1 {
108				break
109			}
110			b.WriteRune(r)
111			used += rw
112		}
113		return b.String() + "…"
114	}
115	
116	// dash renders an empty value as a visible placeholder, so a blank column is
117	// never mistaken for a rendering bug.
118	func dash(s string) string {
119		if strings.TrimSpace(s) == "" {
120			return "—"
121		}
122		return s
123	}
124	
125	// humanAge renders a duration the way a changelog would: "3d", "2w", "5mo".
126	func humanAge(d time.Duration) string {
127		switch {
128		case d <= 0:
129			return "—"
130		case d < time.Hour:
131			return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", int(d.Minutes()))
132		case d < 24*time.Hour:
133			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
134		case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
135			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
136		case d < 60*24*time.Hour:
137			return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
138		default:
139			return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
140		}
141	}
142	
143	// shellQuote makes a path safe to paste into a POSIX shell command.
144	func shellQuote(s string) string {
145		if s == "" {
146			return "''"
147		}
148		safe := true
149		for _, r := range s {
150			if !(r == '/' || r == '.' || r == '-' || r == '_' || r == '~' ||
151				(r >= 'a' && r <= 'z') || (r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z') || (r >= '0' && r <= '9')) {
152				safe = false
153				break
154			}
155		}
156		if safe && utf8.ValidString(s) {
157			return s
158		}
159		return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'"
160	}

18	func newStartCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
19		var (
20			name        string
21			branch      string
22			base        string
23			direct      bool
24			branchOnly  bool
25			noWorktree  bool // deprecated spelling of branch-only
26			noProvision bool
27			focus       bool
28			next        string
29		)
30		cmd := &cobra.Command{
31			Use:   "start [repo]",
32			Short: "Track work directly, on a canonical branch, or in an isolated worktree",
33			Long: `Start a tracked change stream in one of three explicit modes:
34	
35	  default        create a branch + linked worktree, provision it, open a
36	                 runtime session, and record the task. Safest for work that
37	                 may be interrupted or run in parallel.
38	  --branch-only  create/switch a branch in the canonical checkout, with no
39	                 worktree. Lighter, but that checkout cannot host another
40	                 branch concurrently.
41	  --direct       track the branch already checked out in the canonical repo —
42	                 usually main — without creating either a branch or worktree.
43	                 Best for one-session ad-hoc changes.
44	
45	For untracked ad-hoc navigation, use "dev repo open" or press Enter in the
46	TUI's REPOS view; that opens the project without creating any task at all.
47	
48	With no repo argument, the repository containing the current directory is used.
49	Always pass --base for an unattended branch/worktree task.`,
50			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
51			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
52				ctx := ctxOf()
53				if direct && (branchOnly || noWorktree) {
54					return errors.New("--direct and --branch-only are different modes; pick one")
55				}
56				branchOnly = branchOnly || noWorktree
57	
58				// Resolve the repository: an explicit argument, else the cwd.
59				var repoPath, repoName, category string
60				if len(args) == 1 {
61					r, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), args[0])
62					if err != nil {
63						return err
64					}
65					repoPath, repoName, category = r.Path, r.Name, r.Category
66				} else {
67					cwd, err := os.Getwd()
68					if err != nil {
69						return err
70					}
71					g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
72					if err != nil {
73						return fmt.Errorf("no repo argument and %s is not a git repository", config.Contract(cwd))
74					}
75					repoPath, repoName = g.MainRoot, g.Name
76				}
77	
78				if name == "" {
79					if branch != "" && !direct {
80						name = branch
81					} else {
82						return errors.New("give the work a name: dev start <repo> --task <name>")
83					}
84				}
85	
86				mode := task.ModeWorktree
87				switch {
88				case direct:
89					mode = task.ModeDirect
90					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, repoPath)
91					if err != nil {
92						return err
93					}
94					if st.Detached || st.Branch == "" {
95						return errors.New("--direct needs a named branch; this checkout has detached HEAD")
96					}
97					if branch != "" && branch != st.Branch {
98						return fmt.Errorf("--direct tracks the branch already checked out (%s), not --branch %s; "+
99							"omit --branch or use --branch-only", st.Branch, branch)
100					}
101					branch, base = st.Branch, st.Branch
102	
103				case branchOnly:
104					mode = task.ModeBranch
105					if branch == "" {
106						branch = "feat/" + config.Slug(name)
107					}
108					if base == "" {
109						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
110					}
111	
112				default:

114						branch = "feat/" + config.Slug(name)
115					}
116					if base == "" {
117						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
118					}
119				}
120	
121				id := task.MakeID(repoName, branch)
122				if existing, err := app.Tasks.Get(id); err == nil {
123					return fmt.Errorf("task %s already exists (state %s) — use `dev resume %s`",
124						existing.ID, existing.State, existing.ID)
125				}
126	
127				t := &task.Task{
128					Name: name, Repo: repoName, RepoPath: repoPath,
129					Branch: branch, Base: base, Mode: mode,
130					State: task.Hot, Owner: config.Hostname(), Next: next,
131				}
132				rt := app.Runtime()
133	
134				switch mode {
135				case task.ModeDirect:
136					handle, err := rt.Open(ctx, repoPath, repoName+"/"+name)
137					if err != nil {

139					} else if rt.Name() != "none" {
140						t.RuntimeHandle = handle

142	
143				case task.ModeBranch:
144					if gitx.BranchExists(ctx, repoPath, branch) {
145						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "switch", branch); err != nil {
146							return fmt.Errorf("switch to %s: %w", branch, err)
147						}
148					} else {
149						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "switch", "-c", branch, base); err != nil {
150							return fmt.Errorf("create and switch to %s from %s: %w", branch, base, err)
151						}
152					}
153					handle, err := rt.Open(ctx, repoPath, repoName+"/"+branch)
154					if err != nil {
155						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
156					} else if rt.Name() != "none" {
157						t.RuntimeHandle = handle
158					}
159	
160				case task.ModeWorktree:
161					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
162					res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
163						RepoPath: repoPath, RepoName: repoName, Branch: branch, Base: base,
164						Category: category, Label: name, NoProvision: noProvision, Focus: focus,
165					})
166					if err != nil {
167						var exists *wt.ErrExists
168						if errors.As(err, &exists) {
169							return fmt.Errorf("%w\nreuse it with: dev resume %s", err, id)
170						}
171						return err
172					}
173					t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
174					reportProvision(app, res)
175				}
176	
177				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {

179				}
180				annotate(app, rt, t)

183					task.Hot.Icon(), t.Name, t.Repo, t.Branch, t.Mode)
184				if t.WorktreePath != "" {
185					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   worktree  %s\n", config.Contract(t.WorktreePath))
186				}
187				if t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
188					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   session   %s %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
189				}
190				if rt.Name() == "none" {
191					app.cdDirective(checkoutOf(t))
192				}
193				return nil
194			},
195		}

197		f.StringVarP(&name, "task", "t", "", "human name for this change stream")
198		f.StringVarP(&branch, "branch", "b", "", "branch name (default: feat/<task-slug>)")
199		f.StringVar(&base, "base", "", "ref a new branch starts from (default: repo default branch)")

201		f.BoolVar(&direct, "direct", false, "track work on the currently checked-out branch; create no branch/worktree")
202		f.BoolVar(&branchOnly, "branch-only", false, "create/switch a branch in the canonical checkout; no worktree")
203		f.BoolVar(&noWorktree, "no-worktree", false, "deprecated alias for --branch-only")
204		_ = f.MarkDeprecated("no-worktree", "use --branch-only (or --direct to stay on main)")
205		f.BoolVar(&noProvision, "no-provision", false, "skip dependency install and ignored-file copying")
206		f.BoolVar(&focus, "focus", false, "focus the new runtime session")
207		return cmd
208	}
209	
210	// checkoutOf is where a task's code lives right now.
211	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
212		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
213			return t.WorktreePath
214		}
215		return t.RepoPath
216	}
217	
218	// annotate pushes the task's state and next action into the runtime as
219	// display-only metadata, so a sidebar can show why a session is open without
220	// anyone having to ask dev.
221	//
222	// For herdr this lands as workspace metadata tokens. A token only renders if
223	// the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
224	//
225	//	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
226	//	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
227	//
228	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
229	// which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
230	func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
231		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
232			return
233		}
234		kv := map[string]string{
235			"stage": t.State.Label(),
236			"next":  t.Next,
237		}
238		if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
239			app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
240		}
241	}
242	
243	func reportProvision(app *App, res *wt.CreateResult) {
244		p := res.Provision
245		if n := len(p.Copied); n > 0 {
246			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   copied    %d gitignored file(s): %s\n", n, strings.Join(p.Copied, ", "))
247		}
248		if n := len(p.Linked); n > 0 {
249			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   linked    %s\n", strings.Join(p.Linked, ", "))
250		}
251		for _, e := range p.Failures {
252			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   warning   %v\n", e)
253		}
254	}

14	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			noProvision bool
17			fetch       bool
18			force       bool
19		)
20		cmd := &cobra.Command{
21			Use:   "resume <task>",
22			Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
23			Long: `Make a parked task hot again.
24	
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29	
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
33			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
34			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
35				ctx := ctxOf()
36				t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				if err != nil {
38					return err
39				}
40	
41				host := config.Hostname()
42				if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
43					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47	
48				if fetch {
49					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin"); err != nil {
50						app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
51					}
52				}
53	
54				rt := app.Runtime()
55				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
56				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
57	
58				switch mode {
59				case task.ModeWorktree:
60					_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
61					// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
63						base := t.Base
64						// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
65						// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
66						if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
67							base = remote
68						}
69						m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
70						res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
71							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, RepoName: t.Repo, Branch: t.Branch,
72							Base: base, Label: t.Title(), NoProvision: noProvision,
73						})
74						if err != nil {
75							var exists *wt.ErrExists
76							if asError(err, &exists) {
77								t.WorktreePath = exists.Path
78							} else {
79								return err
80							}
81						} else {
82							t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
83							reportProvision(app, res)
84							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebuilt    %s\n", config.Contract(res.Path))
85						}
86						checkout = t.WorktreePath
87					}
88	
89				case task.ModeBranch:
90					checkout = t.RepoPath
91					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
92					if err != nil {
93						return err
94					}
95					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
96						if st.Dirty() {
97							return fmt.Errorf("cannot switch the canonical checkout from %s to %s: %s",
98								st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())
99						}
100						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "switch", t.Branch); err != nil {
101							return err
102						}
103					}
104	
105				case task.ModeDirect:
106					checkout = t.RepoPath
107					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
108					if err != nil {
109						return err
110					}
111					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
112						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s tracks %s, but the canonical checkout is on %s; "+
113							"switch back explicitly or start a worktree task", t.Title(), t.Branch, st.Branch)
114					}
115				}
116				if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
117					handle, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, checkout, t.Title())
118					if err != nil {
119						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
120					}
121					if rt.Name() != "none" {
122						t.RuntimeHandle = handle
123					}
124				}
125	
126				t.State = task.Hot
127				t.Owner = host
128				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
129					return err
130				}
131				annotate(app, rt, t)
132	
133				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s  %s on %s (%s)\n",
134					task.Hot.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, mode)
135				if t.Next != "" {
136					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   next      %s\n", t.Next)
137				}
138				if t.AgentSession != "" {
139					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   agent     %s (resumable)\n", t.AgentSession)
140				}
141				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout); err == nil {
142					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   git       %s\n", st.Summary())
143					if st.Behind > 0 {
144						app.warnf("branch is %d behind upstream — `git pull --ff-only` before you start", st.Behind)
145					}
146				}

156		f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "take ownership of a task owned by another machine")
157		return cmd
158	}

17	// datePrefix matches the "2026-08-27-" a try directory carries.
18	var datePrefix = regexp.MustCompile(`^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-`)
19	
20	func newGraduateCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
21		var (
22			category string
23			name     string
24			private  bool
25			remote   bool
26			push     bool
27			dryRun   bool
28		)
29		cmd := &cobra.Command{
30			Use:   "graduate [try]",
31			Short: "Promote an experiment into a real project",
32			Long: `Move a try out of the scratch directory and into your projects tree.
33	
34	An experiment that turns out to matter should stop being an experiment, and
35	that transition is where things usually get lost — the directory keeps its date
36	prefix forever, or it gets copied by hand and the history is left behind.
37	
38	graduate moves the directory to <project_root>/<category>/<name>, drops the
39	date prefix, makes sure it has a git repo and a first commit, and optionally
40	creates the remote with gh or glab.
41	
42	With no argument, the try containing the current directory is used.`,
43			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
44			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
45				ctx := ctxOf()
46				triesRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot)
47	
48				src, err := resolveTry(app, triesRoot, args)
49				if err != nil {
50					return err
51				}
52				if name == "" {
53					name = datePrefix.ReplaceAllString(filepath.Base(src), "")
54				}
55				if name == "" {
56					return fmt.Errorf("could not derive a project name from %s — pass --name", src)
57				}
58	
59				dest := filepath.Join(config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot), category, name)
60				if _, err := os.Stat(dest); err == nil {
61					return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists", config.Contract(dest))
62				}
63	
64				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "graduate  %s\n", config.Contract(src))
65				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "       →  %s\n", config.Contract(dest))
66				if dryRun {
67					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\n(dry run — nothing moved)")
68					return nil
69				}
70	
71				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dest), 0o755); err != nil {
72					return err
73				}
74				// Rename first: it is atomic within a filesystem and leaves
75				// nothing half-copied if it fails.
76				if err := os.Rename(src, dest); err != nil {
77					return fmt.Errorf("move %s: %w\n"+
78						"If the projects root is on another filesystem, copy it by hand and remove the try",
79						config.Contract(src), err)
80				}
81	
82				if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dest, ".git")); err != nil {
83					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dest, "init", "-b", "main"); err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   git init")
87				}
88				// An experiment usually has files but no commit. A project needs
89				// one: without a HEAD there is no default branch, so `dev start`
90				// would have nothing to base a worktree on.
91				if made, err := ensureInitialCommit(ctx, dest, name); err != nil {
92					app.warnf("could not make an initial commit: %v", err)
93				} else if made {
94					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   committed the existing work")
95				}
96	
97				if remote {
98					f, err := forge.Preferred()
99					if err != nil {
100						app.warnf("%v — the project is in place; add a remote by hand", err)
101					} else {
102						url, err := f.CreateRepo(ctx, dest, forge.RepoRequest{
103							Name: name, Private: private, Push: push,
104						})
105						if err != nil {
106							app.warnf("could not create the remote: %v", err)
107						} else {
108							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   remote    %s\n", url)
109						}
110					}
111				}
112	
113				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%s is now a project. Start work on it with:\n  dev start %s --task <name>\n",
114					name, name)
115				return openOrCD(app, ctx, dest, name)
116			},
