127	
128	// resolveTry finds the try directory to graduate: an explicit reference, or
129	// the try containing the current directory.
130	func resolveTry(app *App, triesRoot string, args []string) (string, error) {
131		if len(args) == 1 {
132			ref := args[0]
133			if abs := config.Expand(ref); isDir(abs) {
134				return abs, nil
135			}
136			direct := filepath.Join(triesRoot, ref)
137			if isDir(direct) {
138				return direct, nil
139			}
140			if match := findTry(triesRoot, ref); match != "" {
141				return match, nil
142			}
143			return "", fmt.Errorf("no try matching %q under %s", ref, config.Contract(triesRoot))
144		}
145	
146		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
147		if err != nil {
148			return "", err
149		}
150		if !strings.HasPrefix(cwd, triesRoot+string(filepath.Separator)) {
151			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not inside %s — name the try to graduate",
152				config.Contract(cwd), config.Contract(triesRoot))
153		}
154		// Walk up to the try's own top-level directory, so running this from a
155		// subdirectory still graduates the whole experiment.
156		rel, _ := filepath.Rel(triesRoot, cwd)
157		first := strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator))[0]
158		return filepath.Join(triesRoot, first), nil
159	}
160	
161	func isDir(p string) bool {
162		info, err := os.Stat(p)
163		return err == nil && info.IsDir()
164	}
165	
166	// ensureInitialCommit gives a repository a first commit if it has none,
167	// seeding a README when the tree is otherwise empty. Reports whether it made
168	// one.
169	func ensureInitialCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) (bool, error) {
170		if _, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, dir); err == nil {
171			return false, nil // already has history
172		}
173		if empty, err := isEmptyTree(dir); err != nil {
174			return false, err
175		} else if empty {
176			readme := filepath.Join(dir, "README.md")
177			if err := os.WriteFile(readme, []byte("# "+name+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
178				return false, err
179			}
180		}
181		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
182			return false, err
183		}
184		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "commit", "-m", "chore: graduate experiment into a project"); err != nil {
185			return false, err
186		}
187		return true, nil
188	}
189	
190	// isEmptyTree reports a directory with nothing in it but git's own metadata.
191	func isEmptyTree(dir string) (bool, error) {
192		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
193		if err != nil {
194			return false, err
195		}
196		for _, e := range entries {
197			if e.Name() != ".git" {
198				return false, nil
199			}
200		}
201		return true, nil
202	}

14	// newEditCmd is the top-level `dev edit` convenience command.
15	func newEditCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
16		return newConfigEditorCommand(app, "edit", "Open dev's config in $VISUAL or $EDITOR")
17	}
18	
19	// newConfigEditCmd is the discoverable form next to config show/init/path.
20	func newConfigEditCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
21		return newConfigEditorCommand(app, "edit", "Open this config in $VISUAL or $EDITOR")
22	}
23	
24	func newConfigEditorCommand(app *App, use, short string) *cobra.Command {
25		var editor string
26		cmd := &cobra.Command{
27			Use:   use,
28			Short: short,
29			Long: `Open the config file used by this invocation.
30	
31	If it does not exist, first generate the same machine-detected, fully commented
32	template as "dev config init". Editor resolution is explicit:
33	
34	    --editor → $VISUAL → $EDITOR → nvim → vim → vi
35	
36	An editor value may contain arguments (for example "code --wait"); it is
37	executed through the user's shell with the config path safely quoted.`,
38			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
39			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
40				proc, chosen, created, err := configEditorProcess(app, editor)
41				if err != nil {
42					return err
43				}
44				if created {
45					path := app.configPath
46					if path == "" {
47						path = config.ConfigFile()
48					}
49					fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "created %s from the detected machine layout\n", config.Contract(config.Expand(path)))
50				}
51				proc.Stdin, proc.Stdout, proc.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
52				if err := proc.Run(); err != nil {
53					return fmt.Errorf("editor %q: %w", chosen, err)
54				}
55				return nil
56			},
57		}
58		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&editor, "editor", "", "editor command, overriding $VISUAL and $EDITOR")
59		return cmd
60	}
61	
62	// configEditorProcess resolves the effective config and editor without running
63	// it. The CLI runs the process directly; the TUI passes it to tea.ExecProcess,
64	// which suspends the alternate screen and redraws after the editor exits.
65	func configEditorProcess(app *App, editor string) (*exec.Cmd, string, bool, error) {
66		path := app.configPath
67		if path == "" {
68			path = config.ConfigFile()
69		}
70		path = config.Expand(path)
71		created, err := ensureConfigForEdit(path)
72		if err != nil {
73			return nil, "", false, err
74		}
75		chosen, err := resolveEditor(editor)
76		if err != nil {
77			return nil, "", false, err
78		}
79		command := chosen + " " + shellQuote(path)
80		return exec.Command(shellPath(), "-c", command), chosen, created, nil
81	}
82	
83	// ensureConfigForEdit generates a usable config before opening an absent path.
84	// Editing an empty file would hide every default the user is trying to change.
85	func ensureConfigForEdit(path string) (bool, error) {
86		info, err := os.Stat(path)
87		switch {
88		case err == nil && info.IsDir():

35				kind := "main checkout"

43				}
44

46					branch := st.Branch
47					if st.Detached {
48						branch = "(detached HEAD)"
49					}
50					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "branch     %s  %s\n", branch, st.Summary())
51					if st.Dirty() {

53						if types := st.TypeBreakdown(); types != "" {

55						}
56					}

67					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "default    %s\n", base)
68				}
69				if k := forge.Detect(ctx, g.MainRoot); k != forge.Unknown {
70					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "forge      %s\n", k)
71				}
72	
73				if list, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, g.MainRoot); err == nil && len(list) > 1 {
74					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "worktrees  %d\n", len(list))

101				}
102				if host := config.Hostname(); !t.OwnedBy(host) {
103					app.warnf("this task is owned by %s — pushing from here can diverge the branch", t.Owner)
104				}

The working tree adds a second axis—`CheckoutMode` (`worktree`, `branch`, `direct`)—without changing the four lifecycle states, plus richer git counts and repo detail/heatmap UI. This reinforces an important design constraint for tries: “kind/mode” should not be conflated with `hot/warm/cold/done`, and compatibility must preserve old TOML entries through an inference method like `Task.EffectiveMode()`.

14	// newEditCmd is the top-level `dev edit` convenience command.
15	func newEditCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

17	}

19	// newConfigEditCmd is the discoverable form next to config show/init/path.

22	}
23	
24	func newConfigEditorCommand(app *App, use, short string) *cobra.Command {
25		var editor string
26		cmd := &cobra.Command{
27			Use:   use,
28			Short: short,
29			Long: `Open the config file used by this invocation.
30	
31	If it does not exist, first generate the same machine-detected, fully commented
32	template as "dev config init". Editor resolution is explicit:
33	
34	    --editor → $VISUAL → $EDITOR → nvim → vim → vi
35	
36	An editor value may contain arguments (for example "code --wait"); it is
37	executed through the user's shell with the config path safely quoted.`,
38			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
39			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
40				proc, chosen, created, err := configEditorProcess(app, editor)
41				if err != nil {
42					return err
43				}
44				if created {
45					path := app.configPath
46					if path == "" {
47						path = config.ConfigFile()
48					}
49					fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "created %s from the detected machine layout\n", config.Contract(config.Expand(path)))
50				}
51				proc.Stdin, proc.Stdout, proc.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
52				if err := proc.Run(); err != nil {
53					return fmt.Errorf("editor %q: %w", chosen, err)
54				}
55				return nil
56			},
57		}
58		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&editor, "editor", "", "editor command, overriding $VISUAL and $EDITOR")
59		return cmd
60	}
61	
62	// configEditorProcess resolves the effective config and editor without running
63	// it. The CLI runs the process directly; the TUI passes it to tea.ExecProcess,
64	// which suspends the alternate screen and redraws after the editor exits.
65	func configEditorProcess(app *App, editor string) (*exec.Cmd, string, bool, error) {
66		path := app.configPath
67		if path == "" {
68			path = config.ConfigFile()
69		}
70		path = config.Expand(path)
71		created, err := ensureConfigForEdit(path)
72		if err != nil {
73			return nil, "", false, err
74		}
75		chosen, err := resolveEditor(editor)
76		if err != nil {
77			return nil, "", false, err
78		}
79		command := chosen + " " + shellQuote(path)
80		return exec.Command(shellPath(), "-c", command), chosen, created, nil
81	}
82	
83	// ensureConfigForEdit generates a usable config before opening an absent path.
84	// Editing an empty file would hide every default the user is trying to change.
85	func ensureConfigForEdit(path string) (bool, error) {
86		info, err := os.Stat(path)
87		switch {
88		case err == nil && info.IsDir():
89			return false, fmt.Errorf("%s is a directory, not a config file", config.Contract(path))

91			return false, nil
92		case !os.IsNotExist(err):
93			return false, err
94		}
95		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
96			return false, err
97		}
98		body := renderStarterConfig(config.DetectLayout().Fallbacks())
99		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
100			return false, err
101		}
102		return true, nil
103	}

275						config.Contract(w.Path), st.Summary())
276				}
277	
278				// Close a runtime session pointing at the checkout first, so the
279				// multiplexer is not left on a deleted directory.
280				rt := app.Runtime()
281				var handle string
282				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
283					for _, s := range sessions {
284						for _, d := range s.Dirs {
285							if d == w.Path {
286								handle = s.Handle
287							}
288						}
289					}
290				}
291				m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
292				if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
293					RepoPath: repoPath, Path: w.Path, Force: force, RuntimeHandle: handle,
294				}); err != nil {
295					return err
296				}
297				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "removed %s (branch %s kept)\n", config.Contract(w.Path), w.Branch)
298	
299				// Keep the registry honest about what is now gone.
300				if t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(w.Path); err == nil {
301					t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = "", ""
302					if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err == nil {
303						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "task %s updated — the branch still has the work\n", t.ID)
304					}
305				}
306				return nil
307			},
308		}
309		f := cmd.Flags()
310		f.StringVarP(&repoRef, "repo", "r", "", "repository (default: the current one)")
311		f.BoolVarP(&force, "force", "f", false, "remove even with uncommitted changes")
312		return cmd
313	}
314	
315	func newWtProvisionCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

317		cmd := &cobra.Command{
318			Use:   "provision [path]",
319			Short: "Re-run provisioning for an existing worktree",
320			Long: `Bring an existing checkout up to a working state again.
321	
322	Copies the gitignored files, applies the dependency strategy and runs the
323	post-create commands — useful after adding a new .env, or when a worktree was
324	created with --no-provision.
325	
326	Use "dev wt plan" to see what it would do first.`,
327			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
328			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
329				ctx := ctxOf()
330				target, err := os.Getwd()
331				if err != nil {
332					return err
333				}
334				if len(args) == 1 {
335					target = config.Expand(args[0])
336				}
337				g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, target)

339					return err
340				}
341	
342				set := wt.SettingsFor(app.Cfg, g.MainRoot)
343				plan := wt.BuildPlan(ctx, set, g.MainRoot)

345					renderPlan(app, plan, g.MainRoot)
346					return nil

350					Settings: set,
351					Timeout:  app.Cfg.Worktree.ProvisionTimeout.Duration,

355				if err != nil {

359				if len(res.Copied) > 0 {

361				}
362				if len(res.Linked) > 0 {

364				}

366					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  ran      %s\n", strings.Join(res.Ran, ", "))
367				}
368				for _, s := range res.Skipped {
369					fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "  skipped  %s\n", s)
370				}
371				for _, e := range res.Failures {
372					app.warnf("%v", e)

374				return nil
375			},
376		}
377		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&dryRun, "dry-run", false, "show the plan instead of applying it")
378		return cmd

380	
381	func newWtPlanCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
382		var (
383			repoRef string
384			write   bool
385		)
386		cmd := &cobra.Command{
387			Use:   "plan",
388			Short: "Show what a new worktree of this repo would be provisioned with",
389			Long: `Report the project types detected in this repository and exactly what
390	provisioning a new worktree would do — which gitignored files get copied,
391	which dependency directories are copied or shared, and which install commands
392	run.
393	
394	A worktree that comes up broken is the commonest reason people abandon
395	worktrees, and the config alone cannot answer "what will this actually do":
396	that depends on which lockfiles exist, which tools are installed here, and
397	which files are genuinely gitignored. This computes all of it and changes
398	nothing.
399	
400	With --write, seed a .dev.toml from what was detected, so the repository can
401	commit its own setup and every machine gets the same one.`,
402			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
403			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
404				ctx := ctxOf()
405				repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
406				if err != nil {
407					return err
408				}
409				set := wt.SettingsFor(app.Cfg, repoPath)
410				plan := wt.BuildPlan(ctx, set, repoPath)
411	
412				if write {
413					return writeRepoTemplate(app, repoPath, plan, set)
414				}
415				renderPlan(app, plan, repoPath)
416				return nil
417			},
418		}
419		f := cmd.Flags()
420		f.StringVarP(&repoRef, "repo", "r", "", "repository (default: the current one)")
421		f.BoolVar(&write, "write", false, "seed a .dev.toml in the repository from what was detected")
422		return cmd
423	}
424	
425	// renderPlan prints a provisioning plan as a table plus its warnings.
426	func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {
427		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n\n", config.Contract(repoPath))
428	
429		if len(plan.Ecosystems) == 0 {
430			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No project type detected — only gitignored files will be carried over.")
431		} else {
432			t := NewTable("PROJECT", "MANAGER", "FROM", "DEPENDENCIES", "TOOL")
433			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
434				deps := "—"
435				if len(e.DepDirs) > 0 {
436					deps = strings.Join(e.DepDirs, ", ")
437				} else {
438					deps = "global cache"
439				}
440				tool := "installed"
441				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
442					tool = "MISSING: " + e.Tool
443				}
444				t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
445			}
446			t.Render(app.Out)
447		}
448	
449		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
450		if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
451			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
452		} else {
453			st := NewTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")
454			for _, s := range plan.Steps {
455				mark := "✓"
456				if s.Skipped {
457					mark = "·"
458				}
459				st.Add(mark, string(s.Kind), truncate(s.What, 34), s.Why)
460			}
461			st.Render(app.Out)
462		}
463	
464		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
465			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\nwarning: %s\n", w)
466		}
467		if plan.Empty() {
468			fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nNothing would run. If a new worktree comes up broken, add what it needs to "+
469				"worktree.post_create, or commit a .dev.toml with `dev wt plan --write`.")
470		}
471	}
472	
473	// writeRepoTemplate seeds a .dev.toml from the detected plan.
474	//
475	// Committing it is what makes a project's worktree setup reproducible: the
476	// next machine, and the next person, get the same one without having to
477	// rediscover it.
478	func writeRepoTemplate(app *App, repoPath string, plan wt.Plan, set wt.Settings) error {
479		path := filepath.Join(repoPath, wt.OverrideFilename)
480		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
481			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists — edit it directly", config.Contract(path))
482		}
483	
484		var b strings.Builder
485		b.WriteString("# dev worktree setup for this repository.\n")
486		b.WriteString("#\n")
487		b.WriteString("# Committed on purpose: a worktree is a clean checkout, so without this a\n")
488		b.WriteString("# new one comes up with no dependencies and none of the gitignored files the\n")
489		b.WriteString("# project needs. Seeded by `dev wt plan --write`; edit freely.\n\n")
490		b.WriteString("[worktree]\n")
491	
492		b.WriteString("# Gitignored files to carry into a new worktree. Only files that are BOTH\n")
493		b.WriteString("# listed here AND gitignored are copied — a tracked file is already in the\n")
494		b.WriteString("# checkout on the correct branch.\n")
495		b.WriteString("include = [")
496		for i, inc := range set.Include {
497			if i > 0 {
498				b.WriteString(", ")
499			}
500			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%q", inc)
501		}
502		b.WriteString("]\n\n")
503	
504		if len(plan.Ecosystems) > 0 {
505			b.WriteString("# Detected in this repository:\n")
506			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
507				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "#   %-8s %-8s (%s) → %s\n", e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, e.Install)
508			}
509			b.WriteString("#\n")
510			b.WriteString("# \"auto\" runs those install commands. Replace with an explicit list if this\n")
511			b.WriteString("# project needs something else:  post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
512			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n\n")
513	
514			b.WriteString("# How each project type gets its dependencies:\n")
515			b.WriteString("#   reinstall  run the install command (correct, the default)\n")
516			b.WriteString("#   copy       duplicate the directory from the source checkout (fast)\n")
517			b.WriteString("#   link       share one directory between checkouts (fastest, risky)\n")
518			b.WriteString("#   skip       leave the worktree without dependencies\n")
519			b.WriteString("[worktree.strategies]\n")
520			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
521				switch {
522				case len(e.DepDirs) == 0:
523					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# %-8s = \"reinstall\"  # %s uses a global cache; nothing to copy\n",
524						e.Name, e.Manager)
525				case e.CopySafe:
526					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # \"copy\" is sound here and much faster\n", e.Name)
527				default:
528					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # copy/link unsupported: %s\n", e.Name, e.Hazard)
529				}
530			}
531		} else {
532			b.WriteString("# No project type detected. Add the commands a fresh checkout needs:\n")
533			b.WriteString("# post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
534			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n")
535		}
536	
537		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
538			return err
539		}
540		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "wrote %s\n", config.Contract(path))
541		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Commit it so every machine provisions worktrees the same way.")
542		return nil
543	}
544

17	// Manager creates and removes worktrees according to the configured policy.
18	type Manager struct {
19		Cfg config.Config
20		// Runtime surfaces a new checkout in the multiplexer. May be nil.
21		Runtime runtime.Runtime
22		Log     io.Writer
23	}
24	
25	// CreateRequest describes one worktree to create.
26	type CreateRequest struct {
27		// RepoPath is the main checkout that owns the worktree.
28		RepoPath string
29		// RepoName is used in the path template and as the session label.
30		RepoName string
31		// Branch is the change stream. Created from Base when it does not exist.
32		Branch string
33		// Base is the ref a new branch starts from.
34		//
35		// Passing this explicitly matters more than it looks: without a base, git
36		// branches from the current HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on
37		// feature/A silently inherits feature/A's commits.
38		Base string
39		// Category feeds the path template.
40		Category string
41		// Path overrides the templated location entirely.
42		Path string
43		// Label names the runtime session.
44		Label string
45		// NoProvision skips dependency install and gitignored-file copying.
46		NoProvision bool
47		// NoRuntime skips surfacing the checkout in the multiplexer.
48		NoRuntime bool
49		// Focus opens the runtime session focused.
50		Focus bool
51	}
52	
53	// CreateResult reports what was created.
54	type CreateResult struct {
55		Path          string
56		Branch        string
57		BranchCreated bool
58		Provision     Result
59		RuntimeHandle string
60		RuntimeName   string
61	}
62	
63	// ErrExists reports a worktree that is already checked out for that branch.
64	type ErrExists struct {
65		Branch string
66		Path   string
67	}
68	
69	func (e *ErrExists) Error() string {
70		return fmt.Sprintf("branch %s is already checked out at %s", e.Branch, e.Path)
71	}
72	
73	func (m *Manager) logf(format string, args ...any) {
74		if m.Log != nil {
75			fmt.Fprintf(m.Log, format+"\n", args...)
76		}
77	}
78	
79	// Create adds a linked worktree, provisions it and surfaces it in the runtime.
80	func (m *Manager) Create(ctx context.Context, req CreateRequest) (*CreateResult, error) {
81		if req.Branch == "" {
82			return nil, errors.New("branch is required")
83		}
84		repo, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, req.RepoPath)
85		if err != nil {
86			return nil, err
87		}
88		// Always operate from the main checkout: creating a worktree from inside
89		// another worktree works, but the relative paths and the base ref get
90		// confusing fast.
91		repoPath := repo.MainRoot
92		if req.RepoName == "" {
93			req.RepoName = repo.Name
94		}
95	
96		// Git refuses to check one branch out twice, so an existing worktree for
97		// this branch is a reuse, not an error the user needs to resolve.
98		if existing, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch); err == nil && ok {
99			return nil, &ErrExists{Branch: req.Branch, Path: existing.Path}
100		}
101	
102		path := req.Path
103		if path == "" {
104			path, err = m.Cfg.WorktreePathFor(req.RepoName, repoPath, req.Branch, req.Category)
105			if err != nil {
106				return nil, err
107			}
108		} else {
109			path = config.Expand(path)
110		}
111		if err := m.checkTarget(path, repoPath); err != nil {
112			return nil, err
113		}
114	
115		base := req.Base
116		branchExisted := gitx.BranchExists(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch)
117		if !branchExisted {
118			if base == "" {
119				base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
120			}
121			if base != "" && !gitx.RefExists(ctx, repoPath, base) {
122				return nil, fmt.Errorf("base ref %q does not exist in %s", base, repoPath)
123			}
124		}
125	
126		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
127			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create worktree parent: %w", err)
128		}
129		if err := gitx.AddWorktree(ctx, repoPath, path, req.Branch, base); err != nil {
130			return nil, err
131		}
132		m.logf("worktree %s -> %s", req.Branch, config.Contract(path))
133	
134		res := &CreateResult{Path: path, Branch: req.Branch, BranchCreated: !branchExisted}
135	
136		if !req.NoProvision {
137			// SettingsFor folds in the repo's own .dev.toml, so a project can pin
138			// its setup where a teammate on another machine picks it up too.
139			p := &Provisioner{
140				Settings: SettingsFor(m.Cfg, repoPath),
141				Timeout:  m.Cfg.Worktree.ProvisionTimeout.Duration,
142				Log:      m.Log,
143			}
144			pr, err := p.Provision(ctx, repoPath, path)
145			if err != nil {
146				// The checkout exists and is usable; provisioning is best-effort.
147				m.logf("warning: provisioning: %v", err)
148			}
149			res.Provision = pr
150		}
151	
152		if !req.NoRuntime && m.Runtime != nil {
153			label := req.Label
154			if label == "" {
155				label = req.RepoName + "/" + req.Branch
156			}
157			handle, err := m.surface(ctx, path, label)
158			if err != nil {
159				m.logf("warning: could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
160			} else if m.Runtime.Name() != "none" {
161				res.RuntimeHandle, res.RuntimeName = handle, m.Runtime.Name()
162			}
163		}
164		return res, nil
165	}
166	
167	// surface registers the checkout with the runtime. When the backend
168	// understands git worktrees it is asked to open it as one, which is what makes
169	// the checkout appear grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
170	// ahead/behind row rather than as an unrelated directory.
171	func (m *Manager) surface(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error) {
172		if wo, ok := m.Runtime.(runtime.WorktreeOpener); ok {
173			return wo.OpenWorktree(ctx, path, label)
174		}
175		return m.Runtime.Open(ctx, path, label)
176	}
177	
178	// checkTarget refuses locations that would cause trouble later.
179	func (m *Manager) checkTarget(path, repoPath string) error {
180		if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
181			if !info.IsDir() {
182				return fmt.Errorf("%s exists and is not a directory", path)
183			}
184			entries, err := os.ReadDir(path)
185			if err != nil {
186				return err
187			}
188			if len(entries) > 0 {
189				return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists and is not empty", config.Contract(path))
190			}
191		}
192		// A worktree nested inside another checkout means every indexer, file
193		// watcher and ripgrep run in the outer repo sees a second copy of the
194		// tree. dev keeps checkouts as siblings under the worktree root instead.
195		if path == repoPath || strings.HasPrefix(path, repoPath+string(filepath.Separator)) {
196			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to create a worktree inside the repository (%s); "+
197				"set paths.worktree_path to a location outside %s",
198				config.Contract(path), config.Contract(repoPath))
199		}
200		return nil
201	}
202	
203	// RemoveRequest describes a worktree removal.
204	type RemoveRequest struct {
205		RepoPath string
206		Path     string
207		// Force allows removing a checkout with uncommitted changes. dev never
208		// sets this on its own: losing uncommitted work is exactly the outcome the
209		// tool exists to prevent.
210		Force bool
211		// RuntimeHandle is closed before the checkout is removed, so the
212		// multiplexer is not left pointing at a deleted directory.
213		RuntimeHandle string
214	}
215	
216	// Remove deletes a worktree checkout. It never deletes the branch — that stays
217	// a separate, explicit decision, matching git's own separation.
218	func (m *Manager) Remove(ctx context.Context, req RemoveRequest) error {
219		if req.RuntimeHandle != "" && m.Runtime != nil {
220			if err := m.Runtime.Close(ctx, req.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
221				m.logf("warning: could not close runtime session %s: %v", req.RuntimeHandle, err)
222			}
223		}
224		if _, err := os.Stat(req.Path); errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
225			// The directory is already gone; clear git's administrative entry.
226			return gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, req.RepoPath)
227		}
228		if err := gitx.RemoveWorktree(ctx, req.RepoPath, req.Path, req.Force); err != nil {
229			return err
230		}
231		m.logf("removed worktree %s", config.Contract(req.Path))
232		return nil
233	}
234	
235	// DirtyCheck reports whether a checkout has uncommitted work, so callers can
236	// refuse to remove it without an explicit --force.
237	func DirtyCheck(ctx context.Context, path string) (bool, gitx.Status, error) {
238		st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, path)
239		if err != nil {
240			return false, st, err
241		}
242		return st.Dirty(), st, nil
243	}

1	package wt
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"os"
7		"path/filepath"
8		"strings"
9	
10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
11		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
12	)
13	
14	// StepKind is what a provisioning step does.
15	type StepKind string
16	
17	const (
18		// StepCopyFile copies one gitignored file into the new checkout.
19		StepCopyFile StepKind = "copy"
20		// StepCopyDir duplicates a dependency directory.
21		StepCopyDir StepKind = "copy-dir"
22		// StepLinkDir symlinks a directory so both checkouts share it.
23		StepLinkDir StepKind = "link"
24		// StepRun executes a shell command in the new checkout.
25		StepRun StepKind = "run"
26	)
27	
28	// Step is one action in a provisioning plan.
29	type Step struct {
30		Kind StepKind
31		// What is the path or command the step acts on.
32		What string
33		// Why explains the step in one line, for `dev wt plan`.
34		Why string
35		// Ecosystem names the language this step belongs to, empty for the
36		// file-copying steps that belong to no ecosystem.
37		Ecosystem string
38		// Skipped marks a step that will not run, with Why holding the reason.
39		Skipped bool
40	}
41	
42	// Plan is everything provisioning would do to a new worktree of a repository,
43	// computed without touching anything.
44	//
45	// Making this inspectable matters more than it looks: a worktree that comes up
46	// broken is the single most common reason people stop using worktrees at all,
47	// and "what will this actually do" is not answerable from the config alone —
48	// it depends on which lockfiles exist, which tools are installed, and which
49	// files are genuinely gitignored.
50	type Plan struct {
51		RepoPath   string
52		Ecosystems []Ecosystem
53		Steps      []Step
54		// Warnings are problems that will not stop provisioning but will surprise
55		// someone: an unsound strategy that was downgraded, a missing tool.
56		Warnings []string
57	}
58	
59	// Runnable returns the steps that will actually execute.
60	func (p Plan) Runnable() []Step {
61		var out []Step
62		for _, s := range p.Steps {
63			if !s.Skipped {
64				out = append(out, s)
65			}
66		}
67		return out
68	}
69	
70	// Empty reports a plan that would do nothing at all.
71	func (p Plan) Empty() bool { return len(p.Runnable()) == 0 }
72	
73	// Settings are the provisioning inputs, resolved from global config and any
74	// per-repo .dev.toml.
75	type Settings struct {
76		Include    []string
77		Link       []string
78		Cmds       config.PostCreate
79		Strategy   Strategy
80		Strategies map[string]string
81	}
82	
83	// SettingsFor resolves the effective provisioning settings for a repository.
84	func SettingsFor(cfg config.Config, repoPath string) Settings {
85		s := Settings{
86			Include:    cfg.Worktree.Include,
87			Link:       cfg.Worktree.Link,
88			Cmds:       cfg.Worktree.PostCreate,
89			Strategy:   Reinstall,
90			Strategies: map[string]string{},
91		}
92		if v, ok := ParseStrategy(cfg.Worktree.Strategy); ok {
93			s.Strategy = v
94		}
95		for k, v := range cfg.Worktree.Strategies {
96			s.Strategies[k] = v
97		}
98		if o, ok := LoadRepoOverride(repoPath); ok {
99			if len(o.Worktree.Include) > 0 {
100				s.Include = o.Worktree.Include
101			}
102			if len(o.Worktree.Link) > 0 {
103				s.Link = o.Worktree.Link
104			}
105			if o.Worktree.PostCreate != nil {
106				s.Cmds = *o.Worktree.PostCreate
107			}
108			if o.Worktree.Strategy != "" {
109				// Keep an invalid value so strategyFor can report it in the plan
110				// instead of silently turning a repo-local typo into reinstall.
111				s.Strategy = Strategy(o.Worktree.Strategy)
112			}
113			for k, v := range o.Worktree.Strategies {
114				s.Strategies[k] = v
115			}
116		}
117		return s
118	}
119	
120	// strategyFor resolves the strategy for one ecosystem, narrowing to something
121	// sound and recording why when it has to.
122	func (s Settings) strategyFor(e Ecosystem) (Strategy, string) {
123		want := s.Strategy
124		if _, ok := ParseStrategy(string(want)); !ok {
125			return Reinstall, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %q is not a strategy (want %s), using reinstall",
126				e.Name, want, joinStrategies())
127		}
128		if v, ok := s.Strategies[e.Name]; ok {
129			if parsed, ok := ParseStrategy(v); ok {
130				want = parsed
131			} else {
132				return Reinstall, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %q is not a strategy (want %s), using reinstall",
133					e.Name, v, joinStrategies())
134			}
135		}
136		// An ecosystem with no dependency directory has nothing to copy or share,
137		// so those strategies collapse to reinstalling — which for a global cache
138		// is nearly free anyway.
139		if len(e.DepDirs) == 0 && (want == Copy || want == Link) {
140			return Reinstall, ""
141		}
142		if ok, hazard := e.SupportsStrategy(want); !ok {
143			return Reinstall, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s is unsound here — %s; using reinstall instead",
144				e.Name, want, hazard)
145		}
146		return want, ""
147	}
148	
149	func joinStrategies() string {
150		parts := make([]string, len(Strategies))
151		for i, s := range Strategies {
152			parts[i] = string(s)
153		}
154		return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
155	}
156	
157	// BuildPlan computes what provisioning a new worktree of repoPath would do.
158	// It reads the filesystem and asks git which files are ignored, but changes
159	// nothing.
160	func BuildPlan(ctx context.Context, set Settings, repoPath string) Plan {
161		p := Plan{RepoPath: repoPath, Ecosystems: DetectEcosystems(repoPath)}
162	
163		// Gitignored files to carry over.
164		if files, err := ignoredMatching(ctx, repoPath, set.Include); err != nil {
165			p.Warnings = append(p.Warnings, "could not list ignored files: "+err.Error())
166		} else {
167			for _, rel := range files {
168				info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(repoPath, rel))
169				if err != nil {
170					continue
171				}
172				if info.IsDir() {
173					continue // directories belong to `link`, not `include`
174				}
175				p.Steps = append(p.Steps, Step{
176					Kind: StepCopyFile, What: rel,
177					Why: "gitignored, so the checkout would not have it",
178				})
179			}
180		}
181	
182		// Explicit symlinks, which are always the user's own decision.
183		for _, rel := range set.Link {
184			step := Step{Kind: StepLinkDir, What: rel, Why: "configured in worktree.link"}
185			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(repoPath, rel)); err != nil {
186				step.Skipped, step.Why = true, "not present in the source checkout"
187			}
188			p.Steps = append(p.Steps, step)
189		}
190	
191		// Dependencies, per ecosystem.
192		//
193		// The strategy and post_create are separate axes. A strategy says how a
194		// dependency directory arrives; post_create says what commands run. So an
195		// explicit command list replaces the *derived install commands* but still
196		// leaves copy and link in effect — a project that bootstraps with `make
197		// setup` may still want its node_modules copied rather than rebuilt.
198		explicit := !set.Cmds.Auto
199		for _, e := range p.Ecosystems {
200			strategy, warn := set.strategyFor(e)
201			if warn != "" {
202				p.Warnings = append(p.Warnings, warn)
203			}
204	
205			switch strategy {
206			case Copy, Link:
207				kind, verb := StepCopyDir, "copied"
208				if strategy == Link {
209					kind, verb = StepLinkDir, "shared"
210				}
211				for _, dir := range e.DepDirs {
212					step := Step{
213						Kind: kind, What: dir, Ecosystem: e.Name,
214						Why: fmt.Sprintf("%s dependencies, %s instead of reinstalling", e.Manager, verb),
215					}
216					if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(repoPath, dir)); err != nil {
217						step.Skipped = true
218						step.Why = "not present in the source checkout — nothing to " + string(strategy)
219					}
220					p.Steps = append(p.Steps, step)
221				}
222	
223			case Skip:
224				if explicit {
225					continue
226				}
227				p.Steps = append(p.Steps, Step{
228					Kind: StepRun, What: e.Install, Ecosystem: e.Name,
229					Why: "strategy is skip", Skipped: true,
230				})
231	
232			default: // Reinstall
233				if explicit {
234					continue // the configured command list replaces this
235				}
236				step := Step{
237					Kind: StepRun, What: e.Install, Ecosystem: e.Name,
238					Why: e.Marker + " detected",
239				}
240				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
241					step.Skipped = true
242					step.Why = e.Tool + " is not installed on this machine"
243					p.Warnings = append(p.Warnings,
244						fmt.Sprintf("%s needs %s, which is not installed — worktrees will come up without its dependencies",
245							e.Name, e.Tool))
246				}
247				p.Steps = append(p.Steps, step)
248			}
249		}
250	
251		// An explicit command list, when configured.
252		if explicit {
253			for _, c := range set.Cmds.Commands {
254				p.Steps = append(p.Steps, Step{Kind: StepRun, What: c, Why: "configured in worktree.post_create"})
255			}
256		}
257		return p
258	}
259	
260	// ignoredMatching asks git which of the patterns name real, ignored files.
261	//
262	// Using git rather than matching by hand means .gitignore semantics —
263	// negations, directory rules, nested ignore files — are exactly right, and
264	// that a *tracked* file matching a pattern is never returned. A tracked file
265	// is already in the new checkout on the correct branch; copying the source
266	// branch's version over it would be wrong.
267	func ignoredMatching(ctx context.Context, src string, patterns []string) ([]string, error) {
268		if len(patterns) == 0 {
269			return nil, nil
270		}
271		args := []string{"ls-files", "--others", "--ignored", "--exclude-standard", "-z", "--"}
272		args = append(args, patterns...)
273		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, src, args...)
274		if err != nil {
275			return nil, err
276		}
277		var rels []string
278		for _, f := range strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(out, "\x00"), "\x00") {
279			if f != "" {
280				rels = append(rels, f)
281			}
282		}
283		return rels, nil
284	}
285

1	// Package wt creates, provisions and removes the linked worktrees dev owns.
2	//
3	// Ownership, stated once so agents and humans stop improvising: dev owns every
4	// worktree a person might come back to tomorrow — features, fixes, experiments,
5	// cross-machine handoffs — and places them at the configured path template.
6	// Claude Code's `.claude/worktrees/` stays for turn-scoped subagent isolation
7	// that dies with the turn. dev never calls `herdr worktree create`, because
8	// the path policy has to hold on machines without herdr; it creates the
9	// worktree with git and asks herdr only to *open* it.
10	package wt
11	
12	import (
13		"bufio"
14		"context"
15		"errors"
16		"fmt"
17		"io"
18		"os"
19		"os/exec"
20		"path/filepath"
21		"time"
22	)
23	
24	// Provisioner brings a fresh checkout up to a working state.
25	//
26	// A worktree is a clean checkout: no node_modules, no .venv, and none of the
27	// gitignored env files the project needs. Without this step every new worktree
28	// starts broken, which is the commonest reason people give up on worktrees.
29	type Provisioner struct {
30		Settings Settings
31		Timeout  time.Duration
32		// Log receives progress lines; nil discards them.
33		Log io.Writer
34	}
35	
36	// Result records what provisioning did, so callers can report it honestly.
37	type Result struct {
38		Copied  []string
39		Linked  []string
40		Ran     []string
41		Skipped []string
42		// Failures are non-fatal: a failed `npm ci` leaves a usable checkout the
43		// user can fix by hand, so it is reported rather than rolled back.
44		Failures []error
45	}
46	
47	func (p *Provisioner) logf(format string, args ...any) {
48		if p.Log != nil {
49			fmt.Fprintf(p.Log, format+"\n", args...)
50		}
51	}
52	
53	// Provision brings dst up to a working state, using src as the source of
54	// gitignored files and any copied dependency trees.
55	func (p *Provisioner) Provision(ctx context.Context, src, dst string) (Result, error) {
56		plan := BuildPlan(ctx, p.Settings, src)
57		return p.Apply(ctx, plan, src, dst)
58	}
59	
60	// Apply executes a plan. Splitting this from BuildPlan is what lets
61	// `dev wt plan` show exactly what would happen without doing any of it.
62	func (p *Provisioner) Apply(ctx context.Context, plan Plan, src, dst string) (Result, error) {
63		var res Result
64		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
65			p.logf("warning: %s", w)
66		}
67	
68		for _, step := range plan.Steps {
69			if step.Skipped {
70				res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, step.What+" ("+step.Why+")")
71				continue
72			}
73			switch step.Kind {
74			case StepCopyFile:
75				if err := p.copyFileStep(src, dst, step.What); err != nil {
76					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, err)
77					continue
78				}
79				res.Copied = append(res.Copied, step.What)
80				p.logf("copied %s", step.What)
81	
82			case StepCopyDir:
83				from, to := filepath.Join(src, step.What), filepath.Join(dst, step.What)
84				if _, err := os.Lstat(to); err == nil {
85					res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, step.What+" (already present)")
86					continue
87				}
88				p.logf("copying %s …", step.What)
89				if err := copyTree(from, to); err != nil {
90					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, fmt.Errorf("copy %s: %w", step.What, err))
91					continue
92				}
93				res.Copied = append(res.Copied, step.What+"/")
94				p.logf("copied %s", step.What)
95	
96			case StepLinkDir:
97				if err := p.linkStep(src, dst, step.What); err != nil {
98					if errors.Is(err, errAlreadyPresent) {
99						res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, step.What+" (already present)")
100						continue
101					}
102					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, err)
103					continue
104				}
105				res.Linked = append(res.Linked, step.What)
106				p.logf("linked %s", step.What)
107	
108			case StepRun:
109				p.logf("running: %s", step.What)
110				if err := p.runShell(ctx, dst, step.What); err != nil {
111					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, err)
112					continue
113				}
114				res.Ran = append(res.Ran, step.What)
115			}
116		}
117		return res, nil
118	}
119	
120	var errAlreadyPresent = errors.New("already present")
121	
122	func (p *Provisioner) copyFileStep(src, dst, rel string) error {
123		from, to := filepath.Join(src, rel), filepath.Join(dst, rel)
124		info, err := os.Lstat(from)
125		if err != nil {
126			return nil // vanished between planning and applying; nothing to do
127		}
128		if _, err := os.Stat(to); err == nil {
129			return nil // never clobber what the checkout already has
130		}
131		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(to), 0o755); err != nil {
132			return err
133		}
134		if err := copyFile(from, to, info.Mode()); err != nil {
135			return fmt.Errorf("copy %s: %w", rel, err)
136		}
137		return nil
138	}
139	
140	func (p *Provisioner) linkStep(src, dst, rel string) error {
141		target, link := filepath.Join(src, rel), filepath.Join(dst, rel)
142		if _, err := os.Stat(target); err != nil {
143			return fmt.Errorf("link %s: not present in the source checkout", rel)
144		}
145		if _, err := os.Lstat(link); err == nil {
146			return errAlreadyPresent
147		}
148		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(link), 0o755); err != nil {
149			return err
150		}
151		if err := os.Symlink(target, link); err != nil {
152			return fmt.Errorf("link %s: %w", rel, err)
153		}
154		return nil
155	}
156	
157	func (p *Provisioner) runShell(ctx context.Context, dir, command string) error {
158		timeout := p.Timeout
159		if timeout <= 0 {
160			timeout = 10 * time.Minute
161		}
162		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
163		defer cancel()
164	
165		shell := os.Getenv("SHELL")
166		if shell == "" {
167			shell = "/bin/sh"
168		}
169		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, shell, "-c", command)
170		cmd.Dir = dir
171		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = p.Log, p.Log
172		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
173			if ctx.Err() == context.DeadlineExceeded {
174				return fmt.Errorf("post_create %q timed out after %s", command, timeout)
175			}
176			return fmt.Errorf("post_create %q: %w", command, err)
177		}
178		return nil
179	}
180	
181	func copyFile(from, to string, mode os.FileMode) error {
182		in, err := os.Open(from)
183		if err != nil {
184			return err
185		}
186		defer in.Close()
187		out, err := os.OpenFile(to, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, mode.Perm())
188		if err != nil {
189			return err
190		}
191		defer out.Close()
192		w := bufio.NewWriter(out)
193		if _, err := io.Copy(w, in); err != nil {
194			return err
195		}
196		return w.Flush()
197	}
198	
199	// copyTree duplicates a directory.
200	//
201	// Symlinks are recreated rather than followed: a pnpm node_modules is a farm
202	// of links into a global store, and dereferencing them would turn a 200MB
203	// copy into several gigabytes of duplicated packages.
204	func copyTree(from, to string) error {
205		return filepath.Walk(from, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, err error) error {
206			if err != nil {
207				return err
208			}
209			rel, err := filepath.Rel(from, path)
210			if err != nil {
211				return err
212			}
213			target := filepath.Join(to, rel)
214	
215			switch {
216			case info.IsDir():
217				return os.MkdirAll(target, info.Mode().Perm())
218			case info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0:
219				dest, err := os.Readlink(path)
220				if err != nil {
221					return err
222				}
223				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(target), 0o755); err != nil {
224					return err
225				}
226				os.Remove(target)
227				return os.Symlink(dest, target)
228			case info.Mode().IsRegular():
229				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(target), 0o755); err != nil {
230					return err
231				}
232				return copyFile(path, target, info.Mode())
233			}
234			return nil // sockets, devices and the like have no place in a checkout
235		})
236	}

1	package wt

3	import (
4		"os"

11	// RepoOverride is a per-repository provisioning override, committed at the
12	// repo root as .dev.toml. Global config sets a sensible default for every
13	// project; a repo that needs something specific (a Makefile bootstrap target,
14	// an extra env file) says so next to its code, where a teammate on another
15	// machine picks it up automatically.
16	//
17	//	# .dev.toml
18	//	[worktree]
19	//	include     = [".env", "config/local.json"]
20	//	post_create = ["make bootstrap"]
21	//
22	//	[worktree.strategies]
23	//	node = "copy"     # node_modules copies soundly; reinstalling is slow here
24	type RepoOverride struct {
25		Worktree struct {
26			Include    []string           `toml:"include"`
27			Link       []string           `toml:"link"`
28			PostCreate *config.PostCreate `toml:"post_create"`
29			Strategy   string             `toml:"strategy"`
30			Strategies map[string]string  `toml:"strategies"`
31		} `toml:"worktree"`
32	}
33	
34	// OverrideFilename is the per-repo config file dev looks for.
35	const OverrideFilename = ".dev.toml"
36	
37	// LoadRepoOverride reads <repoPath>/.dev.toml if present. A malformed file is
38	// reported as absent rather than fatal: a broken override in someone else's
39	// repo must not stop you creating a worktree.
40	func LoadRepoOverride(repoPath string) (RepoOverride, bool) {
41		path := filepath.Join(repoPath, OverrideFilename)
42		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err != nil {
43			return RepoOverride{}, false
44		}
45		var o RepoOverride
46		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &o); err != nil {
47			return RepoOverride{}, false
48		}
49		return o, true
50	}
51	
52	// applyOverride replaces only the fields the repo actually set, so a repo that
53	// pins post_create still inherits the user's global include list.
54

1	// Package gitx wraps the git porcelain commands dev depends on. Every helper
2	// shells out to git rather than linking a Go implementation: git is already a
3	// hard dependency, its porcelain formats are stable and documented, and this
4	// keeps dev's behaviour identical to what the user sees when they run the same
5	// command by hand.
6	package gitx
7	
8	import (
9		"bytes"
10		"context"
11		"errors"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotARepo is returned when a directory is not inside a git working tree.
18	var ErrNotARepo = errors.New("not a git repository")
19	
20	// Error carries the failing command and git's own stderr, which is almost
21	// always more useful than the exit status alone.
22	type Error struct {
23		Args   []string
24		Dir    string
25		Stderr string
26		Err    error
27	}
28	
29	func (e *Error) Error() string {
30		msg := strings.TrimSpace(e.Stderr)
31		if msg == "" {
32			msg = e.Err.Error()
33		}
34		return fmt.Sprintf("git %s: %s", strings.Join(e.Args, " "), msg)
35	}
36	
37	func (e *Error) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
38	
39	// run executes git in dir and returns trimmed stdout.
40	func run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
41		// -c core.quotepath=false keeps non-ASCII paths readable rather than
42		// octal-escaped, which matters for the Chinese-named files in these repos.
43		full := append([]string{"-c", "core.quotepath=false"}, args...)
44		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
45		cmd.Dir = dir
46		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
47		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
48		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
49		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
50			gerr := &Error{Args: args, Dir: dir, Stderr: stderr.String(), Err: err}
51			if strings.Contains(gerr.Stderr, "not a git repository") {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", dir, ErrNotARepo)
53			}
54			return "", gerr
55		}
56		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
57	}
58	
59	// Run executes an arbitrary git command in dir. Exported for the few callers
60	// (park's wip commit, done's merge) that need a one-off command.
61	func Run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
62		return run(ctx, dir, args...)
63	}
64	
65	// lines splits git output into non-empty lines.
66	func lines(s string) []string {
67		if s == "" {
68			return nil
69		}
70		out := strings.Split(s, "\n")
71		filtered := out[:0]
72		for _, l := range out {
73			if l != "" {
74				filtered = append(filtered, l)
75			}
76		}
77		return filtered
78	}
79	
80	// nulLines splits NUL-delimited git output (-z forms).
81	func nulLines(s string) []string {
82		s = strings.TrimRight(s, "\x00")
83		if s == "" {
84			return nil
85		}
86		return strings.Split(s, "\x00")
87	}
88

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
10	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
11	type Repo struct {
12		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
13		Root string
14		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
15		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
16		GitCommonDir string
17		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
18		Name string
19		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
20		// the main checkout.
21		IsLinkedWorktree bool
22		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
23		MainRoot string
24		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
25		Bare bool
26	}
27	
28	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
29	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
30	
31	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
32	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
33		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
34		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
35		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
36			"rev-parse",
37			"--path-format=absolute",
38			"--show-toplevel",
39			"--git-common-dir",
40			"--is-bare-repository",
41		)
42		if err != nil {
43			return Repo{}, err
44		}
45		f := lines(out)
46		r := Repo{}
47		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
48		switch len(f) {
49		case 3:
50			r.Root = f[0]
51			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
52			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
53		case 2:
54			r.GitCommonDir = f[0]
55			r.Bare = f[1] == "true"
56		default:
57			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
58		}
59	
60		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
61		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
62		if r.Bare {
63			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
64		} else {
65			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
66		}
67		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.Root != r.MainRoot
68		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
69		if r.Bare {
70			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
71			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
72			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
73				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
74			}
75		}
76		return r, nil
77	}
78	
79	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
80	// a full Discover.
81	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
82		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
83		return err == nil
84	}
85	
86	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
87	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
88	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
89	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
90	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
91		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
92			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
93				return b
94			}
95		}
96		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
97			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
98				return cand
99			}
100		}
101		return ""
102	}
103	
104	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
105	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
106		if name == "" {
107			name = "origin"
108		}
109		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
110		if err != nil {
111			return ""
112		}
113		return out
114	}

30		Deleted  int `json:"deleted"`

34		Conflicted int `json:"conflicted"`

36	
37	// Dirty reports uncommitted work of any kind.
38	func (s Status) Dirty() bool { return s.Changed > 0 }
39	
40	// Published reports whether the branch has an upstream at all.
41	func (s Status) Published() bool { return s.Upstream != "" }
42	
43	// Synced reports a branch that is published and exactly level with upstream.
44	func (s Status) Synced() bool { return s.Published() && s.Ahead == 0 && s.Behind == 0 }
45	
46	// Summary renders the compact, starship-like column used throughout dev:
47	//
48	//	⇕⇡2⇣1 =1 +3 !2 ?4
49	//
50	// Divergence, conflicts, staged, unstaged and untracked paths remain separate
51	// so "dirty" says how and by how much, rather than collapsing to one ●.
52	func (s Status) Summary() string {
53		var parts []string
54		switch {
55		case s.Ahead > 0 && s.Behind > 0:
56			parts = append(parts, "⇕⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead)+"⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
57		case s.Ahead > 0:
58			parts = append(parts, "⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead))
59		case s.Behind > 0:
60			parts = append(parts, "⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
61		}
62		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
63			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted))
64		}
65		if s.Staged > 0 {
66			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged))
67		}
68		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
69			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged))
70		}
71		if s.Untracked > 0 {
72			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked))
73		}
74		if len(parts) == 0 {
75			if !s.Published() {
76				return "local"
77			}
78			return "clean"
79		}
80		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
81	}

83	// Breakdown renders the detailed change count shown by `dev status` and the
84	// TUI detail pane. Changed is the unique-path total; staged and unstaged may
85	// overlap, which is stated by presenting them as categories rather than a sum.
86	func (s Status) Breakdown() string {
87		if s.Changed == 0 {
88			return "0 changed paths"
89		}
90		var parts []string
91		if s.Staged > 0 {
92			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged)+" staged")

95			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged)+" unstaged")
96		}
97		if s.Untracked > 0 {
98			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked)+" untracked")
99		}
100		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
101			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted)+" conflicted")
102		}
103		return strconv.Itoa(s.Changed) + " changed paths (" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")"

107	func (s Status) TypeBreakdown() string {
108		var parts []string
109		for _, item := range []struct {
110			n    int
111			name string
112		}{
113			{s.Added, "added"}, {s.Modified, "modified"}, {s.Deleted, "deleted"},
114			{s.Renamed, "renamed/copied"},
115		} {
116			if item.n > 0 {
117				parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(item.n)+" "+item.name)
118			}
119		}
120		return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
121	}
122	
123	// StatusOf reads the porcelain v2 status of the checkout at dir. Porcelain v2
124	// is the documented machine-readable format: it reports branch, upstream and
125	// ahead/behind in the same pass as the file states, so one process gives dev
126	// everything it needs.
127	func StatusOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Status, error) {
128		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=normal", "-z")
129		if err != nil {
130			return Status{}, err
131		}
132		var s Status
133		for _, rec := range nulLines(out) {
134			if rec == "" {
135				continue
136			}
137			switch rec[0] {
138			case '#':
139				parseBranchHeader(rec, &s)
140			case '1', '2':
141				// "1 XY ..." ordinary change, "2 XY ..." rename/copy. X is
142				// staged, Y unstaged. This record is one unique changed path even
143				// when both sides are non-dot.
144				f := strings.Fields(rec)
145				if len(f) < 2 || len(f[1]) < 2 {
146					continue
147				}
148				s.Changed++
149				x, y := f[1][0], f[1][1]
150				if x != '.' {
151					s.Staged++
152				}
153				if y != '.' {
154					s.Unstaged++
155				}
156				classifyChange(x, &s)
157				classifyChange(y, &s)
158			case 'u':
159				s.Changed++
160				s.Conflicted++
161			case '?':
162				s.Changed++
163				s.Untracked++
164			}
165		}
166		return s, nil
167	}
168	
169	func classifyChange(code byte, s *Status) {
170		switch code {
171		case 'A':
172			s.Added++
173		case 'M', 'T':
174			s.Modified++
175		case 'D':
176			s.Deleted++
177		case 'R', 'C':
178			s.Renamed++
179		}
180	}
181	
182	func parseBranchHeader(rec string, s *Status) {
183		f := strings.Fields(rec)
184		if len(f) < 3 {
185			return
186		}
187		switch f[1] {
188		case "branch.head":
189			if f[2] == "(detached)" {
190				s.Detached = true
191			} else {
192				s.Branch = f[2]
193			}
194		case "branch.upstream":
195			s.Upstream = f[2]
196		case "branch.ab":
197			// "# branch.ab +2 -1"
198			if len(f) < 4 {
199				return
200			}
201			s.Ahead, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[2], "+"))
202			s.Behind, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[3], "-"))
203		}
204	}
205	
206	// LastCommit reports the author timestamp of HEAD as a Unix epoch, and the
207	// subject line. Used to age a task in `dev sweep`.
208	func LastCommit(ctx context.Context, dir string) (unix int64, subject string, err error) {
209		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "log", "-1", "--format=%at%x00%s")
210		if err != nil || out == "" {
211			return 0, "", err
212		}
213		ts, subj, _ := strings.Cut(out, "\x00")
214		unix, _ = strconv.ParseInt(ts, 10, 64)
215		return unix, subj, nil
216	}
217	
218	// WipCommit stages everything and records a checkpoint commit.
219	//
220	// A checkpoint commit is deliberately preferred over `git stash`: a stash is
221	// invisible in the log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never
222	// travel to another machine, which is exactly what parking a task needs.
223	func WipCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, message string) (bool, error) {
224		st, err := StatusOf(ctx, dir)
225		if err != nil {
226			return false, err
227		}
228		if !st.Dirty() {
229			return false, nil
230		}
231		if st.Conflicted > 0 {
232			return false, &Error{Args: []string{"commit"}, Dir: dir,
233				Stderr: "checkout has unmerged paths; resolve the conflict before parking"}
234		}
235		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
236			return false, err
237		}
238		if message == "" {
239			message = "wip: checkpoint"
240		}
241		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", message); err != nil {
242			return false, err
243		}
244		return true, nil
245	}

1	package gitx

3	import (
4		"context"

6	)
7	
8	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
9	type Worktree struct {
10		Path string
11		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
12		Head string
13		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
14		Branch   string
15		Detached bool
16		Bare     bool
17		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
18		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
19		Locked         bool
20		LockedReason   string
21		Prunable       bool
22		PrunableReason string
23		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
24		Main bool
25	}
26	
27	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
28	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
29	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
30		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		var (
35			list []Worktree
36			cur  *Worktree
37		)
38		flush := func() {
39			if cur != nil {
40				list = append(list, *cur)
41				cur = nil
42			}
43		}
44		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
45			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
46				flush()
47				continue
48			}
49			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
50			switch key {
51			case "worktree":
52				flush()
53				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
54			case "HEAD":
55				if cur != nil {
56					cur.Head = val
57				}
58			case "branch":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
61				}
62			case "detached":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Detached = true
65				}
66			case "bare":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Bare = true
69				}
70			case "locked":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
73				}
74			case "prunable":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
77				}
78			}
79		}
80		flush()
81		return list, nil
82	}
83	
84	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
85	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
86	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
87		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
88		if err != nil {
89			return Worktree{}, false, err
90		}
91		for _, w := range list {
92			if w.Branch == branch {
93				return w, true, nil
94			}
95		}
96		return Worktree{}, false, nil
97	}
98	
99	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
100	//
101	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
102	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
103	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
104	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
105	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
106		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
107		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
108		if exists {
109			args = append(args, path, branch)
110		} else {
111			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
112			if base != "" {
113				args = append(args, base)
114			}
115		}
116		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
117		return err
118	}
119	
120	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
121	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
122	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
123		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
124		if force {
125			args = append(args, "--force")
126		}
127		args = append(args, path)
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
133	// were deleted behind git's back.
134	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
135		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
136		return err
137	}
138	
139	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
140	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
141		if branch == "" {
142			return false
143		}
144		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
145		return err == nil
146	}
147	
148	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
149	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
150		if ref == "" {
151			return false
152		}
153		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
154		return err == nil
155	}

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
38		Bare bool
39		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
40		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
41		// initialise them.
42		HasGit bool
43	}
44	
45	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
46	func (r Repo) Display() string {
47		if r.Category == "" {
48			return r.Name
49		}
50		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
51	}
52	
53	// Options tunes discovery.
54	type Options struct {
55		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
56		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
57		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
58		MaxDepth int
59		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
60		IncludeNonRepos bool
61	}
62	
63	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
64	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
65	
66	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
67	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
68	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
69		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
70		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
71		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
72		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
73	}

75	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
76	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
77	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
78	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
79		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
80			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
81		}
82		seen := map[string]bool{}
83		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
84		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
85		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
86		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
87		identities := map[string]bool{}
88		var out []Repo
89	
90		for _, root := range roots {
91			info, err := os.Stat(root)
92			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
93				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
94			}
95			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
96	
97			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
98				if err != nil {
99					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
100				}
101				if ctx.Err() != nil {
102					return ctx.Err()
103				}
104				if path == rootClean {
105					return nil
106				}
107				name := d.Name()
108				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
109				isDir := d.IsDir()
110				if isLink {
111					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
112					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
113					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
114					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
115						isDir = info.IsDir()
116					}
117				}
118				if !isDir {
119					return nil
120				}
121				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
122					return filepath.SkipDir
123				}
124	
125				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
126				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
127	
128				if isRepoDir(path) {
129					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
130					if real == "" {
131						real = path
132					}
133					bare := isBareDir(path)
134					identity := real
135					if !bare {
136						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
137							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
138							// project in the repo inventory.
139							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
140								return filepath.SkipDir
141							}
142							identity = g.GitCommonDir
143							real = g.MainRoot
144						}
145					}
146					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
147						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
148						out = append(out, Repo{
149							Name:     name,
150							Path:     path,
151							RealPath: real,
152							Symlink:  isLink,
153							Root:     rootClean,
154							Category: filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
155							Bare:     bare,
156							HasGit:   true,
157						})
158					}
159					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
160					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
161					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
162					return filepath.SkipDir
163				}
164				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
165					return filepath.SkipDir
166				}
167				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
168					if !seen[path] {
169						seen[path] = true
170						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
171					}
172				}
173				return nil
174			})
175			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
176				return out, ctx.Err()
177			}
178		}
179	
180		for i := range out {
181			if out[i].Category == "." {
182				out[i].Category = ""
183			}
184		}
185		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
186			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
187				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
188			}
189			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
190		})
191		return out, nil
192	}
193	
194	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
195	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
196	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
197		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
198			return true
199		}
200		return isBareDir(path)
201	}
202	
203	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
204	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
205		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
206			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
207				return false
208			}
209		}
210		return true
211	}
212	
213	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
214	//
215	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
216	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
217	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
218	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
219		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
220		if err != nil {
221			return Repo{}, nil, err
222		}
223		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
224			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
225				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
226				if real == "" {
227					real = g.MainRoot
228				}
229				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
230				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
231				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
232				return Repo{
233					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
234					Symlink: real != abs, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
235				}, nil, nil
236			}
237		}
238		for _, r := range all {
239			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
240				return r, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
244		var hits []Repo
245		for _, r := range all {
246			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
247				hits = append(hits, r)
248			}
249		}
250		switch len(hits) {
251		case 1:
252			return hits[0], nil, nil
253		case 0:
254			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
255		default:
256			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
257		}
258	}
259	
260	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
261	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
262	
263	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
264	
265	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
266	type AmbiguousError struct {
267		Ref        string
268		Candidates []Repo
269	}
270	
271	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
272		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
273		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
274			names[i] = c.Display()
275		}
276		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
277	}
278

329	// repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.
330	func repoNameFromRef(ref string) string {
331		ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
332		if i := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:"); i >= 0 {
333			return ref[i+1:]
334		}
335		return ref
336	}
