 `./README.md`

```text
1	# dev
2	
3	A thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
4	
5	It exists to stop four things collapsing into one:
6	
7	```
8	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
9	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
10	herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
11	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
12	```
13	
14	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
15	only what git cannot answer — a task's **state**, **owner** and **next
16	action** — as one TOML file per task.
17	
18	## The problem
19	
20	When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
21	working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
22	So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
23	defeats the point of having one.
24	
25	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
26	the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
27	
28	Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
29	the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
30	expected.
31	
32	```
33	$ dev ls
34	   TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
35	🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
36	🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
37	❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
38	```
39	
40	## Install
41	
42	```bash
43	make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
44	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
45	```
46	
47	Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
48	
49	```bash
50	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
51	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
52	```
53	
54	The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
55	working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
56	directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
57	
58	```bash
59	dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
60	```
61	
62	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
63	degrade cleanly when absent.
64	
65	## The lifecycle
66	
67	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
70	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
71	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
72	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
73	
74	```bash
75	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
76	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
77	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
78	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
79	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
80	dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
81	```
82	
83	### The dashboard
84	
85	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens three lists, switched with `tab`:
86	
87	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
88	- **REPOS** — every repository under the scan roots, with its branch, dirty
89	  state, worktree count and per-state task tally, sorted so anything in flight
90	  is at the top. What do I have here.
91	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through the authenticated `gh` and `glab`
92	  CLIs, marked when a local clone exists. What can I open or clone.
93	
94	TASKS and REPOS come from the same code paths as `dev ls` and `dev repo list`,
95	so they cannot disagree. The repo list matters on day one: with forty repositories and
96	no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just be empty.
97	
98	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
99	
100	```
101	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
102	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
103	/          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
104	```
105	
106	`enter` opens the selected row in the runtime. In TASKS, `p` parks and prompts
107	for the next action and `c` edits it; in REPOS, `s` starts a task right there —
108	branch, worktree, session and entry — which is the bridge from "what do I have"
109	to "what am I working on" without leaving the dashboard.
110	
111	**External tools are configured, not fixed.** They run through your shell in
112	the selected row's checkout; the dashboard suspends and redraws when they exit:
113	
114	```toml
115	[[tui.tools]]
116	key  = "L"
117	name = "lazygit"
118	run  = "lazygit"
119	
120	[[tui.tools]]
121	key  = "V"
122	name = "nvim"
123	run  = "nvim ."
124	
125	[[tui.tools]]
126	key  = "B"
127	name = "vibe"
128	run  = "vibe"
129	interactive = true     # load + evaluate aliases/functions after shell rc
130	
131	[[tui.tools]]
132	key  = "P"
133	name = "plans here"
134	run  = "claude-plans-here"
135	interactive = true
136	```
137	
138	`dev config init` writes the defaults out in full rather than leaving them
139	implicit, and `dev tui tools` shows what is bound here and whether each one is
140	actually installed — bindings for missing programs are not offered. A tool
141	cannot take a key the dashboard already uses; dev reports the clash on load.
142	
143	REMOTE loads lazily, so dashboard startup never waits on the network. A private
144	15-minute XDG cache makes later switches instant; `r` refreshes both forges.
145	`/` searches provider, owner/name and description; enter opens a local clone,
146	and `c` confirms before cloning an absent repo into `project_root`. The same
147	inventory is available without the full-screen UI via `dev repo remote [query]`;
148	`--cached` is its instant/offline form.
149	See `dev help tui` for the full key map.
150	
151	Going cold is safe because **the branch is the identity and the directory is a
152	cache**. `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, and `dev resume`
153	rebuilds the checkout from `origin/<branch>`. Once that holds, the local
154	filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished worktrees.
155	
156	## Worktree ownership
157	
158	Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
159	to improvise:
160	
161	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
162	|---|---|---|---|
163	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until `dev done` / `dev sweep` |
164	| Turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | dies with the turn |
165	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
166	
167	**Might you come back tomorrow → `dev`. Dies with this agent turn → Claude
168	Code native.**
169	
170	`dev` does not delegate placement to herdr because the path policy has to hold
171	on machines without herdr. It creates the checkout with plain git and asks
172	herdr only to *open* it — which still surfaces it in the sidebar grouped under
173	its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
174	
175	`dev` refuses to create a worktree inside a repository: a checkout nested in
176	another checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second
177	copy of the tree.
178	
179	### Provisioning
180	
181	A worktree is a clean checkout — no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
182	Without provisioning, every new one starts broken. `dev` copies the gitignored
183	files you list, optionally symlinks heavy directories, and runs a setup
184	command detected from the lockfiles:
185	
186	```toml
187	[worktree]
188	include     = [".env", ".env.local"]   # only files that are ALSO gitignored
189	link        = []                       # opt-in; sharing node_modules is risky
190	post_create = "auto"                   # uv.lock → uv sync, package-lock.json → npm ci, …
191	```
192	
193	**Copy or reinstall?** Reinstalling is always correct but can take minutes;
194	copying is fast but only sound for dependency trees carrying no absolute paths.
195	That is a per-ecosystem fact, not a preference, so dev knows it:
196	
197	```toml
198	[worktree]
199	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
200	
201	[worktree.strategies]
202	node = "copy"               # node_modules copies soundly
203	```
204	
205	Asking to copy a virtualenv is refused with the reason — it bakes its own
206	absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg` and `bin/activate` — and narrowed back to
207	reinstalling rather than silently producing a broken checkout.
208	
209	`dev wt plan` shows exactly what a new worktree of a repository would get:
210	which project types were detected, which tools are missing, and every file and
211	command involved. `dev wt plan --write` seeds a `<repo>/.dev.toml` from it, so
212	a project can commit its own setup and every machine provisions the same way.
213	
214	```
215	$ dev wt plan
216	PROJECT  MANAGER  FROM               DEPENDENCIES  TOOL
217	node     npm      package-lock.json  node_modules  installed
218	python   uv       uv.lock            .venv         installed
219	
220	   ACTION    WHAT          WHY
221	✓  copy      .env          gitignored, so the checkout would not have it
222	✓  copy-dir  node_modules  npm dependencies, copied instead of reinstalling
223	✓  run       uv sync       uv.lock detected
224	```
225	
226	## Other things it does
227	
228	```bash
229	dev repo list                  # every repo under the scan roots, with status
230	dev repo clone owner/name -c Web   # clone into the right place, via gh or glab
231	dev repo sync --all            # fetch + prune, and report what moved
232	
233	dev try redis-streams          # dated scratch directory for an experiment
234	dev graduate redis-streams -c Infra --remote   # promote it into a real project
235	
236	dev gitignore                  # .gitignore from GitHub's templates + the rest
237	dev adopt                      # import existing worktrees/sessions as tasks
238	
239	dev stats --heatmap            # where the time actually went
240	dev help worktrees             # quick-reference pages for the workflow
241	```
242	
243	`dev stats` draws a contribution-style heatmap from two sources: a sampler
244	watching live agent sessions (the only way to count time spent reading and
245	debugging), and git history (which backfills the past and survives losing the
246	database). WakaTime can be imported alongside for editor time.
247	
248	```bash
249	dev stats backfill                          # seed from git history, once
250	dev stats sample --interval 5m              # from cron, every five minutes
251	dev stats import-wakatime                   # optional
252	```
253	
254	## Bootstrapping an existing machine
255	
256	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use: `dev` discovers repositories
257	wherever `scan_roots` point and never requires a particular physical layout.
258	When you want a recursive audit or a curated navigation layer, bootstrap is the
259	explicit path:
260	
261	```bash
262	dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work                    # recursive report, no changes
263	dev bootstrap ~/code --json                       # machine-readable inventory
264	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects           # plan a flat symlink catalog
265	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --apply   # create only the ready links
266	dev bootstrap ~/old --move ~/Projects             # plan physical moves
267	```
268	
269	The scanner classifies canonical checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories
270	and symlink aliases, deduplicating by Git common-directory identity rather than
271	path.
272	
273	**A symlink index is the default recommendation.** It gives a flat,
274	metadata-aware navigation root while every physical repository stays exactly
275	where it was. Put the index first in `scan_roots` and that alias becomes the UI;
276	normal discovery follows direct repo symlinks and deduplicates index + physical
277	paths.
278	
279	Physical move exists, but refuses dirty repos, linked worktrees anywhere in the
280	clone, live sessions, a current shell inside, aliases that would break,
281	occupied destinations and cross-filesystem renames. A plan with any blocked row
282	moves nothing. `--config-out` writes a fresh config for the resulting root
283	without silently rewriting the user's current one. See `dev help bootstrap`.
284	
285	## Adopting work in flight
286	
287	There is nothing to migrate. `dev` discovers repositories wherever your scan
288	roots point and **never moves, renames or deletes anything** you already have.
289	`dev config init` probes the conventional locations — `~/Documents/Program`,
290	`~/src`, `~/code`, a `GHQ_ROOT`, and so on — counts the repositories in each,
291	and writes only the ones that exist:
292	
293	```
294	$ dev config init
295	wrote ~/.config/dev/config.toml
296	
297	Detected:
298	ROOT                 REPOS  ROLE
299	~/Documents/Program  40     scan root, new projects land here
300	~/src                16     scan root
301	```
302	
303	Repositories are discovered; *tasks* are not. `dev adopt` finds the work
304	already in flight — linked worktrees from any tool, live runtime sessions, and
305	local branches ahead of the default branch — and offers to record it. It skips
306	branches already merged, and the turn-scoped worktrees an agent harness cleans
307	up itself:
308	
309	```bash
310	dev adopt            # report only
311	dev adopt --apply    # record as tasks; nothing on disk changes
312	```
313	
314	A worktree you already have somewhere else keeps working exactly as it did —
315	`dev` records the path git reports rather than relocating it. Full detail in
316	`dev help adopting`.
317	
318	## .gitignore
319	
320	```bash
321	dev gitignore                 # detect the languages from the repo's files
322	dev gitignore python node     # or say so explicitly
323	dev gitignore --offline       # cached and bundled templates only
324	```
325	
326	Language sections come from [GitHub's templates](https://github.com/github/gitignore),
327	fetched once and cached. On top of those it adds what no language template
328	covers: the host platform's junk files, editor state, local env files, and the
329	directories coding-agent harnesses create — an agent's linked worktree left
330	untracked makes every `git status` in the main checkout unreadable.
331	
332	Everything it writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
333	block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.
334	
335	## Configuration
336	
337	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`. Write a commented starter with
338	`dev config init`; see the effective settings with `dev config show`; open the
339	actual file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` with either form:
340	
341	```bash
342	dev edit
343	dev config edit
344	DEV_EDITOR=unused dev edit --editor "code --wait"   # explicit override
345	```
346	
347	If the file does not exist, `edit` generates the machine-detected starter first
348	rather than opening an empty file. Resolution is `--editor` → `$VISUAL` →
349	`$EDITOR` → `nvim` → `vim` → `vi`.
350	
351	Every path is configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine —
352	a faster volume, a different naming convention:
353	
354	```toml
355	[paths]
356	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"]
357	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
358	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
359	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"        # point at a git repo to sync it
360	```
361	
362	Template variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`,
363	`host`, `date`. Filters: `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`), `|lower`,
364	`|base`. A typo in a variable name fails at load, not as a directory literally
365	named `{{rep}}`.
366	
367	A flat project layout is already first-class — it needs no migration and no
368	special mode:
369	
370	```toml
371	[paths]
372	scan_roots   = ["~/code"]
373	project_root = "~/code"       # repo new/clone/graduate land at ~/code/<repo>
374	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/wt"
375	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}"
376	```
377	
378	Omit `--category` and canonical repos stay flat. Categories are metadata the
379	user may choose, never a directory structure dev imposes.
380	
381	## Multiple machines
382	
383	Do not sync worktrees or runtime state. Sync branches, and let the remote be
384	the handoff boundary:
385	
386	```bash
387	dev park --cold --push      # on the machine holding the work
388	dev resume <task> --fetch   # on the machine picking it up
389	```
390	
391	`dev` records an owner host per task and refuses to resume someone else's
392	without `--force`. Two machines committing to one branch is the reliable way
393	to produce a conflict here; the ownership check prevents it.
394	
395	For a cross-machine view, `dev ls --json` is a stable contract:
396	
397	```bash
398	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
399	```
400	
401	## The agent skill
402	
403	`dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
404	same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
405	tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
406	reading none.
407	
408	```bash
409	dev skill install    # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
410	dev --skill          # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
411	dev skill sync       # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
412	dev skill sync --check   # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
413	```
414	
415	The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
416	SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
417	worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
418	responsibility.
419	
420	## Development
421	
422	```bash
423	make          # fmt, vet, test, build
424	make test
425	make e2e      # drives the real binary through a full lifecycle in a sandbox
426	make skill-check
427	```
428	
429	Tests build throwaway repositories under `t.TempDir()` via
430	`internal/gitx/gittest`, and the runtime adapters share one contract suite that
431	skips backends not installed on the machine — so the suite is meaningful in CI
432	(where only the null backend exists) and locally (where herdr and tmux do).
433

18	A `tv` channel over `dev ls --json` for fuzzy-picking a task, and an `fzf`

22	### P3 · S — `dev stats` per-repo heatmap
23	`--repo X` currently filters the totals and the combined grid. A dedicated
24	per-repo grid, several stacked, would answer "which project did I move to in
25	March" better than the aggregate does.
26	
27	### P4 · M — Raycast extension
28	`dev ls` and `dev resume` from the launcher. Wants the JSON contract and a
29	stable binary path; nothing else new.
30	
31	## Deliberately not doing
32	
33	### Installing dependencies
34	`dev doctor` reports what is missing and what degrades; it will not install
35	anything. This is the one place where being glue matters most: git, herdr,
36	tmux, gh, glab, lazygit and yazi are all installed by a package manager the
37	user already has opinions about (brew, apt, mise, nix, chezmoi), and a tool
38	that shells out to one of them is guessing. `doctor` naming the missing binary
39	is enough — the user knows how they install things on that machine.
40	
41	Reconsider only if `doctor` grows a case where the *right* command is
42	unambiguous and the user has asked for it.
43	
44	### A second git database
45	Anything derivable from git is derived live, every run. The registry holds
46	state, owner, next action and a note — nothing else. The moment it caches a
47	branch name or an ahead/behind count, it can disagree with git, and a tool that
48	disagrees with git about git is worse than no tool.
49	
50	### Syncing runtime state between machines
51	Each host runs its own multiplexer. What crosses machines is branches, through
52	the remote, plus the task registry if `state_dir` is a git repo. Syncing
53	sessions would mean reconciling two live terminal states, which is a much
54	harder problem than the one this tool has.
55	
56	### Owning the worktree path on machines with herdr
57	`herdr worktree create` would be less code, but the path policy has to hold
58	where herdr is not installed. dev creates the checkout with git and asks herdr
59	only to open it. See `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/worktree-ownership.md`.

```text
1	# dev-cli — a thin glue layer over Git, worktrees, forges, and agent runtimes
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	This machine currently has **31 open Herdr workspaces**, 39 repos under
6	`~/Documents/Program`, and 19 experiments in `~/src/tries`. The Herdr sidebar is
7	being used as a *memory of what I'm working on*, so nothing ever gets closed —
8	Herdr is forced to be both "live runtime" and "WIP inventory" at once. Meanwhile
9	worktrees are confusing: Claude Code has a native `--worktree`, Herdr has
10	`herdr worktree create`, Worktrunk exists, and it's unclear who owns what or how
11	a new worktree gets a working environment (`uv sync`, `npm ci`, `.env`).
12	
13	`dev` fixes this by being **glue, not a second Git database**:
14	
15	```
16	Git remote      durable code state       (source of truth)
17	git worktree    disposable local checkout
18	Herdr / tmux    per-host live runtime
19	dev             human intent + inventory + navigation + one worktree policy
20	```
21	
22	Everything derivable from Git or the runtime is **derived live**. `dev` persists
23	only what Git cannot answer: `state`, `next`, `owner`, `note`.
24	
25	Outcome: closing a Herdr workspace stops feeling like abandoning a task, so the
26	sidebar can shrink back to an actual working set.
27	
28	---
29	
30	## 1. Doctrine the tool encodes
31	
32	### 1.1 Task state machine
33	
34	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
35	|---|---|---|---|
36	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | Herdr space open | working on it now |
37	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | space **closed** | back within days |
38	| ❄️ `cold` | committed + pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused; reconstructible anywhere |
39	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | branch + worktree + entry deleted |
40	
41	`dev park` = warm/cold transition. **Closing a space ≠ abandoning a task.**
42	
43	### 1.2 Isolation boundary
44	
45	> **Worktree per change stream, pane per agent.** Not one worktree per agent.
46	
47	### 1.3 Worktree ownership — the confusion-killer
48	
49	This is the question that has been unclear; `dev` takes one explicit stance and
50	the skill teaches agents to respect it.
51	
52	| Worktree kind | Owner | Location | Lifetime |
53	|---|---|---|---|
54	| Feature / bugfix / experiment / cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `worktree.path_template` (default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>`) | until `dev done` / `dev sweep` |
55	| Claude Code subagent `isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree` | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | dies with the turn |
56	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used directly** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` so path policy lives in exactly one place | — | — |
57	| Worktrunk | **not adopted** — `dev wt` fills that role | — | — |
58	
59	Rule of thumb: **might I come back tomorrow → `dev`; dies with this agent turn →
60	Claude Code native.** Never nest a `dev` worktree inside another `dev` worktree.
61	
62	Herdr visibility is preserved: after `git worktree add`, `dev` calls
63	`herdr worktree open --path <path> --label <task>`, which registers the checkout
64	as a Herdr workspace grouped under the parent repo's space with its own
65	branch/ahead/behind row. `dev` additionally pushes
66	`herdr workspace report-metadata --source dev --token stage=HOT --token next="…"`
67	so the sidebar shows the task state (config already documents `$name` tokens
68	require a matching `rows` entry in `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`).
69	
70	### 1.4 Worktree provisioning
71	
72	A fresh checkout has no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`. `dev wt create`
73	runs a provisioning step (skippable with `--no-provision`):
74	
75	1. **Copy gitignored files** listed in `worktree.include` — same semantics as
76	   `.worktreeinclude` in the existing `git-workflow` skill (copies only files
77	   that are *both* matched and gitignored).
78	2. **Optional symlinks** for heavy dirs (`worktree.link`, default empty —
79	   opt-in, since sharing `node_modules` across checkouts can break native deps).
80	3. **Post-create commands**: `worktree.post_create = "auto"` detects
81	   `uv.lock`→`uv sync`, `poetry.lock`→`poetry install`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`→`pnpm i
82	   --frozen-lockfile`, `package-lock.json`→`npm ci`, `yarn.lock`→`yarn install
83	   --immutable`, `go.mod`→`go mod download`, `Cargo.toml`→`cargo fetch`;
84	   otherwise an explicit list. Per-repo override in `<repo>/.dev.toml`.
85	
86	---
87	
88	## 2. Architecture
89	
90	Go 1.26 (installed), pure-Go deps only (no cgo): `spf13/cobra`,
91	`charmbracelet/bubbletea` + `bubbles` + `lipgloss` + `glamour`,
92	`BurntSushi/toml`, `modernc.org/sqlite`.
93	
94	```
95	cmd/dev/main.go
96	internal/config/     TOML load/merge, path templates, XDG resolution
97	internal/gitx/       porcelain wrappers: worktree list, status, ahead/behind,
98	                     branch classification, wip-commit
99	internal/repo/       scan-root discovery + cache
100	internal/wt/         create/open/remove + provisioning (§1.4)
101	internal/task/       one-TOML-per-task registry
102	internal/runtime/    Runtime interface + herdr / tmux / none adapters
103	internal/forge/      gh + glab adapters (both optional)
104	internal/stats/      sampler, SQLite store, heatmap renderer, WakaTime importer
105	internal/tui/        bubbletea dashboard
106	internal/help/       go:embed'd git-workflow quick pages
107	internal/skill/      go:embed'd SKILL.md + install/sync
108	skill/               SKILL.md + references/ (source of truth, embedded at build)
109	docs/                mkdocs-able reference
110	```
111	
112	### Config — `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`
113	
114	Every path is configurable (per the requirement that `~/Worktrees` may need to
115	live on `/mnt`, or be lowercase):
116	
117	```toml
118	[paths]
119	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries", "~/.local/share/chezmoi"]
120	tries_root    = "~/src/tries"
121	worktree_root = "~/Worktrees"                                   # override freely
122	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo}}/{{branch|slug}}"    # full template
123	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"
124	
125	[runtime]
126	backend = "auto"          # auto | herdr | tmux | none
127	
128	[worktree]
129	include     = [".env", ".env.local"]
130	link        = []
131	post_create = "auto"
132	
133	[stats]
134	sampler  = true
135	wakatime = false          # dev stats --import-wakatime reads ~/.wakatime.cfg
136	```
137	
138	Template vars: `{{worktree_root}} {{repo}} {{repo_path}} {{branch}} {{category}}
139	{{host}} {{date}}`, filter `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`).
140	
141	### State — `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/`
142	
143	`tasks/<repo>__<branch-slug>.toml`, **one file per task** so a git-synced
144	`state_dir` doesn't conflict across machines:
145	
146	```toml
147	repo = "atp-sipui"; repo_path = "~/Documents/Program/atp-sipui"
148	branch = "fix/gx-security-recovery"; base = "main"
149	worktree_path = "~/Worktrees/atp-sipui/fix-gx-security-recovery"
150	state = "warm"; owner = "jingle-235"
151	next = "finish refresh regression test"
152	agent_session = "claude:2136a917-…"
153	created = 2026-08-21; updated = 2026-08-27
154	```
155	
156	Plus `stats.db` (SQLite) and `cache/repos.json`. If `state_dir` is a git repo,
157	`dev sync` pulls/pushes it — the cross-machine story, no Herdr sync needed.
158	
159	### Runtime adapter
160	
161	```go
162	type Runtime interface {
163	    Name() string
164	    Available() bool
165	    Open(ctx, dir, label string) (handle string, err error)
166	    Close(ctx, handle string) error
167	    List(ctx) ([]Session, error)
168	    Annotate(ctx, handle string, kv map[string]string) error  // no-op for tmux
169	}
170	```
171	
172	- **herdr**: shells out and parses the JSON already emitted by
173	  `herdr workspace list` / `agent list` / `worktree list`; uses
174	  `worktree open --path`, `workspace close`, `workspace report-metadata`.
175	- **tmux**: `new-session -d -c <dir> -s <label>`.
176	- **none**: prints the path for the shell wrapper to `cd`.
177	
178	### Shell integration (required — a child process cannot `cd` its parent)
179	
180	`eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"` installs a `dev()` wrapper that evals `cd`
181	directives on stdout, exactly like the `try` wrapper already in this shell.
182	
183	---
184	
185	## 3. Command surface
186	
187	```
188	dev                          # TUI if tty, else `dev ls`
189	dev ls [--json] [--state hot|warm|cold] [--repo R]
190	dev status                   # context for cwd: repo, branch, task, worktree, runtime
191	dev start <repo> [--task N] [--branch B] [--base REF] [--no-worktree]
192	dev park [--next "…"] [--wip] [--state warm|cold]
193	dev resume <task>
194	dev done [--ff | --pr] [--keep-branch]
195	dev sweep [--apply]          # stale-candidate report; never auto-deletes
196	dev wt list|create|open|rm|provision
197	dev repo list|clone|open|sync|new     # gh / glab backed
198	dev try [name]               # dated scratch dir in tries_root
199	dev graduate [try] --category <Cat> [--private] [--push]
200	dev stats [--heatmap] [--by repo|branch] [--since 12m] [--import-wakatime]
201	dev help [topic]             # git-workflow quick pages
202	dev skill install|sync|print ;  dev --skill
203	dev doctor ;  dev completion <shell> ;  dev shell-init <shell> ;  dev sync
204	```
205	
206	`dev ls` output shape:
207	
208	```
209	TASK                     STATE  REPO         BRANCH                    GIT      RUNTIME  NEXT
210	atp security recovery    HOT    atp-sipui    fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●     herdr w7 finish refresh regression test
211	orderbook experiment     WARM   trading      exp/orderbook-v2          clean    —        compare against baseline
212	settings redesign        COLD   website      feature/settings          pushed   —        —
213	```
214	
215	### Safety rails (mirrors Herdr's conservative lifecycle)
216	
217	- `dev` never runs `git worktree remove --force` without `--force` **and** a
218	  confirmation; `sweep` reports, `sweep --apply` still prompts per item.
219	- `dev done` refuses on a dirty tree; branch deletion is a separate, explicit step.
220	- `park --wip` makes a `wip:` checkpoint commit rather than a long-lived stash
221	  (stashes are invisible and don't cross machines).
222	
223	---
224	
225	## 4. Milestones (all of these are v1 — each independently shippable)
226	
227	- **M0 — skeleton.** `go mod init`, cobra root, config loader + path templates,
228	  `doctor`, `completion`, `shell-init`. Gate: `dev doctor` reports git / gh /
229	  glab / herdr / tmux presence.
230	- **M1 — inventory + lifecycle.** `internal/gitx`, `internal/repo`,
231	  `internal/task`, runtime adapters; `ls`, `status`, `start`, `park`, `resume`,
232	  `sweep`. Gate: 31 Herdr spaces reconcile against `dev ls` output.
233	- **M2 — worktrees.** `internal/wt` with path template + provisioning + Herdr
234	  surfacing; `wt *`, `done`. Gate: `dev wt create` produces a working checkout
235	  (deps installed, `.env` present) that appears grouped in the Herdr sidebar.
236	- **M3 — repo & forge.** `internal/forge`; `repo list|clone|open|sync|new`,
237	  `dev sync`. Gate: works with `gh`, with `glab`, and with neither.
238	- **M4 — try / graduate.** `dev try` (dated dirs, compatible with the existing
239	  `~/src/tries`), `dev graduate` → move into `Program/<Category>/`, `git init`,
240	  initial commit, optional `gh repo create --source`, register as a task.
241	- **M5 — stats.** SQLite store; sampler recording `herdr agent list` + git
242	  commit/reflog activity; `--import-wakatime`; ASCII heatmap in the
243	  `Mon/Wed/Fri` + `░▒▓█` style already in use.
244	- **M6 — TUI.** Bubbletea dashboard: task list, filter by state, inline `next`
245	  editing, enter → open runtime, `p` park, `s` sweep view, `?` help.
246	- **M7 — help + skill.** `internal/help` glamour-rendered pages; the skill and
247	  its self-install (§5).
248	
249	---
250	
251	## 5. The agent skill
252	
253	Lives at `skill/SKILL.md` in this repo, embedded with `go:embed`, so the binary
254	is the authority for its own skill — the same pattern `herdr --skill` uses and
255	that `~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/lib/herdr_skill.sh` already consumes.
256	
257	- `dev skill sync` regenerates the command-reference section from the live cobra
258	  tree, so the skill can never drift from the tool. `--check` exits non-zero on
259	  drift (wire into CI / a pre-push hook).
260	- `dev skill install` writes `~/.agents/skills/dev/` and symlinks
261	  `~/.claude/skills/dev` → it, matching the existing layout on this machine
262	  (`~/.claude/skills/herdr -> ../../.agents/skills/herdr`).
263	- `dev --skill` prints it, so a chezmoi script can mirror `sync_herdr_skill()`
264	  without `dev` being a hard dependency of the dotfiles.
265	
266	Skill content — **defers rather than duplicates**. Commit conventions, SemVer,
267	branch naming, and PR-vs-main tiering already live in
268	`agent-skills/skills/local/git-workflow`; this skill links there and owns only
269	what's new:
270	
271	- `references/worktree-ownership.md` — §1.3, the dev vs Claude Code vs Herdr
272	  matrix, so an agent stops improvising which worktree mechanism to use.
273	- `references/task-lifecycle.md` — §1.1 HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE and when to park.
274	- `references/commands.md` — generated command reference.
275	- `references/runtime-herdr.md` — how `dev` and Herdr divide responsibility.
276	
277	---
278	
279	## 6. Verification
280	
281	**Unit** — `internal/gitx` and `internal/wt` against throwaway repos built by a
282	test helper (`git init`, commits, branches, worktrees) in `t.TempDir()`;

290	
291	**End-to-end** (`scripts/e2e.sh`, temp HOME + temp scan root):
292	
293	```bash
294	dev doctor

297	dev park --next "add token test" && dev ls   # → WARM, runtime closed

1	# Context
2	
3	`dev-cli` currently has no MkDocs configuration or published GitHub Pages site, while its usage model spans several layers that are easy to conflate: Git branches/worktrees, the `dev` task registry, Herdr/tmux runtimes, and coding-agent orchestration. The requested site should explain both the tool and the surrounding Git/Claude Code knowledge, make safe parallel work easy to follow, and remain structured enough to absorb many future notes.

8	- The intended target is `daviddwlee84/dev-cli`, with automatic deployment from `main`.
9	- English is the default language and every first-release page also has a complete `zh-TW` sibling.
10	- The first release is Claude-first while defining a reusable shape for other coding-agent harnesses later.
11	
12	The repository currently has a heavily modified working tree, an empty `docs/`, no `mkdocs.yml`, and no Git remote. `gh` cannot currently find `daviddwlee84/dev-cli`. The documentation implementation therefore stops after local/CI-ready verification; publishing the repository and enabling Pages remain explicit outward-facing consent gates.
13	
14	## Recommended implementation
15	
16	### 1. Re-check the workspace and persist the approved preferences
17	
18	- Immediately before writing, re-run `git status --short`, verify that `docs/` is still empty and that `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, and `.github/workflows/docs.yml` still do not exist. If another session created any target, stop rather than overwrite it.
19	- Do not stash, reset, clean, rebase, or use any `--force` scaffold option; do not alter the user's existing dirty files.
20	- Verify required local tools (`uv` and mikefarah `yq` v4) before starting.
21	- Use `.claude/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh` to create `.skills/preferences.yaml` with the approved decisions: `enabled=true`, `decided_at=2026-08-27`, `stack=mkdocs-material`, `auto_deploy=true`, `pages_deployed=false`, `existing_docs_decision=none`, `repo_slug=daviddwlee84/dev-cli`, and `site_url=https://daviddwlee84.github.io/dev-cli/`.
22	
23	### 2. Scaffold the site safely, then add i18n
24

26	  - `--site-name "dev-cli"`

13	// Herdr drives the herdr terminal workspace manager over its CLI, which emits
14	// JSON on stdout for every subcommand dev needs.
15	//
16	// Division of responsibility, deliberately: dev creates worktrees with plain
17	// `git worktree add` at its own configured path and then asks herdr to *open*
18	// that path. `herdr worktree create` is not used, because it would put the
19	// path policy in a second place — and that policy has to hold on machines
20	// where herdr is not installed at all.
21	type Herdr struct {
22		bin string
23		// metadataSource namespaces the workspace metadata tokens dev reports.
24		metadataSource string
25	}
26	
27	// NewHerdr returns the herdr adapter.
28	func NewHerdr() *Herdr { return &Herdr{bin: "herdr", metadataSource: "dev"} }
29	
30	// WithMetadataSource sets the --source id used for workspace metadata tokens.
31	func (h *Herdr) WithMetadataSource(src string) *Herdr {
32		if src != "" {
33			h.metadataSource = src
34		}
35		return h
36	}
37	
38	// Name implements Runtime.
39	func (h *Herdr) Name() string { return "herdr" }
40	
41	// Available reports whether the binary exists *and* a server is reachable.
42	// The binary alone is not enough: every dev call goes through the socket API,
43	// so a stopped server must degrade to the next backend rather than making
44	// every command fail.
45	func (h *Herdr) Available() bool {
46		if !haveBinary(h.bin) {
47			return false
48		}
49		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
50		defer cancel()
51		_, err := h.run(ctx, "workspace", "list")
52		return err == nil
53	}
54	
55	func (h *Herdr) run(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
56		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, h.bin, args...)
57		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
58		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
59		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
60			msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
61			if msg == "" {
62				msg = err.Error()
63			}
64			return nil, fmt.Errorf("herdr %s: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), msg)
65		}
66		return stdout.Bytes(), nil
67	}
68	
69	// herdrEnvelope is the common shape of every herdr CLI JSON response.
70	type herdrEnvelope struct {
71		ID     string          `json:"id"`
72		Error  *herdrError     `json:"error"`
73		Result json.RawMessage `json:"result"`
74	}
75	
76	type herdrError struct {
77		Code    string `json:"code"`
78		Message string `json:"message"`
79	}
80	
81	// call runs a herdr subcommand and decodes result into out.
82	func (h *Herdr) call(ctx context.Context, out any, args ...string) error {
83		raw, err := h.run(ctx, args...)
84		if err != nil {
85			return err
86		}
87		var env herdrEnvelope
88		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &env); err != nil {
89			return fmt.Errorf("herdr %s: unexpected output: %w", strings.Join(args, " "), err)
90		}
91		if env.Error != nil {
92			return fmt.Errorf("herdr %s: %s (%s)", strings.Join(args, " "), env.Error.Message, env.Error.Code)
93		}
94		if out == nil {
95			return nil
96		}
97		return json.Unmarshal(env.Result, out)
98	}

127	// List implements Runtime. Workspaces carry no working directory of their own,
128	// so dev joins them against the pane list — panes are what actually have a cwd.
129	func (h *Herdr) List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error) {
130		var ws struct {
131			Workspaces []herdrWorkspace `json:"workspaces"`
132		}
133		if err := h.call(ctx, &ws, "workspace", "list"); err != nil {
134			return nil, err
135		}
136		var ps struct {
137			Panes []herdrPane `json:"panes"`
138		}
139		if err := h.call(ctx, &ps, "pane", "list"); err != nil {
140			// Directories are an enrichment; a workspace listing without them is
141			// still worth returning.
142			ps.Panes = nil
143		}
144	
145		dirs := map[string]map[string]bool{}
146		agents := map[string]map[string]bool{}
147		for _, p := range ps.Panes {
148			if p.CWD != "" {
149				if dirs[p.WorkspaceID] == nil {
150					dirs[p.WorkspaceID] = map[string]bool{}
151				}
152				dirs[p.WorkspaceID][p.CWD] = true
153			}
154			if p.AgentSession != nil && p.AgentSession.Value != "" {
155				if agents[p.WorkspaceID] == nil {
156					agents[p.WorkspaceID] = map[string]bool{}
157				}
158				agents[p.WorkspaceID][p.AgentSession.Agent+":"+p.AgentSession.Value] = true
159			}
160		}
161	
162		out := make([]Session, 0, len(ws.Workspaces))
163		for _, w := range ws.Workspaces {
164			out = append(out, Session{
165				Handle:        w.WorkspaceID,
166				Label:         w.Label,
167				Dirs:          keys(dirs[w.WorkspaceID]),
168				AgentSessions: keys(agents[w.WorkspaceID]),
169				AgentStatus:   w.AgentStatus,
170				Focused:       w.Focused,
171			})
172		}
173		return out, nil
174	}

176	// Open implements Runtime. An already-open directory is focused rather than
177	// opened twice.
178	func (h *Herdr) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error) {
179		if existing, err := h.List(ctx); err == nil {
180			for _, s := range existing {
181				for _, d := range s.Dirs {
182					if d == dir {
183						_ = h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "focus", s.Handle)
184						return s.Handle, nil
185					}
186				}
187			}
188		}
189		args := []string{"workspace", "create", "--cwd", dir, "--no-focus"}
190		if label != "" {
191			args = append(args, "--label", label)
192		}
193		var res struct {
194			Workspace herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
195		}
196		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
197			return "", err
198		}
199		return res.Workspace.WorkspaceID, nil
200	}
201	
202	// OpenWorktree implements WorktreeOpener: it registers an already-created git
203	// worktree as a herdr workspace, which is what makes the checkout appear in
204	// the sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
205	// ahead/behind row.
206	func (h *Herdr) OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error) {
207		args := []string{"worktree", "open", "--path", path, "--no-focus"}
208		if label != "" {
209			args = append(args, "--label", label)
210		}
211		var res struct {
212			Workspace herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
213			Worktree  herdrWorktree  `json:"worktree"`
214		}
215		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
216			// Fall back to a plain workspace: the checkout being visible matters
217			// more than it being tagged with git provenance.
218			return h.Open(ctx, path, label)
219		}
220		if res.Workspace.WorkspaceID != "" {
221			return res.Workspace.WorkspaceID, nil
222		}
223		return res.Worktree.OpenWorkspaceID, nil
224	}
225	
226	// Close implements Runtime. This ends herdr's session state only — it never
227	// removes the checkout, the worktree or the branch, matching herdr's own
228	// separation of `workspace close` from `worktree remove`.
229	func (h *Herdr) Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
230		if handle == "" {
231			return nil
232		}
233		return h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "close", handle)
234	}
235	
236	// Annotate implements Runtime by reporting display-only workspace metadata.
237	//
238	// Note for users: a token only renders if the sidebar row layout in
239	// ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g. rows = [[..., "$stage"], ["$next"]].
240	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds silently and shows
241	// nothing.
242	func (h *Herdr) Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error {
243		if handle == "" || len(kv) == 0 {
244			return nil
245		}
246		args := []string{"workspace", "report-metadata", handle, "--source", h.metadataSource}
247		for k, v := range kv {
248			if v == "" {
249				args = append(args, "--clear-token", k)
250				continue
251			}
252			args = append(args, "--token", k+"="+v)
253		}
254		return h.call(ctx, nil, args...)
255	}
256	
257	func keys(m map[string]bool) []string {
258		if len(m) == 0 {
259			return nil
260		}
261		out := make([]string, 0, len(m))
262		for k := range m {
263			out = append(out, k)
264		}
265		for i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {
266			for j := i; j > 0 && out[j] < out[j-1]; j-- {
267				out[j], out[j-1] = out[j-1], out[j]
268			}
269		}
270		return out
271	}

8		"regexp"
9		"strings"

11	
12	// Tmux is the fallback backend for machines without herdr. It models a task as
13	// a named tmux session rooted at the checkout.
14	type Tmux struct{ bin string }
15	
16	// NewTmux returns the tmux adapter.
17	func NewTmux() *Tmux { return &Tmux{bin: "tmux"} }
18	
19	// Name implements Runtime.
20	func (t *Tmux) Name() string { return "tmux" }
21	
22	// Available reports whether tmux is installed. Unlike herdr, tmux needs no
23	// running server for `new-session -d` to work, so presence is enough.
24	func (t *Tmux) Available() bool { return haveBinary(t.bin) }
25	
26	func (t *Tmux) run(ctx context.Context, args ...string) (string, error) {
27		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, t.bin, args...)
28		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
29		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
30		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
31			msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
32			if msg == "" {
33				msg = err.Error()
34			}
35			return "", fmt.Errorf("tmux %s: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), msg)
36		}
37		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
38	}
39	
40	// tmuxUnsafe covers the characters tmux treats specially in session names:
41	// a "." or ":" would make the name ambiguous with window/pane addressing.
42	var tmuxUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[.:\s]+`)
43	
44	// SessionName converts a task label into a legal tmux session name.
45	func SessionName(label string) string {
46		s := tmuxUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(label, "-")
47		s = strings.Trim(s, "-")
48		if s == "" {
49			return "dev"
50		}
51		return s
52	}
53	
54	// List implements Runtime. An absent server means "no sessions", not an error.
55	func (t *Tmux) List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error) {
56		out, err := t.run(ctx, "list-sessions", "-F", "#{session_name}\t#{session_path}\t#{?session_attached,1,0}")
57		if err != nil {
58			// "no server running on ..." is the normal idle case.
59			if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "no server running") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "error connecting") {
60				return nil, nil
61			}
62			return nil, err
63		}
64		var sessions []Session
65		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
66			if line == "" {
67				continue
68			}
69			f := strings.Split(line, "\t")
70			if len(f) < 2 {
71				continue
72			}
73			s := Session{Handle: f[0], Label: f[0], Dirs: []string{f[1]}}
74			if len(f) > 2 {
75				s.Focused = f[2] == "1"
76			}
77			sessions = append(sessions, s)
78		}
79		return sessions, nil
80	}
81	
82	// Open implements Runtime, reusing a session that already exists under that
83	// name rather than creating a duplicate.
84	func (t *Tmux) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error) {
85		name := SessionName(label)
86		if _, err := t.run(ctx, "has-session", "-t", "="+name); err == nil {
87			return name, nil
88		}
89		if _, err := t.run(ctx, "new-session", "-d", "-s", name, "-c", dir); err != nil {
90			return "", err
91		}
92		return name, nil
93	}
94	
95	// Close implements Runtime: it kills the session only. The checkout is
96	// untouched.
97	func (t *Tmux) Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
98		if handle == "" {
99			return nil
100		}
101		if _, err := t.run(ctx, "has-session", "-t", "="+handle); err != nil {
102			return nil // already gone
103		}
104		_, err := t.run(ctx, "kill-session", "-t", "="+handle)
105		return err
106	}
107	
108	// Annotate implements Runtime. tmux has no metadata channel, so dev writes the
109	// task state into the session's user option, where a status-line format can
110	// pick it up with #{@dev_stage} if the user wants it.
111	func (t *Tmux) Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error {
112		if handle == "" {
113			return nil

11	// process can never change its parent's working directory.

13

16	
17	// Available implements Runtime; the null backend always is.
18	func (None) Available() bool { return true }
19

21	func (None) Open(_ context.Context, dir, _ string) (string, error) { return dir, nil }
22	
23	// Close implements Runtime as a no-op: there is no session to end.
24	func (None) Close(context.Context, string) error { return nil }

50	func newConfigInitCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
51		var (
52			force  bool
53			stdout bool
54		)
55		cmd := &cobra.Command{
56			Use:   "init",
57			Short: "Write a starter config.toml, detecting this machine's layout",
58			Long: `Generate a commented config.toml describing the paths that actually exist on
59	this machine.
60	
61	Where repositories live differs from person to person — ~/Documents/Program,
62	~/src, ~/code, a ghq root — so the generated file is built from what is found
63	rather than from a fixed set of defaults. A config pointing at directories that
64	do not exist is worse than none: dev would discover nothing and give no clue
65	why.
66	
67	Every value it writes is still a default you can change; nothing is inferred
68	that you cannot override.`,
69			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
70			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
71				layout := config.DetectLayout()
72				body := renderStarterConfig(layout.Fallbacks())
73	
74				if stdout {
75					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, body)
76					return nil
77				}
78	
79				path := app.configPath
80				if path == "" {
81					path = config.ConfigFile()
82				}
83				if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil && !force {
84					return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists (use --force to overwrite, or --stdout to preview)",
85						config.Contract(path))
86				}
87				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
88					return err
89				}
90				if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
91					return err
92				}
93	
94				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "wrote %s\n\n", config.Contract(path))
95				reportDetection(app, layout)
96				return nil
97			},
98		}
99		f := cmd.Flags()
100		f.BoolVarP(&force, "force", "f", false, "overwrite an existing config")
101		f.BoolVar(&stdout, "stdout", false, "print the generated config instead of writing it")
102		return cmd
103	}

105	// reportDetection explains what was found, so the user can see whether the
106	// generated config actually matches how they work.
107	func reportDetection(app *App, l config.Layout) {
108		if len(l.Found) == 0 {
109			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No repository directories were recognised, so the defaults were used.")
110			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Edit paths.scan_roots to point at where you keep projects.")
111			return
112		}
113		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Detected:")
114		t := NewTable("ROOT", "REPOS", "ROLE")
115		for _, r := range l.ScanRoots {
116			role := "scan root"
117			switch r {
118			case l.ProjectRoot:
119				role = "scan root, new projects land here"
120			case l.TriesRoot:
121				role = "scan root, experiments"
122			}
123			t.Add(r, fmt.Sprintf("%d", l.Found[r]), role)
124		}
125		t.Render(app.Out)
126		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\nWorktrees will go to %s — change paths.worktree_root if that volume is wrong.\n",
127			l.WorktreeRoot)
128	}
129	
130	// renderStarterConfig fills the annotated template with detected paths.
131	func renderStarterConfig(l config.Layout) string {
132		roots := make([]string, len(l.ScanRoots))
133		for i, r := range l.ScanRoots {
134			roots[i] = strconv.Quote(r)
135		}
136		r := strings.NewReplacer(
137			"@@SCAN_ROOTS@@", strings.Join(roots, ", "),
138			"@@TRIES_ROOT@@", l.TriesRoot,
139			"@@PROJECT_ROOT@@", l.ProjectRoot,
140			"@@WORKTREE_ROOT@@", l.WorktreeRoot,
141		)
142		return r.Replace(starterConfig)
143	}

_**Agent - sidechain (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-27 09:17:48Z)**_

Repository and worktree code confirms reusable boundaries: `repo.Discover/Resolve` owns project discovery; `gitx` owns all porcelain calls; `wt.Manager` owns reversible checkout creation/removal; and CLI commands orchestrate these through callbacks. Tries currently bypass all three domain abstractions except `gitx.StatusOf` and runtime opening, so a serious try TUI/lifecycle feature would benefit from a dedicated `try` domain/store rather than expanding `internal/cli/try.go` further.

284	// visibleTasks applies the state filter and the text query.
285	func (m Model) visibleTasks() []inventory.Row {
286		var out []inventory.Row
287		for _, r := range m.rows {
288			if len(m.states) > 0 {
289				if !containsState(m.states, r.Task.State) {
290					continue
291				}
292			} else if r.Task.State == task.Done && !m.showDone {
293				continue
294			}
295			if !matches(taskSearchText(r), m.filter) {
296				continue
297			}
298			out = append(out, r)
299		}
300		return out
301	}
302	
303	// visibleRepos applies the text query, and sorts repositories with work in
304	// flight to the top — that is what someone opening the dashboard is looking
305	// for, not alphabetical order.
306	func (m Model) visibleRepos() []RepoRow {
307		var out []RepoRow
308		for _, r := range m.repos {
309			if !matches(r.searchText(), m.filter) {
310				continue
311			}
312			out = append(out, r)
313		}
314		sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool {
315			a, b := out[i], out[j]
316			if a.HotTasks() != b.HotTasks() {
317				return a.HotTasks() > b.HotTasks()
318			}
319			if a.Live != b.Live {
320				return a.Live
321			}
322			if len(a.Tasks) != len(b.Tasks) {
323				return len(a.Tasks) > len(b.Tasks)
324			}
325			if a.Status.Dirty() != b.Status.Dirty() {
326				return a.Status.Dirty()
327			}
328			return strings.ToLower(a.Repo.Display()) < strings.ToLower(b.Repo.Display())
329		})
330		return out
331	}
332	
333	// visibleRemotes filters the combined gh/glab inventory. Local clones sort
334	// first, then recently updated repositories.
335	func (m Model) visibleRemotes() []RemoteRow {
336		var out []RemoteRow
337		for _, r := range m.remotes {
338			if matches(r.searchText(), m.filter) {
339				out = append(out, r)
340			}
341		}
342		sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool {
343			if out[i].Cloned() != out[j].Cloned() {
344				return out[i].Cloned()
345			}
346			if !out[i].Repo.UpdatedAt.Equal(out[j].Repo.UpdatedAt) {
347				return out[i].Repo.UpdatedAt.After(out[j].Repo.UpdatedAt)
348			}
349			return out[i].Repo.Label() < out[j].Repo.Label()
350		})
351		return out
352	}
353	
354	func containsState(list []task.State, s task.State) bool {
355		for _, v := range list {
356			if v == s {
357				return true
358			}
359		}
360		return false
361	}
362	
363	// count is how many rows the current view has.
364	func (m Model) count() int {
365		switch m.view {
366		case ViewRepos:
367			return len(m.visibleRepos())
368		case ViewRemote:
369			return len(m.visibleRemotes())
370		default:
371			return len(m.visibleTasks())
372		}
373	}
374	
375	// at is the cursor position in the current view.
376	func (m Model) at() int {
377		switch m.view {
378		case ViewRepos:
379			return m.repoCursor
380		case ViewRemote:
381			return m.remoteCursor
382		default:
383			return m.taskCursor
384		}
385	}
386	
387	// setAt moves the cursor, clamped to the current view's length.
388	func (m *Model) setAt(i int) {
389		n := m.count()
390		switch {
391		case n == 0:
392			i = 0
393		case i >= n:
394			i = n - 1
395		case i < 0:
396			i = 0
397		}
398		switch m.view {
399		case ViewRepos:
400			m.repoCursor = i
401		case ViewRemote:
402			m.remoteCursor = i
403		default:
404			m.taskCursor = i
405		}
406	}
407	
408	// currentTask returns the selected task, if the task view is showing one.
409	func (m Model) currentTask() (inventory.Row, bool) {
410		if m.view != ViewTasks {
411			return inventory.Row{}, false
412		}
413		rows := m.visibleTasks()
414		if m.at() >= len(rows) {
415			return inventory.Row{}, false
416		}
417		return rows[m.at()], true
418	}
419	
420	// currentRepo returns the selected repository, if the repo view is showing one.
421	func (m Model) currentRepo() (RepoRow, bool) {
422		if m.view != ViewRepos {
423			return RepoRow{}, false
424		}
425		repos := m.visibleRepos()
426		if m.at() >= len(repos) {
427			return RepoRow{}, false
428		}
429		return repos[m.at()], true
430	}
431	
432	// currentRemote returns the selected forge repository.
433	func (m Model) currentRemote() (RemoteRow, bool) {
434		if m.view != ViewRemote {
435			return RemoteRow{}, false
436		}
437		rows := m.visibleRemotes()
438		if m.at() >= len(rows) {
439			return RemoteRow{}, false
440		}
441		return rows[m.at()], true
442	}
443	
444	// currentDir is the checkout the selected row points at, for the external
445	// tools and for the cd directive.
446	func (m Model) currentDir() string {
447		if r, ok := m.currentTask(); ok {
448			if r.CheckoutExists {
449				return r.Checkout
450			}
451			return ""
452		}
453		if r, ok := m.currentRepo(); ok {
454			return r.Repo.Path
455		}
456		if r, ok := m.currentRemote(); ok {
457			return r.LocalPath
458		}
459		return ""
460	}
461	
462	// Update implements tea.Model.
463	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
464		switch msg := msg.(type) {
465		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
466			m.width, m.height = msg.Width, msg.Height
467			return m, nil
468	
469		case reloadMsg:
470			if msg.err != nil {
471				m.err = msg.err
472				return m, nil
473			}
474			m.err = nil
475			if msg.rows != nil {
476				m.rows = msg.rows
477			}
478			if msg.repos != nil {
479				m.repos = msg.repos
480			}
481			if msg.remoteSet {
482				m.remotes, m.remotesLoaded, m.remotesLoading = msg.remotes, true, false
483			}
484			m.setAt(m.at())
485			return m, nil
486	
487		case remoteMsg:
488			m.remotes, m.remotesLoaded, m.remotesLoading = msg.rows, true, false
489			m.err = msg.err
490			m.status = ""
491			m.setAt(m.at())
492			return m, nil
493	
494		case configEditedMsg:
495			if msg.err != nil {
496				m.err, m.status = msg.err, ""
497				return m, nil
498			}
499			m.status = "reloading config…"
500			return m, m.reloadConfig(m.view == ViewRemote)
501	
502		case configMsg:
503			if msg.err != nil {
504				m.err, m.status = msg.err, ""
505				return m, nil
506			}
507			m.actions.Tools = msg.tools
508			m.err, m.status = nil, msg.status
509			return m, m.reloadAfterConfig(msg.refreshRemote)
510	
511		case statsMsg:
512			if msg.err != nil {
513				m.err = msg.err
514				m.stats = nil
515			} else {
516				m.err = nil
517				m.stats = &msg.panel
518			}
519			m.status = ""
520			return m, nil
521	
522		case actionMsg:
523			if msg.err != nil {
524				m.err = msg.err
525				return m, nil
526			}
527			m.err, m.status = nil, msg.status
528			if msg.remoteName != "" && msg.localPath != "" {
529				for i := range m.remotes {
530					if m.remotes[i].Repo.FullName == msg.remoteName {
531						m.remotes[i].LocalPath = msg.localPath
532						break
533					}
534				}
535			}
536			if msg.cd != "" {
537				// Under a runtime with no sessions the only useful outcome is
538				// putting the user in the directory, which needs the alternate
539				// screen torn down first.
540				m.chosen, m.quitting = msg.cd, true
541				return m, tea.Quit
542			}
543			if m.view == ViewRemote {
544				// Clone already updated the selected row; only local repo/task
545				// state needs a refresh. A network round-trip here would make a
546				// successful clone feel hung for several seconds.
547				return m, m.reload()
548			}
549			return m, m.reload()
550	
551		case tea.KeyMsg:
552			if m.mode == modeStats {
553				return m.updateStats(msg)
554			}
555			switch m.mode {
556			case modeFilter:
557				return m.updateFilter(msg)
558			case modeEditNext, modeConfirmPark, modeStartTask, modeConfirmClone:
559				return m.updatePrompt(msg)
560			}
561			return m.updateList(msg)
562		}
563		return m, nil
564	}
565	
566	func (m Model) updateList(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
567		n := m.count()
568		page := m.listHeight() / 2
569		if page < 1 {
570			page = 1
571		}
572	
573		switch msg.String() {
574		case "q", "ctrl+c":
575			m.quitting = true
576			return m, tea.Quit
577		case "esc":
578			// One escape clears whatever narrowing is in effect before quitting
579			// becomes the meaning of the key.
580			if m.filter != "" || len(m.states) > 0 {
581				m.filter, m.states = "", nil
582				m.setAt(0)
583				return m, nil
584			}
585			m.quitting = true
586			return m, tea.Quit
587	
588		// Vim-style movement, with the arrow equivalents alongside.
589		case "j", "down", "ctrl+n":
590			m.setAt(m.at() + 1)
591		case "k", "up", "ctrl+p":
592			m.setAt(m.at() - 1)
593		case "ctrl+d", "pgdown":
594			m.setAt(m.at() + page)
595		case "ctrl+u", "pgup":
596			m.setAt(m.at() - page)
597		case "g", "home":
598			m.setAt(0)
599		case "G", "end":
600			m.setAt(n - 1)
601	
602		// View switching. h/l double as left/right between views, since a list has
603		// no horizontal axis of its own.
604		case "tab", "l", "right":
605			m.view = Views[(int(m.view)+1)%len(Views)]
606			return m.afterViewSwitch()
607		case "shift+tab", "h", "left":
608			m.view = Views[(int(m.view)+len(Views)-1)%len(Views)]
609			return m.afterViewSwitch()
610	
611		case "/":
612			m.mode = modeFilter
613			m.input.SetValue(m.filter)
614			m.input.Placeholder = "filter"
615			m.input.CursorEnd()
616			m.input.Focus()
617			return m, textinput.Blink
618	
619		case "r":
620			m.status = "reloading config + data…"
621			if m.view == ViewRemote {
622				m.remotesLoading = true
623			}
624			return m, m.reloadConfig(m.view == ViewRemote)
625	
626		case "1":
627			m.states, m.showDone = []task.State{task.Hot}, false
628			m.view = ViewTasks
629			m.setAt(0)
630		case "2":
631			m.states, m.showDone = []task.State{task.Warm}, false
632			m.view = ViewTasks
633			m.setAt(0)
634		case "3":
635			m.states, m.showDone = []task.State{task.Cold}, false
636			m.view = ViewTasks
637			m.setAt(0)
638		case "0":
639			m.states, m.filter = nil, ""
640			m.setAt(0)
641		case "a":
642			m.showDone, m.states = !m.showDone, nil
643			m.setAt(0)
644	
645		case "enter", "o":
646			return m, m.openSelected()
647	
648		case "p":
649			if _, ok := m.currentTask(); !ok {
650				return m, nil
651			}
652			return m.prompt(modeConfirmPark, "", "what to do when you come back")
653	
654		case "c":
655			if row, ok := m.currentTask(); ok {
656				return m.prompt(modeEditNext, row.Task.Next, "next action")
657			}
658			if row, ok := m.currentRemote(); ok && !row.Cloned() {
659				return m.prompt(modeConfirmClone, row.Repo.FullName,
660					"enter to clone; esc to cancel")
661			}
662			return m, nil
663	
664		case "s":
665			if _, ok := m.currentRepo(); !ok {
666				return m, nil
667			}
668			return m.prompt(modeStartTask, "", "name for the new task")
669	
670		case "e":
671			if m.actions.EditConfig == nil {
672				return m, nil
673			}
674			proc, err := m.actions.EditConfig()
675			if err != nil {
676				m.err = err
677				return m, nil
678			}
679			m.status = "editing config…"
680			return m, tea.ExecProcess(proc, func(err error) tea.Msg {
681				return configEditedMsg{err: err}
682			})
683	
684		case "H":
685			repo := m.selectedRepoName()
686			if repo == "" || m.actions.LoadStats == nil {
687				return m, nil
688			}
689			m.mode, m.stats, m.status = modeStats, nil, "loading activity…"
690			return m, m.loadStats(repo)
691	
692		default:
693			if cmd := m.launchTool(msg.String()); cmd != nil {
694				return m, cmd
695			}
696		}
697		m.setAt(m.at())
698		return m, nil
699	}
700	
701	func (m Model) selectedRepoName() string {
702		if r, ok := m.currentTask(); ok {
703			return r.Task.Repo
704		}
705		if r, ok := m.currentRepo(); ok {
706			return r.Repo.Name
707		}
708		if r, ok := m.currentRemote(); ok && r.Cloned() {
709			if r.LocalName != "" {
710				return filepath.Base(r.LocalName)
711			}
712			return r.Repo.Name
713		}
714		return ""
715	}
716	
717	func (m Model) loadStats(repo string) tea.Cmd {
718		return func() tea.Msg {
719			panel, err := m.actions.LoadStats(context.Background(), repo)
720			return statsMsg{panel: panel, err: err}
721		}
722	}
723	
724	func (m Model) updateStats(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
725		switch msg.String() {
726		case "q", "ctrl+c":
727			m.quitting = true
728			return m, tea.Quit
729		case "esc", "H":
730			m.mode, m.stats, m.err, m.status = modeList, nil, nil, ""
731			return m, nil
732		case "r":
733			repo := ""
734			if m.stats != nil {
735				repo = m.stats.Repo
736			}
737			if repo == "" {
738				repo = m.selectedRepoName()
739			}
740			m.stats, m.status = nil, "loading activity…"
741			return m, m.loadStats(repo)
742		}
743		return m, nil
744	}
745	
746	// afterViewSwitch lazily loads forge data only when REMOTE is first opened,
747	// so starting the dashboard never waits on a network request.
748	func (m Model) afterViewSwitch() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
749		m.setAt(m.at())
750		if m.view == ViewRemote && !m.remotesLoaded && !m.remotesLoading {
751			m.remotesLoading = true
752			m.status = "loading GitHub and GitLab repositories…"
753			return m, m.reloadRemote()
754		}
755		return m, nil
756	}
757	
758	func (m Model) prompt(md mode, value, placeholder string) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
759		m.mode = md
760		m.input.SetValue(value)
761		m.input.Placeholder = placeholder
762		m.input.CursorEnd()
763		m.input.Focus()
764		return m, textinput.Blink
765	}
766	
767	func (m Model) updateFilter(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
768		switch msg.String() {
769		case "esc":
770			m.mode = modeList
771			m.input.Blur()
772			m.filter = ""
773			m.setAt(0)
774			return m, nil
775		case "enter":
776			m.mode = modeList
777			m.input.Blur()
778			return m, nil
779		}
780		var cmd tea.Cmd
781		m.input, cmd = m.input.Update(msg)
782		// Filtering live is the point: seeing the list narrow as you type is what
783		// makes it faster than remembering an exact name.
784		m.filter = m.input.Value()
785		m.setAt(0)
786		return m, cmd
787	}
788	
789	func (m Model) updatePrompt(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
790		switch msg.String() {
791		case "esc":
792			m.mode = modeList
793			m.input.Blur()
794			return m, nil
795		case "enter":
796			md := m.mode
797			value := strings.TrimSpace(m.input.Value())
798			m.mode = modeList
799			m.input.Blur()
800			return m, m.submit(md, value)
801		}
802		var cmd tea.Cmd
803		m.input, cmd = m.input.Update(msg)
804		return m, cmd
805	}
806	
807	func (m Model) submit(md mode, value string) tea.Cmd {
808		switch md {
809		case modeEditNext:
810			row, ok := m.currentTask()
811			if !ok {
812				return nil
813			}
814			t := row.Task
815			return func() tea.Msg {
816				if err := m.actions.SetNext(context.Background(), t, value); err != nil {
817					return actionMsg{err: err}
818				}
819				return actionMsg{status: "next action recorded for " + t.Title()}
820			}
821	
822		case modeConfirmPark:
823			row, ok := m.currentTask()
824			if !ok {
825				return nil
826			}
827			t := row.Task
828			return func() tea.Msg {
829				status, err := m.actions.Park(context.Background(), t, value)
830				return actionMsg{status: status, err: err}
831			}
832	
833		case modeStartTask:
834			r, ok := m.currentRepo()
835			if !ok {
836				return nil
837			}
838			if value == "" {
839				return func() tea.Msg { return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("a task needs a name")} }
840			}
841			return func() tea.Msg {
842				status, err := m.actions.Start(context.Background(), r, value)
843				return actionMsg{status: status, err: err}
844			}
845	
846		case modeConfirmClone:
847			r, ok := m.currentRemote()
848			if !ok {
849				return nil
850			}
851			return func() tea.Msg {
852				status, path, err := m.actions.CloneRemote(context.Background(), r)
853				return actionMsg{
854					status: status, remoteName: r.Repo.FullName, localPath: path, err: err,
855				}
856			}
857		}
858		return nil
859	}
860	
861	func (m Model) openSelected() tea.Cmd {
862		cdWanted := m.actions.Runtime != nil && m.actions.Runtime.Name() == "none"
863	
864		if row, ok := m.currentTask(); ok {
865			t := row.Task
866			dir := row.Checkout
867			return func() tea.Msg {
868				status, err := m.actions.Open(context.Background(), t)
869				cd := ""
870				if err == nil && cdWanted {
871					cd = dir
872				}
873				return actionMsg{status: status, cd: cd, err: err}
874			}
875		}
876		if r, ok := m.currentRepo(); ok {
877			dir := r.Repo.Path
878			return func() tea.Msg {
879				status, err := m.actions.OpenRepo(context.Background(), r)
880				cd := ""
881				if err == nil && cdWanted {
882					cd = dir
883				}
884				return actionMsg{status: status, cd: cd, err: err}
885			}
886		}
887		if r, ok := m.currentRemote(); ok {
888			if !r.Cloned() {
889				return nil // c is the explicit clone action
890			}
891			dir := r.LocalPath
892			return func() tea.Msg {
893				status, err := m.actions.OpenRemote(context.Background(), r)
894				cd := ""
895				if err == nil && cdWanted {
896					cd = dir
897				}
898				return actionMsg{status: status, cd: cd, err: err}
899			}
900		}
901		return nil
902	}
903	
904	// launchTool hands the terminal to an external program running in the selected
905	// row's checkout, then reloads — the tool may well have changed the git state
906	// the dashboard is displaying.
907	func (m Model) launchTool(key string) tea.Cmd {
908		for _, t := range m.actions.Tools {
909			if t.Key != key {
910				continue
911			}
912			if t.Available != nil && !t.Available() {
913				return func() tea.Msg {
914					return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("%s is not installed", t.Command[0])}
915				}
916			}
917			dir := m.currentDir()
918			if dir == "" {
919				return func() tea.Msg {
920					return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("nothing selected with a checkout on disk")}
921				}
922			}
923			c := exec.Command(t.Command[0], t.Command[1:]...)
924			c.Dir = dir
925			return tea.ExecProcess(c, func(err error) tea.Msg {
926				if err != nil {
927					return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", t.Name, err)}
928				}
929				return actionMsg{status: "back from " + t.Name}
930			})
931		}
932		return nil
933	}
934	
935	// Tools lists the external programs available on this machine, so the footer
936	// only advertises bindings that will actually work.
937	func (m Model) Tools() []Tool {
938		var out []Tool
939		for _, t := range m.actions.Tools {
940			if t.Available == nil || t.Available() {
941				out = append(out, t)
942			}
943		}
944		return out
945	}
946	
947	// Summary counts the task states, for the header line.
948	func (m Model) Summary() string {
949		counts := map[task.State]int{}
950		for _, r := range m.rows {
951			counts[r.Task.State]++
952		}
953		var parts []string
954		for _, s := range task.States {
955			if counts[s] > 0 {
956				parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s %d %s", s.Icon(), counts[s], s))
957			}
958		}
959		if len(m.repos) > 0 {
960			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%d repos", len(m.repos)))
961		}
962		if m.remotesLoaded {
963			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%d remote", len(m.remotes)))
964		}
965		if len(parts) == 0 {
966			return "no tasks"
967		}
968		return strings.Join(parts, "   ")

13	)
14	
15	// RepoRow is one repository as the dashboard shows it: what it is, plus how
16	// much of it is currently in flight.
17	//
18	// The repository view exists because the task list alone answers only half the
19	// question. On a machine with forty repositories and no tasks recorded yet,
20	// a task-only dashboard is empty — and the honest answer to "what do I have
21	// here?" has to come before "what am I working on?"
22	type RepoRow struct {
23		Repo   repo.Repo
24		Status gitx.Status
25		// Worktrees is the number of linked worktrees, excluding the main checkout.
26		Worktrees int
27		// Tasks are the recorded tasks belonging to this repository.
28		Tasks []*task.Task
29		// Live reports a runtime session sitting in this repository.
30		Live          bool
31		Runtime       string
32		RuntimeHandle string
33		RuntimeStatus string
34		// RemoteForge / RemoteName identify origin for matching the REMOTE view to
35		// this local checkout without rescanning every repo when a cache opens.
36		RemoteForge forge.Kind
37		RemoteName  string
38	}
39	
40	// HotTasks counts the repository's tasks that are currently hot.
41	func (r RepoRow) HotTasks() int {
42		n := 0
43		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
44			if t.State == task.Hot {
45				n++
46			}
47		}
48		return n
49	}
50	
51	// StateSummary renders the repository's tasks as a compact per-state tally,
52	// which is what makes the list scannable at forty repositories.
53	func (r RepoRow) StateSummary() string {
54		if len(r.Tasks) == 0 {
55			return ""
56		}
57		counts := map[task.State]int{}
58		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
59			counts[t.State]++
60		}
61		var parts []string
62		for _, s := range task.States {
63			if counts[s] > 0 {
64				parts = append(parts, s.Icon()+strconv.Itoa(counts[s]))
65			}
66		}
67		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
68	}
69	
70	// searchText is what a filter query matches against.
71	func (r RepoRow) searchText() string {
72		var b strings.Builder
73		b.WriteString(r.Repo.Display())
74		b.WriteString(" ")
75		b.WriteString(r.Status.Branch)
76		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
77			b.WriteString(" ")
78			b.WriteString(t.Title())
79			b.WriteString(" ")
80			b.WriteString(t.Branch)
81		}
82		return strings.ToLower(b.String())
83	}
84	
85	// taskSearchText is what a filter query matches a task row against.
86	func taskSearchText(r inventory.Row) string {
87		t := r.Task
88		return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
89			t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.Next, t.Note, string(t.State),
90		}, " "))
91	}
92	
93	// matches reports whether every whitespace-separated term of the query appears
94	// in the haystack.
95	//
96	// Term-wise rather than substring so "auth api" finds a task named "api token
97	// auth" — the order words come to mind in is rarely the order they appear in.
98	func matches(haystack, query string) bool {
99		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
100		if query == "" {
101			return true
102		}
103		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
104			if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
105				return false
106			}
107		}
108		return true
109	}
110	
111	// RemoteRow is one repository known to GitHub or GitLab, optionally matched to
112	// a local checkout. The REMOTE view is the bridge between "what exists on the
113	// forge" and "what is already on this machine".
114	type RemoteRow struct {
115		Repo forge.RemoteRepo `json:"repo"`
116		// LocalPath is the checkout under the configured scan roots, empty when the
117		// remote has not been cloned here.
118		LocalPath string `json:"local_path,omitempty"`
119		// LocalName is the discovered repo's display name.
120		LocalName string `json:"local_name,omitempty"`
121	}
122	
123	// Cloned reports whether this remote already has a local checkout.
124	func (r RemoteRow) Cloned() bool { return r.LocalPath != "" }
125	
126	func (r RemoteRow) searchText() string {
127		return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
128			string(r.Repo.Forge), r.Repo.Name, r.Repo.FullName, r.Repo.Description,
129			r.Repo.Visibility, r.Repo.DefaultBranch, r.LocalName,
130		}, " "))
131	}

136		Heatmap    string

138		ActiveDays int
139		Since      time.Time
140		Until      time.Time
141	}

251	func remoteAge(r RemoteRow) string {
252		if r.Repo.UpdatedAt.IsZero() {
253			return "—"
254		}
255		d := time.Since(r.Repo.UpdatedAt)
256		switch {
257		case d < 24*time.Hour:
258			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh ago", int(d.Hours()))
259		case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
260			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd ago", int(d.Hours()/24))
261		case d < 60*24*time.Hour:
262			return fmt.Sprintf("%dw ago", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
263		default:
264			return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo ago", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
265		}
266	}

429		var bindings []string
430		switch m.view {
431		case ViewRepos:
432			bindings = append(bindings, "enter open", "s start task")
433		case ViewRemote:
434			if r, ok := m.currentRemote(); ok && r.Cloned() {
435				bindings = append(bindings, "enter open local")
436			} else {
437				bindings = append(bindings, "c clone")
438			}
439		default:
440			bindings = append(bindings, "enter open", "p park", "c next")
441		}
442		bindings = append(bindings, "tab view", "/ filter", "H stats")
443		for _, t := range m.Tools() {
444			bindings = append(bindings, t.Key+" "+t.Name)
445		}
446		bindings = append(bindings, "1/2/3 state", "0 clear", "r refresh", "q quit")
447	
448		var b strings.Builder
449		if status != "" {
450			b.WriteString("  " + status + "\n")
451		}
452		b.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render(wrapBindings(bindings, m.width-4)))
453		return b.String()
454	}
455	
456	// wrapBindings lays the key hints out over as many lines as the width needs,
457	// rather than truncating them — a hint you cannot read is not a hint.
458	func wrapBindings(items []string, width int) string {
459		if width < 20 {
460			width = 20
461		}
462		var lines []string
463		cur := ""
464		for _, it := range items {
465			candidate := it
466			if cur != "" {
467				candidate = cur + " · " + it
468			}
469			if lipgloss.Width(candidate) > width && cur != "" {
470				lines = append(lines, cur)
471				cur = it
472				continue
473			}
474			cur = candidate
475		}
476		if cur != "" {
477			lines = append(lines, cur)
478		}
479		return strings.Join(lines, "\n  ")
480	}
481	
482	func gitColumn(r inventory.Row) string {
483		switch {
484		case r.StatusErr != nil:
485			return "?"
486		case !r.CheckoutExists:
487			return "no dir"
488		}
489		return r.Status.Summary()
490	}
491	
492	func nextColumn(r inventory.Row) string {
493		if r.Task.Next == "" {
494			return styleDim.Render("—")
495		}
496		return r.Task.Next
497	}
498	
499	func shortAge(r inventory.Row) string {
500		d := r.Age()
501		switch {
502		case d <= 0:
503			return "—"
504		case d.Hours() < 24:
505			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
506		case d.Hours() < 24*14:
507			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
508		case d.Hours() < 24*60:
509			return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
510		default:
511			return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
512		}
513	}
514	
515	func colourState(s task.State, line string) string {
516		switch s {
517		case task.Hot:
518			return styleHot.Render(line)
519		case task.Warm:
520			return styleWarm.Render(line)
521		case task.Cold:
522			return styleCold.Render(line)
523		case task.Done:
524			return styleDone.Render(line)
525		}
526		return line
527	}
528	
529	// pad truncates to n display columns, measuring the way lipgloss renders so
530	// CJK repo and task names do not shift the table.
531	func pad(s string, n int) string {
532		if lipgloss.Width(s) <= n {
533			return s
534		}
535		var b strings.Builder
536		used := 0
537		for _, r := range s {
538			w := lipgloss.Width(string(r))
539			if used+w > n-1 {
540				break
541			}
542			b.WriteRune(r)
543			used += w
544		}
545		return b.String() + "…"
546	}
547	
548	func clamp(v, lo, hi int) int {
549		if v < lo {
550			return lo
551		}
552		if v > hi {
553			return hi
554		}
555		return v
556	}
