1	// Package tui is the interactive dashboard behind a bare `dev`.
2	//
3	// It renders the same inventory that `dev ls` prints, from the same
4	// inventory.Collect call, so the two can never disagree. Its job is the part a
5	// static listing cannot do: let you act on what you are looking at without
6	// retyping a task name.
7	package tui
8	
9	import "github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
10	
11	// Colours are chosen from the 256-colour cube rather than truecolour so the
12	// dashboard degrades sensibly in a basic terminal, and lipgloss adapts them to
13	// the background it detects.

15		styleTitle = lipgloss.NewStyle().Bold(true)

22		styleHeader   = lipgloss.NewStyle().Faint(true).Bold(true)
23	
24		styleHot  = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("209"))
25		styleWarm = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("179"))
26		styleCold = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("110"))
27		styleDone = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("78"))
28	
29		styleDirty = lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(lipgloss.Color("215"))

79	// send feeds a sequence of key presses through Update, running any command the
80	// model returns so the action callbacks actually fire — that is what makes
81	// these tests exercise the real key bindings rather than the model's fields.
82	func send(m tui.Model, msgs ...tea.Msg) tui.Model {
83		var cur tea.Model = m
84		for _, msg := range msgs {
85			var cmd tea.Cmd
86			cur, cmd = cur.Update(msg)
87			// Follow the command chain, so an action's resulting message (and the
88			// reload it triggers) is applied too. Commands that do not return
89			// promptly are the cursor's blink timers; running those would make the
90			// suite sleep for half a second per keystroke.
91			for i := 0; cmd != nil && i < 8; i++ {
92				out, ok := runQuickly(cmd)
93				if !ok || out == nil {
94					break
95				}
96				if _, isBatch := out.(tea.BatchMsg); isBatch {
97					break
98				}
99				cur, cmd = cur.Update(out)
100			}
101		}
102		return cur.(tui.Model)
103	}
104	
105	// runQuickly executes a command, giving up on anything that blocks — which in
106	// practice means the cursor blink timers.
107	func runQuickly(cmd tea.Cmd) (tea.Msg, bool) {
108		done := make(chan tea.Msg, 1)
109		go func() { done <- cmd() }()
110		select {
111		case msg := <-done:
112			return msg, true
113		case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
114			return nil, false
115		}
116	}
117	
118	func key(s string) tea.KeyMsg {
119		switch s {
120		case "enter":
121			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEnter}
122		case "esc":
123			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEsc}
124		case "down":
125			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyDown}
126		case "up":
127			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyUp}
128		}
129		return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune(s)}
130	}
131	
132	func typeText(s string) []tea.KeyMsg {
133		out := make([]tea.KeyMsg, 0, len(s))
134		for _, r := range s {
135			out = append(out, tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune{r}})
136		}
137		return out
138	}

496	func remoteRow(provider forge.Kind, fullName, local string) tui.RemoteRow {
497		name := fullName
498		if i := strings.LastIndexByte(name, '/'); i >= 0 {
499			name = name[i+1:]
500		}
501		return tui.RemoteRow{
502			Repo: forge.RemoteRepo{
503				Forge: provider, Name: name, FullName: fullName,
504				Description:   "description for " + name,
505				URL:           "https://example.com/" + fullName,
506				CloneURL:      "https://example.com/" + fullName + ".git",
507				DefaultBranch: "main", Visibility: "private",
508				UpdatedAt: time.Now().Add(-24 * time.Hour),
509			},
510			LocalPath: local,
511		}
512	}

25					t.Fatal(err)
26				}
27			}

```text
1	# TUI navigation
2	
3	Bare `dev` opens the dashboard when stdin/stdout are terminals; `dev tui`
4	opens it explicitly. When piped, bare `dev` prints `dev ls` instead, so shell
5	composition stays predictable.
6	
7	## Three views
8	
9	Switch with `tab`, `l`/`h`, or right/left:
10	
11	| View | Answers | Data source |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| TASKS | What am I working on? | task registry + live Git/runtime state |
14	| REPOS | What repositories exist here? | recursive configured scan roots |
15	| REMOTE | What can I open or clone? | authenticated `gh` + `glab` inventories |
16	
17	REPOS shows branch, dirty state, linked-worktree count and HOT/WARM/COLD task
18	tallies. Repos with active work sort first; untracked clean repos remain
19	visible below them. On a first run with no tasks, switch to REPOS and press `s`
20	to start one, or run `dev adopt` to import work already in flight.
21	
22	REMOTE loads lazily, so dashboard startup never waits on the network. A
23	private XDG cache makes later switches instant; `r` refreshes explicitly. It
24	marks remotes already cloned under `scan_roots`. Enter opens a local clone; `c`
25	asks before cloning an absent repo into `project_root`.
26	
27	## Vim-style movement
28	
29	```
30	j / k                next / previous
31	ctrl+d / ctrl+u      half page down / up
32	g / G                top / bottom
33	h / l, shift-tab/tab previous / next view
34	/                    filter as you type
35	esc                  clear prompt/filter; when clear, quit
36	q                    quit
37	```
38	
39	The `/` query applies to the current view and matches whitespace-separated
40	terms independently. `gitlab auth` finds a GitLab repo whose name/description
41	also contains auth, regardless of word order.
42	
43	## Actions
44	
45	TASKS:
46	
47	```
48	enter / o  open in the selected runtime
49	p          park warm, prompting for the next action
50	c          edit the next action
51	1 / 2 / 3  show HOT / WARM / COLD
52	0          clear filters
53	a          include DONE
54	```
55	
56	REPOS:
57	
58	```
59	enter / o  open the repository
60	s          start a task: branch + worktree + provisioning + runtime + entry
61	```
62	
63	REMOTE:
64	
65	```
66	enter / o  open an existing local clone
67	c          confirm and clone an absent repo into project_root
68	r          refresh gh + glab, replacing the cache
69	```
70	
71	## External tools are explicit configuration
72	
73	```bash
74	dev tui tools
75	```
76	
77	shows every binding, the exact command, its source, and whether it can run on
78	this machine. `dev config init` writes the defaults out in full:
79	
80	```toml
81	[[tui.tools]]
82	key  = "L"
83	name = "lazygit"
84	run  = "lazygit"
85	
86	[[tui.tools]]
87	key  = "Y"
88	name = "yazi"
89	run  = "yazi"
90	
91	[[tui.tools]]
92	key  = "V"
93	name = "nvim"
94	run  = "nvim ."
95	
96	[[tui.tools]]
97	key  = "B"
98	name = "vibe"
99	run  = "vibe"
100	interactive = true
101	
102	[[tui.tools]]
103	key  = "P"
104	name = "plans here"
105	run  = "claude-plans-here"
106	interactive = true
107	```
108	
109	A configured list replaces the defaults entirely. Commands run through
110	`$SHELL` in the selected row's checkout, so arguments, environment variables
111	and executable scripts work. `interactive = true` runs through `$SHELL -lic`
112	and deliberately evaluates the command *after* rc loading, so this machine's
113	`vibe` alias and `claude-plans-here` function work. Prefer a real script on PATH
114	when the binding should be portable to machines with different shell configs.
115	
116	Keys are case-sensitive. A tool cannot take one the dashboard owns; config
117	loading reports the collision instead of silently shadowing movement or quit.
118
```

```text
1	// Package help serves the git-workflow quick-reference pages dev bundles.
2	//
3	// These exist because the hard part of this workflow is not running the
4	// commands, it is remembering which one applies. A page you can reach in one
5	// keystroke from the terminal you are already in beats a bookmark.
6	package help
7	
8	import (
9		"embed"
10		"fmt"
11		"io/fs"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	)
15	
16	//go:embed all:topics
17	var topics embed.FS
18	
19	// Topic is one reference page.
20	type Topic struct {
21		Name    string
22		Title   string
23		Summary string
24		Body    string
25	}
26	
27	// List returns every topic, sorted by name.
28	func List() ([]Topic, error) {
29		entries, err := fs.ReadDir(topics, "topics")
30		if err != nil {
31			return nil, err
32		}
33		var out []Topic
34		for _, e := range entries {
35			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".md") {
36				continue
37			}
38			t, err := load(strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".md"))
39			if err != nil {
40				continue
41			}
42			out = append(out, t)
43		}
44		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Name < out[j].Name })
45		return out, nil
46	}
47	
48	// Get returns one topic by exact name, or by unique prefix.
49	func Get(name string) (Topic, error) {
50		if t, err := load(name); err == nil {
51			return t, nil
52		}
53		all, err := List()
54		if err != nil {
55			return Topic{}, err
56		}
57		var hits []Topic
58		for _, t := range all {
59			if strings.HasPrefix(t.Name, name) || strings.Contains(t.Name, name) {
60				hits = append(hits, t)
61			}
62		}
63		switch len(hits) {
64		case 1:
65			return hits[0], nil
66		case 0:
67			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("no help topic %q; run `dev help` to list them", name)
68		default:
69			names := make([]string, len(hits))
70			for i, t := range hits {
71				names[i] = t.Name
72			}
73			return Topic{}, fmt.Errorf("%q matches several topics: %s", name, strings.Join(names, ", "))
74		}
75	}
76	
77	func load(name string) (Topic, error) {
78		b, err := topics.ReadFile("topics/" + name + ".md")
79		if err != nil {
80			return Topic{}, err
81		}
82		body := string(b)
83		t := Topic{Name: name, Body: body}
84		// The first heading is the title; the first paragraph after it is the
85		// summary shown in the index.
86		for _, line := range strings.Split(body, "\n") {
87			line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
88			switch {
89			case t.Title == "" && strings.HasPrefix(line, "# "):
90				t.Title = strings.TrimPrefix(line, "# ")
91			case t.Title != "" && t.Summary == "" && line != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(line, "#"):
92				// A page may open with a blockquote or a list; the marker is
93				// formatting, not part of the one-line summary.
94				t.Summary = strings.TrimLeft(line, ">-* ")
95				return t, nil
96			}
97		}
98		return t, nil
99	}
100

16	func newDoneCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

18			ff           bool
19			pr           bool
20			deleteBranch bool
21			keepWorktree bool
22			push         bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "done [task]",

28	
29	Two integration modes, matching the two shapes a branch's history takes:
30	
31	  --ff    rebase onto the base and fast-forward it. Use when the branch's
32	          commits are worth keeping in the base's history.
33	  --pr    push and open a pull/merge request with gh or glab, leaving the
34	          merge to review and CI. Use when someone (or something) should look
35	          at it first.
36	
37	With neither, dev only reports what it would do.

39	Cleanup is deliberately conservative: the worktree is removed, the task entry
40	is marked done, and the branch is deleted only with --delete-branch. A merged
41	branch that still has unpushed commits is never deleted.`,

47					return err
48				}
49				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
50				if _, err := os.Stat(checkout); err != nil {
51					return fmt.Errorf("%s no longer exists — resume the task first", config.Contract(checkout))
52				}
53	
54				st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
55				if err != nil {
56					return err
57				}

59					return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes: %s.\n"+
60						"Commit them, or park the task with --wip, before finishing it",
61						config.Contract(checkout), st.Breakdown())

63

69					}
70					if push {
71						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
72							return err
73						}
74					}
75					rt := app.Runtime()
76					if t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
77						if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
78							app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
79						}
80						t.RuntimeHandle = ""
81					}
82					t.State = task.Done
83					if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s completed directly on %s\n", task.Done.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Branch)
87					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   no branch or worktree was created or removed")
88					return nil

90

92				if base == "" {
93					base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
94				}
95				if base == "" {

97				}
98

108					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nThe branch is under review — run `dev done --ff` or `dev sweep` after it merges.")
109					return nil
110				case ff:
111					if err := fastForward(ctx, app, t, checkout, base); err != nil {

113					}
114				default:

162		f.BoolVar(&pr, "pr", false, "push and open a pull/merge request instead of merging locally")
163		f.BoolVar(&keepWorktree, "keep-worktree", false, "keep the worktree checkout")
164		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the resulting branch (direct mode pushes its current branch)")
165		// Off by default: a branch is cheap to keep and expensive to recreate, and
166		// "merged" is not always "finished" — work often continues on a branch
167		// after its first integration.

169		return cmd
170	}
171	
172	func directPushHint(push bool) string {
173		if push {
174			return " --push"
175		}
176		return ""
177	}
178	
179	// fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
180	// forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
181	//
182	// merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
183	// branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
184	// a merge commit the user did not ask for.
185	func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
186		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
187		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
188			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
189				"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
190				err, config.Contract(checkout))
191		}
192		// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
193		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
194		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
195			return err
196		}
197		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
198			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
199				"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
200		}
201		return nil
202	}
203	
204	// deleteMergedBranch removes a branch only when git agrees its commits are already
205	// contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
206	func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
207		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
208			return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
209		}
210		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "branch", "-d", branch); err != nil {
211			return fmt.Errorf("could not delete %s: %w", branch, err)
212		}
213		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   deleted    branch %s\n", branch)
214		return nil
215	}
216	
217	// openPR pushes the branch and asks the forge CLI to open a pull/merge
218	// request. When no forge CLI is available dev prints the push result and the
219	// URL to open by hand, rather than failing: the branch being published is the
220	// part that actually matters.
221	func openPR(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
222		if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
223			return err
224		}
225		kind := forge.Detect(ctx, t.RepoPath)
226		f, err := forge.For(kind)
227		if err != nil || !f.Available() {
228			app.warnf("no forge CLI for this remote — the branch is pushed; open the request in your browser")
229			return nil
230		}
231		url, err := f.CreatePR(ctx, checkout, forge.PRRequest{
232			Base: base, Head: t.Branch, Fill: true,
233		})
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		if url != "" {
238			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   opened     %s\n", url)
239		}
240		return nil
241	}

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"os"
7	
8		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
9		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"

13	)
14	
15	func newParkCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
16		var (
17			next   string
18			note   string
19			wip    bool
20			push   bool
21			cold   bool
22			keepRT bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "park [task]",
26			Short: "Stop working on a task without losing the thread",
27			Long: `Park the current task (or the one named) so its runtime session can close.
28	
29	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
30	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
31	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
32	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
33	
34	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
35	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstruct
36	                  it anywhere later with dev resume.
37	
38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()
44				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48	
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59	
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69	
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97	
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114	
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124	
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}
136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {
137					// Free the canonical checkout for other work. The branch remains
138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", t.Base); err != nil {
140						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
141							t.Base, err)
142					}
143				}
144	
145				t.State = target
146				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
147				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
148					return err
149				}
150				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
151				if t.Next != "" {
152					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
153				}
154				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
155				return nil
156			},
157		}
158		f := cmd.Flags()
159		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
160		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
161		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
162		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
163		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
164		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
165		return cmd
166	}
167	
168	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
169	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
170		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
171			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
172		}
173		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
174		return nil
175	}
176	
177	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
178	// directory when no argument is given.
179	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
180		if len(args) == 1 {
181			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
182		}
183		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
184		if err != nil {
185			return nil, err
186		}
187		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
188		if err != nil {
189			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
190				config.Contract(cwd))
191		}
192		return t, nil
193	}

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"context"
6		"fmt"
7		"os"
8		"strings"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/inventory"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/wt"
17		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
18	)
19	
20	// suggestion is one proposed change, with the reason and the exact effect.
21	type suggestion struct {
22		row    inventory.Row
23		action string
24		reason string
25		// apply performs the change. nil means "report only".
26		apply func() error
27	}
28	
29	func newSweepCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
30		var (
31			apply     bool
32			staleDays int
33			yes       bool
34		)
35		cmd := &cobra.Command{
36			Use:   "sweep",
37			Short: "Review stale tasks and drifted state, and act on them",
38			Long: `Show which tasks have gone stale or drifted, and what dev would do about it.
39	
40	Cleanup usually fails not because people are unwilling but because there is no
41	trustworthy way to be sure the work is recoverable. So sweep reports first and
42	only changes things with --apply, confirming each one unless you pass --yes.
43	Nothing here ever deletes uncommitted work.`,
44			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
45			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
46				ctx := ctxOf()
47				tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
48				if err != nil {
49					return err
50				}
51				rt := app.Runtime()
52				rows := inventory.Collect(ctx, tasks, rt, inventory.Options{})
53				stale := time.Duration(staleDays) * 24 * time.Hour
54	
55				var sugg []suggestion
56				for _, r := range rows {
57					sugg = append(sugg, suggestFor(app, ctx, rt, r, stale)...)
58				}
59	
60				// Live sessions no task claims: the other half of a crowded sidebar.
61				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
62					if orphans := inventory.Orphans(sessions, rows); len(orphans) > 0 {
63						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d live session(s) with no task recorded:\n", len(orphans))
64						for _, s := range orphans {
65							dir := "—"
66							if len(s.Dirs) > 0 {
67								dir = config.Contract(s.Dirs[0])
68							}
69							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %-24s %s\n", truncate(s.Label, 24), dir)
70						}
71						fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  → `dev start` in one of those directories to track it, or just close it.")
72					}
73				}
74	
75				if len(sugg) == 0 {
76					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nNothing to sweep — every task matches its recorded state.")
77					return nil
78				}
79	
80				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d suggestion(s):\n\n", len(sugg))
81				for _, s := range sugg {
82					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s %-28s %s\n", s.row.Task.State.Icon(),
83						truncate(s.row.Task.Title(), 28), s.reason)
84					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "     → %s\n", s.action)
85				}
86	
87				if !apply {
88					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nRe-run with --apply to act on these (each is confirmed individually).")
89					return nil
90				}
91	
92				in := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
93				for _, s := range sugg {
94					if s.apply == nil {
95						continue
96					}
97					if !yes && !confirm(app, in, s.action) {
98						continue
99					}
100					if err := s.apply(); err != nil {
101						app.warnf("%s: %v", s.row.Task.ID, err)
102						continue
103					}
104					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  done: %s\n", s.action)
105				}
106				return nil
107			},
108		}
109		f := cmd.Flags()
110		f.BoolVar(&apply, "apply", false, "act on the suggestions instead of only reporting")
111		f.IntVar(&staleDays, "stale-days", 14, "days without a commit before a task counts as stale")
112		f.BoolVar(&yes, "yes", false, "with --apply, do not confirm each change")
113		return cmd
114	}
115	
116	func suggestFor(app *App, ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, r inventory.Row, stale time.Duration) []suggestion {
117		t := r.Task
118		var out []suggestion
119	
120		switch {
121		// A hot task with no live session is the commonest drift: the session was
122		// closed (or the machine rebooted) without parking.
123		case t.State == task.Hot && !r.Live():
124			out = append(out, suggestion{
125				row:    r,
126				reason: fmt.Sprintf("hot but no live session, idle %s", humanAge(r.Age())),
127				action: fmt.Sprintf("mark %s warm", t.ID),
128				apply: func() error {
129					t.State = task.Warm
130					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
131				},
132			})
133	
134		// A warm task nobody has touched in weeks is a candidate for cold: keeping
135		// the worktree costs disk and clutters every listing.
136		case t.State == task.Warm && r.Age() > stale:
137			reason := fmt.Sprintf("warm and untouched for %s", humanAge(r.Age()))
138			if r.Status.Dirty() {
139				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but has uncommitted work",
140					action: "commit or `dev park --wip` before going cold — not changed automatically"})
141				break
142			}
143			if !r.Status.Synced() {
144				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + fmt.Sprintf(", not pushed (%s)", r.Status.Summary()),
145					action: fmt.Sprintf("push %s so it can go cold: dev park %s --cold --push", t.Branch, t.ID)})
146				break
147			}
148			out = append(out, suggestion{
149				row:    r,
150				reason: reason + ", clean and pushed",
151				action: fmt.Sprintf("go cold: remove %s (branch and remote keep the work)", config.Contract(r.Checkout)),
152				apply: func() error {
153					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
154					if t.WorktreePath != "" {
155						if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
156							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath, RuntimeHandle: t.RuntimeHandle,
157						}); err != nil {
158							return err
159						}
160						t.WorktreePath = ""
161					}
162					t.State, t.RuntimeHandle = task.Cold, ""
163					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
164				},
165			})
166	
167		// A done task's entry has served its purpose once the branch is gone.
168		case t.State == task.Done:
169			out = append(out, suggestion{
170				row:    r,
171				reason: "merged",
172				action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s", t.ID),
173				apply:  func() error { return app.Tasks.Delete(t.ID) },
174			})
175		}
176	
177		// Drift that is independent of the lifecycle stage.
178		if r.WorktreeMissing && t.WorktreePath != "" {
179			wtPath := t.WorktreePath
180			out = append(out, suggestion{
181				row:    r,
182				reason: "records a worktree that git no longer knows about",
183				action: fmt.Sprintf("clear the stale worktree path %s", config.Contract(wtPath)),
184				apply: func() error {
185					if err := gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, t.RepoPath); err != nil {
186						return err
187					}
188					t.WorktreePath = ""
189					if t.State == task.Hot || t.State == task.Warm {
190						t.State = task.Cold
191					}
192					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
193				},
194			})
195		}
196		return out
197	}
198	
199	func confirm(app *App, in *bufio.Reader, action string) bool {
200		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s? [y/N] ", action)
201		line, err := in.ReadString('\n')
202		if err != nil {
203			return false
204		}
205		answer := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line))
206		return answer == "y" || answer == "yes"
207	}
208

1	package stats
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"sort"
6		"strings"
7		"time"
8	)
9	
10	// shades run from "no activity" to "a lot", using block characters so the
11	// chart reads at a glance in any terminal font.
12	var shades = []rune{'·', '░', '▒', '▓', '█'}
13	
14	// HeatmapOptions tunes the rendering.
15	type HeatmapOptions struct {
16		Since time.Time
17		Until time.Time
18		// Legend appends the "Less ░ ▒ ▓ █ More" scale.
19		Legend bool
20		// WeekdayLabels prints Mon/Wed/Fri down the left edge.
21		WeekdayLabels bool
22	}
23	
24	// Heatmap renders a GitHub-style contribution grid: one column per week, one
25	// row per weekday, most recent week on the right.
26	//
27	// Scaling is by quartile of the *active* days rather than against the maximum.
28	// One 12-hour outlier would otherwise flatten every ordinary day to the
29	// lightest shade and hide the pattern the chart exists to show.
30	func Heatmap(totals map[string]int, opts HeatmapOptions) string {
31		if opts.Until.IsZero() {
32			opts.Until = time.Now()
33		}
34		if opts.Since.IsZero() {
35			opts.Since = opts.Until.AddDate(-1, 0, 0)
36		}
37	
38		start := startOfWeek(opts.Since)
39		end := opts.Until
40		thresholds := quartiles(totals)
41	
42		// Build the grid: grid[weekday][week].
43		var weeks []time.Time
44		for d := start; !d.After(end); d = d.AddDate(0, 0, 7) {
45			weeks = append(weeks, d)
46		}
47		var b strings.Builder
48	
49		b.WriteString(monthHeader(weeks, opts.WeekdayLabels))
50		for wd := 0; wd < 7; wd++ {
51			label := "       "
52			if opts.WeekdayLabels {
53				switch wd {
54				case 1:
55					label = "   Mon "
56				case 3:
57					label = "   Wed "
58				case 5:
59					label = "   Fri "
60				}
61			} else {
62				label = ""
63			}
64			var row strings.Builder
65			for _, weekStart := range weeks {
66				day := weekStart.AddDate(0, 0, wd)
67				if day.Before(opts.Since) || day.After(end) {
68					row.WriteRune(' ')
69					continue
70				}
71				row.WriteRune(shadeFor(totals[day.Format(dayFormat)], thresholds))
72			}
73			b.WriteString(label)
74			// Trailing blanks are days that have not happened yet; printing them
75			// leaves invisible whitespace that breaks copy-paste and diffs.
76			b.WriteString(strings.TrimRight(row.String(), " "))
77			b.WriteByte('\n')
78		}
79	
80		if opts.Legend {
81			pad := ""
82			if opts.WeekdayLabels {
83				pad = "       "
84			}
85			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n%sLess %c %c %c %c More\n", pad, shades[1], shades[2], shades[3], shades[4])
86		}
87		return b.String()
88	}
89	
90	// monthHeader labels the week columns where a new month begins.
91	//
92	// A week is attributed to the month containing its midpoint, so a week
93	// straddling a boundary is labelled once and on the right side. A month is
94	// only labelled when it owns enough columns to fit its name without colliding
95	// with the next one — a partial month at either edge is left unlabelled rather
96	// than shown in the wrong place.
97	func monthHeader(weeks []time.Time, indent bool) string {
98		row := make([]byte, len(weeks))
99		for i := range row {
100			row[i] = ' '
101		}
102		// Run-length encode the months across the columns.
103		type run struct {
104			month time.Month
105			start int
106			width int
107		}
108		var runs []run
109		for i, w := range weeks {
110			m := w.AddDate(0, 0, 3).Month() // midpoint of the week
111			if n := len(runs); n > 0 && runs[n-1].month == m {
112				runs[n-1].width++
113				continue
114			}
115			runs = append(runs, run{month: m, start: i, width: 1})
116		}
117		const label = 3
118		for _, r := range runs {
119			// Needs room for the name plus a separating space before the next run.
120			if r.width < label+1 || r.start+label > len(row) {
121				continue
122			}
123			copy(row[r.start:], r.month.String()[:label])
124		}
125		prefix := ""
126		if indent {
127			prefix = "       "
128		}
129		return prefix + strings.TrimRight(string(row), " ") + "\n"
130	}
131	
132	func allSpace(b []byte) bool {
133		for _, c := range b {
134			if c != ' ' {
135				return false
136			}
137		}
138		return true
139	}
140	
141	func shadeFor(seconds int, thresholds [3]int) rune {
142		switch {
143		case seconds <= 0:
144			return shades[0]
145		case seconds <= thresholds[0]:
146			return shades[1]
147		case seconds <= thresholds[1]:
148			return shades[2]
149		case seconds <= thresholds[2]:
150			return shades[3]
151		default:
152			return shades[4]
153		}
154	}
155	
156	// quartiles returns the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile of the days that had
157	// any activity at all.
158	func quartiles(totals map[string]int) [3]int {
159		var vals []int
160		for _, v := range totals {
161			if v > 0 {
162				vals = append(vals, v)
163			}
164		}
165		if len(vals) == 0 {
166			return [3]int{1, 2, 3}
167		}
168		sort.Ints(vals)
169		at := func(p float64) int {
170			i := int(float64(len(vals)-1) * p)
171			return vals[i]
172		}
173		q := [3]int{at(0.25), at(0.50), at(0.75)}
174		// Keep the thresholds strictly increasing so distinct values map to
175		// distinct shades even on a tiny sample.
176		for i := 1; i < 3; i++ {
177			if q[i] <= q[i-1] {
178				q[i] = q[i-1] + 1
179			}
180		}
181		return q
182	}
183	
184	func startOfWeek(t time.Time) time.Time {
185		d := time.Date(t.Year(), t.Month(), t.Day(), 0, 0, 0, 0, t.Location())
186		return d.AddDate(0, 0, -int(d.Weekday()))
187	}
188	
189	// HumanDuration renders seconds as the compact form a report wants: "4h 20m".
190	func HumanDuration(seconds int) string {
191		d := time.Duration(seconds) * time.Second
192		switch {
193		case d < time.Minute:
194			return fmt.Sprintf("%ds", int(d.Seconds()))
195		case d < time.Hour:
196			return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", int(d.Minutes()))
197		case d < 24*time.Hour:
198			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh %dm", int(d.Hours()), int(d.Minutes())%60)
199		default:
200			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
201		}
202	}
203	
204	// Sparkline renders a compact per-repo bar using the same shade ramp.
205	func Sparkline(value, max int, width int) string {
206		if max <= 0 || width <= 0 {
207			return ""
208		}
209		filled := value * width / max
210		if filled == 0 && value > 0 {
211			filled = 1
212		}
213		return strings.Repeat(string(shades[4]), filled) + strings.Repeat(" ", width-filled)
214	}

```text
1	// Package stats records where development time actually goes, and renders it
2	// as a contribution-style heatmap.
3	//
4	// Two sources, because neither alone is honest. A sampler watches live agent
5	// and terminal sessions, which is the only way to count the hours spent
6	// reading and debugging rather than committing. Git history backfills the days
7	// before dev was installed and survives a lost database. WakaTime, when
8	// enabled, adds editor time dev cannot observe from the terminal.
9	package stats
10	
11	import (
12		"database/sql"
13		"os"
14		"path/filepath"
15		"time"
16	
17		_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
18	)
19	
20	// Source labels where a measurement came from, so double counting is visible
21	// rather than silent: the same hour can legitimately appear from the sampler
22	// and from WakaTime, and a query decides which to trust.
23	type Source string
24	
25	const (
26		// SourceSession is dev's own sampler watching live runtime sessions.
27		SourceSession Source = "session"
28		// SourceGit is derived from commit timestamps.
29		SourceGit Source = "git"
30		// SourceWakaTime is imported from the WakaTime API.
31		SourceWakaTime Source = "wakatime"
32	)
33	
34	// Store is the activity database.
35	type Store struct{ db *sql.DB }
36	
37	// Open creates or opens the database at path.
38	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
39		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
40			return nil, err
41		}
42		// A short busy timeout matters: the sampler may run from cron while an
43		// interactive `dev stats` is reading.
44		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", path+"?_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)")
45		if err != nil {
46			return nil, err
47		}
48		s := &Store{db: db}
49		if err := s.migrate(); err != nil {
50			db.Close()
51			return nil, err
52		}
53		return s, nil
54	}
55	
56	// Close releases the database.
57	func (s *Store) Close() error { return s.db.Close() }
58	
59	func (s *Store) migrate() error {
60		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
61	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS activity (
62	  day     TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- local date, YYYY-MM-DD
63	  repo    TEXT    NOT NULL,
64	  branch  TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
65	  source  TEXT    NOT NULL,
66	  seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
67	  PRIMARY KEY (day, repo, branch, source)
68	);
69	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_day  ON activity(day);
70	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS activity_repo ON activity(repo);
71	
72	-- Records the last successful run of each collector, so a backfill can pick up
73	-- where it left off instead of rescanning every repo's whole history.
74	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS collector (
75	  name    TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
76	  last_at INTEGER NOT NULL
77	);
78	`)
79		return err
80	}
81	
82	// Entry is one measurement.
83	type Entry struct {
84		Day     time.Time
85		Repo    string
86		Branch  string
87		Source  Source
88		Seconds int
89	}
90	
91	// Add accumulates seconds onto a (day, repo, branch, source) bucket.
92	func (s *Store) Add(entries ...Entry) error {
93		if len(entries) == 0 {
94			return nil
95		}
96		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
97		if err != nil {
98			return err
99		}
100		defer tx.Rollback()
101	
102		stmt, err := tx.Prepare(`
103	INSERT INTO activity (day, repo, branch, source, seconds) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
104	ON CONFLICT (day, repo, branch, source) DO UPDATE SET seconds = seconds + excluded.seconds`)
105		if err != nil {
106			return err
107		}
108		defer stmt.Close()
109	
110		for _, e := range entries {
111			if e.Seconds <= 0 || e.Repo == "" {
112				continue
113			}
114			if _, err := stmt.Exec(e.Day.Format(dayFormat), e.Repo, e.Branch, string(e.Source), e.Seconds); err != nil {
115				return err
116			}
117		}
118		return tx.Commit()
119	}
120	
121	// Set replaces a bucket rather than accumulating. Used by importers that are
122	// re-runnable: WakaTime reports the same day's total again on every import, so
123	// adding would inflate it.
124	func (s *Store) Set(entries ...Entry) error {
125		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
126		if err != nil {
127			return err
128		}
129		defer tx.Rollback()
130	
131		stmt, err := tx.Prepare(`
132	INSERT INTO activity (day, repo, branch, source, seconds) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
133	ON CONFLICT (day, repo, branch, source) DO UPDATE SET seconds = excluded.seconds`)
134		if err != nil {
135			return err
136		}
137		defer stmt.Close()
138	
139		for _, e := range entries {
140			if e.Repo == "" {
141				continue
142			}
143			if _, err := stmt.Exec(e.Day.Format(dayFormat), e.Repo, e.Branch, string(e.Source), e.Seconds); err != nil {
144				return err
145			}
146		}
147		return tx.Commit()
148	}
149	
150	const dayFormat = "2006-01-02"
151	
152	// Query narrows a report.
153	type Query struct {
154		Since time.Time
155		Until time.Time
156		Repo  string
157		// Sources limits which collectors count. Empty means all of them.
158		Sources []Source
159	}
160	
161	func (q Query) where() (string, []any) {
162		clause := "WHERE day >= ? AND day <= ?"
163		args := []any{q.Since.Format(dayFormat), q.Until.Format(dayFormat)}
164		if q.Repo != "" {
165			clause += " AND repo LIKE ?"
166			args = append(args, "%"+q.Repo+"%")
167		}
168		if len(q.Sources) > 0 {
169			clause += " AND source IN (" + placeholders(len(q.Sources)) + ")"
170			for _, s := range q.Sources {
171				args = append(args, string(s))
172			}
173		}
174		return clause, args
175	}
176	
177	func placeholders(n int) string {
178		if n == 0 {
179			return ""
180		}
181		out := make([]byte, 0, n*2-1)
182		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
183			if i > 0 {
184				out = append(out, ',')
185			}
186			out = append(out, '?')
187		}
188		return string(out)
189	}
190	
191	// DayTotals returns seconds per calendar day.
192	func (s *Store) DayTotals(q Query) (map[string]int, error) {
193		clause, args := q.where()
194		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT day, SUM(seconds) FROM activity `+clause+` GROUP BY day`, args...)
195		if err != nil {
196			return nil, err
197		}
198		defer rows.Close()
199	
200		out := map[string]int{}
201		for rows.Next() {
202			var day string
203			var secs int
204			if err := rows.Scan(&day, &secs); err != nil {
205				return nil, err
206			}
207			out[day] = secs
208		}
209		return out, rows.Err()
210	}
211	
212	// RepoTotal is one row of the per-repo breakdown.
213	type RepoTotal struct {
214		Repo    string
215		Seconds int
216		Days    int
217		Last    string
218	}
219	
220	// RepoTotals returns seconds per repository, busiest first.
221	func (s *Store) RepoTotals(q Query) ([]RepoTotal, error) {
222		clause, args := q.where()
223		rows, err := s.db.Query(`
224	SELECT repo, SUM(seconds) AS secs, COUNT(DISTINCT day) AS days, MAX(day)
225	FROM activity `+clause+`
226	GROUP BY repo ORDER BY secs DESC`, args...)
227		if err != nil {
228			return nil, err
229		}
230		defer rows.Close()
231	
232		var out []RepoTotal
233		for rows.Next() {
234			var r RepoTotal
235			if err := rows.Scan(&r.Repo, &r.Seconds, &r.Days, &r.Last); err != nil {
236				return nil, err
237			}
238			out = append(out, r)
239		}
240		return out, rows.Err()
241	}
242	
243	// RepoDayTotals returns per-day seconds for one repository, for a per-repo
244	// heatmap.
245	func (s *Store) RepoDayTotals(repo string, q Query) (map[string]int, error) {
246		q.Repo = repo
247		return s.DayTotals(q)
248	}
249	
250	// MarkCollected records that a collector ran, so incremental runs know their
251	// starting point.
252	func (s *Store) MarkCollected(name string, at time.Time) error {
253		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
254	INSERT INTO collector (name, last_at) VALUES (?, ?)
255	ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE SET last_at = excluded.last_at`, name, at.Unix())
256		return err
257	}
258	
259	// LastCollected reports when a collector last ran, zero when never.
260	func (s *Store) LastCollected(name string) time.Time {
261		var unix int64
262		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT last_at FROM collector WHERE name = ?`, name).Scan(&unix); err != nil {
263			return time.Time{}
264		}
265		return time.Unix(unix, 0)
266	}
267	
268	// Empty reports whether anything has been recorded yet, so the CLI can explain
269	// how to start collecting instead of printing a blank chart.
270	func (s *Store) Empty() bool {
271		var n int
272		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activity`).Scan(&n); err != nil {
273			return true
274		}
275		return n == 0
276	}
277	
278	// Path is where the database lives inside a state directory.
279	func Path(stateDir string) string { return filepath.Join(stateDir, "stats.db") }
280

236				start, err := parseSince(since, until)
237				if err != nil {
238					return err
239				}
240				w := &stats.WakaTime{APIKey: key}
241				n, err := w.Import(ctx, store, start, until)
242				if err != nil {

244				}

253	// parseSince accepts a relative window ("30d", "6mo", "1y") or an absolute
254	// date. Relative is what people actually type; absolute is what scripts want.
255	func parseSince(s string, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
256		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
257		if s == "" {
258			return now.AddDate(-1, 0, 0), nil
259		}
260		if d, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02", s, time.Local); err == nil {
261			return d, nil
262		}
263		var n int
264		var unit string
265		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(s, "%d%s", &n, &unit); err != nil || n <= 0 {
266			return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot parse --since %q: want 30d, 6mo, 1y or YYYY-MM-DD", s)
267		}
268		switch strings.ToLower(unit) {
269		case "d", "day", "days":
270			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n), nil
271		case "w", "week", "weeks":
272			return now.AddDate(0, 0, -n*7), nil
273		case "mo", "month", "months":
274			return now.AddDate(0, -n, 0), nil
275		case "y", "yr", "year", "years":
276			return now.AddDate(-n, 0, 0), nil
277		}
278		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("unknown unit %q in --since: want d, w, mo or y", unit)
279	}

8	// PostCreate accepts either of two TOML shapes, because both read naturally:
9	//
10	//	post_create = "auto"
11	//	post_create = ["uv sync", "npm ci"]
12	type PostCreate struct {
13		Auto     bool
14		Commands []string
15	}
16	
17	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
18	func (p *PostCreate) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
19		switch t := v.(type) {
20		case string:
21			if t != "auto" {
22				return fmt.Errorf("post_create: %q is not a valid string form (use \"auto\" or a list of commands)", t)
23			}
24			*p = PostCreate{Auto: true}
25			return nil
26		case []any:
27			cmds := make([]string, 0, len(t))
28			for i, e := range t {
29				s, ok := e.(string)
30				if !ok {
31					return fmt.Errorf("post_create[%d]: want a command string, got %T", i, e)
32				}
33				cmds = append(cmds, s)
34			}
35			*p = PostCreate{Commands: cmds}
36			return nil
37		default:
38			return fmt.Errorf("post_create: want \"auto\" or a list of command strings, got %T", v)
39		}
40	}
41	
42	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler so a config round-trips.
43	func (p PostCreate) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
44		if p.Auto {
45			return []byte(`"auto"`), nil
46		}
47		out := []byte("[")
48		for i, c := range p.Commands {
49			if i > 0 {
50				out = append(out, ", "...)
51			}
52			out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%q", c)...)
53		}
54		return append(out, ']'), nil
55	}
56	
57	// Duration is a time.Duration written in TOML as a Go duration string
58	// ("10m", "90s"), which is friendlier than a bare number of seconds.
59	type Duration struct{ time.Duration }
60	
61	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
62	func (d *Duration) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
63		switch t := v.(type) {
64		case string:
65			parsed, err := time.ParseDuration(t)
66			if err != nil {
67				return fmt.Errorf("duration %q: %w", t, err)
68			}
69			d.Duration = parsed
70			return nil
71		case int64:
72			d.Duration = time.Duration(t) * time.Second
73			return nil
74		default:
75			return fmt.Errorf("duration: want a string like \"10m\", got %T", v)
76		}
77	}
78	
79	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler.
80	func (d Duration) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
81		return []byte(fmt.Sprintf("%q", d.Duration.String())), nil
82	}

1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"os"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// XDG base directories, resolved the way the spec prescribes: honor the
10	// environment variable when it holds an absolute path, otherwise fall back to
11	// the documented default under $HOME.
12	
13	func xdgDir(envVar, fallback string) string {
14		if v := os.Getenv(envVar); filepath.IsAbs(v) {
15			return v
16		}
17		return filepath.Join(home(), fallback)
18	}
19	
20	func home() string {
21		if h, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil && h != "" {
22			return h
23		}
24		return os.Getenv("HOME")
25	}
26	
27	// ConfigHome is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default ~/.config).
28	func ConfigHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ".config") }
29	
30	// DataHome is $XDG_DATA_HOME (default ~/.local/share).
31	func DataHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_DATA_HOME", ".local/share") }
32	
33	// CacheHome is $XDG_CACHE_HOME (default ~/.cache).
34	func CacheHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CACHE_HOME", ".cache") }
35	
36	// ConfigFile is the path dev loads its TOML configuration from.
37	func ConfigFile() string { return filepath.Join(ConfigHome(), "dev", "config.toml") }
38	
39	// Expand resolves a leading ~ and any environment variables in p, then makes
40	// the result absolute. Paths in config.toml are written by humans, so both
41	// "~/Worktrees" and "$WORK/trees" have to work.
42	func Expand(p string) string {
43		if p == "" {
44			return ""
45		}
46		p = os.ExpandEnv(p)
47		switch {
48		case p == "~":
49			p = home()
50		case strings.HasPrefix(p, "~/"):
51			p = filepath.Join(home(), p[2:])
52		}
53		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(p); err == nil {
54			return abs
55		}
56		return filepath.Clean(p)
57	}
58	
59	// Contract renders p with $HOME collapsed back to ~, for display only.
60	func Contract(p string) string {
61		h := home()
62		if h != "" && p == h {
63			return "~"
64		}
65		if h != "" && strings.HasPrefix(p, h+string(filepath.Separator)) {
66			return "~" + p[len(h):]
67		}
68		return p
69	}

220	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
221	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
222	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
223	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
224		cfg := Default()
225		if path == "" {
226			path = ConfigFile()
227		}
228		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
229		switch {
230		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
231			return cfg, nil
232		case err != nil:
233			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
234		}
235		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
236			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
237			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
238			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
239		}
240		cfg.Source = path
241		return cfg, cfg.Validate()

244	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a

247		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
248		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "none":
249		default:
250			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
251		}
252		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
253			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
254		}
255		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
256			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
257		}
258		switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
259		case "", "flat", "preserve":
260		default:
261			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
262		}
263		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
264			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
265		}
266		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
267			return fmt.Errorf("forge.remote_limit must be zero (use default) or positive")
268		}
269		validStrategy := func(v string) bool {
270			switch v {
271			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
272				return true
273			}
274			return false
275		}
276		if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
277			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
278		}
279		for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
280			if !validStrategy(strategy) {
281				return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",
282					ecosystem, strategy)
283			}
284		}
285		seen := map[string]string{}
286		for i, t := range c.TUI.Tools {
287			switch {
288			case t.Key == "":
289				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key is required", i)
290			case t.Run == "":
291				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d] (%s): run is required", i, t.Key)

295					i, t.Key, binding)
296			}
297			if prev, ok := seen[t.Key]; ok {
298				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is already bound to %q", i, t.Key, prev)
299			}
300			seen[t.Key] = t.Name
301		}
302		return nil
303	}

1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123	
124		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
125		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
126	}
127	
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141	
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}

1	package task
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"io/fs"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"regexp"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	
14		"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}
241

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
38		Bare bool
39		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
40		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
41		// initialise them.
42		HasGit bool
43	}
44	
45	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
46	func (r Repo) Display() string {
47		if r.Category == "" {
48			return r.Name
49		}
50		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
51	}
52	
53	// Options tunes discovery.
54	type Options struct {
55		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
56		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
57		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
58		MaxDepth int
59		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
60		IncludeNonRepos bool
61	}
62	
63	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
64	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
65	
66	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
67	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
68	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
69		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
70		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
71		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
72		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
73	}
74	
75	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
76	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
77	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
78	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
79		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
80			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
81		}
82		seen := map[string]bool{}
83		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
84		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
85		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
86		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
87		identities := map[string]bool{}
88		var out []Repo
89	
90		for _, root := range roots {
91			info, err := os.Stat(root)
92			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
93				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
94			}
95			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
96	
97			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
98				if err != nil {
99					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
100				}
101				if ctx.Err() != nil {
102					return ctx.Err()
103				}
104				if path == rootClean {
105					return nil
106				}
107				name := d.Name()
108				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
109				isDir := d.IsDir()
110				if isLink {
111					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
112					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
113					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
114					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
115						isDir = info.IsDir()
116					}
117				}
118				if !isDir {
119					return nil
120				}
121				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
122					return filepath.SkipDir
123				}
124	
125				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
126				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
127	
128				if isRepoDir(path) {
129					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
130					if real == "" {
131						real = path
132					}
133					bare := isBareDir(path)
134					identity := real
135					if !bare {
136						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
137							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
138							// project in the repo inventory.
139							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
140								return filepath.SkipDir
141							}
142							identity = g.GitCommonDir
143							real = g.MainRoot
144						}
145					}
146					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
147						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
148						out = append(out, Repo{
149							Name:     name,
150							Path:     path,
151							RealPath: real,
152							Symlink:  isLink,
153							Root:     rootClean,
154							Category: filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
155							Bare:     bare,
156							HasGit:   true,
157						})
158					}
159					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
160					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
161					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
162					return filepath.SkipDir
163				}
164				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
165					return filepath.SkipDir
166				}
167				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
168					if !seen[path] {
169						seen[path] = true
170						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
171					}
172				}
173				return nil
174			})
175			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
176				return out, ctx.Err()
177			}
178		}
179	
180		for i := range out {
181			if out[i].Category == "." {
182				out[i].Category = ""
183			}
184		}
185		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
186			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
187				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
188			}
189			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
190		})
191		return out, nil
192	}
193	
194	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
195	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
196	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
197		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
198			return true
199		}
200		return isBareDir(path)
201	}
202	
203	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
204	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
205		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
206			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
207				return false
208			}
209		}
210		return true
211	}
212	
213	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
214	//
215	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
216	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
217	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
218	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
219		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
220		if err != nil {
221			return Repo{}, nil, err
222		}
223		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
224			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
225				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
226				if real == "" {
227					real = g.MainRoot
228				}
229				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
230				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
231				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
232				return Repo{
233					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
234					Symlink: real != abs, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
235				}, nil, nil
236			}
237		}
238		for _, r := range all {
239			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
240				return r, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
244		var hits []Repo
245		for _, r := range all {
246			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
247				hits = append(hits, r)
248			}
249		}
250		switch len(hits) {
251		case 1:
252			return hits[0], nil, nil
253		case 0:
254			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
255		default:
256			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
257		}
258	}
259	
260	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
261	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
262	
263	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
264	
265	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
266	type AmbiguousError struct {
267		Ref        string
268		Candidates []Repo
269	}
270	
271	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
272		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
273		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
274			names[i] = c.Display()
275		}
276		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
277	}

1	// Package forge wraps the GitHub and GitLab CLIs. Both are optional: every
2	// entry point degrades to plain git, because a workflow that hard-depends on a
3	// forge CLI being installed and authenticated stops working on exactly the
4	// machines where you most need it.
5	package forge
6	
7	import (
8		"bytes"

21	// Kind identifies a forge.
22	type Kind string
23	
24	const (
25		// GitHub is served by the gh CLI.
26		GitHub Kind = "github"
27		// GitLab is served by the glab CLI.
28		GitLab Kind = "gitlab"
29		// Unknown is any other host, or none.
30		Unknown Kind = "unknown"
31	)
32	
33	// ErrNoCLI reports that the forge's CLI is not installed.

35		Kind Kind

37	}

45		Kind() Kind
46		// Bin is the CLI binary name.

51		// CreateRepo creates a remote repository from an existing local one.
52		CreateRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string, req RepoRequest) (string, error)
53		// CloneURL renders the clone target for an owner/name reference.
54		CloneURL(ref string) string
