105	// Detect infers the forge for a checkout from its origin remote. A repo with
106	// no remote, or one on a self-hosted host neither CLI knows, resolves to
107	// Unknown — which callers must treat as "use plain git".
108	func Detect(ctx context.Context, dir string) Kind {
109		return FromURL(gitx.Remote(ctx, dir, "origin"))
110	}
111	
112	// FromURL classifies a remote URL.
113	func FromURL(url string) Kind {
114		u := strings.ToLower(url)
115		switch {
116		case u == "":
117			return Unknown
118		case strings.Contains(u, "github.com"), strings.Contains(u, "github."):
119			return GitHub
120		case strings.Contains(u, "gitlab.com"), strings.Contains(u, "gitlab."):
121			return GitLab
122		}
123		return Unknown
124	}
125	
126	// For returns the adapter for a kind.
127	func For(k Kind) (Forge, error) {
128		switch k {
129		case GitHub:
130			return &gh{}, nil
131		case GitLab:
132			return &glab{}, nil
133		}
134		return nil, errors.New("no forge CLI for this remote; falling back to plain git")
135	}
136	
137	// Preferred returns the first available forge, for commands like `repo new`
138	// that have no existing remote to infer from.
139	func Preferred() (Forge, error) {
140		for _, f := range []Forge{&gh{}, &glab{}} {
141			if f.Available() {
142				return f, nil
143			}
144		}
145		return nil, errors.New("neither gh nor glab is installed")
146	}
147	
148	// run executes a forge CLI, streaming stderr through so the user sees the
149	// CLI's own authentication prompts and error messages verbatim.
150	func run(ctx context.Context, bin, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
151		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, args...)
152		cmd.Dir = dir
153		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
154		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
155		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
156		cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
157		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
158			detail := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
159			if detail != "" {
160				return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %s: %w",
161					bin, strings.Join(args, " "), detail, err)
162			}
163			return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %w", bin, strings.Join(args, " "), err)
164		}
165		return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), nil
166	}
167	
168	func have(bin string) bool {
169		_, err := exec.LookPath(bin)
170		return err == nil
171	}
172	
173	// IdentityFromURL returns a forge and owner/name identity for an HTTPS or SSH
174	// Git remote. It is used to match remote inventories to local clones without
175	// assuming the checkout directory has the same name.
176	func IdentityFromURL(raw string) (Kind, string) {
177		kind := FromURL(raw)
178		if kind == Unknown {
179			return Unknown, ""
180		}
181		s := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
182		if strings.Contains(s, "://") {
183			if parsed, err := url.Parse(s); err == nil {
184				s = strings.TrimPrefix(parsed.Path, "/")
185			}
186		} else if at := strings.IndexByte(s, '@'); at >= 0 {
187			// SCP-style SSH: git@github.com:owner/repo.git
188			s = s[at+1:]
189			if colon := strings.IndexByte(s, ':'); colon >= 0 {
190				s = s[colon+1:]
191			}
192		}
193		s = strings.Trim(strings.TrimSuffix(s, ".git"), "/")
194		return kind, s
195	}

1	package gitx
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
10	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
11	type Repo struct {
12		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
13		Root string
14		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
15		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
16		GitCommonDir string
17		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
18		Name string
19		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
20		// the main checkout.
21		IsLinkedWorktree bool
22		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
23		MainRoot string
24		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
25		Bare bool
26	}
27	
28	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
29	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
30	
31	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
32	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
33		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
34		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
35		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
36			"rev-parse",
37			"--path-format=absolute",
38			"--show-toplevel",
39			"--git-common-dir",
40			"--is-bare-repository",
41		)
42		if err != nil {
43			return Repo{}, err
44		}
45		f := lines(out)
46		r := Repo{}
47		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
48		switch len(f) {
49		case 3:
50			r.Root = f[0]
51			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
52			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
53		case 2:
54			r.GitCommonDir = f[0]
55			r.Bare = f[1] == "true"
56		default:
57			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
58		}
59	
60		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
61		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
62		if r.Bare {
63			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
64		} else {
65			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
66		}
67		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.Root != r.MainRoot
68		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
69		if r.Bare {
70			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
71			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
72			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
73				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
74			}
75		}
76		return r, nil
77	}
78	
79	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
80	// a full Discover.
81	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
82		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
83		return err == nil
84	}
85	
86	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
87	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
88	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
89	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
90	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
91		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
92			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
93				return b
94			}
95		}
96		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
97			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
98				return cand
99			}
100		}
101		return ""
102	}
103	
104	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
105	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
106		if name == "" {
107			name = "origin"
108		}
109		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
110		if err != nil {
111			return ""
112		}
113		return out
114	}

9	// Status is the live git state of one checkout — everything dev's inventory
10	// shows about a task without persisting any of it.
11	type Status struct {
12		Branch   string `json:"branch,omitempty"`
13		Detached bool   `json:"detached"`
14		// Upstream is the tracking ref (e.g. "origin/feat/auth"), empty when the
15		// branch has never been published.
16		Upstream string `json:"upstream,omitempty"`
17		Ahead    int    `json:"ahead"`
18		Behind   int    `json:"behind"`
19		// Changed counts unique changed paths. Staged and Unstaged are index /
20		// working-tree views and can overlap when one path has both kinds of
21		// changes; Changed does not double-count it.
22		Changed   int `json:"changed"`
23		Staged    int `json:"staged"`
24		Unstaged  int `json:"unstaged"`
25		Untracked int `json:"untracked"`
26		// Added, Modified, Deleted and Renamed classify status letters. One path
27		// can contribute to two when its staged and unstaged states differ.
28		Added    int `json:"added"`
29		Modified int `json:"modified"`
30		Deleted  int `json:"deleted"`
31		Renamed  int `json:"renamed"`
32		// Conflicted counts unmerged paths; a non-zero value means the checkout is
33		// mid-merge or mid-rebase and must not be touched automatically.
34		Conflicted int `json:"conflicted"`
35	}
36	
37	// Dirty reports uncommitted work of any kind.
38	func (s Status) Dirty() bool { return s.Changed > 0 }
39	
40	// Published reports whether the branch has an upstream at all.
41	func (s Status) Published() bool { return s.Upstream != "" }
42	
43	// Synced reports a branch that is published and exactly level with upstream.
44	func (s Status) Synced() bool { return s.Published() && s.Ahead == 0 && s.Behind == 0 }
45	
46	// Summary renders the compact, starship-like column used throughout dev:
47	//
48	//	⇕⇡2⇣1 =1 +3 !2 ?4
49	//
50	// Divergence, conflicts, staged, unstaged and untracked paths remain separate
51	// so "dirty" says how and by how much, rather than collapsing to one ●.
52	func (s Status) Summary() string {
53		var parts []string
54		switch {
55		case s.Ahead > 0 && s.Behind > 0:
56			parts = append(parts, "⇕⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead)+"⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
57		case s.Ahead > 0:
58			parts = append(parts, "⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead))
59		case s.Behind > 0:
60			parts = append(parts, "⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
61		}
62		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
63			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted))
64		}
65		if s.Staged > 0 {
66			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged))
67		}
68		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
69			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged))
70		}
71		if s.Untracked > 0 {
72			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked))
73		}
74		if len(parts) == 0 {
75			if !s.Published() {
76				return "local"
77			}
78			return "clean"
79		}
80		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
81	}
82	
83	// Breakdown renders the detailed change count shown by `dev status` and the
84	// TUI detail pane. Changed is the unique-path total; staged and unstaged may
85	// overlap, which is stated by presenting them as categories rather than a sum.
86	func (s Status) Breakdown() string {
87		if s.Changed == 0 {
88			return "0 changed paths"
89		}
90		var parts []string
91		if s.Staged > 0 {
92			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged)+" staged")
93		}
94		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
95			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged)+" unstaged")
96		}
97		if s.Untracked > 0 {
98			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked)+" untracked")
99		}
100		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
101			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted)+" conflicted")
102		}
103		return strconv.Itoa(s.Changed) + " changed paths (" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")"
104	}

106	// TypeBreakdown classifies the status letters when that detail is available.
107	func (s Status) TypeBreakdown() string {
108		var parts []string
109		for _, item := range []struct {
110			n    int
111			name string
112		}{
113			{s.Added, "added"}, {s.Modified, "modified"}, {s.Deleted, "deleted"},
114			{s.Renamed, "renamed/copied"},
115		} {
116			if item.n > 0 {
117				parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(item.n)+" "+item.name)
118			}
119		}
120		return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
121	}
122	
123	// StatusOf reads the porcelain v2 status of the checkout at dir. Porcelain v2
124	// is the documented machine-readable format: it reports branch, upstream and
125	// ahead/behind in the same pass as the file states, so one process gives dev
126	// everything it needs.
127	func StatusOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Status, error) {
128		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=normal", "-z")
129		if err != nil {
130			return Status{}, err
131		}
132		var s Status
133		for _, rec := range nulLines(out) {
134			if rec == "" {
135				continue
136			}
137			switch rec[0] {
138			case '#':
139				parseBranchHeader(rec, &s)
140			case '1', '2':
141				// "1 XY ..." ordinary change, "2 XY ..." rename/copy. X is
142				// staged, Y unstaged. This record is one unique changed path even
143				// when both sides are non-dot.
144				f := strings.Fields(rec)
145				if len(f) < 2 || len(f[1]) < 2 {
146					continue
147				}
148				s.Changed++
149				x, y := f[1][0], f[1][1]
150				if x != '.' {
151					s.Staged++
152				}
153				if y != '.' {
154					s.Unstaged++
155				}
156				classifyChange(x, &s)
157				classifyChange(y, &s)
158			case 'u':
159				s.Changed++
160				s.Conflicted++
161			case '?':
162				s.Changed++
163				s.Untracked++
164			}
165		}
166		return s, nil
167	}
168	
169	func classifyChange(code byte, s *Status) {
170		switch code {
171		case 'A':
172			s.Added++
173		case 'M', 'T':
174			s.Modified++
175		case 'D':
176			s.Deleted++
177		case 'R', 'C':
178			s.Renamed++
179		}
180	}
181	
182	func parseBranchHeader(rec string, s *Status) {
183		f := strings.Fields(rec)
184		if len(f) < 3 {
185			return
186		}
187		switch f[1] {
188		case "branch.head":
189			if f[2] == "(detached)" {
190				s.Detached = true
191			} else {
192				s.Branch = f[2]
193			}
194		case "branch.upstream":
195			s.Upstream = f[2]
196		case "branch.ab":
197			// "# branch.ab +2 -1"
198			if len(f) < 4 {
199				return
200			}
201			s.Ahead, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[2], "+"))
202			s.Behind, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[3], "-"))
203		}
204	}
205	
206	// LastCommit reports the author timestamp of HEAD as a Unix epoch, and the
207	// subject line. Used to age a task in `dev sweep`.
208	func LastCommit(ctx context.Context, dir string) (unix int64, subject string, err error) {
209		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "log", "-1", "--format=%at%x00%s")
210		if err != nil || out == "" {
211			return 0, "", err
212		}
213		ts, subj, _ := strings.Cut(out, "\x00")
214		unix, _ = strconv.ParseInt(ts, 10, 64)
215		return unix, subj, nil
216	}
217	
218	// WipCommit stages everything and records a checkpoint commit.
219	//
220	// A checkpoint commit is deliberately preferred over `git stash`: a stash is
221	// invisible in the log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never
222	// travel to another machine, which is exactly what parking a task needs.
223	func WipCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, message string) (bool, error) {
224		st, err := StatusOf(ctx, dir)
225		if err != nil {
226			return false, err
227		}
228		if !st.Dirty() {
229			return false, nil
230		}
231		if st.Conflicted > 0 {
232			return false, &Error{Args: []string{"commit"}, Dir: dir,
233				Stderr: "checkout has unmerged paths; resolve the conflict before parking"}
234		}
235		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
236			return false, err
237		}
238		if message == "" {
239			message = "wip: checkpoint"
240		}
241		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", message); err != nil {
242			return false, err
243		}
244		return true, nil
245	}

The TUI is explicitly dependency-injected: `internal/tui.Model` owns only interaction/render state, while `internal/cli/runTUI` supplies every side effect through `tui.Actions`. Adding a tries view is mechanically straightforward but cross-cutting: extend `View/Views`, add try rows/cursor/filter/render/detail/footer branches and action callbacks, then wire domain operations in `runTUI`; destructive archive/delete must use an explicit confirmation mode rather than Enter.

21	// harness runs dev commands against an isolated HOME, config and scan root.

31	func newHarness(t *testing.T) *harness {
32		t.Helper()
33		home := t.TempDir()
34		scanRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Program")
35		wtRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Worktrees")
36		if err := os.MkdirAll(scanRoot, 0o755); err != nil {
37			t.Fatal(err)
38		}
39	
40		// A repo inside the scan root, so `dev` discovers it the way it would in
41		// real use rather than via an absolute path.
42		r := gittest.New(t)
43		dest := filepath.Join(scanRoot, "demo")
44		if err := os.Rename(r.Root, dest); err != nil {
45			t.Fatal(err)
46		}
47		r.Root = dest
48	
49		// Isolate every path dev touches from the developer's real machine.
50		t.Setenv("HOME", home)
51		t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share"))
52		t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".config"))
53		t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".cache"))
54	
55		configPath := filepath.Join(home, "config.toml")
56		cfg := "" +
57			"[paths]\n" +
58			"scan_roots = [\"" + scanRoot + "\"]\n" +
59			"project_root = \"" + scanRoot + "\"\n" +
60			"tries_root = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "tries") + "\"\n" +
61			"worktree_root = \"" + wtRoot + "\"\n" +
62			"state_dir = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "state") + "\"\n" +
63			"\n[runtime]\nbackend = \"none\"\n" +
64			"\n[worktree]\ninclude = [\".env\"]\npost_create = []\n"
65		if err := os.WriteFile(configPath, []byte(cfg), 0o644); err != nil {
66			t.Fatal(err)
67		}
68		return &harness{t: t, home: home, configPath: configPath, scanRoot: scanRoot, wtRoot: wtRoot, repo: r}
69	}
70	
71	// run executes one dev invocation, capturing its output. Commands write
72	// through App, so the writers passed to NewRootCommandWithIO are all that is
73	// needed — no file-descriptor juggling.
74	func (h *harness) run(args ...string) (string, string, error) {
75		h.t.Helper()
76		var out, errBuf bytes.Buffer
77		root := cli.NewRootCommandWithIO(&out, &errBuf)
78		root.SetArgs(append([]string{"--config", h.configPath}, args...))
79		err := root.Execute()
80		return out.String(), errBuf.String(), err
81	}

84		h.t.Helper()
85		out, errOut, err := h.run(args...)
86		if err != nil {
87			h.t.Fatalf("dev %s: %v\nstderr: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), err, errOut)
88		}
89		return out
90	}

```text
1	# dev
2	
3	A thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
4	
5	It exists to stop four things collapsing into one:
6	
7	```
8	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
9	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
10	herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
11	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
12	```
13	
14	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
15	only what git cannot answer — a task's **state**, **owner** and **next
16	action** — as one TOML file per task.
17	
18	## The problem
19	
20	When a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only record of what you are
21	working on, nothing can ever be closed: closing a workspace loses the thread.
22	So the sidebar grows to thirty-odd entries and stops being scannable, which
23	defeats the point of having one.
24	
25	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home outside
26	the runtime, so closing a session is just closing a session.
27	
28	Bare `dev` opens an interactive dashboard when it has a terminal, and prints
29	the plain listing when piped — so `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as
30	expected.
31	
32	```
33	$ dev ls
34	   TASK                   STATE  REPO       BRANCH                    GIT   AGE  SESSION       NEXT
35	🔥 token refresh          HOT    atp-sipui  fix/gx-security-recovery  ↑2 ●  2h   herdr:working add the regression test
36	🌤 orderbook experiment   WARM   trading    exp/orderbook-v2          clean 6d   —             compare against the baseline
37	❄️ settings redesign      COLD   website    feat/settings             clean 3w   —             pick up after the API lands
38	```
39	
40	## Install
41	
42	```bash
43	make install     # builds, installs to ~/.local/bin, installs the agent skill
44	dev config init  # detects this machine's repo roots and writes a config
45	```
46	
47	Then add the shell wrapper to your rc file:
48	
49	```bash
50	eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"      # bash and zsh
51	dev shell-init fish | source      # fish
52	```
53	
54	The wrapper is needed because a child process cannot change its parent's
55	working directory. Commands that move you into a checkout print a `cd`
56	directive; the wrapper evaluates it.
57	
58	```bash
59	dev doctor       # what works on this machine, and what degrades
60	```
61	
62	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
63	degrade cleanly when absent.
64	
65	## The lifecycle
66	
67	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
70	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
71	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
72	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
73	
74	```bash
75	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
76	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
77	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
78	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
79	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
80	dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
81	```
82	
83	### The dashboard
84	
85	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens three lists, switched with `tab`:
86	
87	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
88	- **REPOS** — every repository under the scan roots, with its branch, dirty
89	  state, worktree count and per-state task tally, sorted so anything in flight
90	  is at the top. What do I have here.
91	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through the authenticated `gh` and `glab`
92	  CLIs, marked when a local clone exists. What can I open or clone.
93	
94	TASKS and REPOS come from the same code paths as `dev ls` and `dev repo list`,
95	so they cannot disagree. The repo list matters on day one: with forty repositories and
96	no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just be empty.
97	
98	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
99	
100	```
101	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
102	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
103	/          filter as you type   esc             clear, then quit
104	```
105	
106	`enter` opens the selected row in the runtime. In TASKS, `p` parks and prompts
107	for the next action and `c` edits it; in REPOS, `s` starts a task right there —
108	branch, worktree, session and entry — which is the bridge from "what do I have"
109	to "what am I working on" without leaving the dashboard.
110	
111	**External tools are configured, not fixed.** They run through your shell in
112	the selected row's checkout; the dashboard suspends and redraws when they exit:
113	
114	```toml
115	[[tui.tools]]
116	key  = "L"
117	name = "lazygit"
118	run  = "lazygit"
119	
120	[[tui.tools]]
121	key  = "V"
122	name = "nvim"
123	run  = "nvim ."
124	
125	[[tui.tools]]
126	key  = "B"
127	name = "vibe"
128	run  = "vibe"
129	interactive = true     # load + evaluate aliases/functions after shell rc
130	
131	[[tui.tools]]
132	key  = "P"
133	name = "plans here"
134	run  = "claude-plans-here"
135	interactive = true
136	```
137	
138	`dev config init` writes the defaults out in full rather than leaving them
139	implicit, and `dev tui tools` shows what is bound here and whether each one is
140	actually installed — bindings for missing programs are not offered. A tool
141	cannot take a key the dashboard already uses; dev reports the clash on load.
142	
143	REMOTE loads lazily, so dashboard startup never waits on the network. A private
144	15-minute XDG cache makes later switches instant; `r` refreshes both forges.
145	`/` searches provider, owner/name and description; enter opens a local clone,
146	and `c` confirms before cloning an absent repo into `project_root`. The same
147	inventory is available without the full-screen UI via `dev repo remote [query]`;
148	`--cached` is its instant/offline form.
149	See `dev help tui` for the full key map.
150	
151	Going cold is safe because **the branch is the identity and the directory is a
152	cache**. `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, and `dev resume`
153	rebuilds the checkout from `origin/<branch>`. Once that holds, the local
154	filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished worktrees.
155	
156	## Worktree ownership
157	
158	Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
159	to improvise:
160	
161	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
162	|---|---|---|---|
163	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until `dev done` / `dev sweep` |
164	| Turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | dies with the turn |
165	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
166	
167	**Might you come back tomorrow → `dev`. Dies with this agent turn → Claude
168	Code native.**
169	
170	`dev` does not delegate placement to herdr because the path policy has to hold
171	on machines without herdr. It creates the checkout with plain git and asks
172	herdr only to *open* it — which still surfaces it in the sidebar grouped under
173	its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
174	
175	`dev` refuses to create a worktree inside a repository: a checkout nested in
176	another checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second
177	copy of the tree.
178	
179	### Provisioning
180	
181	A worktree is a clean checkout — no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
182	Without provisioning, every new one starts broken. `dev` copies the gitignored
183	files you list, optionally symlinks heavy directories, and runs a setup
184	command detected from the lockfiles:
185	
186	```toml
187	[worktree]
188	include     = [".env", ".env.local"]   # only files that are ALSO gitignored
189	link        = []                       # opt-in; sharing node_modules is risky
190	post_create = "auto"                   # uv.lock → uv sync, package-lock.json → npm ci, …
191	```
192	
193	**Copy or reinstall?** Reinstalling is always correct but can take minutes;
194	copying is fast but only sound for dependency trees carrying no absolute paths.
195	That is a per-ecosystem fact, not a preference, so dev knows it:
196	
197	```toml
198	[worktree]
199	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
200	
201	[worktree.strategies]
202	node = "copy"               # node_modules copies soundly
203	```
204	
205	Asking to copy a virtualenv is refused with the reason — it bakes its own
206	absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg` and `bin/activate` — and narrowed back to
207	reinstalling rather than silently producing a broken checkout.
208	
209	`dev wt plan` shows exactly what a new worktree of a repository would get:
210	which project types were detected, which tools are missing, and every file and
211	command involved. `dev wt plan --write` seeds a `<repo>/.dev.toml` from it, so
212	a project can commit its own setup and every machine provisions the same way.
213	
214	```
215	$ dev wt plan
216	PROJECT  MANAGER  FROM               DEPENDENCIES  TOOL
217	node     npm      package-lock.json  node_modules  installed
218	python   uv       uv.lock            .venv         installed
219	
220	   ACTION    WHAT          WHY
221	✓  copy      .env          gitignored, so the checkout would not have it
222	✓  copy-dir  node_modules  npm dependencies, copied instead of reinstalling
223	✓  run       uv sync       uv.lock detected
224	```
225	
226	## Other things it does
227	
228	```bash
229	dev repo list                  # every repo under the scan roots, with status
230	dev repo clone owner/name -c Web   # clone into the right place, via gh or glab
231	dev repo sync --all            # fetch + prune, and report what moved
232	
233	dev try redis-streams          # dated scratch directory for an experiment
234	dev graduate redis-streams -c Infra --remote   # promote it into a real project
235	
236	dev gitignore                  # .gitignore from GitHub's templates + the rest
237	dev adopt                      # import existing worktrees/sessions as tasks
238	
239	dev stats --heatmap            # where the time actually went
240	dev help worktrees             # quick-reference pages for the workflow
241	```
242	
243	`dev stats` draws a contribution-style heatmap from two sources: a sampler
244	watching live agent sessions (the only way to count time spent reading and
245	debugging), and git history (which backfills the past and survives losing the
246	database). WakaTime can be imported alongside for editor time.
247	
248	```bash
249	dev stats backfill                          # seed from git history, once
250	dev stats sample --interval 5m              # from cron, every five minutes
251	dev stats import-wakatime                   # optional
252	```
253	
254	## Bootstrapping an existing machine
255	
256	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use: `dev` discovers repositories
257	wherever `scan_roots` point and never requires a particular physical layout.
258	When you want a recursive audit or a curated navigation layer, bootstrap is the
259	explicit path:
260	
261	```bash
262	dev bootstrap ~/code /mnt/work                    # recursive report, no changes
263	dev bootstrap ~/code --json                       # machine-readable inventory
264	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects           # plan a flat symlink catalog
265	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects --apply   # create only the ready links
266	dev bootstrap ~/old --move ~/Projects             # plan physical moves
267	```
268	
269	The scanner classifies canonical checkouts, linked worktrees, bare repositories
270	and symlink aliases, deduplicating by Git common-directory identity rather than
271	path.
272	
273	**A symlink index is the default recommendation.** It gives a flat,
274	metadata-aware navigation root while every physical repository stays exactly
275	where it was. Put the index first in `scan_roots` and that alias becomes the UI;
276	normal discovery follows direct repo symlinks and deduplicates index + physical
277	paths.
278	
279	Physical move exists, but refuses dirty repos, linked worktrees anywhere in the
280	clone, live sessions, a current shell inside, aliases that would break,
281	occupied destinations and cross-filesystem renames. A plan with any blocked row
282	moves nothing. `--config-out` writes a fresh config for the resulting root
283	without silently rewriting the user's current one. See `dev help bootstrap`.
284	
285	## Adopting work in flight
286	
287	There is nothing to migrate. `dev` discovers repositories wherever your scan
288	roots point and **never moves, renames or deletes anything** you already have.
289	`dev config init` probes the conventional locations — `~/Documents/Program`,
290	`~/src`, `~/code`, a `GHQ_ROOT`, and so on — counts the repositories in each,
291	and writes only the ones that exist:
292	
293	```
294	$ dev config init
295	wrote ~/.config/dev/config.toml
296	
297	Detected:
298	ROOT                 REPOS  ROLE
299	~/Documents/Program  40     scan root, new projects land here
300	~/src                16     scan root
301	```
302	
303	Repositories are discovered; *tasks* are not. `dev adopt` finds the work
304	already in flight — linked worktrees from any tool, live runtime sessions, and
305	local branches ahead of the default branch — and offers to record it. It skips
306	branches already merged, and the turn-scoped worktrees an agent harness cleans
307	up itself:
308	
309	```bash
310	dev adopt            # report only
311	dev adopt --apply    # record as tasks; nothing on disk changes
312	```
313	
314	A worktree you already have somewhere else keeps working exactly as it did —
315	`dev` records the path git reports rather than relocating it. Full detail in
316	`dev help adopting`.
317	
318	## .gitignore
319	
320	```bash
321	dev gitignore                 # detect the languages from the repo's files
322	dev gitignore python node     # or say so explicitly
323	dev gitignore --offline       # cached and bundled templates only
324	```
325	
326	Language sections come from [GitHub's templates](https://github.com/github/gitignore),
327	fetched once and cached. On top of those it adds what no language template
328	covers: the host platform's junk files, editor state, local env files, and the
329	directories coding-agent harnesses create — an agent's linked worktree left
330	untracked makes every `git status` in the main checkout unreadable.
331	
332	Everything it writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
333	block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.
334	
335	## Configuration
336	
337	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`. Write a commented starter with
338	`dev config init`; see the effective settings with `dev config show`; open the
339	actual file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` with either form:
340	
341	```bash
342	dev edit
343	dev config edit
344	DEV_EDITOR=unused dev edit --editor "code --wait"   # explicit override
345	```
346	
347	If the file does not exist, `edit` generates the machine-detected starter first
348	rather than opening an empty file. Resolution is `--editor` → `$VISUAL` →
349	`$EDITOR` → `nvim` → `vim` → `vi`.
350	
351	Every path is configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine —
352	a faster volume, a different naming convention:
353	
354	```toml
355	[paths]
356	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"]
357	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
358	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
359	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"        # point at a git repo to sync it
360	```
361	
362	Template variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`,
363	`host`, `date`. Filters: `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`), `|lower`,
364	`|base`. A typo in a variable name fails at load, not as a directory literally
365	named `{{rep}}`.
366	
367	A flat project layout is already first-class — it needs no migration and no
368	special mode:
369	
370	```toml
371	[paths]
372	scan_roots   = ["~/code"]
373	project_root = "~/code"       # repo new/clone/graduate land at ~/code/<repo>
374	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/wt"
375	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}"
376	```
377	
378	Omit `--category` and canonical repos stay flat. Categories are metadata the
379	user may choose, never a directory structure dev imposes.
380	
381	## Multiple machines
382	
383	Do not sync worktrees or runtime state. Sync branches, and let the remote be
384	the handoff boundary:
385	
386	```bash
387	dev park --cold --push      # on the machine holding the work
388	dev resume <task> --fetch   # on the machine picking it up
389	```
390	
391	`dev` records an owner host per task and refuses to resume someone else's
392	without `--force`. Two machines committing to one branch is the reliable way
393	to produce a conflict here; the ownership check prevents it.
394	
395	For a cross-machine view, `dev ls --json` is a stable contract:
396	
397	```bash
398	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
399	```
400	
401	## The agent skill
402	
403	`dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
404	same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
405	tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
406	reading none.
407	
408	```bash
409	dev skill install    # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
410	dev --skill          # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
411	dev skill sync       # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
412	dev skill sync --check   # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
413	```
414	
415	The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
416	SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
417	worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
418	responsibility.
419	
420	## Development
421	
422	```bash
423	make          # fmt, vet, test, build
424	make test
425	make e2e      # drives the real binary through a full lifecycle in a sandbox
426	make skill-check
427	```
428	
429	Tests build throwaway repositories under `t.TempDir()` via
430	`internal/gitx/gittest`, and the runtime adapters share one contract suite that
```

7	### P2 · M — Multi-host aggregation
8	`dev ls --all` fanning out over ssh to the machines in a configured host list,

18	A `tv` channel over `dev ls --json` for fuzzy-picking a task, and an `fzf`
19	fallback. Navigation by metadata rather than by remembering a path is the point
20	of the tool; the TUI covers it, but a picker composes better with other tools.
21	
22	### P3 · S — `dev stats` per-repo heatmap
23	`--repo X` currently filters the totals and the combined grid. A dedicated
24	per-repo grid, several stacked, would answer "which project did I move to in
25	March" better than the aggregate does.
26	
27	### P4 · M — Raycast extension
28	`dev ls` and `dev resume` from the launcher. Wants the JSON contract and a
29	stable binary path; nothing else new.
30	
31	## Deliberately not doing
32	
33	### Installing dependencies
34	`dev doctor` reports what is missing and what degrades; it will not install
35	anything. This is the one place where being glue matters most: git, herdr,
36	tmux, gh, glab, lazygit and yazi are all installed by a package manager the
37	user already has opinions about (brew, apt, mise, nix, chezmoi), and a tool
38	that shells out to one of them is guessing. `doctor` naming the missing binary
39	is enough — the user knows how they install things on that machine.
40	
41	Reconsider only if `doctor` grows a case where the *right* command is
42	unambiguous and the user has asked for it.
43	
44	### A second git database
45	Anything derivable from git is derived live, every run. The registry holds
46	state, owner, next action and a note — nothing else. The moment it caches a
47	branch name or an ahead/behind count, it can disagree with git, and a tool that
48	disagrees with git about git is worse than no tool.
49	
50	### Syncing runtime state between machines
51	Each host runs its own multiplexer. What crosses machines is branches, through
52	the remote, plus the task registry if `state_dir` is a git repo. Syncing
53	sessions would mean reconciling two live terminal states, which is a much
54	harder problem than the one this tool has.
55	
56	### Owning the worktree path on machines with herdr
57	`herdr worktree create` would be less code, but the path policy has to hold
58	where herdr is not installed. dev creates the checkout with git and asks herdr
59	only to open it. See `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/worktree-ownership.md`.

10	// Layout is what `dev config init` discovered about a machine, so a generated
11	// config describes the paths that actually exist rather than the author's own.
12	type Layout struct {
13		// ScanRoots are directories that already hold repositories.
14		ScanRoots []string
15		// ProjectRoot is the best candidate for new and graduated projects: the
16		// scan root with the most repositories in it.
17		ProjectRoot string
18		// TriesRoot is where scratch experiments live.
19		TriesRoot string
20		// WorktreeRoot is where linked worktrees will go.
21		WorktreeRoot string
22		// Found records how many repositories were seen per candidate root, for
23		// the comment written into the generated config.
24		Found map[string]int
25	}
26	
27	// candidateRoots are the conventional places people keep repositories, in no
28	// particular order — ranking is by how many repos each actually holds.
29	var candidateRoots = []string{
30		"~/Documents/Program", "~/Documents/Projects", "~/Documents/Code",
31		"~/src", "~/code", "~/Code", "~/dev", "~/Developer",
32		"~/projects", "~/Projects", "~/work", "~/Work",
33		"~/git", "~/repos", "~/workspace", "~/ghq",
34	}
35	
36	// candidateTries are where an experiment directory is conventionally kept.
37	var candidateTries = []string{"~/src/tries", "~/tries", "~/scratch", "~/sandbox"}
38	
39	// DetectLayout probes the machine for existing repository roots.
40	//
41	// A generated config that points at directories which do not exist is worse
42	// than no config: dev would silently discover nothing and the user would have
43	// no signal about why.
44	func DetectLayout() Layout {
45		l := Layout{Found: map[string]int{}}
46	
47		// ghq keeps a configurable root and is worth honouring when present.
48		roots := append([]string{}, candidateRoots...)
49		if ghq := os.Getenv("GHQ_ROOT"); ghq != "" {
50			for _, p := range filepath.SplitList(ghq) {
51				roots = append(roots, p)
52			}
53		}
54	
55		seen := map[string]bool{}
56		for _, cand := range roots {
57			p := Expand(cand)
58			if seen[p] {
59				continue
60			}
61			seen[p] = true
62			n, ok := countRepos(p)
63			if !ok {
64				continue
65			}
66			l.Found[cand] = n
67			if n > 0 {
68				l.ScanRoots = append(l.ScanRoots, cand)
69			}
70		}
71	
72		// Most repositories wins: that is where the user actually keeps projects,
73		// and so where a new one belongs.
74		best, bestN := "", -1
75		for _, r := range l.ScanRoots {
76			if l.Found[r] > bestN {
77				best, bestN = r, l.Found[r]
78			}
79		}
80		l.ProjectRoot = best
81	
82		// try-cli's own environment variable takes priority, then convention.
83		if tp := os.Getenv("TRY_PATH"); tp != "" {
84			l.TriesRoot = Contract(Expand(tp))
85		} else {
86			for _, cand := range candidateTries {
87				if info, err := os.Stat(Expand(cand)); err == nil && info.IsDir() {

96			if l.Found[l.ScanRoots[i]] != l.Found[l.ScanRoots[j]] {
97				return l.Found[l.ScanRoots[i]] > l.Found[l.ScanRoots[j]]
98			}
99			return l.ScanRoots[i] < l.ScanRoots[j]
100		})

103		// leaving them out would hide half the work in progress.

1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"regexp"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// Path templates are deliberately *not* text/template: the syntax users write
10	// in config.toml ("{{worktree_root}}/{{repo}}/{{branch|slug}}") needs to stay
11	// readable and to fail loudly on an unknown variable rather than silently
12	// rendering "<no value>".
13	
14	var tmplVar = regexp.MustCompile(`\{\{\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*(?:\|\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*)?\}\}`)
15	
16	// Vars is the substitution environment for a path template.
17	type Vars map[string]string
18	
19	// Render substitutes every {{var}} / {{var|filter}} occurrence in tmpl.
20	// An unknown variable or filter is an error — a typo in worktree_path should
21	// surface at create time, not as a directory literally named "{{rep}}".
22	func Render(tmpl string, vars Vars) (string, error) {
23		var firstErr error
24		out := tmplVar.ReplaceAllStringFunc(tmpl, func(m string) string {
25			g := tmplVar.FindStringSubmatch(m)
26			name, filter := g[1], g[2]
27			val, ok := vars[name]
28			if !ok {
29				if firstErr == nil {
30					firstErr = fmt.Errorf("unknown template variable %q in %q (known: %s)", name, tmpl, strings.Join(sortedKeys(vars), ", "))
31				}
32				return m
33			}
34			switch filter {
35			case "":
36				return val
37			case "slug":
38				return Slug(val)
39			case "lower":
40				return strings.ToLower(val)
41			case "base":
42				if i := strings.LastIndexByte(val, '/'); i >= 0 {
43					return val[i+1:]
44				}
45				return val
46			default:
47				if firstErr == nil {
48					firstErr = fmt.Errorf("unknown template filter %q in %q (known: slug, lower, base)", filter, tmpl)
49				}
50				return m
51			}
52		})
53		if firstErr != nil {
54			return "", firstErr
55		}
56		return out, nil
57	}
58	
59	var slugStrip = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
60	
61	// Slug makes a branch name safe to use as a single filesystem component:
62	// "feat/auth/oauth-refresh" becomes "feat-auth-oauth-refresh". Leading dots
63	// and dashes are trimmed so the result can never be a hidden directory or be
64	// mistaken for a flag.
65	func Slug(s string) string {
66		s = slugStrip.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
67		for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
68			s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
69		}
70		s = strings.Trim(s, "-._")
71		if s == "" {
72			return "unnamed"
73		}
74		return s
75	}
76	
77	func sortedKeys(v Vars) []string {
78		out := make([]string, 0, len(v))
79		for k := range v {
80			out = append(out, k)
81		}
82		// small map; insertion sort keeps this dependency-free
83		for i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {
84			for j := i; j > 0 && out[j] < out[j-1]; j-- {
85				out[j], out[j-1] = out[j-1], out[j]
86			}
87		}
88		return out
89	}
90
```

```text
1	# Task lifecycle
2	
3	Read this when work needs to be paused, picked up on another machine, or when
4	a machine has accumulated more open sessions than anyone can hold in mind.
5	
6	## The problem
7	
8	A terminal multiplexer's sidebar is a *runtime* view: it shows what is running
9	now. When it is also the only record of what you are working on, nothing can be
10	closed, because closing it loses the thread. The sidebar grows until it stops
11	being scannable, which defeats its purpose.
12	
13	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home that is
14	not the runtime.
15	
16	## The four states
17	
18	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
19	|---|---|---|---|
20	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
21	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
22	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
23	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
24	
25	Only the transitions between them cost anything:
26	
27	```
28	        dev start
29	            │
30	            ▼
31	         🔥 hot ──── dev done ────► ✅ done
32	          │  ▲
33	   dev park│  │dev resume
34	          ▼  │
35	        🌤 warm
36	          │  ▲
37	dev park  │  │dev resume
38	  --cold  ▼  │  (rebuilds the worktree)
39	        ❄️ cold
40	```
41	
42	**A machine should hold roughly three to seven hot tasks.** That is a
43	cognitive limit, not a technical one. Everything else belongs in `dev ls`.
44	
45	## Parking
46	
47	```bash
48	dev park --next "reproduce the token refresh race, then add a regression test"
49	```
50	
51	This is the move the whole design exists to make safe. It records what to do
52	next, closes the runtime session, and leaves the branch and worktree exactly
53	where they are.
54	
55	`--next` is the important part. Without it, resuming means re-deriving where
56	you were from a diff, which is most of the cost of a context switch. Always
57	supply one.
58	
59	Useful variations:
60	
61	```bash
62	dev park --wip                    # checkpoint uncommitted work first
63	dev park --cold --push            # push, remove the worktree, keep the branch
64	dev park --keep-session           # record the state, leave the session open
65	```
66	
67	## Checkpoint commits, not stashes
68	
69	`--wip` makes a `wip: checkpoint — <next>` commit rather than a `git stash`.
70	
71	A stash is invisible in the log, easy to forget, and **cannot be pushed** — so
72	it can never reach another machine. That last point is decisive: the whole
73	value of parking is that the work is recoverable from anywhere.
74	
75	Messy WIP commits on a feature branch are fine. Branch history is *construction
76	history*; the base branch's history is *product history*. They do not have to
77	match — clean the branch up at the integration boundary with an interactive
78	rebase, or squash it, and decide then.
79	
80	## Cold, and why it is safe
81	
82	Going cold removes the checkout. That feels lossy, and is not, because:
83	
84	- the branch still holds every commit;
85	- `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, so the remote holds
86	  them too;
87	- `dev resume` rebuilds the worktree from `origin/<branch>`.
88	
89	The directory is a cache. The branch is the identity. Once that is true, a
90	local filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished checkouts.
91	
92	## Moving work between machines
93	
94	The remote is the handoff boundary. Do not sync worktrees, runtime state, or
95	the multiplexer's database between machines — sync branches.
96	
97	On the machine holding the work:
98	
99	```bash
100	dev park --cold --push
101	```
102	
103	On the machine picking it up:
104	
105	```bash
106	dev resume <task> --fetch
107	```
108	
109	**One writer per branch at a time.** `dev` records an `owner` host and refuses
110	to resume a task owned by another machine without `--force`. Two machines
111	committing to one branch is the only reliable way to make this workflow produce
112	a conflict; the ownership check is what prevents it.
113	
114	If two machines genuinely need to work the same feature at once, split the
115	branch — `feat/auth-ui` and `feat/auth-api` — and integrate afterwards. That is
116	the same rule as for parallel agents: parallel writers get parallel branches.
117	
118	The task registry itself (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`) is one small TOML file
119	per task, specifically so it can live in a private git repo and merge cleanly
120	across machines. Point `paths.state_dir` at one if you want a shared view.
121	
122	## Sweeping
123	
124	```bash
125	dev sweep            # report only
126	dev sweep --apply    # act, confirming each change
127	```
128	
129	`sweep` reports two kinds of problem:
130	
131	- **Drift** — a task marked hot with no live session, a warm task with one, a
132	  recorded worktree git no longer knows about.
133	- **Staleness** — a warm task nobody has touched in two weeks, clean and
134	  pushed, that could go cold.
135	
136	It also lists **live sessions no task claims** — the other half of a crowded
137	sidebar, and usually the larger half.
138	
139	`sweep` never deletes uncommitted work, and never acts without `--apply`. The
140	reason cleanup usually does not happen is not unwillingness; it is the absence
141	of a trustworthy guarantee that the work is recoverable. Reporting first, and
142	requiring confirmation, is that guarantee.
143	
144	## Integration
145	
146	```bash
147	dev done --ff     # rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it
148	dev done --pr     # push and open a pull/merge request via gh or glab
149	```
150	
151	Which one depends on a single question: **are this branch's commits worth
152	keeping in the base's history?**
153	
154	- Yes → `--ff`. Linear history, no merge commit, `git bisect` and `git blame`
155	  stay legible.
156	- No, it is WIP noise → squash at the integration point.
157	- Someone (or CI) should look first → `--pr`.
158	
159	`dev done` refuses on a dirty tree, and `--delete-branch` only removes a branch
160	git agrees is fully contained in the base. "Merged" is not always "finished" —
161	work often continues on a branch after its first integration, which is why the
162	branch survives by default.
163
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# TUI navigation
2	
3	Bare `dev` opens the dashboard when stdin/stdout are terminals; `dev tui`
4	opens it explicitly. When piped, bare `dev` prints `dev ls` instead, so shell
5	composition stays predictable.
6	
7	## Three views
8	
9	Switch with `tab`, `l`/`h`, or right/left:
10	
11	| View | Answers | Data source |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| TASKS | What am I working on? | task registry + live Git/runtime state |
14	| REPOS | What repositories exist here? | recursive configured scan roots |
15	| REMOTE | What can I open or clone? | authenticated `gh` + `glab` inventories |
16	
17	REPOS shows branch, dirty state, linked-worktree count and HOT/WARM/COLD task
18	tallies. Repos with active work sort first; untracked clean repos remain
19	visible below them. On a first run with no tasks, switch to REPOS and press `s`
20	to start one, or run `dev adopt` to import work already in flight.
21	
22	REMOTE loads lazily, so dashboard startup never waits on the network. A
23	private XDG cache makes later switches instant; `r` refreshes explicitly. It
24	marks remotes already cloned under `scan_roots`. Enter opens a local clone; `c`
25	asks before cloning an absent repo into `project_root`.
26	
27	## Vim-style movement
28	
29	```
30	j / k                next / previous
31	ctrl+d / ctrl+u      half page down / up
32	g / G                top / bottom
33	h / l, shift-tab/tab previous / next view
34	/                    filter as you type
35	esc                  clear prompt/filter; when clear, quit
36	q                    quit
37	```
38	
39	The `/` query applies to the current view and matches whitespace-separated
40	terms independently. `gitlab auth` finds a GitLab repo whose name/description
41	also contains auth, regardless of word order.
42	
43	## Actions
44	
45	TASKS:
46	
47	```
48	enter / o  open in the selected runtime
49	p          park warm, prompting for the next action
50	c          edit the next action
51	1 / 2 / 3  show HOT / WARM / COLD
52	0          clear filters
53	a          include DONE
54	```
55	
56	REPOS:
57	
58	```
59	enter / o  open the repository
60	s          start a task: branch + worktree + provisioning + runtime + entry
61	```
62	
63	REMOTE:
64	
65	```
66	enter / o  open an existing local clone
67	c          confirm and clone an absent repo into project_root
68	r          refresh gh + glab, replacing the cache
69	```
70	
71	## External tools are explicit configuration
72	
73	```bash
74	dev tui tools
75	```
76	
77	shows every binding, the exact command, its source, and whether it can run on
78	this machine. `dev config init` writes the defaults out in full:
79	
80	```toml
81	[[tui.tools]]
82	key  = "L"
83	name = "lazygit"
84	run  = "lazygit"
85	
86	[[tui.tools]]
87	key  = "Y"
88	name = "yazi"
89	run  = "yazi"
90	
91	[[tui.tools]]
92	key  = "V"
93	name = "nvim"
94	run  = "nvim ."
95	
96	[[tui.tools]]
97	key  = "B"
98	name = "vibe"
99	run  = "vibe"
100	interactive = true
101	
102	[[tui.tools]]
103	key  = "P"
104	name = "plans here"
105	run  = "claude-plans-here"
106	interactive = true
107	```
108	
109	A configured list replaces the defaults entirely. Commands run through
110	`$SHELL` in the selected row's checkout, so arguments, environment variables
111	and executable scripts work. `interactive = true` runs through `$SHELL -lic`
112	and deliberately evaluates the command *after* rc loading, so this machine's
113	`vibe` alias and `claude-plans-here` function work. Prefer a real script on PATH
114	when the binding should be portable to machines with different shell configs.
115	
116	Keys are case-sensitive. A tool cannot take one the dashboard owns; config
117	loading reports the collision instead of silently shadowing movement or quit.
118
```

104	// tryEntry is one scratch directory with the facts needed to rank it.
105	type tryEntry struct {
106		name     string
107		path     string
108		modified time.Time
109		isRepo   bool
110		dirty    bool
111	}
112	
113	func listTries(app *App, root string) error {
114		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
115		if err != nil {
116			return err
117		}
118		var tries []tryEntry
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			if !e.IsDir() || strings.HasPrefix(e.Name(), ".") {
121				continue
122			}
123			info, err := e.Info()
124			if err != nil {
125				continue
126			}
127			path := filepath.Join(root, e.Name())
128			t := tryEntry{name: e.Name(), path: path, modified: info.ModTime()}
129			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
130				t.isRepo = true
131				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctxOf(), path); err == nil {
132					t.dirty = st.Dirty()
133				}
134			}
135			tries = append(tries, t)
136		}
137		if len(tries) == 0 {
138			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "No tries yet under %s\n", config.Contract(root))
139			return nil
140		}
141		// Most recently touched first: "what was I doing yesterday?" is the
142		// question a list of experiments actually gets asked.
143		sort.Slice(tries, func(i, j int) bool { return tries[i].modified.After(tries[j].modified) })
144	
145		tbl := NewTable("TRY", "AGE", "GIT")
146		for _, t := range tries {
147			gitCol := "—"
148			switch {
149			case t.isRepo && t.dirty:
150				gitCol = "repo ●"
151			case t.isRepo:
152				gitCol = "repo"
153			}
154			tbl.Add(truncate(t.name, 44), humanAge(time.Since(t.modified)), gitCol)
155		}
156		tbl.Render(app.Out)
157		fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\n%d tries under %s — promote one with `dev graduate <try>`\n",
158			len(tries), config.Contract(root))
159		return nil
160	}
161	
162	// findTry locates an existing try whose name contains the slug, preferring the
163	// most recent when several match.
164	func findTry(root, slug string) string {
165		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
166		if err != nil {
167			return ""
168		}
169		var best string
170		var bestTime time.Time
171		for _, e := range entries {
172			if !e.IsDir() || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(e.Name()), strings.ToLower(slug)) {
173				continue
174			}
175			info, err := e.Info()
176			if err != nil {
177				continue
178			}
179			if info.ModTime().After(bestTime) {
180				best, bestTime = filepath.Join(root, e.Name()), info.ModTime()
181			}
182		}
183		return best
184	}
185	
186	func openOrCD(app *App, ctx context.Context, dir, label string) error {
187		rt := app.Runtime()
188		if rt.Name() == "none" {
189			app.cdDirective(dir)
190			return nil
191		}
192		if _, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, dir, label); err != nil {
193			app.warnf("could not open a session: %v", err)
194		}
195		return nil
196	}

22			category string
23			name     string

32			Long: `Move a try out of the scratch directory and into your projects tree.
33	
34	An experiment that turns out to matter should stop being an experiment, and
35	that transition is where things usually get lost — the directory keeps its date
36	prefix forever, or it gets copied by hand and the history is left behind.
37	
38	graduate moves the directory to <project_root>/<category>/<name>, drops the
39	date prefix, makes sure it has a git repo and a first commit, and optionally
40	creates the remote with gh or glab.
41	
42	With no argument, the try containing the current directory is used.`,
43			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
44			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
45				ctx := ctxOf()
46				triesRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot)
47	
48				src, err := resolveTry(app, triesRoot, args)
49				if err != nil {
50					return err
51				}
52				if name == "" {
53					name = datePrefix.ReplaceAllString(filepath.Base(src), "")
54				}
55				if name == "" {
56					return fmt.Errorf("could not derive a project name from %s — pass --name", src)
57				}
58	
59				dest := filepath.Join(config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot), category, name)
60				if _, err := os.Stat(dest); err == nil {
61					return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists", config.Contract(dest))
62				}
63	
64				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "graduate  %s\n", config.Contract(src))
65				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "       →  %s\n", config.Contract(dest))
66				if dryRun {
67					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\n(dry run — nothing moved)")
68					return nil
69				}
70	
71				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dest), 0o755); err != nil {
72					return err
73				}
74				// Rename first: it is atomic within a filesystem and leaves
75				// nothing half-copied if it fails.
76				if err := os.Rename(src, dest); err != nil {
77					return fmt.Errorf("move %s: %w\n"+
78						"If the projects root is on another filesystem, copy it by hand and remove the try",
79						config.Contract(src), err)
80				}
81	
82				if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dest, ".git")); err != nil {
83					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dest, "init", "-b", "main"); err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   git init")
87				}
88				// An experiment usually has files but no commit. A project needs
89				// one: without a HEAD there is no default branch, so `dev start`
90				// would have nothing to base a worktree on.
91				if made, err := ensureInitialCommit(ctx, dest, name); err != nil {
92					app.warnf("could not make an initial commit: %v", err)
93				} else if made {
94					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   committed the existing work")
95				}
96	
97				if remote {
98					f, err := forge.Preferred()
99					if err != nil {
100						app.warnf("%v — the project is in place; add a remote by hand", err)
101					} else {
102						url, err := f.CreateRepo(ctx, dest, forge.RepoRequest{
103							Name: name, Private: private, Push: push,
104						})
105						if err != nil {
106							app.warnf("could not create the remote: %v", err)
107						} else {
108							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   remote    %s\n", url)
109						}
110					}
111				}
112	
113				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%s is now a project. Start work on it with:\n  dev start %s --task <name>\n",
114					name, name)
115				return openOrCD(app, ctx, dest, name)
116			},
117		}
118		f := cmd.Flags()
119		f.StringVarP(&category, "category", "c", "", "category subdirectory under project_root")
120		f.StringVar(&name, "name", "", "project name (default: the try name without its date prefix)")
121		f.BoolVar(&private, "private", true, "create the remote as private")
122		f.BoolVar(&remote, "remote", false, "create a remote repository with gh or glab")
123		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", true, "push after creating the remote")
124		f.BoolVar(&dryRun, "dry-run", false, "show what would happen without moving anything")
125		return cmd
126	}
127	
128	// resolveTry finds the try directory to graduate: an explicit reference, or
129	// the try containing the current directory.
130	func resolveTry(app *App, triesRoot string, args []string) (string, error) {
131		if len(args) == 1 {
132			ref := args[0]
133			if abs := config.Expand(ref); isDir(abs) {
134				return abs, nil
135			}
136			direct := filepath.Join(triesRoot, ref)
137			if isDir(direct) {
138				return direct, nil
139			}
140			if match := findTry(triesRoot, ref); match != "" {
141				return match, nil
142			}
143			return "", fmt.Errorf("no try matching %q under %s", ref, config.Contract(triesRoot))
144		}
145	
146		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
147		if err != nil {
148			return "", err
149		}
150		if !strings.HasPrefix(cwd, triesRoot+string(filepath.Separator)) {
151			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not inside %s — name the try to graduate",
152				config.Contract(cwd), config.Contract(triesRoot))
153		}
154		// Walk up to the try's own top-level directory, so running this from a
155		// subdirectory still graduates the whole experiment.
156		rel, _ := filepath.Rel(triesRoot, cwd)
157		first := strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator))[0]
158		return filepath.Join(triesRoot, first), nil
159	}
160	
161	func isDir(p string) bool {
162		info, err := os.Stat(p)
163		return err == nil && info.IsDir()
164	}
165	
166	// ensureInitialCommit gives a repository a first commit if it has none,
167	// seeding a README when the tree is otherwise empty. Reports whether it made
168	// one.
169	func ensureInitialCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) (bool, error) {
170		if _, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, dir); err == nil {
171			return false, nil // already has history
172		}
173		if empty, err := isEmptyTree(dir); err != nil {
174			return false, err
175		} else if empty {
176			readme := filepath.Join(dir, "README.md")
177			if err := os.WriteFile(readme, []byte("# "+name+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
178				return false, err
179			}
180		}
181		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
182			return false, err
183		}
184		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "commit", "-m", "chore: graduate experiment into a project"); err != nil {
185			return false, err
186		}
187		return true, nil
188	}
189	
190	// isEmptyTree reports a directory with nothing in it but git's own metadata.
191	func isEmptyTree(dir string) (bool, error) {
192		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
193		if err != nil {
194			return false, err
195		}
196		for _, e := range entries {
197			if e.Name() != ".git" {
198				return false, nil
199			}
200		}
201		return true, nil
202	}
203

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"context"

7		"os"
8		"strings"
9		"time"

11		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"

18	)
19	
20	// suggestion is one proposed change, with the reason and the exact effect.
21	type suggestion struct {
22		row    inventory.Row
23		action string
24		reason string
25		// apply performs the change. nil means "report only".
26		apply func() error
27	}
28	
29	func newSweepCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
30		var (
31			apply     bool
32			staleDays int
33			yes       bool
34		)
35		cmd := &cobra.Command{
36			Use:   "sweep",
37			Short: "Review stale tasks and drifted state, and act on them",
38			Long: `Show which tasks have gone stale or drifted, and what dev would do about it.
39	
40	Cleanup usually fails not because people are unwilling but because there is no
41	trustworthy way to be sure the work is recoverable. So sweep reports first and
42	only changes things with --apply, confirming each one unless you pass --yes.
43	Nothing here ever deletes uncommitted work.`,
44			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
45			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
46				ctx := ctxOf()
47				tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
48				if err != nil {
49					return err
50				}
51				rt := app.Runtime()
52				rows := inventory.Collect(ctx, tasks, rt, inventory.Options{})
53				stale := time.Duration(staleDays) * 24 * time.Hour
54	
55				var sugg []suggestion
56				for _, r := range rows {
57					sugg = append(sugg, suggestFor(app, ctx, rt, r, stale)...)
58				}
59	
60				// Live sessions no task claims: the other half of a crowded sidebar.
61				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
62					if orphans := inventory.Orphans(sessions, rows); len(orphans) > 0 {
63						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d live session(s) with no task recorded:\n", len(orphans))
64						for _, s := range orphans {
65							dir := "—"
66							if len(s.Dirs) > 0 {
67								dir = config.Contract(s.Dirs[0])
68							}
69							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %-24s %s\n", truncate(s.Label, 24), dir)
70						}
71						fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  → `dev start` in one of those directories to track it, or just close it.")
72					}
73				}
74	
75				if len(sugg) == 0 {
76					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nNothing to sweep — every task matches its recorded state.")
77					return nil
78				}
79	
80				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d suggestion(s):\n\n", len(sugg))
81				for _, s := range sugg {
82					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s %-28s %s\n", s.row.Task.State.Icon(),
83						truncate(s.row.Task.Title(), 28), s.reason)
84					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "     → %s\n", s.action)
85				}
86	
87				if !apply {
88					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nRe-run with --apply to act on these (each is confirmed individually).")
89					return nil
90				}
91	
92				in := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
93				for _, s := range sugg {
94					if s.apply == nil {
95						continue
96					}
97					if !yes && !confirm(app, in, s.action) {
98						continue
99					}
100					if err := s.apply(); err != nil {
101						app.warnf("%s: %v", s.row.Task.ID, err)
102						continue
103					}
104					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  done: %s\n", s.action)
105				}
106				return nil
107			},
108		}
109		f := cmd.Flags()
110		f.BoolVar(&apply, "apply", false, "act on the suggestions instead of only reporting")
111		f.IntVar(&staleDays, "stale-days", 14, "days without a commit before a task counts as stale")
112		f.BoolVar(&yes, "yes", false, "with --apply, do not confirm each change")
113		return cmd
114	}
115	
116	func suggestFor(app *App, ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, r inventory.Row, stale time.Duration) []suggestion {
117		t := r.Task
118		var out []suggestion
119	
120		switch {
121		// A hot task with no live session is the commonest drift: the session was
122		// closed (or the machine rebooted) without parking.
123		case t.State == task.Hot && !r.Live():
124			out = append(out, suggestion{
125				row:    r,
126				reason: fmt.Sprintf("hot but no live session, idle %s", humanAge(r.Age())),
127				action: fmt.Sprintf("mark %s warm", t.ID),
128				apply: func() error {
129					t.State = task.Warm
130					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
131				},
132			})
133	
134		// A warm task nobody has touched in weeks is a candidate for cold: keeping
135		// the worktree costs disk and clutters every listing.
136		case t.State == task.Warm && r.Age() > stale:
137			reason := fmt.Sprintf("warm and untouched for %s", humanAge(r.Age()))
138			if r.Status.Dirty() {
139				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but has uncommitted work",
140					action: "commit or `dev park --wip` before going cold — not changed automatically"})
141				break
142			}
143			if !r.Status.Synced() {
144				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + fmt.Sprintf(", not pushed (%s)", r.Status.Summary()),
145					action: fmt.Sprintf("push %s so it can go cold: dev park %s --cold --push", t.Branch, t.ID)})
146				break
147			}
148			out = append(out, suggestion{
149				row:    r,
150				reason: reason + ", clean and pushed",
151				action: fmt.Sprintf("go cold: remove %s (branch and remote keep the work)", config.Contract(r.Checkout)),
152				apply: func() error {
153					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
154					if t.WorktreePath != "" {
155						if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
156							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath, RuntimeHandle: t.RuntimeHandle,
157						}); err != nil {
158							return err
159						}
160						t.WorktreePath = ""
161					}
162					t.State, t.RuntimeHandle = task.Cold, ""
163					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
164				},
165			})
166	
167		// A done task's entry has served its purpose once the branch is gone.
168		case t.State == task.Done:
169			out = append(out, suggestion{
170				row:    r,
171				reason: "merged",
172				action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s", t.ID),
173				apply:  func() error { return app.Tasks.Delete(t.ID) },
174			})
175		}
176	
177		// Drift that is independent of the lifecycle stage.
178		if r.WorktreeMissing && t.WorktreePath != "" {
179			wtPath := t.WorktreePath
180			out = append(out, suggestion{
181				row:    r,
182				reason: "records a worktree that git no longer knows about",
183				action: fmt.Sprintf("clear the stale worktree path %s", config.Contract(wtPath)),
184				apply: func() error {
185					if err := gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, t.RepoPath); err != nil {
186						return err
187					}
188					t.WorktreePath = ""
189					if t.State == task.Hot || t.State == task.Warm {
190						t.State = task.Cold
191					}
192					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
193				},
194			})
195		}
196		return out
197	}
198	
199	func confirm(app *App, in *bufio.Reader, action string) bool {
200		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s? [y/N] ", action)
201		line, err := in.ReadString('\n')
202		if err != nil {
203			return false
204		}
205		answer := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line))
206		return answer == "y" || answer == "yes"
207	}

16	func newDoneCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
17		var (
18			ff           bool
19			pr           bool
20			deleteBranch bool
21			keepWorktree bool
22			push         bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "done [task]",
26			Short: "Integrate a finished change stream and clean up",
27			Long: `Finish a task: integrate the branch, then remove what it leaves behind.
28	
29	Two integration modes, matching the two shapes a branch's history takes:
30	
31	  --ff    rebase onto the base and fast-forward it. Use when the branch's
32	          commits are worth keeping in the base's history.
33	  --pr    push and open a pull/merge request with gh or glab, leaving the
34	          merge to review and CI. Use when someone (or something) should look
35	          at it first.
36	
37	With neither, dev only reports what it would do.
38	
39	Cleanup is deliberately conservative: the worktree is removed, the task entry
40	is marked done, and the branch is deleted only with --delete-branch. A merged
41	branch that still has unpushed commits is never deleted.`,
42			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
43			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
44				ctx := ctxOf()
45				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
46				if err != nil {
47					return err
48				}
49				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
50				if _, err := os.Stat(checkout); err != nil {
51					return fmt.Errorf("%s no longer exists — resume the task first", config.Contract(checkout))
52				}
53	
54				st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
55				if err != nil {
56					return err
57				}
58				if st.Dirty() {
59					return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes: %s.\n"+
60						"Commit them, or park the task with --wip, before finishing it",
61						config.Contract(checkout), st.Breakdown())
62				}
63	
64				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
65				if mode == task.ModeDirect {
66					if ff || pr || deleteBranch || keepWorktree {
67						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s is already on %s; it has no branch/worktree to integrate. "+
68							"Run `dev done` without --ff/--pr/--delete-branch/--keep-worktree", t.Title(), t.Branch)
69					}
70					if push {
71						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
72							return err
73						}
74					}
75					rt := app.Runtime()
76					if t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
77						if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
78							app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
79						}
80						t.RuntimeHandle = ""
81					}
82					t.State = task.Done
83					if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s completed directly on %s\n", task.Done.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Branch)
87					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   no branch or worktree was created or removed")
88					return nil
89				}
90	
91				base := t.Base
92				if base == "" {
93					base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
94				}
95				if base == "" {
96					return fmt.Errorf("cannot determine the base branch for %s — pass --base when starting a task", t.Repo)
97				}
98	
99				switch {
100				case ff && pr:
101					return fmt.Errorf("--ff and --pr are alternatives; pick one")
102				case pr:
103					if err := openPR(ctx, app, t, checkout, base); err != nil {
104						return err
105					}
106					// A PR hands integration to review; the task is not done yet,
107					// so state and cleanup stay untouched.
108					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nThe branch is under review — run `dev done --ff` or `dev sweep` after it merges.")
109					return nil
110				case ff:
111					if err := fastForward(ctx, app, t, checkout, base); err != nil {
112						return err
113					}
114				default:
115					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s on %s (base %s, %s)\n", t.Title(), t.Branch, base, st.Summary())
116					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing done. Choose an integration mode:")
117					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  dev done --ff    rebase onto "+base+" and fast-forward it")
118					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  dev done --pr    push and open a pull request")
119					return nil
120				}
121	
122				if push {
123					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "push", "origin", base); err != nil {
124						app.warnf("could not push %s: %v", base, err)
125					} else {
126						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", base)
127					}
128				}
129	
130				rt := app.Runtime()
131				if t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
132					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
133						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
134					}
135					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
136				}
137				if t.WorktreePath != "" && !keepWorktree {
138					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
139					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath}); err != nil {
140						app.warnf("could not remove the worktree: %v", err)
141					} else {
142						t.WorktreePath = ""
143					}
144				}
145				if deleteBranch {
146					if err := deleteMergedBranch(ctx, app, t.RepoPath, t.Branch, base); err != nil {
147						app.warnf("%v", err)
148					}
149				}
150	
151				t.State = task.Done
152				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
153					return err
154				}
155				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s merged into %s\n", task.Done.Icon(), t.Title(), base)
156				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   the task entry stays until `dev sweep --apply` reaps it\n")
157				return nil
158			},
159		}
160		f := cmd.Flags()
161		f.BoolVar(&ff, "ff", false, "rebase onto the base and fast-forward it")
162		f.BoolVar(&pr, "pr", false, "push and open a pull/merge request instead of merging locally")
163		f.BoolVar(&keepWorktree, "keep-worktree", false, "keep the worktree checkout")
164		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the resulting branch (direct mode pushes its current branch)")
165		// Off by default: a branch is cheap to keep and expensive to recreate, and
166		// "merged" is not always "finished" — work often continues on a branch
167		// after its first integration.
168		f.BoolVar(&deleteBranch, "delete-branch", false, "delete the branch once its commits are in the base")
169		return cmd
170	}
171	
172	func directPushHint(push bool) string {
173		if push {
174			return " --push"
175		}
176		return ""
177	}
178	
179	// fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
180	// forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
181	//
182	// merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
183	// branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
184	// a merge commit the user did not ask for.
185	func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
186		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
187		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
188			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
189				"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
190				err, config.Contract(checkout))
191		}
192		// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
193		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
194		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
195			return err
196		}
197		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
198			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
199				"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
200		}
201		return nil
202	}
203	
204	// deleteMergedBranch removes a branch only when git agrees its commits are already
205	// contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
206	func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
207		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
208			return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
209		}
210		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "branch", "-d", branch); err != nil {
211			return fmt.Errorf("could not delete %s: %w", branch, err)
212		}
213		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   deleted    branch %s\n", branch)
214		return nil
215	}
216	
217	// openPR pushes the branch and asks the forge CLI to open a pull/merge
218	// request. When no forge CLI is available dev prints the push result and the
219	// URL to open by hand, rather than failing: the branch being published is the
220	// part that actually matters.
221	func openPR(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
222		if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
223			return err
224		}
225		kind := forge.Detect(ctx, t.RepoPath)
226		f, err := forge.For(kind)
227		if err != nil || !f.Available() {
228			app.warnf("no forge CLI for this remote — the branch is pushed; open the request in your browser")
229			return nil
230		}
231		url, err := f.CreatePR(ctx, checkout, forge.PRRequest{
232			Base: base, Head: t.Branch, Fill: true,
233		})
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		if url != "" {
238			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   opened     %s\n", url)
239		}
240		return nil
241	}
242
