329	// repoNameFromRef derives a directory name from a clone reference.

332		if i := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:"); i >= 0 {
333			return ref[i+1:]
334		}
335		return ref
336	}

11	// worktree when it knows how — that is what groups the checkout under its

13	func openCheckout(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, dir, label string) (string, error) {

2	===== spec/delete_spec.md =====
3	# Delete Mode Specification
4	
5	## Overview
6	
7	Delete mode allows batch deletion of directories with visual feedback and confirmation. This is a multi-step operation designed to prevent accidental deletions.
8	
9	## Workflow
10	
11	### Step 1: Mark Items
12	
13	- Press `Ctrl-D` on any directory entry to mark it for deletion
14	- Marked entries display with `{strike}` token (dark red background)
15	- Selection indicator changes to show marked state
16	- Can continue navigating and marking multiple items
17	- Pressing `Ctrl-D` on an already-marked item unmarks it (toggle)
18	- Cannot mark the `[new]` entry
19	
20	### Step 2: Delete Mode UI
21	
22	When one or more items are marked:
23	
24	- Footer changes to show delete mode status
25	- Format: `DELETE MODE | X marked | Ctrl-D: Toggle | Enter: Confirm | Esc: Cancel`
26	- Marked items remain visible with strikethrough styling
27	
28	### Step 3: Confirm or Cancel
29	
30	| Key | Action |
31	|-----|--------|
32	| Enter | Show confirmation dialog |
33	| Esc | Exit delete mode, clear all marks |
34	| Ctrl-D | Toggle mark on current item |
35	| Arrow keys | Continue navigating |
36	
37	### Step 4: Type YES to Delete
38	
39	Confirmation dialog shows:
40	
41	```
42	Delete X directories?
43	
44	  - directory-1
45	  - directory-2
46	  - ...
47	
48	Type YES to confirm:
49	```
50	
51	- Must type exactly `YES` (case-sensitive) to proceed
52	- Any other input cancels the operation
53	- After typing, press Enter to submit
54	
55	## Script Output Format
56	
57	In exec mode, delete outputs a shell script that is evaluated by the shell wrapper.
58	
59	### Script Structure
60	
61	```sh
62	cd '/path/to/tries' && \
63	  test -d 'dir-name-1' ]] && rm -rf 'dir-name-1' && \
64	  test -d 'dir-name-2' ]] && rm -rf 'dir-name-2' && \
65	  cd '/original/pwd' 2>/dev/null || cd '/path/to/tries'
66	```
67	
68	Each command is on its own line, chained with `&& \` for readability, with 2-space indent on continuation lines.
69	
70	### Script Components
71	
72	1. **Change to tries base directory**
73	   ```sh
74	   cd '/path/to/tries' && \
75	   ```
76	   All deletions happen relative to the tries base path.
77	
78	2. **Per-item delete commands**
79	   ```sh
80	     test -d 'name' ]] && rm -rf 'name' && \
81	   ```
82	   - Check directory exists before deletion
83	   - Use basename only (not full path)
84	   - Each on its own line with continuation
85	
86	3. **PWD restoration**
87	   ```sh
88	    cd '/original/pwd' 2>/dev/null || cd '/path/to/tries'
89	   ```
90	   - Attempt to return to original working directory
91	   - Fall back to tries base path if original no longer exists
92	   - Avoid shell-specific subshell syntax so output stays shell-neutral
93	
94	### Quote Escaping
95	
96	All paths use single quotes with proper escaping:
97	- Single quotes in names: `'` becomes `'"'"'`
98	- Example: `it's-a-test` becomes `'it'"'"'s-a-test'`
99	
100	### Example Output
101	
102	For deleting two directories from `/home/user/tries`:
103	
104	```sh
105	# if you can read this, you didn't launch try from an alias. run try --help.
106	cd '/home/user/tries' && \
107	  test -d '2025-11-29-old-project' ]] && rm -rf '2025-11-29-old-project' && \
108	  test -d '2025-11-28-abandoned' ]] && rm -rf '2025-11-28-abandoned' && \
109	  cd '/home/user/code' 2>/dev/null || cd '/home/user/tries'
110	```
111	
112	## Safety Guarantees
113	
114	### Path Containment
115	
116	- Deletions only happen within the tries base directory
117	- The `cd` to tries base ensures relative paths stay contained
118	- No symlink traversal outside tries directory
119	
120	### PWD Handling
121	
122	- If shell's PWD is inside a directory being deleted:
123	  - Script changes to tries base first
124	  - Then performs deletion
125	  - Attempts to restore PWD (which will fail gracefully)
126	  - Falls back to $HOME
127	
128	### Existence Check
129	
130	- `test -d 'name' ]]` prevents errors on already-deleted directories
131	- Safe for concurrent operations
132	
133	## Visual Tokens
134	
135	| Token | Effect | Usage |
136	|-------|--------|-------|
137	| `{strike}` | Dark red background (#5f0000) | Marked for deletion |
138	| `{/strike}` | Reset background | End deletion marking |
139	
140	## Keyboard Reference
141	
142	| Context | Key | Action |
143	|---------|-----|--------|
144	| Normal mode | Ctrl-D | Mark item, enter delete mode |
145	| Delete mode | Ctrl-D | Toggle mark on current item |
146	| Delete mode | Enter | Show confirmation dialog |
147	| Delete mode | Esc | Exit delete mode, clear marks |
148	| Confirmation | YES + Enter | Execute deletion |
149	| Confirmation | Other + Enter | Cancel deletion |
150	
151	===== spec/init_spec.md =====
152	# Init Command Specification
153	
154	The `init` command outputs a shell function definition that must be evaluated (sourced) by the user's shell to enable the `try` command.
155	
156	## Purpose
157	
158	The shell function wrapper is necessary because:
159	1. A subprocess cannot change the parent shell's working directory
160	2. The wrapper captures `try exec` output and `eval`s it in the current shell
161	3. This allows commands like `cd` to actually change the current directory
162	
163	## Shell Detection
164	
165	The init command should detect the user's shell via the `$SHELL` environment variable and output the appropriate function syntax.
166	
167	Supported shells:
168	- **Bash/Zsh**: POSIX-compatible function syntax
169	- **Fish**: Fish-specific function syntax
170	
171	## Function Output Format
172	
173	### Bash/Zsh Format
174	
175	```bash
176	try() {
177	  local out
178	  out=$('/path/to/try' exec --path '/default/tries/path' "$@" 2>/dev/tty)
179	  if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
180	    eval "$out"
181	  else
182	    echo "$out"
183	  fi
184	}
185	```
186	
187	Key elements:
188	- Function name: `try`
189	- Captures `try exec` output to local variable
190	- Redirects stderr to `/dev/tty` (TUI renders to stderr)
191	- Exit code 0: Evaluates the output (executes cd, git clone, etc.)
192	- Exit code non-0: Prints the output (shows error/cancellation message)
193	
194	### Fish Format
195	
196	```fish
197	function try
198	  set -l out (/path/to/try exec --path '/default/tries/path' $argv 2>/dev/tty | string collect)
199	  if test $pipestatus[1] -eq 0
200	    eval $out
201	  else
202	    echo $out
203	  end
204	end
205	```
206	
207	## Path Embedding
208	
209	The init output must embed:
210	1. The full path to the `try` binary (resolved at init time)
211	2. The default tries path (typically `~/src/tries`)
212	
213	This ensures the wrapper always calls the correct binary regardless of `$PATH` changes.
214	
215	## Installation Instructions
216	
217	The user should add one of the following to their shell configuration:
218	
219	### Bash (~/.bashrc)
220	```bash
221	eval "$(try init)"
222	```
223	
224	### Zsh (~/.zshrc)
225	```zsh
226	eval "$(try init)"
227	```
228	
229	### Fish (~/.config/fish/config.fish)
230	```fish
231	try init | source
232	```
233	
234	## Exit Code Semantics
235	
236	The wrapper interprets `try exec` exit codes:
237	
238	| Exit Code | Meaning | Wrapper Action |
239	|-----------|---------|----------------|
240	| 0 | Success | `eval` the output (execute shell commands) |
241	| 1 | Cancelled/Error | Print the output (show message to user) |
242	
243	## Testing
244	
245	Test that init produces valid shell syntax:
246	```bash
247	# Test Bash syntax
248	bash -n <(try init)
249	
250	# Test Fish syntax (if fish is available)
251	fish -n <(SHELL=/usr/bin/fish try init)
252	```
253	
254	Test that the wrapper works correctly:
255	```bash
256	eval "$(try init)"
257	try cd  # Should launch selector and cd on selection
258	```
259	
260	===== spec/performance.md =====
261	# Performance Specification
262	
263	## Overview
264	
265	The `try` tool should feel instant even with hundreds of directories. This document specifies performance requirements and design patterns.
266	
267	## Directory Scanning
268	
269	### Single Pass Loading
270	
271	- Directory list is loaded **once** at startup
272	- Subsequent operations (filtering, sorting) work on the cached list
273	- List is only reloaded after mutations (delete, create)
274	
275	### Efficient Metadata Retrieval
276	
277	- Use single syscall per directory to get modification time
278	- Prefer `stat()` over `readdir()` + `stat()` when possible
279	- Cache modification times in memory
280	
281	### Platform-Specific Optimizations
282	
283	On systems that support it:
284	- Use `getdents64` for batch directory reading (Linux)
285	- Use `getattrlistbulk` for bulk metadata (macOS)
286	
287	## Fuzzy Matching
288	
289	### Forward-Only Algorithm
290	
291	The fuzzy matcher must be **O(n×m)** where:
292	- n = length of query
293	- m = length of directory name
294	
295	**Requirements:**
296	- Single forward pass through both strings
297	- No backtracking or recursion
298	- Early termination on mismatch
299	
300	### Scoring Algorithm
```

203	// RemoveRequest describes a worktree removal.
204	type RemoveRequest struct {
205		RepoPath string
206		Path     string
207		// Force allows removing a checkout with uncommitted changes. dev never
208		// sets this on its own: losing uncommitted work is exactly the outcome the
209		// tool exists to prevent.
210		Force bool
211		// RuntimeHandle is closed before the checkout is removed, so the
212		// multiplexer is not left pointing at a deleted directory.
213		RuntimeHandle string
214	}
215	
216	// Remove deletes a worktree checkout. It never deletes the branch — that stays
217	// a separate, explicit decision, matching git's own separation.
218	func (m *Manager) Remove(ctx context.Context, req RemoveRequest) error {
219		if req.RuntimeHandle != "" && m.Runtime != nil {
220			if err := m.Runtime.Close(ctx, req.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
221				m.logf("warning: could not close runtime session %s: %v", req.RuntimeHandle, err)
222			}
223		}
224		if _, err := os.Stat(req.Path); errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
225			// The directory is already gone; clear git's administrative entry.
226			return gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, req.RepoPath)
227		}
228		if err := gitx.RemoveWorktree(ctx, req.RepoPath, req.Path, req.Force); err != nil {
229			return err
230		}
231		m.logf("removed worktree %s", config.Contract(req.Path))
232		return nil
233	}
234	
235	// DirtyCheck reports whether a checkout has uncommitted work, so callers can
236	// refuse to remove it without an explicit --force.
237	func DirtyCheck(ctx context.Context, path string) (bool, gitx.Status, error) {
238		st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, path)
239		if err != nil {
240			return false, st, err
241		}
242		return st.Dirty(), st, nil
243	}

1	package forge
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"errors"
6		"io/fs"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"time"
10	)
11	
12	// Cache is the on-disk forge inventory. It exists for UI latency, not as a
13	// source of truth: the REMOTE tab should open instantly, and r refreshes it.
14	type Cache struct {
15		FetchedAt time.Time    `json:"fetched_at"`
16		Repos     []RemoteRepo `json:"repos"`
17	}
18	
19	// LoadCache returns a fresh cache, or false when it is missing, malformed or
20	// older than maxAge. A stale cache is deliberately not returned: showing a
21	// deleted private repo as current is more confusing than a brief reload.
22	func LoadCache(path string, maxAge time.Duration) (Cache, bool) {
23		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
24		if err != nil {
25			return Cache{}, false
26		}
27		var c Cache
28		if json.Unmarshal(b, &c) != nil || c.FetchedAt.IsZero() {
29			return Cache{}, false
30		}
31		if maxAge > 0 && time.Since(c.FetchedAt) > maxAge {
32			return Cache{}, false
33		}
34		return c, true
35	}
36	
37	// SaveCache atomically replaces the cache. A partial forge response may be
38	// cached — its FetchedAt still says exactly when it was observed.
39	func SaveCache(path string, repos []RemoteRepo) error {
40		if path == "" {
41			return errors.New("empty cache path")
42		}
43		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
44			return err
45		}
46		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(Cache{FetchedAt: time.Now().UTC(), Repos: repos}, "", "  ")
47		if err != nil {
48			return err
49		}
50		b = append(b, '\n')
51		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ".remotes-*.tmp")
52		if err != nil {
53			return err
54		}
55		name := tmp.Name()
56		defer os.Remove(name)
57		if _, err := tmp.Write(b); err != nil {
58			tmp.Close()
59			return err
60		}
61		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
62			return err
63		}
64		if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o600); err != nil {
65			return err
66		}
67		return os.Rename(name, path)
68	}
69	
70	// CacheExists reports whether any cache file exists, even stale. Used only for
71	// diagnostics.
72	func CacheExists(path string) bool {
73		_, err := os.Stat(path)
74		return err == nil || !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)
75	}
76

## Executive findings

`dev-cli` already has a committed `dev try` / `dev graduate` foundation. The missing lifecycle pieces are chiefly:

1. Persistent try-level metadata distinct from task metadata.
2. Explicit cleanup/list-size commands and policy.
3. Reliable “last used” tracking.
4. Byte-size collection with clearly defined semantics.
5. Strong containment and recoverability checks for deleting arbitrary try directories.

The local checkout had pre-existing uncommitted changes; I made no edits.

## Upstream `try` research

### Relationship between the repositories

- [`daviddwlee84/try`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/try) is a fork of [`tobi/try`](https://github.com/tobi/try).
- At inspection time the fork was 3 commits ahead and 17 behind.
- Its substantive lifecycle delta is live Git metadata:
  - [`lib/git_info.rb`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/try/blob/main/lib/git_info.rb)
  - [`try.rb`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/try/blob/main/try.rb), `TrySelector#load_all_tries`
- Current upstream `tobi/try` additionally supports GitHub PR URLs, more SSH URL shapes, and terminal-manager metadata updates.

### UX and commands worth reusing

Both implementations use a top-level scratch root:

- `TRY_PATH`, default `~/src/tries`.
- `TRY_PROJECTS`, defaulting effectively to the parent of the tries root for graduation.
- No database or manifest: each immediate child directory is one try.

Relevant commands/actions:

- Browse and fuzzy-filter all tries.
- Enter an existing try or create a date-prefixed one.
- `new <name>`.
- Clone from URL, including URL shorthand.
- Create a detached linked worktree from the current or named repository.
- Rename.
- “Graduate”/ascend a try into the projects directory.
- Batch-mark and delete tries.
- Shell initialization that evaluates emitted `cd`/filesystem commands in the parent shell.

Important symbols:

- Fork:
  - `TrySelector#load_all_tries`, `#handle_create_new`, `#confirm_batch_delete`, `#process_delete_confirmation`
  - `parse_git_uri`, `generate_clone_directory_name`
  - `script_clone`, `script_worktree`, `script_delete`, `script_ascend`, `script_rename`
  - [`try.rb`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/try/blob/main/try.rb)
- Current upstream:
  - `TrySelector#load_all_tries`, `#finalize_rename`, `#finalize_ascend`
  - `parse_git_uri`, `github_pr_details`, `resolve_unique_name_with_versioning`
  - `script_clone_pr`, `script_worktree`, `script_delete`, `script_ascend`
  - [`try.rb`](https://github.com/tobi/try/blob/main/try.rb)

Useful behavior:

- Date-prefixed names make age and disposable status visually obvious.
- Existing entries are favored over making `test2`-style duplicates.
- Current `tobi/try` explicitly `touch`es a directory when selected in `script_cd`; this makes directory mtime a meaningful “last opened” value.
- Clone names incorporate owner and repository, reducing collisions compared with basename alone.
- Name collisions are versioned rather than overwritten.
- Graduation strips the date prefix and preserves the existing Git history.
- Linked worktrees are moved with `git worktree move`, not raw `mv`.

### Storage and metadata

Upstream intentionally has almost no persisted metadata:

- Directory basename is identity and display metadata.
- Directory ctime/mtime drives age and recency.
- Symlinks are recognized and resolved.
- The fork derives Git branch, remote, ahead/behind, and dirty state live.

The fork’s `GitInfo.collect` in [`lib/git_info.rb`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/try/blob/main/lib/git_info.rb) runs several Git processes per directory:

- branch lookup;
- possibly a second lookup for detached HEAD;
- remote listing and URL lookup;
- upstream divergence;
- status.

That is acceptable for small roots but scales poorly in an interactive list. `dev-cli`’s single-process porcelain-v2 status implementation is already better.

### Cleanup and safety semantics

The strongest upstream pattern is staged batch deletion:

1. `Ctrl-D` toggles marks.
2. Enter shows the complete target list.
3. The user must type exact, case-sensitive `YES`.
4. All paths are validated before any action.
5. Each real path must start below the canonical real tries root.
6. The generated script changes to the root first and deletes only child basenames.
7. It tries to recover the shell’s working directory afterward.

References:

- [`spec/delete_spec.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/try/blob/main/spec/delete_spec.md)
- [`spec/tests/test_16_delete.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/try/blob/main/spec/tests/test_16_delete.sh)
- `TrySelector#confirm_batch_delete`
- `TrySelector#process_delete_confirmation`
- `script_delete`

There is no automatic age- or quota-based garbage collection. Cleanup is manually selected and confirmed.

Safety caveats not worth copying:

- The shell-eval architecture adds quoting and injection surface that a native Go command does not need.
- The fork’s clone command interpolates the URI less safely than current upstream.
- `script_worktree` suppresses worktree creation failures with `|| true`; it can proceed into a pre-created but empty directory.
- Prefix containment must use separator-aware, canonical path checks. A naïve string prefix is insufficient on paths such as `/tries-old`.

## Existing `dev-cli` capabilities

### Config and storage

Configuration is already structured for this feature:

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/config/paths.go`
  - `ConfigHome`, `DataHome`, `CacheHome`
  - `ConfigFile`
  - `Expand` and `Contract`
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/config/config.go`
  - `Config`
  - `Paths.TriesRoot`
  - `Paths.StateDir`
  - `Paths.ProjectRoot`
  - `Default`, `Load`, `Validate`
  - `StateDir`, `TasksDir`

Defaults already include:

- tries root: `~/src/tries`;
- state: `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev`;
- project root: `~/Documents/Program`.

`Load` overlays TOML on defaults, rejects malformed configuration, and warns on unknown keys.

Persistent task state provides a strong model:

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/task/task.go`
  - `Task`
  - `Task.Tags`
  - `Created`, `Updated`

  - one TOML file per task;

For tries, a separate store is preferable to overloading `Task`: a try may have no branch, task, runtime, or remote. A state-side record could hold canonical path, display name, created/last-opened time, origin URL/repo identity, disposition, tags, and optional graduated destination.

### Metadata and tagging gaps

Existing metadata:

- Task-level `Tags`, persisted and emitted through JSON.
- Repository category inferred from the path hierarchy.
- Repository facts: path, real path, scan root, category, bare/non-bare, Git presence.
- Remote inventory facts: forge, full name, URLs, visibility, archived/fork, default branch, update time.

References:

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/task/task.go`, `Task.Tags`
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/repo/discover.go`, `Repo`
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/forge/forge.go`, `RemoteRepo`
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/list.go`

Gaps:

- No repository-level or try-level tag registry.
- No CLI path currently appears to assign `Task.Tags`; the field is principally persistence/output capability.
- No persisted “disposable”, “keep”, “origin”, “last opened”, or cleanup-exempt marker.
- No stable metadata key for a non-Git scratch directory.

### Existing try lifecycle

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/try.go`:

- `newTryCmd`
- `listTries`
- `findTry`
- `openOrCD`

Current behavior:

- Creates `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>`.
- Initializes Git by default.
- Supports `--clone` and `--no-git`.
- Reuses a case-insensitive substring match, preferring the newest mtime.
- Lists age and basic dirty status.
- Sorts by directory mtime.

Important limitation: directory mtime is not a dependable activity timestamp. Editing a nested file does not necessarily update the top-level directory mtime, and `openOrCD` does not touch it. Reusing upstream’s explicit last-opened update—or storing that timestamp—is advisable.

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/graduate.go`:

- `newGraduateCmd`
- `resolveTry`
- `ensureInitialCommit`
- `isEmptyTree`

It already:

- strips date prefixes;
- supports category/name;
- previews the source and destination;
- has `--dry-run`;
- refuses an existing destination;
- uses same-filesystem atomic rename;
- initializes Git and creates a first commit when needed;
- optionally creates a private remote and pushes.

Safety gap: `resolveTry` accepts any existing explicit absolute/expanded directory before testing tries-root containment. This may be intentional general promotion, but cleanup code should not inherit that permissiveness. Delete/reap should require canonical containment below `TriesRoot`, with explicit handling for symlinks and the root itself.

### Git and remote helpers

Repository identity and worktree awareness are strong:

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/gitx/repo.go`
  - `Repo.GitCommonDir`
  - `Repo.Key`
  - `Discover`
  - `IsRepo`
  - `DefaultBranch`
  - `Remote`
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/repo/discover.go`
  - deduplicates by Git common-dir;

  - prunes dependency/build directories;
  - does not descend into repository source trees.

Remote helpers:

  - `IdentityFromURL`
  - `Preferred`

`IdentityFromURL` already normalizes common HTTPS and SCP-style GitHub/GitLab URLs. It is a better basis for try origin metadata than copying upstream’s regexes, though it currently only returns identities for recognized GitHub/GitLab hosts.

Live Git status is efficient:

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/gitx/status.go`
  - `StatusOf` gets branch, upstream, ahead/behind, staged/unstaged/untracked/conflicted state in one porcelain-v2 process.
  - `LastCommit` supports meaningful age.
  - `Status.Dirty`, `Published`, and `Synced` provide cleanup gates.

### Existing destructive-action patterns

The repository has a consistent safety vocabulary:

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/sweep.go`
  - report-only by default;
  - `--apply` required;
  - individual `[y/N]` confirmations;
  - `--yes` automation escape hatch;
  - never auto-removes dirty or unpublished work.
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/worktree.go`
  - dirty checkout removal requires explicit `--force`.
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/wt/manager.go`
  - `Manager.Remove`
  - closes the runtime first;
  - never deletes a branch;
  - prunes stale Git bookkeeping if the directory is already gone.
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/gitx/worktree.go`
  - `RemoveWorktree`
  - `PruneWorktrees`
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/done.go`
  - refuses dirty trees;
  - branch deletion requires `--delete-branch`;
  - `deleteMergedBranch` verifies ancestry and still uses safe `git branch -d`.
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/bootstrap.go`
  - plans first, then `--apply`, per-item confirmation, optional `--yes`.

Recommended try cleanup policy:

- listing/inspection is always read-only;
- `clean` reports candidates by default;
- `--apply` performs cleanup;
- interactive bulk deletion shows names, paths, size, Git state, and remote/recoverability;
- require typed `YES` for direct recursive deletion;
- reserve `--yes` for explicit scripted use;
- refuse dirty Git tries unless a separately named discard flag is supplied;
- distinguish “has a remote” from “fully recoverable”: an unpublished local branch or untracked file is not protected by the remote;
- never delete a shared Git common directory while another worktree/clone record depends on it.

## Size semantics and implementation options

There is currently no production filesystem-size utility. The only `go-humanize` reference is an indirect dependency in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/go.mod`; no Go source uses it.

### 1. Total on-disk subtree size

Definition: recursively count everything physically under the try directory, including its ordinary `.git`, dependencies, caches, build output, and untracked files.

Pros:

- Best answer to “how much space disappears if this standalone try directory is deleted?”
- Intuitive for ordinary clones and non-Git experiments.

Cons:

- O(number of entries).
- Walking `node_modules`, `.venv`, loose Git objects, and build outputs can dominate list latency.
- Logical byte totals from `FileInfo.Size` differ from allocated disk blocks for sparse files, APFS clones, compression, and hard links.
- Hard links can be double-counted without inode tracking.
- Symlink policy must be explicit; do not follow by default.

Use this for an opt-in `--size=total`, detailed view, or cached/background calculation—not every normal list/TUI refresh.

### 2. Worktree/reclaimable checkout size

Definition: recurse through the checkout while excluding the ordinary `.git` directory or linked-worktree `.git` pointer.

Pros:

- Shows the checked-out files, dependency directories, and build artifacts that worktree removal reclaims.
- Correctly avoids charging shared Git objects to each linked worktree.
- Most useful metric for comparing warm worktrees and try cleanup candidates.

Cons:

- Still expensive for dependency-heavy trees.
- For a standalone clone, it understates total deletion savings because Git objects are excluded.
- The name should be explicit: “checkout size” or “worktree files”, not simply “size”.

This is the best default metric when the feature spans linked worktrees and standalone tries.

### 3. Git/common-dir size

Definition: measure the canonical `GitCommonDir`, once per `Repo.Key`.

Options:

- Walk `Repo.GitCommonDir` for actual subtree bytes, including LFS cache and administrative files.
- Use `git count-objects -v` for object database statistics; this is cheap for packed repositories but does not represent every byte beneath `.git`.
- Use platform `du` for allocated blocks, accepting subprocess and portability differences.

Critical rule: linked worktrees share `GitCommonDir`; never attribute its full size to every worktree. Report it once at repository scope or show it as a separate shared value.

### Suggested display model

Expose separate columns/fields:

- `checkout_bytes`: recursively reclaimable with this directory/worktree.
- `git_bytes`: private `.git` for a standalone clone, or shared common-dir bytes with a `shared_git: true` marker.
- `total_bytes`: `checkout + private git` only when ownership is unambiguous.

For linked worktrees, avoid presenting `checkout + shared common-dir` as reclaimable total.

### Performance recommendations

- Keep default `dev try` scanning shallow: one `ReadDir`, stat, and optionally one Git status process.
- Add byte collection only under `--size`, `--long`, detail view, or background TUI jobs.
- Use bounded concurrency and context cancellation.
- Cache by canonical path with a TTL/manual refresh; top-level directory mtime alone does not invalidate nested-file changes reliably.
- Do not reuse repository-discovery skip rules for an “exact total”; skipping `node_modules` would omit precisely the data users often want.
- Define error behavior: unreadable entries should produce a partial/unknown marker, not silently claim an exact total.
- Start with logical regular-file bytes in portable Go; allocated-block accounting can be a later platform-specific mode.

## Important current inconsistencies

1. **Refresh drops external tools.**

   Pending code adds `Actions.ReloadConfig`, but `runTUI` does not populate it. Pressing `r` therefore receives a nil-tool `configMsg`, and `Update` assigns:

   ```

   This removes every configured tool for the remainder of the session.

2. **Config editing is inert.**

   `e` and `Actions.EditConfig` exist in the model, but `runTUI` does not supply the callback.

3. **Missing checkouts are not rebuilt from the TUI.**

   Comments and detail text say Enter rebuilds a cold/missing checkout, but `Actions.Open` in `internal/cli/tui.go:180` returns an error telling the user to run `dev resume`. It does not reuse resume behavior.

4. **Domain reuse is incomplete.**

   Task inventory genuinely shares `inventory.Collect`, but TUI Start/Park/Open/Clone are separate closures duplicating Cobra command semantics. This is already diverging: CLI `start` now supports direct, branch-only, and worktree modes, whereas TUI Start always creates a worktree task.

5. **Combined reloads discard partial success.**

   If either task or repository loading fails, `reloadMsg` causes `Update` to reject both successful and failed portions. Remote loading behaves differently and retains partial rows alongside the error.

## 2. Existing `dev try` implementation

Everything is currently in:

### Creation/open call path

```text
newTryCmd.RunE
  → config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot)
  → os.MkdirAll(root)
  → derive name
       explicit positional name
       or repoNameFromRef(clone)
  → config.Slug(strings.ReplaceAll(name, " ", "-"))
  → findTry(root, slug)                 [reuse, except clone]
  → date-prefixed destination
  → either:
       gitx.Run(root, "clone", url, dir)
       or os.MkdirAll(dir) + gitx.Run(dir, "init", "-b", "main")
  → config.Contract(dir) output
  → openOrCD(app, ctx, dir, basename)
       → App.Runtime()
       → runtime.None: App.cdDirective(dir)
       → otherwise openCheckout()
```

Reusable symbols:

- `newTryCmd`
- `tryEntry`
- `listTries`
- `findTry`
- `openOrCD`
- `repoNameFromRef` in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/repo.go`
- `config.Slug`, `config.Expand`, `config.Contract`
- `gitx.Run`, `gitx.StatusOf`
- `openCheckout` in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/helpers.go`

### Current identity and matching

A try’s implicit identity is its directory basename:

```text
YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>
```

`findTry(root, slug)`:

- scans only immediate child directories;
- performs case-insensitive substring matching;
- silently chooses the directory with the newest directory mtime when several match.

There is no exact-ID layer, ambiguity error, or stable UUID. By contrast, `task.Store.Resolve()` gives exact ID/branch precedence and errors on ambiguous substrings.

### Listing

`listTries()`:

- scans immediate non-hidden directories;
- takes `DirEntry.Info().ModTime()` as age;
- recognizes a repository only by the existence of `<try>/.git`;
- uses `gitx.StatusOf()` for dirty state;
- sorts newest directory mtime first;
- renders `TRY / AGE / GIT` using the shared CLI `Table`;
- writes the summary/promotion hint to stderr.

Important age constraint: a directory’s mtime changes when entries are created, removed, or renamed, but usually not when an existing file’s contents are edited. Thus `AGE` is not reliably “last worked on.” `gitx.LastCommit()` would improve committed tries but still miss dirty-file edit time.

There is no JSON try listing, recursive status, runtime/live column, archive state, owner, note, tags, next action, created timestamp, or persisted last-opened timestamp.

### Relationship to repository discovery

Tries are not a separate repository domain:

- Git-initialized tries can appear as ordinary repos if `tries_root` is also in `scan_roots`.
- `config.Default()` includes both `~/Documents/Program` and `~/src/tries`.
- `config.DetectLayout()` explicitly adds detected `TriesRoot` to scan roots.
- A manually customized `tries_root` is not automatically appended during ordinary `config.Load()`; the generated config handles this, but arbitrary overlays must keep the roots consistent.
- `--no-git` tries cannot appear in the REPOS TUI through repo discovery.

## 3. Graduation

Implementation:

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/graduate.go`
  - `newGraduateCmd`
  - `resolveTry`
  - `ensureInitialCommit`
  - `isEmptyTree`

Call path:

```text
newGraduateCmd.RunE
  → resolveTry(app, triesRoot, args)
       explicit absolute/expanded directory
       or exact child
       or findTry substring
       or enclosing try inferred from cwd
  → strip datePrefix unless --name supplied
  → destination = project_root/category/name
  → collision check
  → dry-run output, or:
       os.MkdirAll(parent)
       os.Rename(src, dest)
       git init if .git absent
       ensureInitialCommit()
       optional forge.Preferred().CreateRepo()
  → openOrCD(dest)
```

Semantics and constraints:

- Graduation moves, rather than copies, preserving `.git` history.
- `os.Rename` is atomic only on the same filesystem. Cross-device graduation explicitly fails and asks the user to copy/remove manually.
- There is no rollback after the rename if later git setup fails.
- `ensureInitialCommit()`:
  - keeps existing history;
  - creates `README.md` only if `.git` is the sole entry;
  - stages everything and commits `chore: graduate experiment into a project`.
- Initial-commit failure is only warned after the move; git-init failure is fatal.
- Remote creation is best-effort and optional.
- Graduation does not create a task entry.
- An explicit existing path accepted by `resolveTry()` need not be under `tries_root`.
- `--category` and `--name` are joined directly and are not slugged or explicitly rejected for `..` path components.
- CWD containment is lexical and does not resolve symlinks.

## 4. Domain models and persistence

### Tasks

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/task/task.go`
  - `State`: `Hot`, `Warm`, `Cold`, `Done`

  - `ParseState`, `JoinStates`

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/task/store.go`
  - `Store`
  - `Save`, `Get`, `List`, `Resolve`, `FindByWorktree`, `Delete`, `Sort`

Persistence convention:

```text
<paths.state_dir>/tasks/<repo>__<branch>.toml
```

`Store.Save()` stamps UTC second-resolution timestamps and writes through a temporary file plus `os.Rename`, making each task update atomic. One-file-per-task is intentionally sync-friendly.

`Store.Delete()` deletes only the TOML entry; it never touches git or a checkout.

### Current uncommitted mode axis

The current working tree adds:

```go
type CheckoutMode string

const (
    ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
    ModeBranch   CheckoutMode = "branch"
    ModeDirect   CheckoutMode = "direct"
)
```

`Task.EffectiveMode()` preserves old TOML compatibility:

- explicit `mode` wins;
- old entry with `worktree_path` infers worktree;
- otherwise branch;
- direct is never inferred because it changes integration semantics.

This is a good precedent for tries: resource kind/mode and lifecycle state should remain separate axes.

### Repository models

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/gitx/repo.go`

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/repo/discover.go`
  - `repo.Repo`: display path, real path, scan root, category, symlink/bare/git facts.
  - `Discover`, `Resolve`.

Repository discovery intentionally treats linked worktrees as execution state, not separate projects, and deduplicates aliases/physical paths by Git common-directory identity.

There is currently no:

- `internal/try` or `internal/experiment` package;
- `Try` model;
- try store;

`tryEntry` is a private presentation struct inside `internal/cli/try.go`.

## 6. Existing lifecycle and destructive-operation semantics

### Task transitions

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/start.go`
  - creates hot tasks.
  - Current uncommitted behavior supports worktree, branch-only, and direct modes.
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/park.go`
  - hot→warm by closing runtime and retaining checkout;
  - warm/hot→cold only after clean/pushed/reconstructible checks;
  - direct tasks cannot go cold.
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/resume.go`
  - warm/cold→hot;
  - reconstructs missing worktree from `origin/<branch>`;
  - enforces host ownership unless `--force`.
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/done.go`
  - dirty checkout is refused;
  - default is report-only;
  - `--ff` or `--pr` performs integration;
  - task is marked done rather than deleted;

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/sweep.go`
  - report-only unless `--apply`;
  - confirms each action unless `--yes`;
  - never deletes uncommitted work;
  - reaps done task metadata with `Store.Delete`;
  - can remove clean/pushed stale worktrees while preserving branches.

### Other deletion/move precedents

- `dev wt rm` in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/cli/worktree.go`
  - refuses dirty removal without `--force`;
  - removes checkout only, retains branch;
  - repairs the task record afterward.
- Bootstrap moves in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/dev-cli/internal/bootstrap/organize.go`
  - use plan-first validation and guarded `os.Rename`.
- Remote forge repositories have an `Archived` display fact, but there is no local-project archive operation.

Therefore, no existing command permanently deletes a try. The dominant policy is:

1. report/plan first;
2. establish recoverability;
3. require explicit destructive intent;
4. separate checkout deletion, branch deletion, and metadata deletion.

## 10. Best extension points

### Recommended domain seam

Create a dedicated try/experiment domain rather than putting more policy in `internal/cli/try.go`:

```text
Try/List(root)
Try/Resolve(root, ref)
Try/Create(request)
Try/Open
Try/Graduate(request)
Try/Archive
Try/Delete
```

Keep CLI rendering in `internal/cli`, and inject those operations into the TUI.

Do not model tries as `task.Task` directly:

- tries may use `--no-git`;
- `Task.Validate()` requires repo, branch, and repo path;
- task cold semantics require pushed reconstruction;
- graduation changes location and conceptual identity.

### TUI seam

A fourth `ViewTries` would require:

- `TryRow` alongside `RepoRow`/`RemoteRow`;
- `tries []TryRow` and `tryCursor`;
- `ReloadTries`, `OpenTry`, `GraduateTry`, `ArchiveTry` callbacks;
- `visibleTries/currentTry/currentDir` integration;
- list/detail/footer rendering;
- explicit confirmation mode for archive/delete;
- updates to `config.reservedKeys`;
- TUI tests mirroring view-switch/filter/open/confirmation tests.

### Lifecycle recommendation

Keep try lifecycle separate from task temperature:

- derived active/live facts: directory exists, Git status, runtime session;
- human intent: active vs archived;
- terminal outcome: graduated;
- permanent deletion only from an archived state or with a forceful, separately confirmed path.

An archive implemented as an atomic move under a hidden child such as `tries_root/.archive/` would fit existing conventions:

- reversible;
- same-filesystem rename likely;
- hidden by current `listTries`;
- hidden from current repo discovery because hidden directories are skipped.

If metadata is needed, follow `task.Store` with one TOML file per try under `paths.state_dir/tries`, temporary-file-plus-rename writes, and no cached Git facts. A stable ID should survive archive/path changes.

### Must-fix constraints before expanding behavior

1. Replace directory mtime as the sole age signal.
2. Make resolution exact-first and ambiguity-safe.
3. Enforce graduation/archive source containment or explicitly document arbitrary-path promotion.
4. Sanitize or reject `..` in category/name destination components.
5. Extract operations before wiring the TUI, avoiding a third copy of lifecycle logic.
6. Preserve current positional `dev try <name>` compatibility when designing subcommands.
7. Keep archive, permanent delete, graduation, and task lifecycle as distinct operations.

18	func newTryCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

20			list  bool
21			clone string
22			noGit bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "try [name]",
26			Short: "Make a dated scratch directory for an experiment",
27			Long: `Create (or jump to) a dated experiment directory under paths.tries_root.
28	
29	Experiments need a home that is neither /tmp (where they vanish) nor your
30	projects directory (where they accumulate as clutter you are afraid to delete).
31	A try is date-prefixed, disposable by default, and promotable with
32	"dev graduate" when it turns out to be real.
33	
34	  dev try                    list what is there
35	  dev try redis-streams      jump to a matching try, or create 2026-08-27-redis-streams
36	  dev try --clone <url>      clone a repo into a dated try directory`,
37			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
38			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
39				ctx := ctxOf()
40				root := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot)
41				if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
42					return err
43				}
44	
45				if list || (len(args) == 0 && clone == "") {
46					return listTries(app, root)
47				}
48	
49				name := ""
50				if len(args) == 1 {
51					name = args[0]
52				}
53				if clone != "" && name == "" {
54					name = repoNameFromRef(clone)
55				}
56				slug := config.Slug(strings.ReplaceAll(name, " ", "-"))
57	
58				// An existing try wins over creating a near-duplicate: the whole
59				// point is to stop accumulating test/test2/test-actually.
60				if match := findTry(root, slug); match != "" && clone == "" {
61					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(match))
62					return openOrCD(app, ctx, match, filepath.Base(match))
63				}
64	
65				dir := filepath.Join(root, time.Now().Format("2006-01-02")+"-"+slug)
66				if _, err := os.Stat(dir); err == nil {
67					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(dir))
68					return openOrCD(app, ctx, dir, filepath.Base(dir))
69				}
70	
71				if clone != "" {
72					url := clone

88						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "init", "-b", "main"); err != nil {
89							app.warnf("could not git init: %v", err)
90						}
91					}
92				}
93				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n", config.Contract(dir))
94				return openOrCD(app, ctx, dir, filepath.Base(dir))
95			},
96		}

101		return cmd
102	}

104	// tryEntry is one scratch directory with the facts needed to rank it.
105	type tryEntry struct {
106		name     string
107		path     string
108		modified time.Time
109		isRepo   bool
110		dirty    bool
111	}
112	
113	func listTries(app *App, root string) error {
114		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
115		if err != nil {
116			return err
117		}
118		var tries []tryEntry
119		for _, e := range entries {
120			if !e.IsDir() || strings.HasPrefix(e.Name(), ".") {
121				continue
122			}
123			info, err := e.Info()
124			if err != nil {
125				continue
126			}
127			path := filepath.Join(root, e.Name())
128			t := tryEntry{name: e.Name(), path: path, modified: info.ModTime()}
129			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
130				t.isRepo = true
131				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctxOf(), path); err == nil {
132					t.dirty = st.Dirty()
133				}
134			}
135			tries = append(tries, t)
136		}
137		if len(tries) == 0 {
138			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "No tries yet under %s\n", config.Contract(root))
139			return nil
140		}
141		// Most recently touched first: "what was I doing yesterday?" is the
142		// question a list of experiments actually gets asked.
143		sort.Slice(tries, func(i, j int) bool { return tries[i].modified.After(tries[j].modified) })
144	
145		tbl := NewTable("TRY", "AGE", "GIT")
146		for _, t := range tries {
147			gitCol := "—"
148			switch {
149			case t.isRepo && t.dirty:
150				gitCol = "repo ●"
151			case t.isRepo:
152				gitCol = "repo"
153			}
154			tbl.Add(truncate(t.name, 44), humanAge(time.Since(t.modified)), gitCol)
155		}
156		tbl.Render(app.Out)
157		fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\n%d tries under %s — promote one with `dev graduate <try>`\n",
158			len(tries), config.Contract(root))
159		return nil
160	}
161	
162	// findTry locates an existing try whose name contains the slug, preferring the
163	// most recent when several match.
164	func findTry(root, slug string) string {
165		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
166		if err != nil {
167			return ""
168		}
169		var best string
170		var bestTime time.Time
171		for _, e := range entries {
172			if !e.IsDir() || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(e.Name()), strings.ToLower(slug)) {
173				continue
174			}
175			info, err := e.Info()
176			if err != nil {
177				continue
178			}
179			if info.ModTime().After(bestTime) {
180				best, bestTime = filepath.Join(root, e.Name()), info.ModTime()
181			}
182		}
183		return best
184	}
185	
186	func openOrCD(app *App, ctx context.Context, dir, label string) error {
187		rt := app.Runtime()
188		if rt.Name() == "none" {
189			app.cdDirective(dir)
190			return nil
191		}
192		if _, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, dir, label); err != nil {
193			app.warnf("could not open a session: %v", err)
194		}
195		return nil
196	}

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"os"
7		"path/filepath"
8		"regexp"
9		"strings"
10	
11		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/forge"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
14		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
15	)
16	
17	// datePrefix matches the "2026-08-27-" a try directory carries.
18	var datePrefix = regexp.MustCompile(`^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-`)
19	
20	func newGraduateCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
21		var (
22			category string
23			name     string
24			private  bool
25			remote   bool
26			push     bool
27			dryRun   bool
28		)
29		cmd := &cobra.Command{
30			Use:   "graduate [try]",
31			Short: "Promote an experiment into a real project",
32			Long: `Move a try out of the scratch directory and into your projects tree.
33	
34	An experiment that turns out to matter should stop being an experiment, and
35	that transition is where things usually get lost — the directory keeps its date
36	prefix forever, or it gets copied by hand and the history is left behind.
37	
38	graduate moves the directory to <project_root>/<category>/<name>, drops the
39	date prefix, makes sure it has a git repo and a first commit, and optionally
40	creates the remote with gh or glab.
41	
42	With no argument, the try containing the current directory is used.`,
43			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
44			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
45				ctx := ctxOf()
46				triesRoot := config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.TriesRoot)
47	
48				src, err := resolveTry(app, triesRoot, args)
49				if err != nil {
50					return err
51				}
52				if name == "" {
53					name = datePrefix.ReplaceAllString(filepath.Base(src), "")
54				}
55				if name == "" {
56					return fmt.Errorf("could not derive a project name from %s — pass --name", src)
57				}
58	
59				dest := filepath.Join(config.Expand(app.Cfg.Paths.ProjectRoot), category, name)
60				if _, err := os.Stat(dest); err == nil {
61					return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists", config.Contract(dest))
62				}
63	
64				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "graduate  %s\n", config.Contract(src))
65				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "       →  %s\n", config.Contract(dest))
66				if dryRun {
67					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\n(dry run — nothing moved)")
68					return nil
69				}
70	
71				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dest), 0o755); err != nil {
72					return err
73				}
74				// Rename first: it is atomic within a filesystem and leaves
75				// nothing half-copied if it fails.
76				if err := os.Rename(src, dest); err != nil {
77					return fmt.Errorf("move %s: %w\n"+
78						"If the projects root is on another filesystem, copy it by hand and remove the try",
79						config.Contract(src), err)
80				}
81	
82				if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dest, ".git")); err != nil {
83					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dest, "init", "-b", "main"); err != nil {
84						return err
85					}
86					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   git init")
87				}
88				// An experiment usually has files but no commit. A project needs
89				// one: without a HEAD there is no default branch, so `dev start`
90				// would have nothing to base a worktree on.
91				if made, err := ensureInitialCommit(ctx, dest, name); err != nil {
92					app.warnf("could not make an initial commit: %v", err)
93				} else if made {
94					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   committed the existing work")
95				}
96	
97				if remote {
98					f, err := forge.Preferred()
99					if err != nil {
100						app.warnf("%v — the project is in place; add a remote by hand", err)
101					} else {
102						url, err := f.CreateRepo(ctx, dest, forge.RepoRequest{
103							Name: name, Private: private, Push: push,
104						})
105						if err != nil {
106							app.warnf("could not create the remote: %v", err)
107						} else {
108							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   remote    %s\n", url)
109						}
110					}
111				}
112	
113				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%s is now a project. Start work on it with:\n  dev start %s --task <name>\n",
114					name, name)
115				return openOrCD(app, ctx, dest, name)
116			},
117		}
118		f := cmd.Flags()
119		f.StringVarP(&category, "category", "c", "", "category subdirectory under project_root")
120		f.StringVar(&name, "name", "", "project name (default: the try name without its date prefix)")
121		f.BoolVar(&private, "private", true, "create the remote as private")
122		f.BoolVar(&remote, "remote", false, "create a remote repository with gh or glab")
123		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", true, "push after creating the remote")
124		f.BoolVar(&dryRun, "dry-run", false, "show what would happen without moving anything")
125		return cmd
126	}
127	
128	// resolveTry finds the try directory to graduate: an explicit reference, or
129	// the try containing the current directory.
130	func resolveTry(app *App, triesRoot string, args []string) (string, error) {
131		if len(args) == 1 {
132			ref := args[0]
133			if abs := config.Expand(ref); isDir(abs) {
134				return abs, nil
135			}
136			direct := filepath.Join(triesRoot, ref)
137			if isDir(direct) {
138				return direct, nil
139			}
140			if match := findTry(triesRoot, ref); match != "" {
141				return match, nil
142			}
143			return "", fmt.Errorf("no try matching %q under %s", ref, config.Contract(triesRoot))
144		}
145	
146		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
147		if err != nil {
148			return "", err
149		}
150		if !strings.HasPrefix(cwd, triesRoot+string(filepath.Separator)) {
151			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s is not inside %s — name the try to graduate",
152				config.Contract(cwd), config.Contract(triesRoot))
153		}
154		// Walk up to the try's own top-level directory, so running this from a
155		// subdirectory still graduates the whole experiment.
156		rel, _ := filepath.Rel(triesRoot, cwd)
157		first := strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator))[0]
158		return filepath.Join(triesRoot, first), nil
159	}
160	
161	func isDir(p string) bool {
162		info, err := os.Stat(p)
163		return err == nil && info.IsDir()
164	}
165	
166	// ensureInitialCommit gives a repository a first commit if it has none,
167	// seeding a README when the tree is otherwise empty. Reports whether it made
168	// one.
169	func ensureInitialCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) (bool, error) {
170		if _, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, dir); err == nil {
171			return false, nil // already has history
172		}
173		if empty, err := isEmptyTree(dir); err != nil {
174			return false, err
175		} else if empty {
176			readme := filepath.Join(dir, "README.md")
177			if err := os.WriteFile(readme, []byte("# "+name+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
178				return false, err
179			}
180		}
181		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
182			return false, err
183		}
184		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "commit", "-m", "chore: graduate experiment into a project"); err != nil {
185			return false, err
186		}
187		return true, nil
188	}
189	
190	// isEmptyTree reports a directory with nothing in it but git's own metadata.
191	func isEmptyTree(dir string) (bool, error) {
192		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
193		if err != nil {
194			return false, err
195		}
196		for _, e := range entries {
197			if e.Name() != ".git" {
198				return false, nil
199			}
200		}
201		return true, nil
202	}
203

1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12	
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15	
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26	
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29	
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40	
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49	
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64	
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67	
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70	
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80	
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86	
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105	
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
111		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
112		Next string   `toml:"next"`
113		Note string   `toml:"note"`
114		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
115	
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`

129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}

143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149	
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153	
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}

1	package task
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"io/fs"
7		"os"
8		"path/filepath"
9		"regexp"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"time"
13	
14		"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotFound is returned when no task matches an identifier.
18	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such task")
19	
20	// Store is a directory of one-TOML-file-per-task.
21	//
22	// One file per task, rather than a single registry document, is a deliberate
23	// choice: the state directory is meant to be syncable across machines (it can
24	// simply be a git repo), and a shared central file would conflict on every
25	// parallel edit while separate files merge cleanly.
26	type Store struct{ Dir string }
27	
28	// NewStore returns a store rooted at dir.
29	func NewStore(dir string) *Store { return &Store{Dir: dir} }
30	
31	var idUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
32	
33	// MakeID derives the stable filename stem for a repo+branch pair.
34	func MakeID(repo, branch string) string {
35		clean := func(s string) string {
36			s = idUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
37			for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
38				s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
39			}
40			return strings.Trim(s, "-._")
41		}
42		r, b := clean(repo), clean(branch)
43		if r == "" {
44			r = "repo"
45		}
46		if b == "" {
47			b = "branch"
48		}
49		return r + "__" + b
50	}
51	
52	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }
53	
54	// Save writes a task, stamping Updated (and Created on first write).
55	func (s *Store) Save(t *Task) error {
56		if t.ID == "" {
57			t.ID = MakeID(t.Repo, t.Branch)
58		}
59		if err := t.Validate(); err != nil {
60			return err
61		}
62		now := time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
63		if t.Created.IsZero() {
64			t.Created = now
65		}
66		t.Updated = now
67	
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
69			return fmt.Errorf("create state dir: %w", err)
70		}
71		// Write to a temp file and rename, so an interrupted write can never leave
72		// a half-parsed task behind.
73		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+t.ID+".*.tmp")
74		if err != nil {
75			return err
76		}
77		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
78		enc := toml.NewEncoder(tmp)
79		if err := enc.Encode(t); err != nil {
80			tmp.Close()
81			return fmt.Errorf("encode task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
82		}
83		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
84			return err
85		}
86		if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
87			return err
88		}
89		return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), s.path(t.ID))
90	}
91	
92	// Get loads one task by its exact id.
93	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Task, error) {
94		var t Task
95		if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &t); err != nil {
96			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
97				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
98			}
99			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read task %s: %w", id, err)
100		}
101		t.ID = id
102		return &t, nil
103	}
104	
105	// List loads every task, sorted by state (hot first) then most recent.
106	func (s *Store) List() ([]*Task, error) {
107		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
108		if err != nil {
109			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
110				return nil, nil // no state yet is a normal, empty inventory
111			}
112			return nil, err
113		}
114		var out []*Task
115		for _, e := range entries {
116			name := e.Name()
117			if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") {
118				continue
119			}
120			id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
121			t, err := s.Get(id)
122			if err != nil {
123				// One corrupt file must not hide the rest of the inventory.
124				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: skipping %s: %v\n", name, err)
125				continue
126			}
127			out = append(out, t)
128		}
129		Sort(out)
130		return out, nil
131	}
132	
133	// Delete removes a task entry. It never touches git state.
134	func (s *Store) Delete(id string) error {
135		err := os.Remove(s.path(id))
136		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137			return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
138		}
139		return err
140	}
141	
142	// Resolve finds a task from a loose user-supplied reference: an exact id, an
143	// exact branch, or a unique case-insensitive substring of the id, name or
144	// branch. An ambiguous reference is an error listing the candidates rather
145	// than a silent pick.
146	func (s *Store) Resolve(ref string) (*Task, error) {
147		if ref == "" {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("empty task reference: %w", ErrNotFound)
149		}
150		all, err := s.List()
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154		for _, t := range all {
155			if t.ID == ref || t.Branch == ref {
156				return t, nil
157			}
158		}
159		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
160		var hits []*Task
161		for _, t := range all {
162			hay := strings.ToLower(t.ID + " " + t.Name + " " + t.Branch + " " + t.Repo)
163			if strings.Contains(hay, needle) {
164				hits = append(hits, t)
165			}
166		}
167		switch len(hits) {
168		case 1:
169			return hits[0], nil
170		case 0:
171			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", ref, ErrNotFound)
172		default:
173			names := make([]string, len(hits))
174			for i, t := range hits {
175				names[i] = t.ID
176			}
177			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q is ambiguous: %s", ref, strings.Join(names, ", "))
178		}
179	}
180	
181	// FindByWorktree returns the task whose checkout contains dir.
182	//
183	// A task lives at exactly one place: its worktree when it has one, otherwise
184	// the main checkout. A task that has a linked worktree therefore does *not*
185	// claim the main checkout — otherwise standing in the main repo would match
186	// every worktree-based task of that repo. Among candidates, the longest path
187	// match wins so a nested checkout beats its parent.
188	func (s *Store) FindByWorktree(dir string) (*Task, error) {
189		all, err := s.List()
190		if err != nil {
191			return nil, err
192		}
193		under := func(dir, root string) bool {
194			return root != "" && (dir == root || strings.HasPrefix(dir, root+string(filepath.Separator)))
195		}
196		var best *Task
197		var bestLen int
198		for _, t := range all {
199			root := t.WorktreePath
200			if root == "" {
201				root = t.RepoPath
202			}
203			if under(dir, root) && len(root) > bestLen {
204				best, bestLen = t, len(root)
205			}
206		}
207		if best == nil {
208			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", dir, ErrNotFound)
209		}
210		return best, nil
211	}
212	
213	// stateRank orders states so the inventory reads as an attention queue.
214	func stateRank(s State) int {
215		switch s {
216		case Hot:
217			return 0
218		case Warm:
219			return 1
220		case Cold:
221			return 2
222		case Done:
223			return 3
224		}
225		return 4
226	}
227	
228	// Sort orders tasks hot-first, then by most recently updated.
229	func Sort(ts []*Task) {
230		sort.SliceStable(ts, func(i, j int) bool {
231			ri, rj := stateRank(ts[i].State), stateRank(ts[j].State)
232			if ri != rj {
233				return ri < rj
234			}
235			if !ts[i].Updated.Equal(ts[j].Updated) {
236				return ts[i].Updated.After(ts[j].Updated)
237			}
238			return ts[i].ID < ts[j].ID
239		})
240	}

1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"os"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// XDG base directories, resolved the way the spec prescribes: honor the
10	// environment variable when it holds an absolute path, otherwise fall back to
11	// the documented default under $HOME.
12	
13	func xdgDir(envVar, fallback string) string {
14		if v := os.Getenv(envVar); filepath.IsAbs(v) {
15			return v
16		}
17		return filepath.Join(home(), fallback)
18	}
19	
20	func home() string {
21		if h, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil && h != "" {
22			return h
23		}
24		return os.Getenv("HOME")
25	}
26	
27	// ConfigHome is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default ~/.config).
28	func ConfigHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ".config") }
29	
30	// DataHome is $XDG_DATA_HOME (default ~/.local/share).
31	func DataHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_DATA_HOME", ".local/share") }
32	
33	// CacheHome is $XDG_CACHE_HOME (default ~/.cache).
34	func CacheHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CACHE_HOME", ".cache") }
35	
36	// ConfigFile is the path dev loads its TOML configuration from.
37	func ConfigFile() string { return filepath.Join(ConfigHome(), "dev", "config.toml") }
38	
39	// Expand resolves a leading ~ and any environment variables in p, then makes
40	// the result absolute. Paths in config.toml are written by humans, so both
41	// "~/Worktrees" and "$WORK/trees" have to work.
42	func Expand(p string) string {
43		if p == "" {
44			return ""
45		}
46		p = os.ExpandEnv(p)
47		switch {
48		case p == "~":
49			p = home()
50		case strings.HasPrefix(p, "~/"):
51			p = filepath.Join(home(), p[2:])
52		}
53		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(p); err == nil {
54			return abs
55		}
56		return filepath.Clean(p)
57	}
58	
59	// Contract renders p with $HOME collapsed back to ~, for display only.
60	func Contract(p string) string {
61		h := home()
62		if h != "" && p == h {
63			return "~"
64		}
65		if h != "" && strings.HasPrefix(p, h+string(filepath.Separator)) {
66			return "~" + p[len(h):]
67		}
68		return p
69	}

119	// Tool is one external program bound to a key in the dashboard.
120	type Tool struct {
121		// Key launches it. A single character, and not one of the dashboard's own
122		// bindings — dev reports a clash rather than silently shadowing.
123		Key string `toml:"key"`
124		// Name is shown in the footer.
125		Name string `toml:"name"`
126		// Run is a shell command, executed in the selected row's checkout.
127		Run string `toml:"run"`
128		// Interactive runs through $SHELL -lic, loading the user's rc file so a
129		// shell alias or function can be used. Off by default: startup files can
130		// print output and alter environment in ways an ordinary command should
131		// not inherit accidentally.
132		Interactive bool `toml:"interactive"`
133	}
134	
135	// reservedKeys are the dashboard's own bindings. A tool cannot take one,
136	// because losing the ability to quit or move is not a trade anyone wants.
137	var reservedKeys = map[string]string{
138		"q": "quit", "j": "down", "k": "up", "g": "top", "G": "bottom",
139		"h": "previous view", "l": "next view", "tab": "next view",
140		"/": "filter", "r": "refresh", "o": "open", "p": "park",
141		"c": "edit next action", "s": "start a worktree task", "d": "start a direct task", "a": "include done",
142		"0": "clear filters", "1": "hot", "2": "warm", "3": "cold",
143		"?": "help", "H": "repo activity heatmap", "e": "edit config",
144	}
145	
146	// ReservedKey reports the dashboard binding a key would collide with.
147	func ReservedKey(key string) (string, bool) {
148		name, ok := reservedKeys[key]
149		return name, ok
150	}
151	
152	// DefaultTools are the programs bound when nothing is configured. They are
153	// written out in full by `dev config init` rather than left implicit, so what
154	// is bound is visible rather than something to discover by pressing keys.
155	func DefaultTools() []Tool {
156		return []Tool{
157			{Key: "L", Name: "lazygit", Run: "lazygit"},
158			{Key: "Y", Name: "yazi", Run: "yazi"},
159			{Key: "E", Name: "editor", Run: "$EDITOR ."},
160			{Key: "S", Name: "shell", Run: "$SHELL"},
161		}
162	}
163	
164	// EffectiveTools returns the configured tools, or the defaults when none are
165	// configured. A configured list replaces the defaults entirely — a partial
166	// merge would make it unclear which bindings are in effect.
167	func (c Config) EffectiveTools() []Tool {
168		if len(c.TUI.Tools) == 0 {
169			return DefaultTools()
170		}
171		return c.TUI.Tools
172	}
173	
174	// Stats configures activity collection for the heatmap.
175	type Stats struct {
176		// Sampler enables recording live agent/runtime activity into stats.db.
177		Sampler bool `toml:"sampler"`
178		// WakaTime enables the WakaTime importer as an additional source.
179		WakaTime bool `toml:"wakatime"`
180		// WakaTimeConfig points at the ini file holding the API key.
181		WakaTimeConfig string `toml:"wakatime_config"`
182	}
183	
184	// Default returns the built-in configuration: what dev does with no config.toml
185	// at all. It matches the layout documented in the README.
186	func Default() Config {
187		return Config{
188			Paths: Paths{
189				ScanRoots:    []string{"~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"},
190				TriesRoot:    "~/src/tries",
191				WorktreeRoot: "~/Worktrees",
192				WorktreePath: "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo}}/{{branch|slug}}",
193				StateDir:     filepath.Join(DataHome(), "dev"),
194				ProjectRoot:  "~/Documents/Program",
195			},
196			Runtime: Runtime{
197				Backend:        "auto",
198				MetadataSource: "dev",
199			},
200			Worktree: Worktree{
201				Include:          []string{".env", ".env.local"},
202				Link:             nil,
203				PostCreate:       PostCreate{Auto: true},
204				Strategy:         "reinstall",
205				ProvisionTimeout: Duration{10 * time.Minute},
206			},
207			Bootstrap: Bootstrap{
208				MaxDepth:       8,
209				FollowSymlinks: true,
210				Layout:         "flat",
211			},
212			Stats: Stats{
213				Sampler:        true,
214				WakaTime:       false,
215				WakaTimeConfig: "~/.wakatime.cfg",
216			},
217		}
218	}
219	
220	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
221	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
222	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
223	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
224		cfg := Default()
225		if path == "" {
226			path = ConfigFile()
227		}
228		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
229		switch {
230		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
231			return cfg, nil
232		case err != nil:
233			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
234		}
235		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
236			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
237			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
238			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
239		}
240		cfg.Source = path
241		return cfg, cfg.Validate()
242	}
243	
244	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a
245	// worktree create, when a directory has already been made.
246	func (c Config) Validate() error {
247		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
248		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "none":
249		default:
250			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
251		}
252		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
253			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
254		}
255		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
256			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
257		}
258		switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
259		case "", "flat", "preserve":
260		default:
261			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
262		}
263		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
264			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
265		}
266		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
267			return fmt.Errorf("forge.remote_limit must be zero (use default) or positive")
268		}
269		validStrategy := func(v string) bool {
270			switch v {
271			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
272				return true
273			}
274			return false
275		}
276		if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
277			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
278		}
279		for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
280			if !validStrategy(strategy) {
281				return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",
282					ecosystem, strategy)
283			}
284		}
285		seen := map[string]string{}
286		for i, t := range c.TUI.Tools {
287			switch {
288			case t.Key == "":
289				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key is required", i)
290			case t.Run == "":
291				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d] (%s): run is required", i, t.Key)
292			}
293			if binding, ok := ReservedKey(t.Key); ok {
294				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is the dashboard's %q binding; pick another",
295					i, t.Key, binding)
296			}
297			if prev, ok := seen[t.Key]; ok {
298				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is already bound to %q", i, t.Key, prev)
299			}
300			seen[t.Key] = t.Name
301		}
302		return nil
303	}
304	
305	// probeVars is a dummy environment used to validate a template without having
306	// a real repo in hand.
307	func (c Config) probeVars() Vars {
308		return Vars{
309			"worktree_root": Expand(c.Paths.WorktreeRoot),
310			"repo":          "repo",
311			"repo_path":     "/repo",
312			"branch":        "branch",
313			"category":      "category",
314			"host":          "host",
315			"date":          "2006-01-02",
316		}
317	}
318	
319	// StateDir is the expanded directory holding tasks/, stats.db and cache/.
320	func (c Config) StateDir() string { return Expand(c.Paths.StateDir) }
321	
322	// TasksDir holds one TOML file per task.
323	func (c Config) TasksDir() string { return filepath.Join(c.StateDir(), "tasks") }
324	
325	// ScanRoots returns the expanded repo discovery roots.
326	func (c Config) ScanRoots() []string {
327		out := make([]string, 0, len(c.Paths.ScanRoots))
328		for _, r := range c.Paths.ScanRoots {
329			if e := Expand(r); e != "" {
330				out = append(out, e)
331			}
332		}
333		return out
334	}
335	
336	// WorktreePathFor renders the configured template for one repo+branch pair.
337	func (c Config) WorktreePathFor(repoName, repoPath, branch, category string) (string, error) {
338		v := Vars{
339			"worktree_root": Expand(c.Paths.WorktreeRoot),
340			"repo":          repoName,
341			"repo_path":     repoPath,
342			"branch":        branch,
343			"category":      category,
344			"host":          Hostname(),
345			"date":          time.Now().Format("2006-01-02"),
346		}
347		rendered, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, v)
348		if err != nil {
349			return "", err
350		}
351		return Expand(rendered), nil
352	}
353	
354	// Hostname is the machine identity recorded as a task's owner.
355	func Hostname() string {
356		if h, err := os.Hostname(); err == nil && h != "" {
357			return h
358		}
359		return "unknown"
360	}

1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"time"
6	)
7	
8	// PostCreate accepts either of two TOML shapes, because both read naturally:
9	//
10	//	post_create = "auto"
11	//	post_create = ["uv sync", "npm ci"]
12	type PostCreate struct {
13		Auto     bool
14		Commands []string
15	}
16	
17	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
18	func (p *PostCreate) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
19		switch t := v.(type) {
20		case string:
21			if t != "auto" {
22				return fmt.Errorf("post_create: %q is not a valid string form (use \"auto\" or a list of commands)", t)
23			}
24			*p = PostCreate{Auto: true}
25			return nil
26		case []any:
27			cmds := make([]string, 0, len(t))
28			for i, e := range t {
29				s, ok := e.(string)
30				if !ok {
31					return fmt.Errorf("post_create[%d]: want a command string, got %T", i, e)
32				}
33				cmds = append(cmds, s)
34			}
35			*p = PostCreate{Commands: cmds}
36			return nil
37		default:
38			return fmt.Errorf("post_create: want \"auto\" or a list of command strings, got %T", v)
39		}
40	}
41	
42	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler so a config round-trips.
43	func (p PostCreate) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
44		if p.Auto {
45			return []byte(`"auto"`), nil
46		}
47		out := []byte("[")
48		for i, c := range p.Commands {
49			if i > 0 {
50				out = append(out, ", "...)
51			}
52			out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%q", c)...)
53		}
54		return append(out, ']'), nil
55	}
56	
57	// Duration is a time.Duration written in TOML as a Go duration string
58	// ("10m", "90s"), which is friendlier than a bare number of seconds.
59	type Duration struct{ time.Duration }
60	
61	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
62	func (d *Duration) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
63		switch t := v.(type) {
64		case string:
65			parsed, err := time.ParseDuration(t)
66			if err != nil {
67				return fmt.Errorf("duration %q: %w", t, err)
68			}
69			d.Duration = parsed
70			return nil
71		case int64:
72			d.Duration = time.Duration(t) * time.Second
73			return nil
74		default:
75			return fmt.Errorf("duration: want a string like \"10m\", got %T", v)
76		}
77	}
78	
79	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler.
80	func (d Duration) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
81		return []byte(fmt.Sprintf("%q", d.Duration.String())), nil
82	}
83
