11	)
12	
13	// Version is set at build time via -ldflags.
14	var Version = "dev"
15	
16	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
17	
18	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
19	
20	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
21	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
22	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
23	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
24	
25	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
26	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
27	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`
28	
29	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
30	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
31		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
32	}
33	
34	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
35	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
36	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
37	// descriptors.
38	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
39		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
40	
41		root := &cobra.Command{
42			Use:           "dev",
43			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
44			Long:          rootLong,
45			Version:       Version,
46			SilenceUsage:  true,
47			SilenceErrors: true,
48			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
49			// exists to answer.
50			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
51				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
52					out, err := skill.Render()
53					if err != nil {
54						return err
55					}
56					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
57					return nil
58				}
59				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
60				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
61				if interactive() {
62					return runTUI(app)
63				}
64				return runList(app, listOptions{})
65			},
66			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
67				return app.Load()
68			},
69		}
70	
71		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
72		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
73		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")
74		pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")
75	
76		// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
77		// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
78		root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")
79	
80		root.AddCommand(
81			newListCmd(app),
82			newTUICmd(app),
83			newStatusCmd(app),
84			newStartCmd(app),
85			newParkCmd(app),
86			newResumeCmd(app),
87			newDoneCmd(app),
88			newSweepCmd(app),
89			newAdoptCmd(app),
90			newBootstrapCmd(app),
91			newWorktreeCmd(app),
92			newRepoCmd(app),
93			newGitignoreCmd(app),
94			newTryCmd(app),
95			newGraduateCmd(app),
96			newStatsCmd(app),
97			newHelpTopicCmd(app),
98			newSkillCmd(app),
99			newDoctorCmd(app),
100			newShellInitCmd(app),
101			newConfigCmd(app),
102			newEditCmd(app),
103		)
104		root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
105		root.SetOut(out)
106		root.SetErr(errOut)
107		return root
108	}
109	
110	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
111	func Execute() int {
112		root := NewRootCommand()
113		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
114			msg := err.Error()
115			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
116			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
117				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
118			}
119			return 1
120		}
121		return 0
122	}

1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	}
32	
33	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
34	func (a *App) Load() error {
35		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
36		if err != nil {
37			return err
38		}
39		a.Cfg = cfg
40		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
41		if a.Out == nil {
42			a.Out = os.Stdout
43		}
44		if a.Err == nil {
45			a.Err = os.Stderr
46		}
47		return nil
48	}
49	
50	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
51	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
52	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
53		if a.noRuntime {
54			return runtime.None{}
55		}
56		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
57		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
58			backend = a.runtimeOverride
59		}
60		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
61		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
62			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
63		}
64		return rt
65	}
66	
67	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
68	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
69		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
70	}
71	
72	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
73	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
74		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
75	}
76	
77	// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
78	// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
79	// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
80	// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
81	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
82		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
83	}
84	
85	// ctx is the cancellable context commands run under.
86	func ctxOf() context.Context { return context.Background() }
87

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
10	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
11	type Repo struct {
12		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
13		Root string
14		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
15		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
16		GitCommonDir string
17		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
18		Name string
19		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
20		// the main checkout.
21		IsLinkedWorktree bool
22		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
23		MainRoot string
24		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
25		Bare bool
26	}
27	
28	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
29	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
30	
31	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
32	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
33		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
34		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
35		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
36			"rev-parse",
37			"--path-format=absolute",
38			"--show-toplevel",
39			"--git-common-dir",
40			"--is-bare-repository",
41		)
42		if err != nil {
43			return Repo{}, err
44		}
45		f := lines(out)
46		r := Repo{}
47		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
48		switch len(f) {
49		case 3:
50			r.Root = f[0]
51			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
52			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
53		case 2:
54			r.GitCommonDir = f[0]
55			r.Bare = f[1] == "true"
56		default:
57			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
58		}
59	
60		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
61		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
62		if r.Bare {
63			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
64		} else {
65			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
66		}
67		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.Root != r.MainRoot
68		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
69		if r.Bare {
70			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
71			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
72			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
73				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
74			}
75		}
76		return r, nil
77	}
78	
79	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
80	// a full Discover.
81	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
82		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
83		return err == nil
84	}
85	
86	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
87	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
88	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
89	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
90	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
91		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
92			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
93				return b
94			}
95		}
96		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
97			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
98				return cand
99			}
100		}
101		return ""
102	}
103	
104	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
105	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
106		if name == "" {
107			name = "origin"
108		}
109		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
110		if err != nil {
111			return ""
112		}
113		return out
114	}

1	package gitx
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"strconv"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// Status is the live git state of one checkout — everything dev's inventory
10	// shows about a task without persisting any of it.
11	type Status struct {
12		Branch   string `json:"branch,omitempty"`
13		Detached bool   `json:"detached"`
14		// Upstream is the tracking ref (e.g. "origin/feat/auth"), empty when the
15		// branch has never been published.
16		Upstream string `json:"upstream,omitempty"`
17		Ahead    int    `json:"ahead"`
18		Behind   int    `json:"behind"`
19		// Changed counts unique changed paths. Staged and Unstaged are index /
20		// working-tree views and can overlap when one path has both kinds of
21		// changes; Changed does not double-count it.
22		Changed   int `json:"changed"`
23		Staged    int `json:"staged"`
24		Unstaged  int `json:"unstaged"`
25		Untracked int `json:"untracked"`
26		// Added, Modified, Deleted and Renamed classify status letters. One path
27		// can contribute to two when its staged and unstaged states differ.
28		Added    int `json:"added"`
29		Modified int `json:"modified"`
30		Deleted  int `json:"deleted"`
31		Renamed  int `json:"renamed"`
32		// Conflicted counts unmerged paths; a non-zero value means the checkout is
33		// mid-merge or mid-rebase and must not be touched automatically.
34		Conflicted int `json:"conflicted"`
35	}
36	
37	// Dirty reports uncommitted work of any kind.
38	func (s Status) Dirty() bool { return s.Changed > 0 }
39	
40	// Published reports whether the branch has an upstream at all.
41	func (s Status) Published() bool { return s.Upstream != "" }
42	
43	// Synced reports a branch that is published and exactly level with upstream.
44	func (s Status) Synced() bool { return s.Published() && s.Ahead == 0 && s.Behind == 0 }
45	
46	// Summary renders the compact, starship-like column used throughout dev:
47	//
48	//	⇕⇡2⇣1 =1 +3 !2 ?4
49	//
50	// Divergence, conflicts, staged, unstaged and untracked paths remain separate
51	// so "dirty" says how and by how much, rather than collapsing to one ●.
52	func (s Status) Summary() string {
53		var parts []string
54		switch {
55		case s.Ahead > 0 && s.Behind > 0:
56			parts = append(parts, "⇕⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead)+"⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
57		case s.Ahead > 0:
58			parts = append(parts, "⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead))
59		case s.Behind > 0:
60			parts = append(parts, "⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
61		}
62		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
63			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted))
64		}
65		if s.Staged > 0 {
66			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged))
67		}
68		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
69			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged))
70		}
71		if s.Untracked > 0 {
72			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked))
73		}
74		if len(parts) == 0 {
75			if !s.Published() {
76				return "local"
77			}
78			return "clean"
79		}
80		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
81	}
82	
83	// Breakdown renders the detailed change count shown by `dev status` and the
84	// TUI detail pane. Changed is the unique-path total; staged and unstaged may
85	// overlap, which is stated by presenting them as categories rather than a sum.
86	func (s Status) Breakdown() string {
87		if s.Changed == 0 {
88			return "0 changed paths"
89		}
90		var parts []string
91		if s.Staged > 0 {
92			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged)+" staged")
93		}
94		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
95			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged)+" unstaged")
96		}
97		if s.Untracked > 0 {
98			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked)+" untracked")
99		}
100		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
101			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted)+" conflicted")
102		}
103		return strconv.Itoa(s.Changed) + " changed paths (" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")"
104	}
105	
106	// TypeBreakdown classifies the status letters when that detail is available.
107	func (s Status) TypeBreakdown() string {
108		var parts []string
109		for _, item := range []struct {
110			n    int
111			name string
112		}{
113			{s.Added, "added"}, {s.Modified, "modified"}, {s.Deleted, "deleted"},
114			{s.Renamed, "renamed/copied"},
115		} {
116			if item.n > 0 {
117				parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(item.n)+" "+item.name)
118			}
119		}
120		return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
121	}
122	
123	// StatusOf reads the porcelain v2 status of the checkout at dir. Porcelain v2
124	// is the documented machine-readable format: it reports branch, upstream and
125	// ahead/behind in the same pass as the file states, so one process gives dev
126	// everything it needs.
127	func StatusOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Status, error) {
128		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=normal", "-z")
129		if err != nil {
130			return Status{}, err
131		}
132		var s Status
133		for _, rec := range nulLines(out) {
134			if rec == "" {
135				continue
136			}
137			switch rec[0] {
138			case '#':
139				parseBranchHeader(rec, &s)
140			case '1', '2':
141				// "1 XY ..." ordinary change, "2 XY ..." rename/copy. X is
142				// staged, Y unstaged. This record is one unique changed path even
143				// when both sides are non-dot.
144				f := strings.Fields(rec)
145				if len(f) < 2 || len(f[1]) < 2 {
146					continue
147				}
148				s.Changed++
149				x, y := f[1][0], f[1][1]
150				if x != '.' {
151					s.Staged++
152				}
153				if y != '.' {
154					s.Unstaged++
155				}
156				classifyChange(x, &s)
157				classifyChange(y, &s)
158			case 'u':
159				s.Changed++
160				s.Conflicted++
161			case '?':
162				s.Changed++
163				s.Untracked++
164			}
165		}
166		return s, nil
167	}
168	
169	func classifyChange(code byte, s *Status) {
170		switch code {
171		case 'A':
172			s.Added++
173		case 'M', 'T':
174			s.Modified++
175		case 'D':
176			s.Deleted++
177		case 'R', 'C':
178			s.Renamed++
179		}
180	}
181	
182	func parseBranchHeader(rec string, s *Status) {
183		f := strings.Fields(rec)
184		if len(f) < 3 {
185			return
186		}
187		switch f[1] {
188		case "branch.head":
189			if f[2] == "(detached)" {
190				s.Detached = true
191			} else {
192				s.Branch = f[2]
193			}
194		case "branch.upstream":
195			s.Upstream = f[2]
196		case "branch.ab":
197			// "# branch.ab +2 -1"
198			if len(f) < 4 {
199				return
200			}
201			s.Ahead, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[2], "+"))
202			s.Behind, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[3], "-"))
203		}
204	}
205	
206	// LastCommit reports the author timestamp of HEAD as a Unix epoch, and the
207	// subject line. Used to age a task in `dev sweep`.
208	func LastCommit(ctx context.Context, dir string) (unix int64, subject string, err error) {
209		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "log", "-1", "--format=%at%x00%s")
210		if err != nil || out == "" {
211			return 0, "", err
212		}
213		ts, subj, _ := strings.Cut(out, "\x00")
214		unix, _ = strconv.ParseInt(ts, 10, 64)
215		return unix, subj, nil
216	}
217	
218	// WipCommit stages everything and records a checkpoint commit.
219	//
220	// A checkpoint commit is deliberately preferred over `git stash`: a stash is
221	// invisible in the log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never
222	// travel to another machine, which is exactly what parking a task needs.
223	func WipCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, message string) (bool, error) {
224		st, err := StatusOf(ctx, dir)
225		if err != nil {
226			return false, err
227		}
228		if !st.Dirty() {
229			return false, nil
230		}
231		if st.Conflicted > 0 {
232			return false, &Error{Args: []string{"commit"}, Dir: dir,
233				Stderr: "checkout has unmerged paths; resolve the conflict before parking"}
234		}
235		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
236			return false, err
237		}
238		if message == "" {
239			message = "wip: checkpoint"
240		}
241		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", message); err != nil {
242			return false, err
243		}
244		return true, nil
245	}

1	package gitx
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"strings"
6	)
7	
8	// Worktree is one entry of `git worktree list --porcelain`.
9	type Worktree struct {
10		Path string
11		// Head is the commit the worktree is checked out at.
12		Head string
13		// Branch is the short branch name, empty when detached.
14		Branch   string
15		Detached bool
16		Bare     bool
17		// Locked reports a `git worktree lock`; Prunable reports a checkout whose
18		// directory has gone missing. Both block a plain remove.
19		Locked         bool
20		LockedReason   string
21		Prunable       bool
22		PrunableReason string
23		// Main reports the primary (non-linked) checkout.
24		Main bool
25	}
26	
27	// Worktrees lists every worktree of the repository containing dir, in git's
28	// own order: the main checkout first, then linked worktrees.
29	func Worktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]Worktree, error) {
30		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		var (
35			list []Worktree
36			cur  *Worktree
37		)
38		flush := func() {
39			if cur != nil {
40				list = append(list, *cur)
41				cur = nil
42			}
43		}
44		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
45			if line == "" { // records are blank-line separated
46				flush()
47				continue
48			}
49			key, val, _ := strings.Cut(line, " ")
50			switch key {
51			case "worktree":
52				flush()
53				cur = &Worktree{Path: val, Main: len(list) == 0}
54			case "HEAD":
55				if cur != nil {
56					cur.Head = val
57				}
58			case "branch":
59				if cur != nil {
60					cur.Branch = strings.TrimPrefix(val, "refs/heads/")
61				}
62			case "detached":
63				if cur != nil {
64					cur.Detached = true
65				}
66			case "bare":
67				if cur != nil {
68					cur.Bare = true
69				}
70			case "locked":
71				if cur != nil {
72					cur.Locked, cur.LockedReason = true, val
73				}
74			case "prunable":
75				if cur != nil {
76					cur.Prunable, cur.PrunableReason = true, val
77				}
78			}
79		}
80		flush()
81		return list, nil
82	}
83	
84	// WorktreeFor finds the worktree checked out on branch, if any. Git refuses to
85	// check the same branch out twice, so at most one can match.
86	func WorktreeFor(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) (Worktree, bool, error) {
87		list, err := Worktrees(ctx, dir)
88		if err != nil {
89			return Worktree{}, false, err
90		}
91		for _, w := range list {
92			if w.Branch == branch {
93				return w, true, nil
94			}
95		}
96		return Worktree{}, false, nil
97	}
98	
99	// AddWorktree creates a linked worktree at path.
100	//
101	// When branch already exists it is checked out; otherwise it is created from
102	// base. Passing an explicit base matters: without one git branches from the
103	// *current* HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on feature/A would
104	// silently inherit feature/A's commits.
105	func AddWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path, branch, base string) error {
106		exists := BranchExists(ctx, dir, branch)
107		args := []string{"worktree", "add"}
108		if exists {
109			args = append(args, path, branch)
110		} else {
111			args = append(args, "-b", branch, path)
112			if base != "" {
113				args = append(args, base)
114			}
115		}
116		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
117		return err
118	}
119	
120	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
121	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
122	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
123		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
124		if force {
125			args = append(args, "--force")
126		}
127		args = append(args, path)
128		_, err := run(ctx, dir, args...)
129		return err
130	}
131	
132	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
133	// were deleted behind git's back.
134	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
135		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
136		return err
137	}
138	
139	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
140	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
141		if branch == "" {
142			return false
143		}
144		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
145		return err == nil
146	}
147	
148	// RefExists reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves.
149	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
150		if ref == "" {
151			return false
152		}
153		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
154		return err == nil
155	}

1	// Package gitx wraps the git porcelain commands dev depends on. Every helper
2	// shells out to git rather than linking a Go implementation: git is already a
3	// hard dependency, its porcelain formats are stable and documented, and this
4	// keeps dev's behaviour identical to what the user sees when they run the same
5	// command by hand.
6	package gitx
7	
8	import (
9		"bytes"
10		"context"
11		"errors"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotARepo is returned when a directory is not inside a git working tree.
18	var ErrNotARepo = errors.New("not a git repository")
19	
20	// Error carries the failing command and git's own stderr, which is almost
21	// always more useful than the exit status alone.
22	type Error struct {
23		Args   []string
24		Dir    string
25		Stderr string
26		Err    error
27	}
28	
29	func (e *Error) Error() string {
30		msg := strings.TrimSpace(e.Stderr)
31		if msg == "" {
32			msg = e.Err.Error()
33		}
34		return fmt.Sprintf("git %s: %s", strings.Join(e.Args, " "), msg)
35	}
36	
37	func (e *Error) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
38	
39	// run executes git in dir and returns trimmed stdout.
40	func run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
41		// -c core.quotepath=false keeps non-ASCII paths readable rather than
42		// octal-escaped, which matters for the Chinese-named files in these repos.
43		full := append([]string{"-c", "core.quotepath=false"}, args...)
44		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
45		cmd.Dir = dir
46		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
47		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
48		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
49		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
50			gerr := &Error{Args: args, Dir: dir, Stderr: stderr.String(), Err: err}
51			if strings.Contains(gerr.Stderr, "not a git repository") {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", dir, ErrNotARepo)
53			}
54			return "", gerr
55		}
56		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
57	}
58	
59	// Run executes an arbitrary git command in dir. Exported for the few callers
60	// (park's wip commit, done's merge) that need a one-off command.
61	func Run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
62		return run(ctx, dir, args...)
63	}
64	
65	// lines splits git output into non-empty lines.
66	func lines(s string) []string {
67		if s == "" {
68			return nil
69		}
70		out := strings.Split(s, "\n")
71		filtered := out[:0]
72		for _, l := range out {
73			if l != "" {
74				filtered = append(filtered, l)
75			}
76		}
77		return filtered
78	}
79	
80	// nulLines splits NUL-delimited git output (-z forms).
81	func nulLines(s string) []string {
82		s = strings.TrimRight(s, "\x00")
83		if s == "" {
84			return nil
85		}
86		return strings.Split(s, "\x00")
87	}
88

1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
38		Bare bool
39		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
40		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
41		// initialise them.
42		HasGit bool
43	}
44	
45	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
46	func (r Repo) Display() string {
47		if r.Category == "" {
48			return r.Name
49		}
50		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
51	}
52	
53	// Options tunes discovery.
54	type Options struct {
55		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
56		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
57		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
58		MaxDepth int
59		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
60		IncludeNonRepos bool
61	}
62	
63	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
64	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
65	
66	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
67	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
68	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
69		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
70		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
71		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
72		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
73	}
74	
75	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
76	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
77	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
78	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
79		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
80			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
81		}
82		seen := map[string]bool{}
83		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
84		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
85		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
86		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
87		identities := map[string]bool{}
88		var out []Repo
89	
90		for _, root := range roots {
91			info, err := os.Stat(root)
92			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
93				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
94			}
95			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
96	
97			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
98				if err != nil {
99					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
100				}
101				if ctx.Err() != nil {
102					return ctx.Err()
103				}
104				if path == rootClean {
105					return nil
106				}
107				name := d.Name()
108				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
109				isDir := d.IsDir()
110				if isLink {
111					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
112					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
113					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
114					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
115						isDir = info.IsDir()
116					}
117				}
118				if !isDir {
119					return nil
120				}
121				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
122					return filepath.SkipDir
123				}
124	
125				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
126				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
127	
128				if isRepoDir(path) {
129					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
130					if real == "" {
131						real = path
132					}
133					bare := isBareDir(path)
134					identity := real
135					if !bare {
136						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
137							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
138							// project in the repo inventory.
139							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
140								return filepath.SkipDir
141							}
142							identity = g.GitCommonDir
143							real = g.MainRoot
144						}
145					}
146					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
147						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
148						out = append(out, Repo{
149							Name:     name,
150							Path:     path,
151							RealPath: real,
152							Symlink:  isLink,
153							Root:     rootClean,
154							Category: filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
155							Bare:     bare,
156							HasGit:   true,
157						})
158					}
159					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
160					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
161					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
162					return filepath.SkipDir
163				}
164				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
165					return filepath.SkipDir
166				}
167				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
168					if !seen[path] {
169						seen[path] = true
170						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
171					}
172				}
173				return nil
174			})
175			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
176				return out, ctx.Err()
177			}
178		}
179	
180		for i := range out {
181			if out[i].Category == "." {
182				out[i].Category = ""
183			}
184		}
185		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
186			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
187				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
188			}
189			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
190		})
191		return out, nil
192	}
193	
194	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
195	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
196	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
197		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
198			return true
199		}
200		return isBareDir(path)
201	}
202	
203	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
204	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
205		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
206			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
207				return false
208			}
209		}
210		return true
211	}
212	
213	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
214	//
215	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
216	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
217	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
218	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
219		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
220		if err != nil {
221			return Repo{}, nil, err
222		}
223		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
224			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
225				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
226				if real == "" {
227					real = g.MainRoot
228				}
229				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
230				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
231				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
232				return Repo{
233					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
234					Symlink: real != abs, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
235				}, nil, nil
236			}
237		}
238		for _, r := range all {
239			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
240				return r, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
244		var hits []Repo
245		for _, r := range all {
246			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
247				hits = append(hits, r)
248			}
249		}
250		switch len(hits) {
251		case 1:
252			return hits[0], nil, nil
253		case 0:
254			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
255		default:
256			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
257		}
258	}
259	
260	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
261	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
262	
263	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
264	
265	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
266	type AmbiguousError struct {
267		Ref        string
268		Candidates []Repo
269	}
270	
271	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
272		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
273		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
274			names[i] = c.Display()
275		}
276		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
277	}
278

```text
1	// Package inventory joins the three sources that describe work in progress:
2	// the task registry (human intent), git (durable code state) and the runtime
3	// (what is live right now). It is the single code path behind `dev ls`,
4	// `dev status`, `dev sweep` and the TUI, so all four can never disagree.
5	package inventory
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"os"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"sync"
13		"time"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
18	)
19	
20	// Row is one task enriched with everything derived live.
21	type Row struct {
22		Task *task.Task
23	
24		// Checkout is where the task's code currently lives: its worktree if it
25		// has one, else the repo. Empty when nothing exists on disk.
26		Checkout string
27		// CheckoutExists reports whether that directory is actually present. A
28		// cold task, or one whose worktree was removed behind dev's back, is not.
29		CheckoutExists bool
30		// WorktreeMissing flags a task that records a worktree path which is no
31		// longer a registered git worktree — the drift `dev sweep` reports.
32		WorktreeMissing bool
33	
34		// Status is the live git status of Checkout. Zero when there is nothing
35		// on disk to inspect.
36		Status    gitx.Status
37		StatusErr error
38	
39		// LastCommit is the author time of HEAD, used to age a task.
40		LastCommit time.Time
41	
42		// Session is the live runtime session hosting this checkout, if any.
43		Session *runtime.Session
44		// sessionsTracked reports whether the runtime can observe sessions at all.
45		// With the "none" backend it cannot, so "hot but nothing live" is not
46		// drift — it is the only state that backend can ever produce.
47		sessionsTracked bool
48	}
49	
50	// Live reports whether a runtime session is currently hosting this task.
51	func (r Row) Live() bool { return r.Session != nil }
52	
53	// StateDrift reports a task whose recorded state disagrees with reality:
54	// hot with no live session, or warm/cold with one. It is what `dev sweep`
55	// turns into suggestions — dev reports drift and never silently rewrites it.
56	func (r Row) StateDrift() string {
57		if r.sessionsTracked {
58			switch r.Task.State {
59			case task.Hot:
60				if !r.Live() {
61					return "no live session"
62				}
63			case task.Warm, task.Cold:
64				if r.Live() {
65					return "session is live"
66				}
67			}
68		}
69		if r.Task.State == task.Cold && r.CheckoutExists && r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
70			return "worktree still on disk"
71		}
72		if r.WorktreeMissing {
73			return "worktree is gone"
74		}
75		return ""
76	}
77	
78	// Age is how long since the task's last commit, falling back to when the entry
79	// was last written for a task with no commits of its own.
80	func (r Row) Age() time.Duration {
81		ref := r.LastCommit
82		if ref.IsZero() || r.Task.Updated.After(ref) {
83			ref = r.Task.Updated
84		}
85		if ref.IsZero() {
86			return 0
87		}
88		return time.Since(ref)
89	}
90	
91	// Options tunes what a Collect call spends time on.
92	type Options struct {
93		// SkipRuntime avoids querying the multiplexer, for callers that only need
94		// git facts (and for tests).
95		SkipRuntime bool
96		// SkipGit avoids running git per task, for a fast listing.
97		SkipGit bool
98	}
99	
100	// Collect builds the enriched inventory. Git probes run concurrently: each is
101	// a handful of process spawns, and a machine with dozens of tasks would
102	// otherwise make `dev ls` feel slow.
103	func Collect(ctx context.Context, tasks []*task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opts Options) []Row {
104		rows := make([]Row, len(tasks))
105	
106		var sessions []runtime.Session
107		tracked := false
108		if !opts.SkipRuntime && rt != nil && rt.Name() != "none" {
109			if s, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
110				sessions, tracked = s, true
111			}
112		}
113	
114		var wg sync.WaitGroup
115		// Bound concurrency: git is process-heavy and an unbounded fan-out over a
116		// large inventory would thrash.
117		sem := make(chan struct{}, 8)
118	
119		for i, t := range tasks {
120			rows[i].Task = t
121			rows[i].Checkout = checkoutOf(t)
122	
123			if opts.SkipGit || rows[i].Checkout == "" {
124				continue
125			}
126			wg.Add(1)
127			go func(i int) {
128				defer wg.Done()
129				sem <- struct{}{}
130				defer func() { <-sem }()
131				enrich(ctx, &rows[i])
132			}(i)
133		}
134		wg.Wait()
135	
136		for i := range rows {
137			rows[i].Session = matchSession(sessions, rows[i])
138			rows[i].sessionsTracked = tracked
139		}
140		return rows
141	}
142	
143	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
144		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
145			return t.WorktreePath
146		}
147		return t.RepoPath
148	}
149	
150	func enrich(ctx context.Context, r *Row) {
151		info, err := os.Stat(r.Checkout)
152		r.CheckoutExists = err == nil && info.IsDir()
153		if !r.CheckoutExists {
154			if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
155				r.WorktreeMissing = true
156			}
157			return
158		}
159		if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Checkout); err != nil {
160			r.StatusErr = err
161		} else {
162			r.Status = st
163		}
164		if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Checkout); err == nil && unix > 0 {
165			r.LastCommit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
166		}
167		// A recorded worktree that git no longer knows about is drift worth
168		// surfacing: the directory may exist while the administrative entry is gone.
169		if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
170			if _, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Task.RepoPath, r.Task.Branch); err == nil && !ok {
171				r.WorktreeMissing = true
172			}
173		}
174	}
175	
176	// matchSession picks the runtime session hosting a row's checkout. An exact
177	// directory match is preferred over a containing one, so a worktree's own
178	// session always wins over the parent repo's.
179	func matchSession(sessions []runtime.Session, r Row) *runtime.Session {
180		if r.Checkout == "" {
181			return nil
182		}
183		var contains *runtime.Session
184		for i := range sessions {
185			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
186				if d == r.Checkout {
187					return &sessions[i]
188				}
189				if strings.HasPrefix(d, r.Checkout+"/") && contains == nil {
190					contains = &sessions[i]
191				}
192			}
193		}
194		return contains
195	}
196	
197	// Filter narrows rows by state and repo. An empty filter matches everything.
198	type Filter struct {
199		States []task.State
200		Repo   string
201		// LiveOnly keeps only tasks with a runtime session.
202		LiveOnly bool
203		// DirtyOnly keeps only tasks with uncommitted work.
204		DirtyOnly bool
205	}
206	
207	// Apply returns the rows matching f.
208	func (f Filter) Apply(rows []Row) []Row {
209		out := rows[:0:0]
210		for _, r := range rows {
211			if len(f.States) > 0 && !containsState(f.States, r.Task.State) {
212				continue
213			}
214			if f.Repo != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Task.Repo), strings.ToLower(f.Repo)) {
215				continue
216			}
217			if f.LiveOnly && !r.Live() {
218				continue
219			}
220			if f.DirtyOnly && !r.Status.Dirty() {
221				continue
222			}
223			out = append(out, r)
224		}
225		return out
226	}
227	
228	func containsState(list []task.State, s task.State) bool {
229		for _, v := range list {
230			if v == s {
231				return true
232			}
233		}
234		return false
235	}
236	
237	// Orphans reports live runtime sessions that no task claims — the "I opened
238	// this and never wrote it down" case that makes a sidebar grow without bound.
239	func Orphans(sessions []runtime.Session, rows []Row) []runtime.Session {
240		claimed := map[string]bool{}
241		for _, r := range rows {
242			if r.Session != nil {
243				claimed[r.Session.Handle] = true
244			}
245		}
246		var out []runtime.Session
247		for _, s := range sessions {
248			if !claimed[s.Handle] {
249				out = append(out, s)
250			}
251		}
252		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Label < out[j].Label })
253		return out
254	}
255

12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/inventory"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/wt"
17		"github.com/spf13/cobra"
18	)
19	
20	// suggestion is one proposed change, with the reason and the exact effect.
21	type suggestion struct {
22		row    inventory.Row
23		action string
24		reason string
25		// apply performs the change. nil means "report only".
26		apply func() error
27	}
28	
29	func newSweepCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
30		var (
31			apply     bool
32			staleDays int
33			yes       bool
34		)
35		cmd := &cobra.Command{
36			Use:   "sweep",
37			Short: "Review stale tasks and drifted state, and act on them",
38			Long: `Show which tasks have gone stale or drifted, and what dev would do about it.
39	
40	Cleanup usually fails not because people are unwilling but because there is no
41	trustworthy way to be sure the work is recoverable. So sweep reports first and
42	only changes things with --apply, confirming each one unless you pass --yes.
43	Nothing here ever deletes uncommitted work.`,
44			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
45			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
46				ctx := ctxOf()
47				tasks, err := app.Tasks.List()
48				if err != nil {
49					return err
50				}
51				rt := app.Runtime()
52				rows := inventory.Collect(ctx, tasks, rt, inventory.Options{})
53				stale := time.Duration(staleDays) * 24 * time.Hour
54	
55				var sugg []suggestion
56				for _, r := range rows {
57					sugg = append(sugg, suggestFor(app, ctx, rt, r, stale)...)
58				}
59	
60				// Live sessions no task claims: the other half of a crowded sidebar.
61				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
62					if orphans := inventory.Orphans(sessions, rows); len(orphans) > 0 {
63						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d live session(s) with no task recorded:\n", len(orphans))
64						for _, s := range orphans {
65							dir := "—"
66							if len(s.Dirs) > 0 {
67								dir = config.Contract(s.Dirs[0])
68							}
69							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %-24s %s\n", truncate(s.Label, 24), dir)
70						}
71						fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "  → `dev start` in one of those directories to track it, or just close it.")
72					}
73				}
74	
75				if len(sugg) == 0 {
76					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nNothing to sweep — every task matches its recorded state.")
77					return nil
78				}
79	
80				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d suggestion(s):\n\n", len(sugg))
81				for _, s := range sugg {
82					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s %-28s %s\n", s.row.Task.State.Icon(),
83						truncate(s.row.Task.Title(), 28), s.reason)
84					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "     → %s\n", s.action)
85				}
86	
87				if !apply {
88					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nRe-run with --apply to act on these (each is confirmed individually).")
89					return nil
90				}
91	
92				in := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
93				for _, s := range sugg {
94					if s.apply == nil {
95						continue
96					}
97					if !yes && !confirm(app, in, s.action) {
98						continue
99					}
100					if err := s.apply(); err != nil {
101						app.warnf("%s: %v", s.row.Task.ID, err)
102						continue
103					}
104					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  done: %s\n", s.action)
105				}
106				return nil
107			},
108		}
109		f := cmd.Flags()
110		f.BoolVar(&apply, "apply", false, "act on the suggestions instead of only reporting")
111		f.IntVar(&staleDays, "stale-days", 14, "days without a commit before a task counts as stale")
112		f.BoolVar(&yes, "yes", false, "with --apply, do not confirm each change")
113		return cmd
114	}
115	
116	func suggestFor(app *App, ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, r inventory.Row, stale time.Duration) []suggestion {
117		t := r.Task
118		var out []suggestion
119	
120		switch {
121		// A hot task with no live session is the commonest drift: the session was
122		// closed (or the machine rebooted) without parking.
123		case t.State == task.Hot && !r.Live():
124			out = append(out, suggestion{
125				row:    r,
126				reason: fmt.Sprintf("hot but no live session, idle %s", humanAge(r.Age())),
127				action: fmt.Sprintf("mark %s warm", t.ID),
128				apply: func() error {
129					t.State = task.Warm
130					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
131				},
132			})
133	
134		// A warm task nobody has touched in weeks is a candidate for cold: keeping
135		// the worktree costs disk and clutters every listing.
136		case t.State == task.Warm && r.Age() > stale:
137			reason := fmt.Sprintf("warm and untouched for %s", humanAge(r.Age()))
138			if r.Status.Dirty() {
139				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but has uncommitted work",
140					action: "commit or `dev park --wip` before going cold — not changed automatically"})
141				break
142			}
143			if !r.Status.Synced() {
144				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + fmt.Sprintf(", not pushed (%s)", r.Status.Summary()),
145					action: fmt.Sprintf("push %s so it can go cold: dev park %s --cold --push", t.Branch, t.ID)})
146				break
147			}
148			out = append(out, suggestion{
149				row:    r,
150				reason: reason + ", clean and pushed",
151				action: fmt.Sprintf("go cold: remove %s (branch and remote keep the work)", config.Contract(r.Checkout)),
152				apply: func() error {
153					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
154					if t.WorktreePath != "" {
155						if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
156							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath, RuntimeHandle: t.RuntimeHandle,
157						}); err != nil {
158							return err
159						}
160						t.WorktreePath = ""
161					}
162					t.State, t.RuntimeHandle = task.Cold, ""
163					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
164				},
165			})
166	
167		// A done task's entry has served its purpose once the branch is gone.
168		case t.State == task.Done:
169			out = append(out, suggestion{
170				row:    r,
171				reason: "merged",
172				action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s", t.ID),
173				apply:  func() error { return app.Tasks.Delete(t.ID) },
174			})
175		}
176	
177		// Drift that is independent of the lifecycle stage.
178		if r.WorktreeMissing && t.WorktreePath != "" {
179			wtPath := t.WorktreePath
180			out = append(out, suggestion{
181				row:    r,
182				reason: "records a worktree that git no longer knows about",
183				action: fmt.Sprintf("clear the stale worktree path %s", config.Contract(wtPath)),
184				apply: func() error {
185					if err := gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, t.RepoPath); err != nil {
186						return err
187					}
188					t.WorktreePath = ""
189					if t.State == task.Hot || t.State == task.Warm {
190						t.State = task.Cold
191					}
192					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
193				},
194			})
195		}
196		return out
197	}
198	
199	func confirm(app *App, in *bufio.Reader, action string) bool {
200		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s? [y/N] ", action)
201		line, err := in.ReadString('\n')
202		if err != nil {
203			return false
204		}
205		answer := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line))
206		return answer == "y" || answer == "yes"
207	}

29	Two integration modes, matching the two shapes a branch's history takes:
30	
31	  --ff    rebase onto the base and fast-forward it. Use when the branch's

69					}

73						}
74					}

172	func directPushHint(push bool) string {
173		if push {
174			return " --push"
175		}
176		return ""
177	}
178	
179	// fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
180	// forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
181	//
182	// merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
183	// branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
184	// a merge commit the user did not ask for.
185	func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
186		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
187		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
188			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
189				"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
190				err, config.Contract(checkout))
191		}
192		// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
193		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
194		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
195			return err
196		}
197		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
198			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
199				"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
200		}
201		return nil
202	}
203	
204	// deleteMergedBranch removes a branch only when git agrees its commits are already
205	// contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
206	func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
207		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
208			return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
209		}
210		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "branch", "-d", branch); err != nil {
211			return fmt.Errorf("could not delete %s: %w", branch, err)
212		}
213		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   deleted    branch %s\n", branch)
214		return nil
215	}
216	
217	// openPR pushes the branch and asks the forge CLI to open a pull/merge
218	// request. When no forge CLI is available dev prints the push result and the
219	// URL to open by hand, rather than failing: the branch being published is the
220	// part that actually matters.
221	func openPR(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
222		if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
223			return err
224		}
225		kind := forge.Detect(ctx, t.RepoPath)
226		f, err := forge.For(kind)
227		if err != nil || !f.Available() {
228			app.warnf("no forge CLI for this remote — the branch is pushed; open the request in your browser")
229			return nil
230		}
231		url, err := f.CreatePR(ctx, checkout, forge.PRRequest{
232			Base: base, Head: t.Branch, Fill: true,
233		})
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		if url != "" {
238			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   opened     %s\n", url)
239		}
240		return nil
241	}

3	import (

15	)
16	
17	// Manager creates and removes worktrees according to the configured policy.
18	type Manager struct {
19		Cfg config.Config
20		// Runtime surfaces a new checkout in the multiplexer. May be nil.
21		Runtime runtime.Runtime
22		Log     io.Writer
23	}
24	
25	// CreateRequest describes one worktree to create.
26	type CreateRequest struct {
27		// RepoPath is the main checkout that owns the worktree.
28		RepoPath string
29		// RepoName is used in the path template and as the session label.
30		RepoName string
31		// Branch is the change stream. Created from Base when it does not exist.
32		Branch string
33		// Base is the ref a new branch starts from.
34		//
35		// Passing this explicitly matters more than it looks: without a base, git
36		// branches from the current HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on
37		// feature/A silently inherits feature/A's commits.
38		Base string
39		// Category feeds the path template.
40		Category string
41		// Path overrides the templated location entirely.
42		Path string
43		// Label names the runtime session.
44		Label string
45		// NoProvision skips dependency install and gitignored-file copying.
46		NoProvision bool
47		// NoRuntime skips surfacing the checkout in the multiplexer.
48		NoRuntime bool
49		// Focus opens the runtime session focused.
50		Focus bool
51	}
52	
53	// CreateResult reports what was created.
54	type CreateResult struct {
55		Path          string
56		Branch        string
57		BranchCreated bool
58		Provision     Result
59		RuntimeHandle string
60		RuntimeName   string
61	}
62	
63	// ErrExists reports a worktree that is already checked out for that branch.
64	type ErrExists struct {
65		Branch string
66		Path   string
67	}
68	
69	func (e *ErrExists) Error() string {
70		return fmt.Sprintf("branch %s is already checked out at %s", e.Branch, e.Path)
71	}
72	
73	func (m *Manager) logf(format string, args ...any) {
74		if m.Log != nil {
75			fmt.Fprintf(m.Log, format+"\n", args...)
76		}
77	}
78	
79	// Create adds a linked worktree, provisions it and surfaces it in the runtime.
80	func (m *Manager) Create(ctx context.Context, req CreateRequest) (*CreateResult, error) {
81		if req.Branch == "" {
82			return nil, errors.New("branch is required")
83		}
84		repo, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, req.RepoPath)
85		if err != nil {
86			return nil, err
87		}
88		// Always operate from the main checkout: creating a worktree from inside
89		// another worktree works, but the relative paths and the base ref get
90		// confusing fast.
91		repoPath := repo.MainRoot
92		if req.RepoName == "" {
93			req.RepoName = repo.Name
94		}
95	
96		// Git refuses to check one branch out twice, so an existing worktree for
97		// this branch is a reuse, not an error the user needs to resolve.
98		if existing, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch); err == nil && ok {
99			return nil, &ErrExists{Branch: req.Branch, Path: existing.Path}
100		}
101	
102		path := req.Path
103		if path == "" {
104			path, err = m.Cfg.WorktreePathFor(req.RepoName, repoPath, req.Branch, req.Category)
105			if err != nil {
106				return nil, err
107			}
108		} else {
109			path = config.Expand(path)
110		}
111		if err := m.checkTarget(path, repoPath); err != nil {
112			return nil, err
113		}
114	
115		base := req.Base
116		branchExisted := gitx.BranchExists(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch)
117		if !branchExisted {
118			if base == "" {
119				base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
120			}
121			if base != "" && !gitx.RefExists(ctx, repoPath, base) {
122				return nil, fmt.Errorf("base ref %q does not exist in %s", base, repoPath)
123			}
124		}
125	
126		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
127			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create worktree parent: %w", err)
128		}
129		if err := gitx.AddWorktree(ctx, repoPath, path, req.Branch, base); err != nil {
130			return nil, err
131		}
132		m.logf("worktree %s -> %s", req.Branch, config.Contract(path))
133	
134		res := &CreateResult{Path: path, Branch: req.Branch, BranchCreated: !branchExisted}
135	
136		if !req.NoProvision {
137			// SettingsFor folds in the repo's own .dev.toml, so a project can pin
138			// its setup where a teammate on another machine picks it up too.
139			p := &Provisioner{
140				Settings: SettingsFor(m.Cfg, repoPath),
141				Timeout:  m.Cfg.Worktree.ProvisionTimeout.Duration,
142				Log:      m.Log,
143			}
144			pr, err := p.Provision(ctx, repoPath, path)
145			if err != nil {
146				// The checkout exists and is usable; provisioning is best-effort.
147				m.logf("warning: provisioning: %v", err)
148			}
149			res.Provision = pr
150		}
151	
152		if !req.NoRuntime && m.Runtime != nil {
153			label := req.Label
154			if label == "" {
155				label = req.RepoName + "/" + req.Branch
156			}
157			handle, err := m.surface(ctx, path, label)
158			if err != nil {
159				m.logf("warning: could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
160			} else if m.Runtime.Name() != "none" {
161				res.RuntimeHandle, res.RuntimeName = handle, m.Runtime.Name()
162			}
163		}
164		return res, nil
165	}
166	
167	// surface registers the checkout with the runtime. When the backend
168	// understands git worktrees it is asked to open it as one, which is what makes
169	// the checkout appear grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
170	// ahead/behind row rather than as an unrelated directory.
171	func (m *Manager) surface(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error) {
172		if wo, ok := m.Runtime.(runtime.WorktreeOpener); ok {
173			return wo.OpenWorktree(ctx, path, label)
174		}
175		return m.Runtime.Open(ctx, path, label)
176	}
177	
178	// checkTarget refuses locations that would cause trouble later.
179	func (m *Manager) checkTarget(path, repoPath string) error {
180		if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
181			if !info.IsDir() {
182				return fmt.Errorf("%s exists and is not a directory", path)
183			}
184			entries, err := os.ReadDir(path)
185			if err != nil {
186				return err
187			}
188			if len(entries) > 0 {
189				return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists and is not empty", config.Contract(path))
190			}
191		}
192		// A worktree nested inside another checkout means every indexer, file
193		// watcher and ripgrep run in the outer repo sees a second copy of the
194		// tree. dev keeps checkouts as siblings under the worktree root instead.
195		if path == repoPath || strings.HasPrefix(path, repoPath+string(filepath.Separator)) {
196			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to create a worktree inside the repository (%s); "+
197				"set paths.worktree_path to a location outside %s",
198				config.Contract(path), config.Contract(repoPath))
199		}
200		return nil
201	}
202	
203	// RemoveRequest describes a worktree removal.
204	type RemoveRequest struct {
205		RepoPath string
206		Path     string
207		// Force allows removing a checkout with uncommitted changes. dev never
208		// sets this on its own: losing uncommitted work is exactly the outcome the
209		// tool exists to prevent.
210		Force bool
211		// RuntimeHandle is closed before the checkout is removed, so the
212		// multiplexer is not left pointing at a deleted directory.
213		RuntimeHandle string
214	}
215	
216	// Remove deletes a worktree checkout. It never deletes the branch — that stays
217	// a separate, explicit decision, matching git's own separation.
218	func (m *Manager) Remove(ctx context.Context, req RemoveRequest) error {
219		if req.RuntimeHandle != "" && m.Runtime != nil {
220			if err := m.Runtime.Close(ctx, req.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
221				m.logf("warning: could not close runtime session %s: %v", req.RuntimeHandle, err)
222			}
223		}
224		if _, err := os.Stat(req.Path); errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
225			// The directory is already gone; clear git's administrative entry.
226			return gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, req.RepoPath)
227		}
228		if err := gitx.RemoveWorktree(ctx, req.RepoPath, req.Path, req.Force); err != nil {
229			return err
230		}
231		m.logf("removed worktree %s", config.Contract(req.Path))
232		return nil
233	}
234	
235	// DirtyCheck reports whether a checkout has uncommitted work, so callers can
236	// refuse to remove it without an explicit --force.
237	func DirtyCheck(ctx context.Context, path string) (bool, gitx.Status, error) {
238		st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, path)
239		if err != nil {
240			return false, st, err
241		}
242		return st.Dirty(), st, nil
243	}
