```text
1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11	
12		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16	
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21	
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24	
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	}
32	
33	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
34	func (a *App) Load() error {
35		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
36		if err != nil {
37			return err
38		}
39		a.Cfg = cfg
40		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
41		if a.Out == nil {
42			a.Out = os.Stdout
43		}
44		if a.Err == nil {
45			a.Err = os.Stderr
46		}
47		return nil
48	}
49	
50	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
51	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
52	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
53		if a.noRuntime {
54			return runtime.None{}
55		}
56		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
57		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
58			backend = a.runtimeOverride
59		}
60		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
61		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
62			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
63		}
64		return rt
65	}
66	
67	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
68	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
69		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
70	}
71	
72	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
73	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
74		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
75	}

79	// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
80	// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
81	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
82		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
83	}
```

```text
256	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
257	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
258	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
259	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
260		cfg := Default()
261		if path == "" {
262			path = ConfigFile()
263		}
264		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
265		switch {
266		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
267			return cfg, nil
268		case err != nil:
269			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
270		}
271		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
272			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
273			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
274			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
275		}

298		}

314		}

318					ecosystem, strategy)

324			"category": true, "path": true,
```

```text
1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"regexp"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// Path templates are deliberately *not* text/template: the syntax users write
10	// in config.toml ("{{worktree_root}}/{{repo}}/{{branch|slug}}") needs to stay
11	// readable and to fail loudly on an unknown variable rather than silently
12	// rendering "<no value>".
13	
14	var tmplVar = regexp.MustCompile(`\{\{\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*(?:\|\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*)?\}\}`)
15	
16	// Vars is the substitution environment for a path template.
17	type Vars map[string]string
18	
19	// Render substitutes every {{var}} / {{var|filter}} occurrence in tmpl.
20	// An unknown variable or filter is an error — a typo in worktree_path should
21	// surface at create time, not as a directory literally named "{{rep}}".
22	func Render(tmpl string, vars Vars) (string, error) {
23		var firstErr error
24		out := tmplVar.ReplaceAllStringFunc(tmpl, func(m string) string {
25			g := tmplVar.FindStringSubmatch(m)
26			name, filter := g[1], g[2]
27			val, ok := vars[name]
28			if !ok {
29				if firstErr == nil {
30					firstErr = fmt.Errorf("unknown template variable %q in %q (known: %s)", name, tmpl, strings.Join(sortedKeys(vars), ", "))
31				}
32				return m
33			}
34			switch filter {
35			case "":
36				return val
37			case "slug":
38				return Slug(val)
39			case "lower":
40				return strings.ToLower(val)
41			case "base":
42				if i := strings.LastIndexByte(val, '/'); i >= 0 {
43					return val[i+1:]
44				}
45				return val
46			default:
47				if firstErr == nil {
48					firstErr = fmt.Errorf("unknown template filter %q in %q (known: slug, lower, base)", filter, tmpl)
49				}
50				return m
51			}
52		})
53		if firstErr != nil {
54			return "", firstErr
55		}
56		return out, nil
57	}
58	
59	var slugStrip = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
60	
61	// Slug makes a branch name safe to use as a single filesystem component:
62	// "feat/auth/oauth-refresh" becomes "feat-auth-oauth-refresh". Leading dots
63	// and dashes are trimmed so the result can never be a hidden directory or be
64	// mistaken for a flag.
65	func Slug(s string) string {
66		s = slugStrip.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
67		for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
68			s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
69		}
70		s = strings.Trim(s, "-._")
71		if s == "" {
72			return "unnamed"
73		}
74		return s
75	}
76	
77	func sortedKeys(v Vars) []string {
78		out := make([]string, 0, len(v))
79		for k := range v {
80			out = append(out, k)
81		}
82		// small map; insertion sort keeps this dependency-free
83		for i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {
84			for j := i; j > 0 && out[j] < out[j-1]; j-- {
85				out[j], out[j-1] = out[j-1], out[j]
86			}
87		}
88		return out
89	}
```

```text
76	func (h *harness) run(args ...string) (string, string, error) {

251	func TestTryAndGraduate(t *testing.T) {
252		h := newHarness(t)
253	
254		out := h.mustRun("try", "redis-streams")
255		if !strings.Contains(out, "redis-streams") {
256			t.Fatalf("try output: %q", out)
257		}
258		triesRoot := filepath.Join(h.home, "tries")
259		entries, _ := os.ReadDir(triesRoot)
260		if len(entries) != 1 {
261			t.Fatalf("want one try directory, got %d", len(entries))
262		}
263		tryName := entries[0].Name()
264		if !strings.HasSuffix(tryName, "-redis-streams") || len(tryName) < 21 {
265			t.Errorf("a try should be date-prefixed, got %q", tryName)
266		}
267	
268		// A second `try` with the same name reuses the existing directory rather
269		// than creating a near-duplicate.
270		h.mustRun("try", "redis-streams")
271		entries, _ = os.ReadDir(triesRoot)
272		if len(entries) != 1 {
273			t.Errorf("try should reuse an existing match, got %d directories", len(entries))
274		}
275	
276		out = h.mustRun("graduate", "redis-streams", "--category", "Infra")
277		if !strings.Contains(out, "is now a project") {
278			t.Fatalf("graduate output: %q", out)
279		}
280		dest := filepath.Join(h.scanRoot, "Infra", "redis-streams")
281		if _, err := os.Stat(dest); err != nil {
282			t.Fatalf("graduated project should exist at %s: %v", dest, err)
283		}
284		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(triesRoot, tryName)); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
285			t.Error("the try directory should have been moved, not copied")
286		}
287		// The date prefix is dropped, and it is a repo with history.
288		if _, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(gittest.Ctx(), dest); err != nil {
289			t.Errorf("a graduated project should have a commit: %v", err)
290		}
291	}

398	func TestAdoptReportsThenApplies(t *testing.T) {
399		h := newHarness(t)
400	
401		// A branch ahead of main, which is exactly the unfinished work adopt is for.
402		h.repo.Branch("feat/in-flight")
403		h.repo.Commit("wip.txt", "half done\n", "feat: in flight")
404		h.repo.Git("switch", "main")
405	
406		out := h.mustRun("adopt")
407		if !strings.Contains(out, "feat/in-flight") {
408			t.Fatalf("adopt should find the unmerged branch:\n%s", out)
409		}
410		if !strings.Contains(out, "--apply") {
411			t.Error("reporting run should say how to act on it")
412		}
413		// Reporting must not have created anything.
414		if ls := h.mustRun("ls"); !strings.Contains(ls, "No tasks yet") {
415			t.Errorf("adopt without --apply must create nothing, got:\n%s", ls)
416		}
417	
418		h.mustRun("adopt", "--apply", "--yes")
419		ls := h.mustRun("ls")
420		if !strings.Contains(ls, "feat/in-flight") {
421			t.Errorf("adopted task should appear in the inventory:\n%s", ls)
422		}
423	
424		// Adopting twice must not duplicate.
425		out = h.mustRun("adopt")
426		if strings.Contains(out, "feat/in-flight") {
427			t.Errorf("an already-tracked branch should not be offered again:\n%s", out)
428		}
429	}

530		root.SetArgs([]string{"--config", generated, "repo", "list", "--long"})
531		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
532			t.Fatal(err)

534		if !strings.Contains(listed.String(), config.Contract(filepath.Join(index, "demo"))) {
```

```text
1	// Package inventory joins the three sources that describe work in progress:
2	// the task registry (human intent), git (durable code state) and the runtime
3	// (what is live right now). It is the single code path behind `dev ls`,
4	// `dev status`, `dev sweep` and the TUI, so all four can never disagree.
5	package inventory
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"os"
10		"sort"
11		"strings"
12		"sync"
13		"time"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
18	)
19	
20	// Row is one task enriched with everything derived live.
21	type Row struct {
22		Task *task.Task
23	
24		// Checkout is where the task's code currently lives: its worktree if it
25		// has one, else the repo. Empty when nothing exists on disk.
26		Checkout string
27		// CheckoutExists reports whether that directory is actually present. A
28		// cold task, or one whose worktree was removed behind dev's back, is not.
29		CheckoutExists bool
30		// WorktreeMissing flags a task that records a worktree path which is no
31		// longer a registered git worktree — the drift `dev sweep` reports.
32		WorktreeMissing bool
33	
34		// Status is the live git status of Checkout. Zero when there is nothing
35		// on disk to inspect.
36		Status    gitx.Status
37		StatusErr error
38	
39		// LastCommit is the author time of HEAD, used to age a task.
40		LastCommit time.Time
41	
42		// Session is the live runtime session hosting this checkout, if any.
43		Session *runtime.Session
44		// sessionsTracked reports whether the runtime can observe sessions at all.
45		// With the "none" backend it cannot, so "hot but nothing live" is not
46		// drift — it is the only state that backend can ever produce.
47		sessionsTracked bool
48	}
49	
50	// Live reports whether a runtime session is currently hosting this task.
51	func (r Row) Live() bool { return r.Session != nil }
52	
53	// StateDrift reports a task whose recorded state disagrees with reality:
54	// hot with no live session, or warm/cold with one. It is what `dev sweep`
55	// turns into suggestions — dev reports drift and never silently rewrites it.
56	func (r Row) StateDrift() string {
57		if r.sessionsTracked {
58			switch r.Task.State {
59			case task.Hot:
60				if !r.Live() {
61					return "no live session"
62				}
63			case task.Warm, task.Cold:
64				if r.Live() {
65					return "session is live"
66				}
67			}
68		}
69		if r.Task.State == task.Cold && r.CheckoutExists && r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
70			return "worktree still on disk"
71		}
72		if r.WorktreeMissing {
73			return "worktree is gone"
74		}
75		return ""
76	}
77	
78	// Age is how long since the task's last commit, falling back to when the entry
79	// was last written for a task with no commits of its own.
80	func (r Row) Age() time.Duration {
81		ref := r.LastCommit
82		if ref.IsZero() || r.Task.Updated.After(ref) {
83			ref = r.Task.Updated
84		}
85		if ref.IsZero() {
86			return 0
87		}
88		return time.Since(ref)
89	}
90	
91	// Options tunes what a Collect call spends time on.
92	type Options struct {
93		// SkipRuntime avoids querying the multiplexer, for callers that only need
94		// git facts (and for tests).
95		SkipRuntime bool
96		// SkipGit avoids running git per task, for a fast listing.
97		SkipGit bool
98	}
99	
100	// Collect builds the enriched inventory. Git probes run concurrently: each is
101	// a handful of process spawns, and a machine with dozens of tasks would
102	// otherwise make `dev ls` feel slow.
103	func Collect(ctx context.Context, tasks []*task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opts Options) []Row {
104		rows := make([]Row, len(tasks))
105	
106		var sessions []runtime.Session
107		tracked := false
108		if !opts.SkipRuntime && rt != nil && rt.Name() != "none" {
109			if s, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
110				sessions, tracked = s, true
111			}
112		}
113	
114		var wg sync.WaitGroup
115		// Bound concurrency: git is process-heavy and an unbounded fan-out over a
116		// large inventory would thrash.
117		sem := make(chan struct{}, 8)
118	
119		for i, t := range tasks {
120			rows[i].Task = t
121			rows[i].Checkout = checkoutOf(t)
122	
123			if opts.SkipGit || rows[i].Checkout == "" {
124				continue
125			}
126			wg.Add(1)
127			go func(i int) {
128				defer wg.Done()
129				sem <- struct{}{}
130				defer func() { <-sem }()
131				enrich(ctx, &rows[i])
132			}(i)
133		}
134		wg.Wait()
135	
136		for i := range rows {
137			rows[i].Session = matchSession(sessions, rows[i])
138			rows[i].sessionsTracked = tracked
139		}
140		return rows
141	}
142	
143	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
144		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
145			return t.WorktreePath
146		}
147		return t.RepoPath
148	}
149	
150	func enrich(ctx context.Context, r *Row) {
151		info, err := os.Stat(r.Checkout)
152		r.CheckoutExists = err == nil && info.IsDir()
153		if !r.CheckoutExists {
154			if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
155				r.WorktreeMissing = true
156			}
157			return
158		}
159		if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Checkout); err != nil {
160			r.StatusErr = err
161		} else {
162			r.Status = st
163		}
164		if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Checkout); err == nil && unix > 0 {
165			r.LastCommit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
166		}
167		// A recorded worktree that git no longer knows about is drift worth
168		// surfacing: the directory may exist while the administrative entry is gone.
169		if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
170			if _, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Task.RepoPath, r.Task.Branch); err == nil && !ok {
171				r.WorktreeMissing = true
172			}
173		}
174	}
175	
176	// matchSession picks the runtime session hosting a row's checkout. An exact
177	// directory match is preferred over a containing one, so a worktree's own
178	// session always wins over the parent repo's.
179	func matchSession(sessions []runtime.Session, r Row) *runtime.Session {
180		if r.Checkout == "" {
181			return nil
182		}
183		var contains *runtime.Session
184		for i := range sessions {
185			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
186				if d == r.Checkout {
187					return &sessions[i]
188				}
189				if strings.HasPrefix(d, r.Checkout+"/") && contains == nil {
190					contains = &sessions[i]
191				}
192			}
193		}
194		return contains
195	}
196	
197	// Filter narrows rows by state and repo. An empty filter matches everything.
198	type Filter struct {
199		States []task.State
200		Repo   string
201		// LiveOnly keeps only tasks with a runtime session.
202		LiveOnly bool
203		// DirtyOnly keeps only tasks with uncommitted work.
204		DirtyOnly bool
205	}
206	
207	// Apply returns the rows matching f.
208	func (f Filter) Apply(rows []Row) []Row {
209		out := rows[:0:0]
210		for _, r := range rows {
211			if len(f.States) > 0 && !containsState(f.States, r.Task.State) {
212				continue
213			}
214			if f.Repo != "" && !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Task.Repo), strings.ToLower(f.Repo)) {
215				continue
216			}
217			if f.LiveOnly && !r.Live() {
218				continue
219			}
220			if f.DirtyOnly && !r.Status.Dirty() {
221				continue
222			}
223			out = append(out, r)
224		}
225		return out
226	}
227	
228	func containsState(list []task.State, s task.State) bool {
229		for _, v := range list {
230			if v == s {
231				return true
232			}
233		}
234		return false
235	}
236	
237	// Orphans reports live runtime sessions that no task claims — the "I opened
238	// this and never wrote it down" case that makes a sidebar grow without bound.
239	func Orphans(sessions []runtime.Session, rows []Row) []runtime.Session {
240		claimed := map[string]bool{}
241		for _, r := range rows {
242			if r.Session != nil {
243				claimed[r.Session.Handle] = true
244			}
245		}
246		var out []runtime.Session
247		for _, s := range sessions {
248			if !claimed[s.Handle] {
249				out = append(out, s)
250			}
251		}
252		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Label < out[j].Label })
253		return out
254	}
255
```

```text
1	// Package repo discovers the repositories a user actually owns by walking the
2	// configured scan roots. It answers "what projects do I have?", which is a
3	// different question from "what am I working on?" — that one belongs to
4	// package task.
5	package repo
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"io/fs"
10		"os"
11		"path/filepath"
12		"sort"
13		"strings"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
16	)
17	
18	// Repo is one discovered repository.
19	type Repo struct {
20		// Name is the directory basename, which is how users refer to it.
21		Name string
22		// Path is the absolute path reached through the scan root. It may be a
23		// symlink from a bootstrap index; commands intentionally keep that human
24		// navigation path rather than replacing it with the physical one.
25		Path string
26		// RealPath is the physical checkout path.
27		RealPath string
28		// Symlink reports that Path is an alias to RealPath.
29		Symlink bool
30		// Root is the scan root it was found under.
31		Root string
32		// Category is the path between the scan root and the repo ("Quant",
33		// "Web/Frontend"), empty for a repo sitting directly in the root. It is
34		// human organisation metadata, preserved for `dev graduate` to place new
35		// projects consistently.
36		Category string
37		// CommonDir is Git's shared administrative directory. Its worktrees/
38		// children let inventory count linked checkouts without another git
39		// process per repository.
40		CommonDir string
41		// Bare reports a bare repository (a worktree hub).
42		Bare bool
43		// HasGit distinguishes a real repo from a plain directory that was found
44		// in a scan root; non-repos are reported so `dev repo list` can offer to
45		// initialise them.
46		HasGit bool
47	}
48	
49	// Display renders "Category/Name" or just "Name".
50	func (r Repo) Display() string {
51		if r.Category == "" {
52			return r.Name
53		}
54		return r.Category + "/" + r.Name
55	}
56	
57	// Options tunes discovery.
58	type Options struct {
59		// MaxDepth limits how deep below a scan root a repo may be found. The
60		// default layout is <root>/<Category>/<Repo>, so 2 suffices; 3 leaves room
61		// for a nested grouping without walking an entire home directory.
62		MaxDepth int
63		// IncludeNonRepos reports plain directories alongside repositories.
64		IncludeNonRepos bool
65	}
66	
67	// DefaultOptions is the discovery configuration used by dev's commands.
68	func DefaultOptions() Options { return Options{MaxDepth: 3} }
69	
70	// skipDirs are never descended into. These are large, never contain a project
71	// the user organises by hand, and walking them dominates scan time.
72	var skipDirs = map[string]bool{
73		"node_modules": true, ".venv": true, "venv": true, "target": true,
74		"vendor": true, "__pycache__": true, ".tox": true, "dist": true,
75		"build": true, ".next": true, ".cache": true, ".terraform": true,
76		"Library": true, ".Trash": true,
77	}
78	
79	// Discover walks every root and returns the repositories found, sorted by
80	// display name. Unreadable directories are skipped rather than fatal — a scan
81	// root that has been unmounted must not break `dev ls`.
82	func Discover(ctx context.Context, roots []string, opts Options) ([]Repo, error) {
83		if opts.MaxDepth <= 0 {
84			opts.MaxDepth = DefaultOptions().MaxDepth
85		}
86		seen := map[string]bool{}
87		// clone identities stop a physical path and a symlink index from showing
88		// the same repository twice. The first scan root wins, which lets users
89		// choose whether the curated index or the physical hierarchy is their UI
90		// simply by ordering scan_roots.
91		identities := map[string]bool{}
92		var out []Repo
93	
94		for _, root := range roots {
95			info, err := os.Stat(root)
96			if err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
97				continue // a missing scan root is normal on a fresh machine
98			}
99			rootClean := filepath.Clean(root)
100	
101			err = filepath.WalkDir(rootClean, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
102				if err != nil {
103					return nil // unreadable entry: skip, keep walking
104				}
105				if ctx.Err() != nil {
106					return ctx.Err()
107				}
108				if path == rootClean {
109					return nil
110				}
111				name := d.Name()
112				isLink := d.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
113				isDir := d.IsDir()
114				if isLink {
115					// WalkDir does not follow symlinks. Inspect a direct symlink to
116					// a repository, but do not recurse through arbitrary symlinked
117					// containers — bootstrap does that with cycle detection.
118					if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
119						isDir = info.IsDir()
120					}
121				}
122				if !isDir {
123					return nil
124				}
125				if skipDirs[name] || (strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") && name != ".bare") {
126					return filepath.SkipDir
127				}
128	
129				rel, _ := filepath.Rel(rootClean, path)
130				depth := len(strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)))
131	
132				if isRepoDir(path) {
133					real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
134					if real == "" {
135						real = path
136					}
137					bare := isBareDir(path)
138					identity, commonDir := real, real
139					if !bare {
140						if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
141							// A linked worktree is execution state, not another
142							// project in the repo inventory.
143							if g.IsLinkedWorktree {
144								return filepath.SkipDir
145							}
146							identity, commonDir = g.GitCommonDir, g.GitCommonDir
147							real = g.MainRoot
148						}
149					}
150					if !seen[path] && !identities[identity] {
151						seen[path], identities[identity] = true, true
152						out = append(out, Repo{
153							Name:      name,
154							Path:      path,
155							RealPath:  real,
156							Symlink:   isLink,
157							Root:      rootClean,
158							Category:  filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(rel)),
159							CommonDir: commonDir,
160							Bare:      bare,
161							HasGit:    true,
162						})
163					}
164					// Never descend into a repo: its subdirectories are source
165					// code, and any nested .git is a submodule or a worktree that
166					// belongs to this repo, not a project of its own.
167					return filepath.SkipDir
168				}
169				if depth >= opts.MaxDepth {
170					return filepath.SkipDir
171				}
172				if opts.IncludeNonRepos && depth == 1 {
173					if !seen[path] {
174						seen[path] = true
175						out = append(out, Repo{Name: name, Path: path, Root: rootClean, Category: ""})
176					}
177				}
178				return nil
179			})
180			if err != nil && ctx.Err() != nil {
181				return out, ctx.Err()
182			}
183		}
184	
185		for i := range out {
186			if out[i].Category == "." {
187				out[i].Category = ""
188			}
189		}
190		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool {
191			if out[i].Name != out[j].Name {
192				return strings.ToLower(out[i].Name) < strings.ToLower(out[j].Name)
193			}
194			return out[i].Path < out[j].Path
195		})
196		return out, nil
197	}
198	
199	// isRepoDir reports whether path is a repository root: it holds a .git entry
200	// (directory for a normal clone, file for a linked worktree or submodule).
201	func isRepoDir(path string) bool {
202		if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, ".git")); err == nil {
203			return true
204		}
205		return isBareDir(path)
206	}
207	
208	// isBareDir recognises a bare repository by its skeleton, without shelling out.
209	func isBareDir(path string) bool {
210		for _, marker := range []string{"HEAD", "objects", "refs"} {
211			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(path, marker)); err != nil {
212				return false
213			}
214		}
215		return true
216	}
217	
218	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
219	//
220	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
221	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
222	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
223	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
224		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, DefaultOptions())
225		if err != nil {
226			return Repo{}, nil, err
227		}
228		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
229			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
230				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
231				if real == "" {
232					real = g.MainRoot
233				}
234				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
235				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
236				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
237				return Repo{
238					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
239					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
240				}, nil, nil
241			}
242		}
243		for _, r := range all {
244			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
245				return r, nil, nil
246			}
247		}
248		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
249		var hits []Repo
250		for _, r := range all {
251			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
252				hits = append(hits, r)
253			}
254		}
255		switch len(hits) {
256		case 1:
257			return hits[0], nil, nil
258		case 0:
259			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
260		default:
261			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
266	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
267	
268	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
269	
270	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
271	type AmbiguousError struct {
272		Ref        string
273		Candidates []Repo
274	}
275	
276	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
277		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
278		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
279			names[i] = c.Display()
280		}
281		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
282	}
```

```text
1	package gitx

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"os"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"strings"
8	)
9	
10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
11	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
16		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
17		GitCommonDir string
18		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
19		Name string
20		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
21		// the main checkout.
22		IsLinkedWorktree bool
23		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
24		MainRoot string
25		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
26		Bare bool
27	}
28	
29	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
30	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
31	
32	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
33	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
34		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
35		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
36		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
37			"rev-parse",
38			"--path-format=absolute",
39			"--show-toplevel",
40			"--git-common-dir",
41			"--is-bare-repository",
42		)
43		if err != nil {
44			return Repo{}, err
45		}
46		f := lines(out)
47		r := Repo{}
48		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
49		switch len(f) {
50		case 3:
51			r.Root = f[0]
52			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
53			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
54		case 2:
55			r.GitCommonDir = f[0]
56			r.Bare = f[1] == "true"
57		default:
58			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
59		}
60	
61		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
62		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
63		if r.Bare {
64			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
65		} else {
66			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
67		}
68		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.Root != r.MainRoot
69		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
70		if r.Bare {
71			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
72			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
73			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
74				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
75			}
76		}
77		return r, nil
78	}
79	
80	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
81	// a full Discover.
82	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
83		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
84		return err == nil
85	}
86	
87	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
88	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
89	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
90	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
91	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
92		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
93			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
94				return b
95			}
96		}
97		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
98			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
99				return cand
100			}
101		}
102		return ""
103	}
104	
105	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
106	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
107		if name == "" {
108			name = "origin"
109		}
110		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
111		if err != nil {
112			return ""
113		}
114		return out
115	}
116	
117	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
118	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
119	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
120	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
121	// semantics should use Remote instead.
122	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
123		if commonDir == "" {
124			return ""
125		}
126		if name == "" {
127			name = "origin"
128		}
129		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
130		if err != nil {
131			return ""
132		}
133		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
134		section := ""
135		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
136			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
137			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
138				continue
139			}
140			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
141				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
142				continue
143			}
144			if section != want {
145				continue
146			}
147			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
148			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
149				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
150			}
151		}
152		return ""
153	}
```

```go
// Package pathx provides the path-safety checks shared by filesystem lifecycle
// operations. The checks are strict: a destination must be below its root, not
// merely share a string prefix with it, and symlinks are resolved before that
// decision is made.
package pathx

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"strings"
)

var (
	// ErrOutsideRoot reports a path that does not resolve below the requested root.
	ErrOutsideRoot = errors.New("path is outside root")
	// ErrRoot reports an operation that named the root itself rather than a child.
	ErrRoot = errors.New("path is the root itself")
	// ErrTraversal reports an explicit .. component in an unclean input path.
	ErrTraversal = errors.New("path contains parent traversal")
	// ErrInvalidComponent reports a value that is not one filesystem component.
	ErrInvalidComponent = errors.New("invalid path component")
)

// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
// before creating or moving anything into it.
func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
	if path == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
	}
	absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
	}
	absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)

	probe := absolute
	var missing []string
	for {
		resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
		if err == nil {
			slices.Reverse(missing)
			parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
			return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
		}
		if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
		if parent == probe {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
		}
		missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
		probe = parent
	}
}

// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
// confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
	if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
	}
	canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
	}
	canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize candidate: %w", err)
	}

	rel, err := filepath.Rel(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("compare %q with root %q: %w", candidate, root, err)
	}
	switch {
	case rel == ".":
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrRoot)
	case filepath.IsAbs(rel), rel == "..", strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)):
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
	default:
		return canonicalCandidate, nil
	}
}

// IsChild reports whether candidate resolves strictly below root. Policy
// rejections are returned as false without hiding filesystem errors.
func IsChild(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
	_, err := CanonicalChild(root, candidate)
	if err == nil {
		return true, nil
	}
	if errors.Is(err, ErrOutsideRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrTraversal) {
		return false, nil
	}
	return false, err
}

// ValidateComponent requires a non-empty relative value containing exactly one
// path component. Both slash styles are rejected so state synced between Unix
// and Windows cannot acquire a different meaning on another host.
func ValidateComponent(component string) error {
	switch {
	case component == "":
		return fmt.Errorf("empty component: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
	case strings.ContainsRune(component, '\x00'):
		return fmt.Errorf("component contains NUL: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
	case component == "." || component == "..":
		return fmt.Errorf("component %q is reserved: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
	case filepath.IsAbs(component) || filepath.VolumeName(component) != "":
		return fmt.Errorf("component %q is absolute: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
	case strings.ContainsAny(component, `/\\`):
		return fmt.Errorf("component %q contains a path separator: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
	case filepath.Clean(component) != component || filepath.Base(component) != component:
		return fmt.Errorf("component %q is not a single clean name: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
	default:
		return nil
	}
}

// JoinChild validates every component, joins it below root, and returns the
// canonical destination. It is suitable for paths such as
// <project-root>/<category>/<name>, where each user-supplied value must remain a
// single component.
func JoinChild(root string, components ...string) (string, error) {
	if len(components) == 0 {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("join child: no components: %w", ErrRoot)
	}
	for i, component := range components {
		if err := ValidateComponent(component); err != nil {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("component %d: %w", i, err)
		}
	}
	return CanonicalChild(root, filepath.Join(append([]string{root}, components...)...))
}

func hasParentTraversal(path string) bool {
	for _, component := range strings.FieldsFunc(path, func(r rune) bool {
		return r == '/' || r == '\\'
	}) {
		if component == ".." {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
```

```go
package pathx_test

import (
	"errors"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
)

func TestCanonicalChildAcceptsChildAndRejectsRoot(t *testing.T) {
	root := t.TempDir()
	child := filepath.Join(root, "child")
	if err := os.Mkdir(child, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	got, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(root, child)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("CanonicalChild: %v", err)
	}
	want, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(child)
	if got != want {
		t.Errorf("CanonicalChild = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
	if _, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(root, root); !errors.Is(err, pathx.ErrRoot) {
		t.Errorf("root itself should be rejected with ErrRoot, got %v", err)
	}
}

func TestCanonicalChildRejectsSiblingPrefixAndTraversal(t *testing.T) {
	parent := t.TempDir()
	root := filepath.Join(parent, "repo")
	sibling := filepath.Join(parent, "repo-archive")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(sibling, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	if _, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(root, sibling); !errors.Is(err, pathx.ErrOutsideRoot) {
		t.Errorf("sibling prefix should not count as containment, got %v", err)
	}
	traversal := filepath.Join(root, "child") + string(filepath.Separator) + ".." + string(filepath.Separator) + "other"
	if _, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(root, traversal); !errors.Is(err, pathx.ErrTraversal) {
		t.Errorf("explicit .. should be rejected before cleaning, got %v", err)
	}
}

func TestValidateComponent(t *testing.T) {
	for _, good := range []string{"Infra", "redis-streams", "name with spaces"} {
		if err := pathx.ValidateComponent(good); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("ValidateComponent(%q): %v", good, err)
		}
	}
	for _, bad := range []string{"", ".", "..", "/absolute", "two/parts", `two\parts`} {
		if err := pathx.ValidateComponent(bad); !errors.Is(err, pathx.ErrInvalidComponent) {
			t.Errorf("ValidateComponent(%q) = %v, want ErrInvalidComponent", bad, err)
		}
	}
}

func TestCanonicalChildRejectsSymlinkEscape(t *testing.T) {
	parent := t.TempDir()
	root := filepath.Join(parent, "root")
	outside := filepath.Join(parent, "outside")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(outside, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	link := filepath.Join(root, "escape")
	if err := os.Symlink(outside, link); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("symlinks unavailable: %v", err)
	}

	if _, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(root, filepath.Join(link, "new")); !errors.Is(err, pathx.ErrOutsideRoot) {
		t.Errorf("symlink escape should be rejected, got %v", err)
	}
}

func TestCanonicalChildResolvesNearestExistingAncestor(t *testing.T) {
	parent := t.TempDir()
	physical := filepath.Join(parent, "physical")
	if err := os.MkdirAll(physical, 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	root := filepath.Join(parent, "root-link")
	if err := os.Symlink(physical, root); err != nil {
		t.Skipf("symlinks unavailable: %v", err)
	}

	got, err := pathx.JoinChild(root, "category", "new-repo")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("JoinChild with missing destination: %v", err)
	}
	want := filepath.Join(physical, "category", "new-repo")
	if got != want {
		t.Errorf("JoinChild = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(got); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		t.Errorf("path validation must not create the destination, stat error = %v", err)
	}
}
```

```go
// Package catalog stores durable identity and lifecycle metadata for experiments
// and ordinary repositories. Filesystem presence is host-local, so one logical
// asset can carry a separate location for every machine that observes it.
package catalog

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

const CurrentSchemaVersion = 1

var (
	// ErrUnsupportedSchema identifies a catalog record written with an unknown
	// nonzero schema. Callers must surface it instead of interpreting newer data
	// using today's shape.
	ErrUnsupportedSchema = errors.New("unsupported catalog schema version")
	// ErrInvalidID identifies a filename stem that cannot safely name one record.
	ErrInvalidID = errors.New("invalid catalog ID")
)

// UnsupportedSchemaError describes a record whose schema this version cannot
// read. It supports errors.Is(err, ErrUnsupportedSchema).
type UnsupportedSchemaError struct {
	ID      string
	Version int
}

func (e *UnsupportedSchemaError) Error() string {
	if e.ID == "" {
		return fmt.Sprintf("catalog schema version %d: %v", e.Version, ErrUnsupportedSchema)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("catalog asset %s has schema version %d: %v", e.ID, e.Version, ErrUnsupportedSchema)
}

func (e *UnsupportedSchemaError) Unwrap() error { return ErrUnsupportedSchema }

// Kind distinguishes short-lived experiments from ordinary repositories.
type Kind string

const (
	KindTry        Kind = "try"
	KindRepository Kind = "repository"

	// Short aliases keep call sites readable when the type already supplies the
	// context, for example Entry{Kind: catalog.Repository}.
	Try        = KindTry
	Repository = KindRepository
)

// ExperimentPhase is the retained lifecycle of an experiment, including after
// it graduates into a repository.
type ExperimentPhase string

const (
	PhaseActive     ExperimentPhase = "active"
	PhaseDeprecated ExperimentPhase = "deprecated"
	PhaseGraduated  ExperimentPhase = "graduated"

	Active     = PhaseActive
	Deprecated = PhaseDeprecated
	Graduated  = PhaseGraduated
)

// LocationState describes what remains on one host.
type LocationState string

const (
	LocationPresent  LocationState = "present"
	LocationArchived LocationState = "archived"
	LocationEvicted  LocationState = "evicted"

	Present  = LocationPresent
	Archived = LocationArchived
	Evicted  = LocationEvicted
)

// Experiment records provenance that must survive renames and graduation.
type Experiment struct {
	Phase ExperimentPhase `toml:"phase" json:"phase"`

	Started      time.Time `toml:"started" json:"started"`
	OriginalPath string    `toml:"original_path" json:"original_path"`

	DeprecatedAt   time.Time `toml:"deprecated_at" json:"deprecated_at"`
	DeprecatedPath string    `toml:"deprecated_path" json:"deprecated_path"`
	GraduatedAt    time.Time `toml:"graduated_at" json:"graduated_at"`
	GraduatedPath  string    `toml:"graduated_path" json:"graduated_path"`
}

// Location is one host's knowledge of an asset. CurrentPath is where bytes live
// now; RestorePath is where an archived or evicted asset should return. RealPath
// and GitCommonDir make symlink aliases and linked worktrees match the same clone.
type Location struct {
	State LocationState `toml:"state" json:"state"`

	CurrentPath  string `toml:"current_path" json:"current_path"`
	RestorePath  string `toml:"restore_path" json:"restore_path"`
	RealPath     string `toml:"real_path" json:"real_path"`
	GitCommonDir string `toml:"git_common_dir" json:"git_common_dir"`

	Updated time.Time `toml:"updated" json:"updated"`
}

// RecoveryReceipt is enough metadata to explain and verify how an evicted asset
// can be reconstructed. Different recovery methods use different subsets.
type RecoveryReceipt struct {
	Host           string `toml:"host" json:"host"`
	Method         string `toml:"method" json:"method"`
	SourcePath     string `toml:"source_path" json:"source_path"`
	RestorePath    string `toml:"restore_path" json:"restore_path"`
	RemoteIdentity string `toml:"remote_identity" json:"remote_identity"`
	Revision       string `toml:"revision" json:"revision"`
	ArchivePath    string `toml:"archive_path" json:"archive_path"`
	Checksum       string `toml:"checksum" json:"checksum"`
	Created        time.Time `toml:"created" json:"created"`
	Verified       time.Time `toml:"verified" json:"verified"`
}

// MoveIntent is written before a filesystem rename and cleared after the new
// location is durable. A surviving intent lets later commands reconcile a move
// interrupted between those two points.
type MoveIntent struct {
	Host            string    `toml:"host" json:"host"`
	Operation       string    `toml:"operation" json:"operation"`
	SourcePath      string    `toml:"source_path" json:"source_path"`
	DestinationPath string    `toml:"destination_path" json:"destination_path"`
	Started         time.Time `toml:"started" json:"started"`
}

// Entry is one logical asset. ID is the stable filename stem and is deliberately
// not duplicated inside the TOML document.
type Entry struct {
	SchemaVersion int    `toml:"schema_version" json:"schema_version"`
	ID            string `toml:"-" json:"id"`
	Kind          Kind   `toml:"kind" json:"kind"`
	Name          string `toml:"name" json:"name"`
	Note          string `toml:"note" json:"note"`
	Tags          []string `toml:"tags" json:"tags"`

	// RemoteIdentity is a relocation hint, never sufficient on its own when
	// several records or live clones could be the observation's owner.
	RemoteIdentity string `toml:"remote_identity" json:"remote_identity"`

	Experiment      *Experiment      `toml:"experiment,omitempty" json:"experiment,omitempty"`
	Locations       map[string]Location `toml:"locations" json:"locations"`
	RecoveryReceipt *RecoveryReceipt `toml:"recovery_receipt,omitempty" json:"recovery_receipt,omitempty"`
	MoveIntent      *MoveIntent      `toml:"move_intent,omitempty" json:"move_intent,omitempty"`

	Created    time.Time `toml:"created" json:"created"`
	Discovered time.Time `toml:"discovered" json:"discovered"`
	LastOpened time.Time `toml:"last_opened" json:"last_opened"`
	Updated    time.Time `toml:"updated" json:"updated"`
}

var validID = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`)

// ValidateID checks that id can be used as exactly one visible filename stem.
func ValidateID(id string) error {
	if !validID.MatchString(id) || filepath.Base(id) != id || id == "." || id == ".." {
		return fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrInvalidID)
	}
	return nil
}

// NormalizeTags trims, lowercases, deduplicates and sorts tags. Sorting makes
// persisted output deterministic regardless of the order in which callers add
// labels.
func NormalizeTags(tags []string) []string {
	seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(tags))
	for _, tag := range tags {
		tag = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(tag))
		if tag != "" {
			seen[tag] = struct{}{}
		}
	}
	out := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
	for tag := range seen {
		out = append(out, tag)
	}
	sort.Strings(out)
	return out
}

// Normalize applies the lossless normalizations stores use before validation.
func (e *Entry) Normalize() {
	if e == nil {
		return
	}
	e.Name = strings.TrimSpace(e.Name)
	e.Tags = NormalizeTags(e.Tags)
	if e.Experiment != nil && e.Experiment.Phase == "" {
		e.Experiment.Phase = PhaseActive
	}
}

// Title is the human label, falling back to the stable ID for damaged display
// data. Persisted entries still require a name during validation.
func (e Entry) Title() string {
	if e.Name != "" {
		return e.Name
	}
	return e.ID
}

// HasTag reports membership after applying the same normalization as storage.
func (e Entry) HasTag(tag string) bool {
	tag = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(tag))
	return tag != "" && slices.Contains(e.Tags, tag)
}

// LocationFor returns host's location without exposing the map for mutation.
func (e Entry) LocationFor(host string) (Location, bool) {
	location, ok := e.Locations[host]
	return location, ok
}

// SetLocation validates and records one host location.
func (e *Entry) SetLocation(host string, location Location) error {
	if e == nil {
		return errors.New("set location on nil catalog entry")
	}
	if err := validateLocation(host, location); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if e.Locations == nil {
		e.Locations = make(map[string]Location)
	}
	e.Locations[host] = location
	return nil
}

// Clone returns a deep copy suitable for mutation before an atomic update.
func (e Entry) Clone() *Entry {
	clone := e
	clone.Tags = append([]string(nil), e.Tags...)
	if e.Experiment != nil {
		value := *e.Experiment
		clone.Experiment = &value
	}
	if e.RecoveryReceipt != nil {
		value := *e.RecoveryReceipt
		clone.RecoveryReceipt = &value
	}
	if e.MoveIntent != nil {
		value := *e.MoveIntent
		clone.MoveIntent = &value
	}
	if e.Locations != nil {
		clone.Locations = make(map[string]Location, len(e.Locations))
		for host, location := range e.Locations {
			clone.Locations[host] = location
		}
	}
	return &clone
}

// Validate rejects records that later lifecycle operations could not interpret
// safely. Store.Create fills identity and timestamps before calling it.
func (e Entry) Validate() error {
	if e.SchemaVersion != CurrentSchemaVersion {
		return &UnsupportedSchemaError{ID: e.ID, Version: e.SchemaVersion}
	}
	if err := ValidateID(e.ID); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	switch e.Kind {
	case KindTry, KindRepository:
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: unknown kind %q", e.ID, e.Kind)
	}
	if strings.TrimSpace(e.Name) == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: name is required", e.ID)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(e.Tags, NormalizeTags(e.Tags)) {
		return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: tags must be normalized lowercase values", e.ID)
	}
	if e.Experiment != nil {
		switch e.Experiment.Phase {
		case PhaseActive, PhaseDeprecated, PhaseGraduated:
		default:
			return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: unknown experiment phase %q", e.ID, e.Experiment.Phase)
		}
	}
	for host, location := range e.Locations {
		if err := validateLocation(host, location); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: %w", e.ID, err)
		}
	}
	if e.MoveIntent != nil {
		if e.MoveIntent.SourcePath == "" || e.MoveIntent.DestinationPath == "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: move intent requires source and destination paths", e.ID)
		}
		if e.MoveIntent.SourcePath == e.MoveIntent.DestinationPath {
			return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: move intent source and destination are identical", e.ID)
		}
	}
	if e.Created.IsZero() || e.Discovered.IsZero() || e.Updated.IsZero() {
		return fmt.Errorf("catalog asset %s: created, discovered and updated timestamps are required", e.ID)
	}
	return nil
}

func validateLocation(host string, location Location) error {
	if strings.TrimSpace(host) == "" {
		return errors.New("location host is required")
	}
	for field, value := range map[string]string{
		"current_path": location.CurrentPath,
		"restore_path": location.RestorePath,
		"real_path": location.RealPath,
		"git_common_dir": location.GitCommonDir,
	} {
		if strings.ContainsRune(value, '\x00') {
			return fmt.Errorf("location %s %s contains NUL", host, field)
		}
	}
	switch location.State {
	case LocationPresent:
		if location.CurrentPath == "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("location %s: present state requires current_path", host)
		}
	case LocationArchived:
		if location.CurrentPath == "" || location.RestorePath == "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("location %s: archived state requires current_path and restore_path", host)
		}
	case LocationEvicted:
		if location.RestorePath == "" {
			return fmt.Errorf("location %s: evicted state requires restore_path", host)
		}
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("location %s: unknown state %q", host, location.State)
	}
	return nil
}
```

```go
package catalog

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/BurntSushi/toml"
	"github.com/google/uuid"
)

var (
	// ErrNotFound is returned when an asset ID has no record.
	ErrNotFound = errors.New("catalog asset not found")
	// ErrAlreadyExists is returned when ID generation repeatedly collides.
	ErrAlreadyExists = errors.New("catalog asset already exists")
)

// Diagnostic describes one record skipped by a directory listing. The listing
// still returns every valid record; callers decide whether and where to render
// these notices.
type Diagnostic struct {
	Path string
	Err  error
}

func (d Diagnostic) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("skipping %s: %v", filepath.Base(d.Path), d.Err)
}

func (d Diagnostic) Unwrap() error { return d.Err }

// IDGenerator supplies stable random filename stems. It is injectable so tests
// can assert exact filenames without weakening production randomness.
type IDGenerator func() string

// DiagnosticSink receives non-fatal per-record listing failures.
type DiagnosticSink func(Diagnostic)

// StoreOption configures a Store.
type StoreOption func(*Store)

// WithIDGenerator replaces UUID generation.
func WithIDGenerator(generator IDGenerator) StoreOption {
	return func(store *Store) { store.generateID = generator }
}

// WithClock replaces timestamp generation.
func WithClock(clock func() time.Time) StoreOption {
	return func(store *Store) { store.clock = clock }
}

// WithDiagnosticSink directs skipped-record notices to sink.
func WithDiagnosticSink(sink DiagnosticSink) StoreOption {
	return func(store *Store) { store.diagnostics = sink }
}

// WithDiagnosticWriter writes one line per skipped record to writer. It never
// defaults to a process-global stream.
func WithDiagnosticWriter(writer io.Writer) StoreOption {
	if writer == nil {
		return func(*Store) {}
	}
	return WithDiagnosticSink(func(diagnostic Diagnostic) {
		fmt.Fprintln(writer, diagnostic.Error())
	})
}

// Store is a directory of one TOML file per asset.
type Store struct {
	Dir string

	mu          sync.Mutex
	generateID  IDGenerator
	clock       func() time.Time
	diagnostics DiagnosticSink
}

// NewStore returns a catalog rooted at dir.
func NewStore(dir string, options ...StoreOption) *Store {
	store := &Store{
		Dir:        dir,
		generateID: uuid.NewString,
		clock:      time.Now,
	}
	for _, option := range options {
		if option != nil {
			option(store)
		}
	}
	return store
}

func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".toml") }

// Create assigns a random stable ID and atomically persists entry. The caller's
// value is updated only after the rename succeeds.
func (s *Store) Create(entry *Entry) error {
	if entry == nil {
		return errors.New("create nil catalog entry")
	}
	if entry.ID != "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("create catalog asset: ID is assigned by the store")
	}

	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()

	if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create catalog directory: %w", err)
	}
	for range 32 {
		candidate := entry.Clone()
		candidate.ID = s.nextID()
		if err := ValidateID(candidate.ID); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("generated catalog ID: %w", err)
		}
		if _, err := os.Lstat(s.path(candidate.ID)); err == nil {
			continue
		} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			return fmt.Errorf("check catalog ID %s: %w", candidate.ID, err)
		}

		now := s.now()
		candidate.SchemaVersion = CurrentSchemaVersion
		if candidate.Created.IsZero() {
			candidate.Created = now
		}
		if candidate.Discovered.IsZero() {
			candidate.Discovered = now
		}
		candidate.Updated = now
		prepareNested(candidate, now)
		candidate.Normalize()
		if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := s.writeAtomic(candidate); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		*entry = *candidate
		return nil
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("generate unique catalog ID: %w", ErrAlreadyExists)
}

// Get loads one asset by exact ID.
func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Entry, error) {
	if err := ValidateID(id); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return s.get(id)
}

func (s *Store) get(id string) (*Entry, error) {
	var entry Entry
	if _, err := toml.DecodeFile(s.path(id), &entry); err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", id, ErrNotFound)
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read catalog asset %s: %w", id, err)
	}
	entry.ID = id
	if entry.SchemaVersion != 0 && entry.SchemaVersion != CurrentSchemaVersion {
		return nil, &UnsupportedSchemaError{ID: id, Version: entry.SchemaVersion}
	}
	// Version zero is the only implicit form: it means the schema marker was
	// absent, not that an unknown future layout should be guessed.
	if entry.SchemaVersion == 0 {
		entry.SchemaVersion = CurrentSchemaVersion
	}
	entry.Normalize()
	if err := entry.Validate(); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("validate catalog asset %s: %w", id, err)
	}
	return &entry, nil
}

// List loads every valid record in deterministic ID order. Per-record failures
// are skipped and sent to the configured diagnostic sink; directory-level
// failures are returned.
func (s *Store) List() ([]*Entry, error) {
	entries, diagnostics, err := s.ListWithDiagnostics()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if s.diagnostics != nil {
		for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
			s.diagnostics(diagnostic)
		}
	}
	return entries, nil
}

// ListWithDiagnostics is List's explicit diagnostic form. It is useful to
// services that want to aggregate notices rather than render them immediately.
func (s *Store) ListWithDiagnostics() ([]*Entry, []Diagnostic, error) {
	directoryEntries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			return nil, nil, nil
		}
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("read catalog directory: %w", err)
	}

	var entries []*Entry
	var diagnostics []Diagnostic
	for _, directoryEntry := range directoryEntries {
		name := directoryEntry.Name()
		if directoryEntry.IsDir() || strings.HasPrefix(name, ".") || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".toml") {
			continue
		}
		id := strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".toml")
		entry, err := s.Get(id)
		if err != nil {
			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, Diagnostic{Path: filepath.Join(s.Dir, name), Err: err})
			continue
		}
		entries = append(entries, entry)
	}
	Sort(entries)
	sort.Slice(diagnostics, func(i, j int) bool { return diagnostics[i].Path < diagnostics[j].Path })
	return entries, diagnostics, nil
}

// Update applies mutate to a deep copy and atomically replaces the record only
// if the mutation and validation both succeed. ID, Created, and Discovered are
// immutable.
func (s *Store) Update(id string, mutate func(*Entry) error) (*Entry, error) {
	if err := ValidateID(id); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if mutate == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("catalog update requires a mutation")
	}

	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()

	current, err := s.get(id)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	updated := current.Clone()
	if err := mutate(updated); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if updated.ID != current.ID {
		return nil, errors.New("catalog update cannot change ID")
	}
	if updated.SchemaVersion != current.SchemaVersion {
		return nil, errors.New("catalog update cannot change schema version")
	}
	if !updated.Created.Equal(current.Created) {
		return nil, errors.New("catalog update cannot change Created")
	}
	if !updated.Discovered.Equal(current.Discovered) {
		return nil, errors.New("catalog update cannot change Discovered")
	}

	now := s.now()
	updated.Updated = now
	prepareNested(updated, now)
	updated.Normalize()
	if err := updated.Validate(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := s.writeAtomic(updated); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return updated.Clone(), nil
}

// Sort orders entries by stable ID.
func Sort(entries []*Entry) {
	sort.SliceStable(entries, func(i, j int) bool {
		return entries[i].ID < entries[j].ID
	})
}

func (s *Store) writeAtomic(entry *Entry) error {
	temporary, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, "."+entry.ID+".*.tmp")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create catalog temp file: %w", err)
	}
	name := temporary.Name()
	defer os.Remove(name)

	if err := toml.NewEncoder(temporary).Encode(entry); err != nil {
		_ = temporary.Close()
		return fmt.Errorf("encode catalog asset %s: %w", entry.ID, err)
	}
	if err := temporary.Close(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("close catalog temp file: %w", err)
	}
	if err := os.Chmod(name, 0o644); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("set catalog file mode: %w", err)
	}
	if err := os.Rename(name, s.path(entry.ID)); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("replace catalog asset %s: %w", entry.ID, err)
	}
	return nil
}

func (s *Store) nextID() string {
	if s.generateID == nil {
		return uuid.NewString()
	}
	return s.generateID()
}

func (s *Store) now() time.Time {
	if s.clock == nil {
		return time.Now().UTC()
	}
	return s.clock().UTC()
}

func prepareNested(entry *Entry, now time.Time) {
	if entry.Experiment != nil && entry.Experiment.Started.IsZero() {
		entry.Experiment.Started = now
	}
	for host, location := range entry.Locations {
		if location.Updated.IsZero() {
			location.Updated = now
			entry.Locations[host] = location
		}
	}
	if entry.RecoveryReceipt != nil && entry.RecoveryReceipt.Created.IsZero() {
		entry.RecoveryReceipt.Created = now
	}
	if entry.MoveIntent != nil && entry.MoveIntent.Started.IsZero() {
		entry.MoveIntent.Started = now
	}
}
```

```go
package catalog_test

import (
	"errors"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/catalog"
)

const (
	firstID  = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
	secondID = "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"
)

func fixedClock() time.Time {
	return time.Date(2026, time.August, 27, 9, 30, 0, 123, time.FixedZone("test", 8*60*60))
}

func sampleEntry(root string) *catalog.Entry {
	return &catalog.Entry{
		Kind: catalog.KindTry,
		Name: "  Redis Streams  ",
		Note: "compare consumer groups",
		Tags: []string{" Go ", "infra", "GO", ""},
		RemoteIdentity: "github.com/example/redis-streams",
		Experiment: &catalog.Experiment{
			Phase:        catalog.PhaseActive,
			OriginalPath: filepath.Join(root, "tries", "redis-streams"),
		},
		Locations: map[string]catalog.Location{
			"laptop": {
				State:        catalog.LocationPresent,
				CurrentPath:  filepath.Join(root, "tries", "redis-streams"),
				RealPath:     filepath.Join(root, "tries", "redis-streams"),
				GitCommonDir: filepath.Join(root, "tries", "redis-streams", ".git"),
			},
			"server": {
				State:       catalog.LocationArchived,
				CurrentPath: filepath.Join(root, "archives", "redis-streams.tar.zst"),
				RestorePath: "/srv/tries/redis-streams",
			},
		},
		RecoveryReceipt: &catalog.RecoveryReceipt{
			Host:        "server",
			Method:      "archive",
			ArchivePath: filepath.Join(root, "archives", "redis-streams.tar.zst"),
			RestorePath: "/srv/tries/redis-streams",
			Checksum:    "sha256:abc123",
		},
		MoveIntent: &catalog.MoveIntent{
			Host:            "laptop",
			Operation:       "archive",
			SourcePath:      filepath.Join(root, "tries", "redis-streams"),
			DestinationPath: filepath.Join(root, "archives", "redis-streams"),
		},
	}
}

func newFixedStore(dir string) *catalog.Store {
	return catalog.NewStore(dir,
		catalog.WithIDGenerator(func() string { return firstID }),
		catalog.WithClock(fixedClock),
	)
}

func TestStoreRoundTripAndFilenameIdentity(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	store := newFixedStore(dir)
	entry := sampleEntry(dir)

	if err := store.Create(entry); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Create: %v", err)
	}
	if entry.ID != firstID {
		t.Errorf("ID = %q, want injected UUID", entry.ID)
	}
	if entry.SchemaVersion != catalog.CurrentSchemaVersion {
		t.Errorf("schema = %d", entry.SchemaVersion)
	}
	if entry.Name != "Redis Streams" {
		t.Errorf("name was not trimmed: %q", entry.Name)
	}
	if want := []string{"go", "infra"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(entry.Tags, want) {
		t.Errorf("tags = %v, want %v", entry.Tags, want)
	}
	if entry.Created.Location() != time.UTC || !entry.Created.Equal(fixedClock()) {
		t.Errorf("created = %v, want UTC %v", entry.Created, fixedClock())
	}

	path := filepath.Join(dir, firstID+".toml")
	body, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(body), "\nid =") || strings.HasPrefix(string(body), "id =") {
		t.Errorf("ID must live only in the filename:\n%s", body)
	}
	if info, err := os.Stat(path); err != nil || info.Mode().Perm() != 0o644 {
		t.Errorf("record mode = %v, err = %v", info.Mode().Perm(), err)
	}

	got, err := store.Get(firstID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Get: %v", err)
	}
	if got.ID != firstID || got.Experiment == nil || got.Experiment.OriginalPath != entry.Experiment.OriginalPath {
		t.Errorf("experiment/identity did not round trip: %+v", got)
	}
	for _, host := range []string{"laptop", "server"} {
		location, ok := got.LocationFor(host)
		if !ok || location.State != entry.Locations[host].State || location.CurrentPath != entry.Locations[host].CurrentPath {
			t.Errorf("location %s did not round trip: %+v", host, location)
		}
	}
	if got.RecoveryReceipt == nil || got.RecoveryReceipt.Checksum != "sha256:abc123" || got.MoveIntent == nil {
		t.Errorf("recovery/move metadata did not round trip: %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestUpdatePreservesIdentityAndIsAtomicOnMutationFailure(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	currentTime := fixedClock()
	store := catalog.NewStore(dir,
		catalog.WithIDGenerator(func() string { return firstID }),
		catalog.WithClock(func() time.Time { return currentTime }),
	)
	entry := sampleEntry(dir)
	entry.MoveIntent = nil
	if err := store.Create(entry); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	created, discovered := entry.Created, entry.Discovered
	path := filepath.Join(dir, firstID+".toml")
	before, _ := os.ReadFile(path)

	sentinel := errors.New("stop update")
	if _, err := store.Update(firstID, func(candidate *catalog.Entry) error {
		candidate.Note = "must not persist"
		return sentinel
	}); !errors.Is(err, sentinel) {
		t.Fatalf("Update error = %v, want sentinel", err)
	}
	afterRejected, _ := os.ReadFile(path)
	if string(afterRejected) != string(before) {
		t.Error("a rejected mutation changed the record")
	}

	currentTime = currentTime.Add(time.Minute)
	updated, err := store.Update(firstID, func(candidate *catalog.Entry) error {
		candidate.Note = "new note"
		candidate.Tags = append(candidate.Tags, " DATABASE ")
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("Update: %v", err)
	}
	if updated.ID != firstID || !updated.Created.Equal(created) || !updated.Discovered.Equal(discovered) {
		t.Errorf("stable fields changed: %+v", updated)
	}
	if updated.Note != "new note" || !updated.HasTag("database") || !updated.Updated.Equal(currentTime) {
		t.Errorf("update not applied: %+v", updated)
	}
	entries, _ := os.ReadDir(dir)
	for _, entry := range entries {
		if strings.HasPrefix(entry.Name(), ".") || strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".tmp") {
			t.Errorf("temporary file left behind: %s", entry.Name())
		}
	}
}

func TestListMissingDirectoryAndDeterministicOrder(t *testing.T) {
	parent := t.TempDir()
	missing := filepath.Join(parent, "not-created")
	store := catalog.NewStore(missing)
	entries, err := store.List()
	if err != nil || len(entries) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("missing directory = %d entries, %v", len(entries), err)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(missing); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		t.Errorf("List should not create its directory, stat error = %v", err)
	}

	ids := []string{secondID, firstID}
	index := 0
	store = catalog.NewStore(missing, catalog.WithIDGenerator(func() string {
		id := ids[index]
		index++
		return id
	}))
	for _, name := range []string{"second", "first"} {
		if err := store.Create(&catalog.Entry{Kind: catalog.Repository, Name: name}); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	entries, err = store.List()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(entries) != 2 || entries[0].ID != firstID || entries[1].ID != secondID {
		t.Errorf("List order = %+v", entries)
	}
}

func TestListIsolatesCorruptionAndReportsDiagnostics(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	var diagnostics []catalog.Diagnostic
	store := catalog.NewStore(dir,
		catalog.WithIDGenerator(func() string { return firstID }),
		catalog.WithDiagnosticSink(func(diagnostic catalog.Diagnostic) {
			diagnostics = append(diagnostics, diagnostic)
		}),
	)
	if err := store.Create(&catalog.Entry{Kind: catalog.Repository, Name: "good"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "broken.toml"), []byte("this is not = = toml"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	entries, err := store.List()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("corruption must not fail the directory listing: %v", err)
	}
	if len(entries) != 1 || entries[0].ID != firstID {
		t.Errorf("valid record was hidden: %+v", entries)
	}
	if len(diagnostics) != 1 || !strings.Contains(diagnostics[0].Error(), "broken.toml") {
		t.Errorf("diagnostics = %+v", diagnostics)
	}

	entries, explicit, err := store.ListWithDiagnostics()
	if err != nil || len(entries) != 1 || len(explicit) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("ListWithDiagnostics = %d entries, %d diagnostics, %v", len(entries), len(explicit), err)
	}
}

func TestUnknownSchemaIsSurfacedAndNeverGuessed(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	store := newFixedStore(dir)
	if err := store.Create(&catalog.Entry{Kind: catalog.Repository, Name: "good"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	futureID := secondID
	future := `schema_version = 99
kind = "repository"
name = "future"
tags = []
created = 2026-08-27T00:00:00Z
discovered = 2026-08-27T00:00:00Z
updated = 2026-08-27T00:00:00Z
`
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, futureID+".toml"), []byte(future), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	if _, err := store.Get(futureID); !errors.Is(err, catalog.ErrUnsupportedSchema) {
		t.Fatalf("Get future schema = %v, want ErrUnsupportedSchema", err)
	} else {
		var schemaError *catalog.UnsupportedSchemaError
		if !errors.As(err, &schemaError) || schemaError.Version != 99 {
			t.Errorf("typed schema error = %#v", err)
		}
	}
	entries, diagnostics, err := store.ListWithDiagnostics()
	if err != nil || len(entries) != 1 || len(diagnostics) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ListWithDiagnostics = %d entries, %d diagnostics, %v", len(entries), len(diagnostics), err)
	}
	if !errors.Is(diagnostics[0], catalog.ErrUnsupportedSchema) {
		t.Errorf("schema diagnostic lost its cause: %v", diagnostics[0])
	}
}

func TestUpdateRejectsStableFieldChanges(t *testing.T) {
	store := newFixedStore(t.TempDir())
	entry := &catalog.Entry{Kind: catalog.Repository, Name: "repo"}
	if err := store.Create(entry); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for name, mutate := range map[string]func(*catalog.Entry){
		"ID":         func(candidate *catalog.Entry) { candidate.ID = secondID },
		"Created":    func(candidate *catalog.Entry) { candidate.Created = candidate.Created.Add(time.Hour) },
		"Discovered": func(candidate *catalog.Entry) { candidate.Discovered = candidate.Discovered.Add(time.Hour) },
	} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if _, err := store.Update(entry.ID, func(candidate *catalog.Entry) error {
				mutate(candidate)
				return nil
			}); err == nil {
				t.Error("stable-field mutation should fail")
			}
		})
	}
}
```
