```text
11	
12	// Status is the live git state of one checkout — everything dev's inventory
13	// shows about a task without persisting any of it.
14	type Status struct {
15		Branch   string `json:"branch,omitempty"`
16		Detached bool   `json:"detached"`
17		// Upstream is the tracking ref (e.g. "origin/feat/auth"), empty when the
18		// branch has never been published.
19		Upstream string `json:"upstream,omitempty"`
20		Ahead    int    `json:"ahead"`
21		Behind   int    `json:"behind"`
22		// Changed counts unique changed paths. Staged and Unstaged are index /
23		// working-tree views and can overlap when one path has both kinds of
24		// changes; Changed does not double-count it.
25		Changed   int `json:"changed"`
26		Staged    int `json:"staged"`
27		Unstaged  int `json:"unstaged"`
28		Untracked int `json:"untracked"`
29		// Added, Modified, Deleted and Renamed classify status letters. One path
30		// can contribute to two when its staged and unstaged states differ.
31		Added    int `json:"added"`
32		Modified int `json:"modified"`
33		Deleted  int `json:"deleted"`
34		Renamed  int `json:"renamed"`
35		// LatestChange is the newest mtime among changed files that still exist.
36		// Deleted paths fall back to the checkout's last commit time at the repo
37		// aggregation layer.
38		LatestChange time.Time `json:"latest_change,omitempty"`
39		// Conflicted counts unmerged paths; a non-zero value means the checkout is
40		// mid-merge or mid-rebase and must not be touched automatically.
41		Conflicted int `json:"conflicted"`
42	}
43	
44	// Dirty reports uncommitted work of any kind.
45	func (s Status) Dirty() bool { return s.Changed > 0 }
46	
47	// Published reports whether the branch has an upstream at all.
48	func (s Status) Published() bool { return s.Upstream != "" }
49	
50	// Synced reports a branch that is published and exactly level with upstream.
51	func (s Status) Synced() bool { return s.Published() && s.Ahead == 0 && s.Behind == 0 }
52	
53	// Summary renders the compact, starship-like column used throughout dev:
54	//
55	//	⇕⇡2⇣1 =1 +3 !2 ?4
56	//
57	// Divergence, conflicts, staged, unstaged and untracked paths remain separate
58	// so "dirty" says how and by how much, rather than collapsing to one ●.
59	func (s Status) Summary() string {
60		var parts []string
61		switch {
62		case s.Ahead > 0 && s.Behind > 0:
63			parts = append(parts, "⇕⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead)+"⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
64		case s.Ahead > 0:
65			parts = append(parts, "⇡"+strconv.Itoa(s.Ahead))
66		case s.Behind > 0:
67			parts = append(parts, "⇣"+strconv.Itoa(s.Behind))
68		}
69		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
70			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted))
71		}
72		if s.Staged > 0 {
73			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged))
74		}
75		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
76			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged))
77		}
78		if s.Untracked > 0 {
79			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked))
80		}
81		if len(parts) == 0 {
82			if !s.Published() {
83				return "local"
84			}
85			return "clean"
86		}
87		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
88	}
89	
90	// Breakdown renders the detailed change count shown by `dev status` and the
91	// TUI detail pane. Changed is the unique-path total; staged and unstaged may
92	// overlap, which is stated by presenting them as categories rather than a sum.
93	func (s Status) Breakdown() string {
94		if s.Changed == 0 {
95			return "0 changed paths"
96		}
97		var parts []string
98		if s.Staged > 0 {
99			parts = append(parts, "+"+strconv.Itoa(s.Staged)+" staged")
100		}
101		if s.Unstaged > 0 {
102			parts = append(parts, "!"+strconv.Itoa(s.Unstaged)+" unstaged")
103		}
104		if s.Untracked > 0 {
105			parts = append(parts, "?"+strconv.Itoa(s.Untracked)+" untracked")
106		}
107		if s.Conflicted > 0 {
108			parts = append(parts, "="+strconv.Itoa(s.Conflicted)+" conflicted")
109		}
110		return strconv.Itoa(s.Changed) + " changed paths (" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")"
111	}
112	
113	// TypeBreakdown classifies the status letters when that detail is available.
114	func (s Status) TypeBreakdown() string {
115		var parts []string
116		for _, item := range []struct {
117			n    int
118			name string
119		}{
120			{s.Added, "added"}, {s.Modified, "modified"}, {s.Deleted, "deleted"},
121			{s.Renamed, "renamed/copied"},
122		} {
123			if item.n > 0 {
124				parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(item.n)+" "+item.name)
125			}
126		}
127		return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
128	}
129	
130	// StatusOf reads the porcelain v2 status of the checkout at dir. Porcelain v2
131	// is the documented machine-readable format: it reports branch, upstream and
132	// ahead/behind in the same pass as the file states, so one process gives dev
133	// everything it needs.
134	func StatusOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Status, error) {
135		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=normal", "-z")
136		if err != nil {
137			return Status{}, err
138		}
139		var s Status
140		for _, rec := range nulLines(out) {
141			if rec == "" {
142				continue
143			}
144			switch rec[0] {
145			case '#':
146				parseBranchHeader(rec, &s)
147			case '1', '2':
148				// "1 XY ..." ordinary change, "2 XY ..." rename/copy. X is
149				// staged, Y unstaged. This record is one unique changed path even
150				// when both sides are non-dot.
151				f := strings.Fields(rec)
152				if len(f) < 2 || len(f[1]) < 2 {
153					continue
154				}
155				s.Changed++
156				x, y := f[1][0], f[1][1]
157				if x != '.' {
158					s.Staged++
159				}
160				if y != '.' {
161					s.Unstaged++
162				}
163				classifyChange(x, &s)
164				classifyChange(y, &s)
165				updateLatestChange(dir, statusPath(rec), &s)
166			case 'u':
167				s.Changed++
168				s.Conflicted++
169				updateLatestChange(dir, statusPath(rec), &s)
170			case '?':
171				s.Changed++
172				s.Untracked++
173				updateLatestChange(dir, strings.TrimPrefix(rec, "? "), &s)
174			}
175		}
176		return s, nil
177	}
178	
179	// statusPath extracts the final pathname from a porcelain-v2 record while
180	// preserving spaces in it. Rename records have one extra score field; their
181	// old path arrives as the next NUL record and is intentionally ignored.
182	func statusPath(rec string) string {
183		if rec == "" {
184			return ""
185		}
186		var fields int
187		switch rec[0] {
188		case '1':
189			fields = 9
190		case '2':
191			fields = 10
192		case 'u':
193			fields = 11
194		default:
195			return ""
196		}
197		parts := strings.SplitN(rec, " ", fields)
198		if len(parts) != fields {
199			return ""
200		}
201		return parts[fields-1]
202	}
203	
204	func updateLatestChange(dir, path string, s *Status) {
205		if path == "" {
206			return
207		}
208		info, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, filepath.FromSlash(path)))
209		if err == nil && info.ModTime().After(s.LatestChange) {
210			s.LatestChange = info.ModTime()
211		}
212	}
213	
214	func classifyChange(code byte, s *Status) {
215		switch code {
216		case 'A':
217			s.Added++
218		case 'M', 'T':
219			s.Modified++
220		case 'D':
221			s.Deleted++
222		case 'R', 'C':
223			s.Renamed++
224		}
225	}
226	
227	func parseBranchHeader(rec string, s *Status) {
228		f := strings.Fields(rec)
229		if len(f) < 3 {
230			return
231		}
232		switch f[1] {
233		case "branch.head":
234			if f[2] == "(detached)" {
235				s.Detached = true
236			} else {
237				s.Branch = f[2]
238			}
239		case "branch.upstream":
240			s.Upstream = f[2]
241		case "branch.ab":
242			// "# branch.ab +2 -1"
243			if len(f) < 4 {
244				return
245			}
246			s.Ahead, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[2], "+"))
247			s.Behind, _ = strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(f[3], "-"))
248		}
249	}
250	
251	// LastCommit reports the author timestamp of HEAD as a Unix epoch, and the
252	// subject line. Used to age a task in `dev sweep`.
253	func LastCommit(ctx context.Context, dir string) (unix int64, subject string, err error) {
254		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "log", "-1", "--format=%at%x00%s")
255		if err != nil || out == "" {
256			return 0, "", err
257		}
258		ts, subj, _ := strings.Cut(out, "\x00")
259		unix, _ = strconv.ParseInt(ts, 10, 64)
260		return unix, subj, nil
261	}
262	
263	// WipCommit stages everything and records a checkpoint commit.
264	//
265	// A checkpoint commit is deliberately preferred over `git stash`: a stash is
266	// invisible in the log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never
267	// travel to another machine, which is exactly what parking a task needs.
268	func WipCommit(ctx context.Context, dir, message string) (bool, error) {
269		st, err := StatusOf(ctx, dir)
270		if err != nil {
271			return false, err
272		}
273		if !st.Dirty() {
274			return false, nil
275		}
276		if st.Conflicted > 0 {
277			return false, &Error{Args: []string{"commit"}, Dir: dir,
278				Stderr: "checkout has unmerged paths; resolve the conflict before parking"}
279		}
280		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "add", "--all"); err != nil {
281			return false, err
282		}
283		if message == "" {
284			message = "wip: checkpoint"
285		}
286		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "commit", "--no-verify", "-m", message); err != nil {
287			return false, err
288		}
289		return true, nil
290	}
291
```

```text
37	}

40		return fmt.Sprintf("%s support needs the %q CLI, which is not installed", e.Kind, e.Bin)
41	}

43	// Forge is the subset of forge behaviour dev uses.
44	type Forge interface {
45		Kind() Kind
46		// Bin is the CLI binary name.
47		Bin() string
48		Available() bool
49		// CreatePR opens a pull/merge request from head into base.

105	// Detect infers the forge for a checkout from its origin remote. A repo with
106	// no remote, or one on a self-hosted host neither CLI knows, resolves to
107	// Unknown — which callers must treat as "use plain git".
108	func Detect(ctx context.Context, dir string) Kind {
109		return FromURL(gitx.Remote(ctx, dir, "origin"))
110	}
111	
112	// FromURL classifies a remote URL.
113	func FromURL(url string) Kind {
114		u := strings.ToLower(url)
115		switch {
116		case u == "":
117			return Unknown
118		case strings.Contains(u, "github.com"), strings.Contains(u, "github."):
119			return GitHub
120		case strings.Contains(u, "gitlab.com"), strings.Contains(u, "gitlab."):
121			return GitLab
122		}
123		return Unknown
124	}
125	
126	// For returns the adapter for a kind.
127	func For(k Kind) (Forge, error) {
128		switch k {
129		case GitHub:
130			return &gh{}, nil
131		case GitLab:
132			return &glab{}, nil
133		}
134		return nil, errors.New("no forge CLI for this remote; falling back to plain git")
135	}
136	
137	// Preferred returns the first available forge, for commands like `repo new`
138	// that have no existing remote to infer from.
139	func Preferred() (Forge, error) {
140		for _, f := range []Forge{&gh{}, &glab{}} {
141			if f.Available() {
142				return f, nil
143			}
144		}
145		return nil, errors.New("neither gh nor glab is installed")
146	}
147	
148	// run executes a forge CLI, streaming stderr through so the user sees the
149	// CLI's own authentication prompts and error messages verbatim.
150	func run(ctx context.Context, bin, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
151		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, args...)
152		cmd.Dir = dir
153		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
154		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
155		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
156		cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
157		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
158			detail := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
159			if detail != "" {
160				return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %s: %w",
161					bin, strings.Join(args, " "), detail, err)
162			}
163			return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %w", bin, strings.Join(args, " "), err)
164		}
165		return strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String()), nil
166	}
167	
168	func have(bin string) bool {
169		_, err := exec.LookPath(bin)
170		return err == nil
171	}
172	
173	// IdentityFromURL returns a forge and owner/name identity for an HTTPS or SSH
174	// Git remote. It is used to match remote inventories to local clones without
175	// assuming the checkout directory has the same name.
176	func IdentityFromURL(raw string) (Kind, string) {
177		kind := FromURL(raw)
178		if kind == Unknown {
179			return Unknown, ""
180		}
181		s := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
182		if strings.Contains(s, "://") {
183			if parsed, err := url.Parse(s); err == nil {
184				s = strings.TrimPrefix(parsed.Path, "/")
185			}
186		} else if at := strings.IndexByte(s, '@'); at >= 0 {
187			// SCP-style SSH: git@github.com:owner/repo.git
188			s = s[at+1:]
189			if colon := strings.IndexByte(s, ':'); colon >= 0 {
190				s = s[colon+1:]
191			}
192		}
193		s = strings.Trim(strings.TrimSuffix(s, ".git"), "/")
194		return kind, s
195	}
```

```text
1	package config

3	import (

6	)
7	
8	// PostCreate accepts either of two TOML shapes, because both read naturally:
9	//
10	//	post_create = "auto"
11	//	post_create = ["uv sync", "npm ci"]
12	type PostCreate struct {
13		Auto     bool
14		Commands []string
15	}
16	
17	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
18	func (p *PostCreate) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
19		switch t := v.(type) {
20		case string:
21			if t != "auto" {
22				return fmt.Errorf("post_create: %q is not a valid string form (use \"auto\" or a list of commands)", t)
23			}
24			*p = PostCreate{Auto: true}
25			return nil
26		case []any:
27			cmds := make([]string, 0, len(t))
28			for i, e := range t {
29				s, ok := e.(string)
30				if !ok {
31					return fmt.Errorf("post_create[%d]: want a command string, got %T", i, e)
32				}
33				cmds = append(cmds, s)
34			}
35			*p = PostCreate{Commands: cmds}
36			return nil
37		default:
38			return fmt.Errorf("post_create: want \"auto\" or a list of command strings, got %T", v)
39		}
40	}
41	
42	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler so a config round-trips.
43	func (p PostCreate) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
44		if p.Auto {
45			return []byte(`"auto"`), nil
46		}
47		out := []byte("[")
48		for i, c := range p.Commands {
49			if i > 0 {
50				out = append(out, ", "...)
51			}
52			out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%q", c)...)
53		}
54		return append(out, ']'), nil
55	}
56	
57	// Duration is a time.Duration written in TOML as a Go duration string
58	// ("10m", "90s"), which is friendlier than a bare number of seconds.
59	type Duration struct{ time.Duration }
60	
61	// UnmarshalTOML implements toml.Unmarshaler.
62	func (d *Duration) UnmarshalTOML(v any) error {
63		switch t := v.(type) {
64		case string:
65			parsed, err := time.ParseDuration(t)
66			if err != nil {
67				return fmt.Errorf("duration %q: %w", t, err)
68			}
69			d.Duration = parsed
70			return nil
71		case int64:
72			d.Duration = time.Duration(t) * time.Second
73			return nil
74		default:
75			return fmt.Errorf("duration: want a string like \"10m\", got %T", v)
76		}
77	}
78	
79	// MarshalTOML implements toml.Marshaler.
80	func (d Duration) MarshalTOML() ([]byte, error) {
81		return []byte(fmt.Sprintf("%q", d.Duration.String())), nil
82	}
```

```text
256	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
257	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
258	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
259	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
260		cfg := Default()
261		if path == "" {
262			path = ConfigFile()
263		}
264		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
265		switch {
266		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
267			return cfg, nil
268		case err != nil:
269			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
270		}
271		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
272			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
273			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
274			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
275		}
276		cfg.Source = path
277		return cfg, cfg.Validate()

280	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a
281	// worktree create, when a directory has already been made.
282	func (c Config) Validate() error {
283		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
284		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "none":
285		default:
286			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
287		}
288		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
289			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
290		}
291		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
292			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
293		}
294		switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
295		case "", "flat", "preserve":
296		default:
297			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
298		}
299		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
300			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
301		}
302		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
303			return fmt.Errorf("forge.remote_limit must be zero (use default) or positive")
304		}
305		validStrategy := func(v string) bool {
306			switch v {
307			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
308				return true
309			}
310			return false
311		}
312		if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
313			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
314		}
315		for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
316			if !validStrategy(strategy) {
317				return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",
318					ecosystem, strategy)
319			}
320		}
321		validColumns := map[string]bool{
322			"repo": true, "branch": true, "git": true, "live": true,
323			"latest": true, "worktrees": true, "tasks": true,
324			"category": true, "path": true,
325		}
326		for i, column := range c.TUI.Repos.Columns {
327			if !validColumns[column] {
328				return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.columns[%d] %q: unknown column", i, column)
329			}
330		}
331		switch c.EffectiveRepoSort() {
332		case "activity", "latest", "name", "git", "tasks":
333		default:
334			return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.sort %q: want activity, latest, name, git or tasks", c.TUI.Repos.Sort)
335		}
336		seen := map[string]string{}
337		for i, t := range c.TUI.Tools {
338			switch {
339			case t.Key == "":
340				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key is required", i)
341			case t.Run == "":
342				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d] (%s): run is required", i, t.Key)
343			}
344			if binding, ok := ReservedKey(t.Key); ok {
345				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is the dashboard's %q binding; pick another",
346					i, t.Key, binding)
347			}
348			if prev, ok := seen[t.Key]; ok {
349				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is already bound to %q", i, t.Key, prev)
350			}
351			seen[t.Key] = t.Name
352		}
353		return nil
354	}
```

```text
1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"os"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// XDG base directories, resolved the way the spec prescribes: honor the
10	// environment variable when it holds an absolute path, otherwise fall back to
11	// the documented default under $HOME.
12	
13	func xdgDir(envVar, fallback string) string {
14		if v := os.Getenv(envVar); filepath.IsAbs(v) {
15			return v
16		}
17		return filepath.Join(home(), fallback)
18	}
19	
20	func home() string {
21		if h, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil && h != "" {
22			return h
23		}
24		return os.Getenv("HOME")
25	}
26	
27	// ConfigHome is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default ~/.config).
28	func ConfigHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ".config") }
29	
30	// DataHome is $XDG_DATA_HOME (default ~/.local/share).
31	func DataHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_DATA_HOME", ".local/share") }
32	
33	// CacheHome is $XDG_CACHE_HOME (default ~/.cache).
34	func CacheHome() string { return xdgDir("XDG_CACHE_HOME", ".cache") }
35	
36	// ConfigFile is the path dev loads its TOML configuration from.
37	func ConfigFile() string { return filepath.Join(ConfigHome(), "dev", "config.toml") }
38	
39	// Expand resolves a leading ~ and any environment variables in p, then makes
40	// the result absolute. Paths in config.toml are written by humans, so both
41	// "~/Worktrees" and "$WORK/trees" have to work.
42	func Expand(p string) string {
43		if p == "" {
44			return ""
45		}
46		p = os.ExpandEnv(p)
47		switch {
48		case p == "~":
49			p = home()
50		case strings.HasPrefix(p, "~/"):
51			p = filepath.Join(home(), p[2:])
52		}
53		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(p); err == nil {
54			return abs
55		}
56		return filepath.Clean(p)
57	}
58	
59	// Contract renders p with $HOME collapsed back to ~, for display only.
60	func Contract(p string) string {
61		h := home()
62		if h != "" && p == h {
63			return "~"
64		}
65		if h != "" && strings.HasPrefix(p, h+string(filepath.Separator)) {
66			return "~" + p[len(h):]
67		}
68		return p
69	}
70
```

```text
1	// Package gitx wraps the git porcelain commands dev depends on. Every helper
2	// shells out to git rather than linking a Go implementation: git is already a
3	// hard dependency, its porcelain formats are stable and documented, and this
4	// keeps dev's behaviour identical to what the user sees when they run the same
5	// command by hand.
6	package gitx
7	
8	import (
9		"bytes"
10		"context"
11		"errors"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16	
17	// ErrNotARepo is returned when a directory is not inside a git working tree.
18	var ErrNotARepo = errors.New("not a git repository")
19	
20	// Error carries the failing command and git's own stderr, which is almost
21	// always more useful than the exit status alone.
22	type Error struct {
23		Args   []string
24		Dir    string
25		Stderr string
26		Err    error
27	}
28	
29	func (e *Error) Error() string {
30		msg := strings.TrimSpace(e.Stderr)
31		if msg == "" {
32			msg = e.Err.Error()
33		}
34		return fmt.Sprintf("git %s: %s", strings.Join(e.Args, " "), msg)
35	}
36	
37	func (e *Error) Unwrap() error { return e.Err }
38	
39	// run executes git in dir and returns trimmed stdout.
40	func run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
41		// -c core.quotepath=false keeps non-ASCII paths readable rather than
42		// octal-escaped, which matters for the Chinese-named files in these repos.
43		full := append([]string{"-c", "core.quotepath=false"}, args...)
44		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
45		cmd.Dir = dir
46		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
47		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
48		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
49		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
50			gerr := &Error{Args: args, Dir: dir, Stderr: stderr.String(), Err: err}
51			if strings.Contains(gerr.Stderr, "not a git repository") {
52				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", dir, ErrNotARepo)
53			}
54			return "", gerr
55		}
56		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
57	}
58	
59	// Run executes an arbitrary git command in dir. Exported for the few callers
60	// (park's wip commit, done's merge) that need a one-off command.
61	func Run(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
62		return run(ctx, dir, args...)
63	}
64	
65	// lines splits git output into non-empty lines.
66	func lines(s string) []string {
67		if s == "" {
68			return nil
69		}
70		out := strings.Split(s, "\n")
71		filtered := out[:0]
72		for _, l := range out {
73			if l != "" {
74				filtered = append(filtered, l)
75			}
76		}
77		return filtered
78	}
79	
80	// nulLines splits NUL-delimited git output (-z forms).
81	func nulLines(s string) []string {
82		s = strings.TrimRight(s, "\x00")
83		if s == "" {
84			return nil
85		}
86		return strings.Split(s, "\x00")
87	}
88
```

```text
1	package forge
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"fmt"
7		"strconv"
8		"strings"
9		"time"
10	)
11	
12	// gh drives the GitHub CLI.
13	type gh struct{}
14	
15	func (g *gh) Kind() Kind      { return GitHub }
16	func (g *gh) Bin() string     { return "gh" }
17	func (g *gh) Available() bool { return have("gh") }
18	
19	// CreatePR opens a GitHub pull request.
20	func (g *gh) CreatePR(ctx context.Context, dir string, req PRRequest) (string, error) {
21		if !g.Available() {
22			return "", &ErrNoCLI{Kind: GitHub, Bin: "gh"}
23		}
24		args := []string{"pr", "create", "--base", req.Base, "--head", req.Head}
25		switch {
26		case req.Title != "":
27			args = append(args, "--title", req.Title, "--body", req.Body)
28		default:
29			// --fill derives title and body from the branch's commits, which is
30			// the right default for a solo workflow where the commits already say
31			// what happened.
32			args = append(args, "--fill")
33		}
34		if req.Draft {
35			args = append(args, "--draft")
36		}
37		if req.Web {
38			args = append(args, "--web")
39		}
40		out, err := run(ctx, "gh", dir, args...)
41		return lastURL(out), err
42	}
43	
44	// CreateRepo creates a GitHub repository from the local checkout.
45	func (g *gh) CreateRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string, req RepoRequest) (string, error) {
46		if !g.Available() {
47			return "", &ErrNoCLI{Kind: GitHub, Bin: "gh"}
48		}
49		remote := req.RemoteName
50		if remote == "" {
51			remote = "origin"
52		}
53		args := []string{"repo", "create", req.Name, "--source", ".", "--remote", remote}
54		if req.Private {
55			args = append(args, "--private")
56		} else {
57			args = append(args, "--public")
58		}
59		if req.Description != "" {
60			args = append(args, "--description", req.Description)
61		}
62		if req.Push {
63			args = append(args, "--push")
64		}
65		out, err := run(ctx, "gh", dir, args...)
66		return lastURL(out), err
67	}
68	
69	// CloneURL renders a clone target. gh accepts a bare owner/name, so a
70	// shorthand reference is passed through untouched.
71	func (g *gh) CloneURL(ref string) string {
72		if strings.Contains(ref, "://") || strings.HasPrefix(ref, "git@") {
73			return ref
74		}
75		return "https://github.com/" + strings.TrimSuffix(ref, ".git") + ".git"
76	}
77	
78	// lastURL picks the URL out of a CLI's chatter, which may print progress
79	// lines before the created resource's address.
80	func lastURL(out string) string {
81		var found string
82		for _, line := range strings.Fields(out) {
83			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "http://") || strings.HasPrefix(line, "https://") {
84				found = line
85			}
86		}
87		if found == "" {
88			return strings.TrimSpace(out)
89		}
90		return found
91	}
92	
93	// ListRepos lists GitHub repositories visible to the authenticated user —
94	// owned, collaborated on, and organisation membership — most recently pushed
95	// first. gh api is intentionally used instead of a custom HTTP client:
96	// authentication and token refresh stay owned by the forge CLI.
97	func (g *gh) ListRepos(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]RemoteRepo, error) {
98		if !g.Available() {
99			return nil, &ErrNoCLI{Kind: GitHub, Bin: "gh"}
100		}
101		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 15*time.Second)
102		defer cancel()
103		if limit <= 0 {
104			limit = 100
105		}
106		// GitHub caps per_page at 100. The remote view is a navigator, not a
107		// complete backup inventory; / filters this recent working set.
108		if limit > 100 {
109			limit = 100
110		}
111		out, err := run(ctx, "gh", "", "api", "user/repos", "--method", "GET",
112			"-f", "per_page="+strconv.Itoa(limit), "-f", "sort=pushed", "-f", "direction=desc")
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, err
115		}
116		return parseGitHubRepos(out)
117	}
118	
119	func parseGitHubRepos(out string) ([]RemoteRepo, error) {
120		var raw []struct {
121			Name          string `json:"name"`
122			FullName      string `json:"full_name"`
123			Description   string `json:"description"`
124			URL           string `json:"html_url"`
125			CloneURL      string `json:"clone_url"`
126			SSHURL        string `json:"ssh_url"`
127			Visibility    string `json:"visibility"`
128			Fork          bool   `json:"fork"`
129			Archived      bool   `json:"archived"`
130			PushedAt      string `json:"pushed_at"`
131			DefaultBranch string `json:"default_branch"`
132		}
133		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &raw); err != nil {
134			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode gh api user/repos: %w", err)
135		}
136		result := make([]RemoteRepo, 0, len(raw))
137		for _, r := range raw {
138			updated, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, r.PushedAt)
139			result = append(result, RemoteRepo{
140				Forge: GitHub, Name: r.Name, FullName: r.FullName,
141				Description: r.Description, URL: r.URL,
142				CloneURL: r.CloneURL, SSHURL: r.SSHURL,
143				Visibility: r.Visibility, DefaultBranch: r.DefaultBranch,
144				Archived: r.Archived, Fork: r.Fork, UpdatedAt: updated,
145			})
146		}
147		return result, nil
148	}
```

```text
1	package forge
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"fmt"
7		"strconv"
8		"strings"
9		"time"
10	)
11	
12	// glab drives the GitLab CLI. GitLab calls the same concept a merge request,
13	// and its flags differ enough from gh that the two need separate adapters
14	// rather than a shared one with conditionals.
15	type glab struct{}
16	
17	func (g *glab) Kind() Kind      { return GitLab }
18	func (g *glab) Bin() string     { return "glab" }
19	func (g *glab) Available() bool { return have("glab") }
20	
21	// CreatePR opens a GitLab merge request.
22	func (g *glab) CreatePR(ctx context.Context, dir string, req PRRequest) (string, error) {
23		if !g.Available() {
24			return "", &ErrNoCLI{Kind: GitLab, Bin: "glab"}
25		}
26		args := []string{"mr", "create", "--target-branch", req.Base, "--source-branch", req.Head}
27		switch {
28		case req.Title != "":
29			args = append(args, "--title", req.Title, "--description", req.Body)
30		default:
31			args = append(args, "--fill")
32		}
33		if req.Draft {
34			args = append(args, "--draft")
35		}
36		if req.Web {
37			args = append(args, "--web")
38		}
39		// Without this glab prompts interactively even when everything is supplied.
40		args = append(args, "--yes")
41		out, err := run(ctx, "glab", dir, args...)
42		return lastURL(out), err
43	}
44	
45	// CreateRepo creates a GitLab project from the local checkout.
46	func (g *glab) CreateRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string, req RepoRequest) (string, error) {
47		if !g.Available() {
48			return "", &ErrNoCLI{Kind: GitLab, Bin: "glab"}
49		}
50		remote := req.RemoteName
51		if remote == "" {
52			remote = "origin"
53		}
54		args := []string{"repo", "create", req.Name, "--remoteName", remote}
55		if req.Private {
56			args = append(args, "--private")
57		} else {
58			args = append(args, "--public")
59		}
60		if req.Description != "" {
61			args = append(args, "--description", req.Description)
62		}
63		out, err := run(ctx, "glab", dir, args...)
64		return lastURL(out), err
65	}
66	
67	// CloneURL renders a clone target.
68	func (g *glab) CloneURL(ref string) string {
69		if strings.Contains(ref, "://") || strings.HasPrefix(ref, "git@") {
70			return ref
71		}
72		return "https://gitlab.com/" + strings.TrimSuffix(ref, ".git") + ".git"
73	}
74	
75	// ListRepos lists GitLab projects owned by the authenticated user, most
76	// recently active first. glab's broader --member endpoint is avoided here:
77	// older releases can hang against GitLab.com, which would freeze the TUI. glab owns authentication and self-hosted instance
78	// selection; dev only normalises the JSON into the shared shape.
79	func (g *glab) ListRepos(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]RemoteRepo, error) {
80		if !g.Available() {
81			return nil, &ErrNoCLI{Kind: GitLab, Bin: "glab"}
82		}
83		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 15*time.Second)
84		defer cancel()
85		if limit <= 0 {
86			limit = 100
87		}
88		out, err := run(ctx, "glab", "", "repo", "list", "--mine",
89			"--per-page", strconv.Itoa(limit), "--order", "last_activity_at",
90			"--sort", "desc", "--output", "json")
91		if err != nil {
92			return nil, err
93		}
94		return parseGitLabRepos(out)
95	}
96	
97	func parseGitLabRepos(out string) ([]RemoteRepo, error) {
98		var raw []struct {
99			Name              string `json:"name"`
100			PathWithNamespace string `json:"path_with_namespace"`
101			Description       string `json:"description"`
102			DefaultBranch     string `json:"default_branch"`
103			Visibility        string `json:"visibility"`
104			SSHURL            string `json:"ssh_url_to_repo"`
105			HTTPURL           string `json:"http_url_to_repo"`
106			WebURL            string `json:"web_url"`
107			Archived          bool   `json:"archived"`
108			ForkedFrom        any    `json:"forked_from_project"`
109			LastActivityAt    string `json:"last_activity_at"`
110		}
111		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &raw); err != nil {
112			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode glab repo list: %w", err)
113		}
114		result := make([]RemoteRepo, 0, len(raw))
115		for _, r := range raw {
116			updated, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, r.LastActivityAt)
117			result = append(result, RemoteRepo{
118				Forge: GitLab, Name: r.Name, FullName: r.PathWithNamespace,
119				Description: r.Description, URL: r.WebURL,
120				CloneURL: r.HTTPURL, SSHURL: r.SSHURL,
121				Visibility: r.Visibility, DefaultBranch: r.DefaultBranch,
122				Archived: r.Archived, Fork: r.ForkedFrom != nil, UpdatedAt: updated,
123			})
124		}
125		return result, nil
126	}
```

```text
10	// openCheckout makes a directory live, asking the backend to treat it as a git
11	// worktree when it knows how — that is what groups the checkout under its
12	// parent repo in a sidebar instead of listing it as an unrelated directory.
13	func openCheckout(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, dir, label string) (string, error) {
14		if wo, ok := rt.(runtime.WorktreeOpener); ok {
15			return wo.OpenWorktree(ctx, dir, label)
16		}
17		return rt.Open(ctx, dir, label)
18	}
19	
20	// asError is errors.As with a typed target, kept here so call sites read as
21	// one line.
22	func asError[T error](err error, target *T) bool { return errors.As(err, target) }
```

```text
23	// harness runs dev commands against an isolated HOME, config and scan root.
24	type harness struct {

26		home       string
27		configPath string

33	func newHarness(t *testing.T) *harness {
34		t.Helper()
35		home := t.TempDir()
36		scanRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Program")
37		wtRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Worktrees")
38		if err := os.MkdirAll(scanRoot, 0o755); err != nil {
39			t.Fatal(err)
40		}
41	
42		// A repo inside the scan root, so `dev` discovers it the way it would in
43		// real use rather than via an absolute path.
44		r := gittest.New(t)
45		dest := filepath.Join(scanRoot, "demo")
46		if err := os.Rename(r.Root, dest); err != nil {
47			t.Fatal(err)
48		}
49		r.Root = dest
50	
51		// Isolate every path dev touches from the developer's real machine.
52		t.Setenv("HOME", home)
53		t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share"))
54		t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".config"))
55		t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".cache"))
56	
57		configPath := filepath.Join(home, "config.toml")
58		cfg := "" +
59			"[paths]\n" +
60			"scan_roots = [\"" + scanRoot + "\"]\n" +
61			"project_root = \"" + scanRoot + "\"\n" +
62			"tries_root = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "tries") + "\"\n" +
63			"worktree_root = \"" + wtRoot + "\"\n" +
64			"state_dir = \"" + filepath.Join(home, "state") + "\"\n" +
65			"\n[runtime]\nbackend = \"none\"\n" +
66			"\n[worktree]\ninclude = [\".env\"]\npost_create = []\n"
67		if err := os.WriteFile(configPath, []byte(cfg), 0o644); err != nil {
68			t.Fatal(err)
69		}
70		return &harness{t: t, home: home, configPath: configPath, scanRoot: scanRoot, wtRoot: wtRoot, repo: r}
71	}

73	// run executes one dev invocation, capturing its output. Commands write
74	// through App, so the writers passed to NewRootCommandWithIO are all that is
75	// needed — no file-descriptor juggling.
76	func (h *harness) run(args ...string) (string, string, error) {
77		h.t.Helper()
78		var out, errBuf bytes.Buffer
79		root := cli.NewRootCommandWithIO(&out, &errBuf)
80		root.SetArgs(append([]string{"--config", h.configPath}, args...))
81		err := root.Execute()
82		return out.String(), errBuf.String(), err
83	}

90		}

94	func TestLifecycleEndToEnd(t *testing.T) {
95		h := newHarness(t)
96	
97		// An empty inventory should tell the user how to start, not print nothing.
98		out := h.mustRun("ls")
99		if !strings.Contains(out, "No tasks yet") {
100			t.Errorf("empty ls output: %q", out)
101		}
102	
103		// start: branch + worktree + task entry.
104		out = h.mustRun("start", "demo", "--task", "auth", "--branch", "feat/auth", "--base", "main")
105		if !strings.Contains(out, "feat/auth") {
106			t.Fatalf("start output: %q", out)
107		}
108		wtPath := filepath.Join(h.wtRoot, "demo", "feat-auth")
109		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(wtPath, "README.md")); err != nil {
110			t.Fatalf("worktree should exist at the templated path: %v", err)
111		}
112	
113		// The task appears in the inventory as hot.
114		out = h.mustRun("ls")
115		if !strings.Contains(out, "auth") || !strings.Contains(out, "HOT") {
116			t.Errorf("ls after start: %q", out)
117		}
118	
119		// JSON is a stable contract for other tools.
120		out = h.mustRun("ls", "--json")
121		var rows []map[string]any
122		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &rows); err != nil {
123			t.Fatalf("ls --json is not valid JSON: %v\n%s", err, out)
124		}
125		if len(rows) != 1 {
126			t.Fatalf("want 1 row, got %d", len(rows))
127		}
128		if rows[0]["branch"] != "feat/auth" || rows[0]["state"] != "hot" {
129			t.Errorf("json row: %+v", rows[0])
130		}
131	
132		// park: records the next action, closes the session, keeps the worktree.
133		out = h.mustRun("park", "feat/auth", "--next", "add the regression test")
134		if !strings.Contains(out, "WARM") {
135			t.Errorf("park output: %q", out)
136		}
137		out = h.mustRun("ls")
138		if !strings.Contains(out, "WARM") || !strings.Contains(out, "add the regression test") {
139			t.Errorf("ls after park: %q", out)
140		}
141		if _, err := os.Stat(wtPath); err != nil {
142			t.Error("a warm task keeps its worktree")
143		}
144	
145		// resume: back to hot.
146		out = h.mustRun("resume", "auth")
147		if !strings.Contains(out, "feat/auth") {
148			t.Errorf("resume output: %q", out)
149		}
150		out = h.mustRun("ls")
151		if !strings.Contains(out, "HOT") {
152			t.Errorf("ls after resume: %q", out)
153		}
154	
155		// Commit something on the branch so there is work to integrate.
156		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "config", "user.email", "dev@example.test")
157		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "config", "user.name", "dev test")
158		os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(wtPath, "auth.go"), []byte("package auth\n"), 0o644)
159		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "add", "auth.go")
160		h.repo.GitIn(wtPath, "commit", "-m", "feat: add auth")
161	
162		// done --ff: rebase and fast-forward, then clean up.
163		out = h.mustRun("done", "auth", "--ff")
164		if !strings.Contains(out, "merged into main") {
165			t.Fatalf("done output: %q", out)
166		}
167		if _, err := os.Stat(wtPath); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
168			t.Error("done should remove the worktree")
169		}
170		// The commit is on main, and the history stayed linear.

172			t.Error("the branch's commit should be on main")
173		}
174		merges, _ := gitx.Run(gittest.Ctx(), h.repo.Root, "log", "--merges", "--oneline")
175		if merges != "" {
176			t.Errorf("--ff must not create a merge commit, got:\n%s", merges)
177		}
178		// The branch survives by default: merged is not always finished.
179		if !gitx.BranchExists(gittest.Ctx(), h.repo.Root, "feat/auth") {

185		if !strings.Contains(out, "reap") {
186			t.Errorf("sweep should offer to reap a done task: %q", out)
187		}
188	}
```

```text
338		ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")

340			return ref[i+1:]
341		}
342		return ref
343	}
```

```text
1	package config
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"regexp"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// Path templates are deliberately *not* text/template: the syntax users write
10	// in config.toml ("{{worktree_root}}/{{repo}}/{{branch|slug}}") needs to stay
11	// readable and to fail loudly on an unknown variable rather than silently
12	// rendering "<no value>".
13	
14	var tmplVar = regexp.MustCompile(`\{\{\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*(?:\|\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*)?\}\}`)
15	
16	// Vars is the substitution environment for a path template.
17	type Vars map[string]string
18	
19	// Render substitutes every {{var}} / {{var|filter}} occurrence in tmpl.
20	// An unknown variable or filter is an error — a typo in worktree_path should
21	// surface at create time, not as a directory literally named "{{rep}}".
22	func Render(tmpl string, vars Vars) (string, error) {
23		var firstErr error
24		out := tmplVar.ReplaceAllStringFunc(tmpl, func(m string) string {
25			g := tmplVar.FindStringSubmatch(m)
26			name, filter := g[1], g[2]
27			val, ok := vars[name]
28			if !ok {
29				if firstErr == nil {
30					firstErr = fmt.Errorf("unknown template variable %q in %q (known: %s)", name, tmpl, strings.Join(sortedKeys(vars), ", "))
31				}
32				return m
33			}
34			switch filter {
35			case "":
36				return val
37			case "slug":
38				return Slug(val)
39			case "lower":
40				return strings.ToLower(val)
41			case "base":
42				if i := strings.LastIndexByte(val, '/'); i >= 0 {
43					return val[i+1:]
44				}
45				return val
46			default:
47				if firstErr == nil {
48					firstErr = fmt.Errorf("unknown template filter %q in %q (known: slug, lower, base)", filter, tmpl)
49				}
50				return m
51			}
52		})
53		if firstErr != nil {
54			return "", firstErr
55		}
56		return out, nil
57	}
58	
59	var slugStrip = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`)
60	
61	// Slug makes a branch name safe to use as a single filesystem component:
62	// "feat/auth/oauth-refresh" becomes "feat-auth-oauth-refresh". Leading dots
63	// and dashes are trimmed so the result can never be a hidden directory or be
64	// mistaken for a flag.
65	func Slug(s string) string {
66		s = slugStrip.ReplaceAllString(s, "-")
67		for strings.Contains(s, "--") {
68			s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "--", "-")
69		}
70		s = strings.Trim(s, "-._")
71		if s == "" {
72			return "unnamed"
73		}
74		return s
75	}
76	
77	func sortedKeys(v Vars) []string {
78		out := make([]string, 0, len(v))
79		for k := range v {
80			out = append(out, k)
81		}
82		// small map; insertion sort keeps this dependency-free
83		for i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {
84			for j := i; j > 0 && out[j] < out[j-1]; j-- {
85				out[j], out[j-1] = out[j-1], out[j]
86			}
87		}
88		return out
89	}
90
```

```text
1	// Package gittest builds throwaway git repositories for tests. It is a test
2	// helper that lives in a normal package so every package's tests can share it.
3	package gittest
4	
5	import (
6		"context"
7		"os"
8		"os/exec"
9		"path/filepath"
10		"strings"
11		"testing"
12	)
13	
14	// Repo is a scratch repository under t.TempDir().
15	type Repo struct {
16		T    *testing.T
17		Root string
18	}
19	
20	// New initialises a repository with one commit on branch "main".
21	func New(t *testing.T) *Repo {
22		t.Helper()
23		root := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "repo")
24		if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
25			t.Fatal(err)
26		}
27		r := &Repo{T: t, Root: root}
28		r.Git("init", "--initial-branch=main")
29		// Identity and signing are configured locally so the test never depends on
30		// (or is broken by) the developer's global git config.
31		r.Git("config", "user.email", "dev@example.test")
32		r.Git("config", "user.name", "dev test")
33		r.Git("config", "commit.gpgsign", "false")
34		r.Write("README.md", "# test repo\n")
35		r.Git("add", "README.md")
36		r.Git("commit", "-m", "chore: initial commit")
37		return r
38	}
39	
40	// Git runs a git command in the repo root and fails the test on error.
41	func (r *Repo) Git(args ...string) string {
42		r.T.Helper()
43		return r.GitIn(r.Root, args...)
44	}
45	
46	// GitIn runs a git command in an arbitrary directory (e.g. a linked worktree).
47	func (r *Repo) GitIn(dir string, args ...string) string {
48		r.T.Helper()
49		cmd := exec.Command("git", args...)
50		cmd.Dir = dir
51		cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
52			"GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null", // ignore the developer's ~/.gitconfig
53			"GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null",
54			"GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
55			"GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
56		)
57		out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
58		if err != nil {
59			r.T.Fatalf("git %s in %s: %v\n%s", strings.Join(args, " "), dir, err, out)
60		}
61		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
62	}
63	
64	// Write creates or replaces a file relative to the repo root.
65	func (r *Repo) Write(rel, content string) string {
66		r.T.Helper()
67		p := filepath.Join(r.Root, rel)
68		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p), 0o755); err != nil {
69			r.T.Fatal(err)
70		}
71		if err := os.WriteFile(p, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
72			r.T.Fatal(err)
73		}
74		return p
75	}
76	
77	// Commit writes a file and commits it.
78	func (r *Repo) Commit(rel, content, message string) {
79		r.T.Helper()
80		r.Write(rel, content)
81		r.Git("add", rel)
82		r.Git("commit", "-m", message)
83	}
84	
85	// Branch creates and checks out a new branch from the current HEAD.
86	func (r *Repo) Branch(name string) {
87		r.T.Helper()
88		r.Git("switch", "-c", name)
89	}
90	
91	// WithRemote turns a second bare repository into "origin" and pushes main,
92	// so tests can exercise ahead/behind and published-branch logic.
93	func (r *Repo) WithRemote() string {
94		r.T.Helper()
95		remote := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(r.Root), "origin.git")
96		r.GitIn(filepath.Dir(r.Root), "init", "--bare", "--initial-branch=main", remote)
97		r.Git("remote", "add", "origin", remote)
98		r.Git("push", "-u", "origin", "main")
99		return remote
100	}
101	
102	// Ctx is a convenience background context for gitx calls in tests.
103	func Ctx() context.Context { return context.Background() }
```

```text
1	# `dev try` TUI、asset metadata 與安全回收
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	目前 `dev try`（`internal/cli/try.go`）只掃描 `paths.tries_root` 的第一層目錄，以 directory mtime 排序，並把 create/clone/open/render 全放在 Cobra handler；`dev graduate`（`internal/cli/graduate.go`）也自行處理 resolve、move、Git 初始化與 remote。這足以快速開實驗，卻無法可靠回答「最近用過什麼、哪些值得保留、哪些可安全釋放空間」，也沒有能在 local directory 被移除後繼續存在的索引。
6	
7	目標是把 TRY 作為主 TUI 的第四個 view，同時保留 `dev try <name>` 的低摩擦與可腳本化 CLI。資料與安全規則放在共用 domain service，不放進 Bubble Tea；普通 repository 與 Try 共用 tags／notes／穩定 ID，但只有真正的 Try entry 具有 Try lifecycle。容量預設代表刪除該 local checkout 真正擁有、可回收的 logical bytes，而不是含糊地選擇是否「扣掉 `.git`」。
8	
9	採用以下產品語意：
10	
11	- `active`／`deprecated`／`graduated` 是人為 lifecycle phase。
12	- `present`／`archived`／`evicted` 是每台機器的 local disposition；archive 不等於刪除，evict 不等於 deprecated。
13	- `important`、`keep`、`experiment` 等 tags 可組合；普通 repo 的 `experiment` tag 只分類，不會建立 Try lifecycle。
14	- Git tries 預設只顯示於 TRY，避免與 REPOS 重複；可用 `--include-tries`／TUI「顯示全部」查看。Graduated entry 保留歷史與 ID，並改在 REPOS 顯示。
15	- Archive 是 `TriesRoot` 內同 filesystem 的可逆隱藏搬移；evict 才釋放空間。Remote create/push 永遠需要明示，且「有 remote」不等於「資料可恢復」。
16	
17	## 1. 建立共享 asset catalog 與安全 path primitives
18	
19	新增 `internal/catalog`，不要擴充 `task.Task`：Try 可以是 non-Git，也沒有 branch/task/runtime，而 `task.State` 的 hot/warm/cold/done 是另一種生命週期。
20	
21	- `Entry` 以隨機穩定 ID（檔名）保存 `schema_version`、kind (`try|repository`)、name/note/tags、可選的 `Experiment` metadata、timestamps、per-host `Location`、已驗證的 `RecoveryReceipt` 與短暫 `MoveIntent`。

31	## 2. 抽出 `internal/experiment`，讓舊 CLI 與 TUI 共用
32	
33	把 `internal/cli/try.go`、`internal/cli/graduate.go` 的 policy 移入 `experiment.Service`；Cobra 只解析 flags、呼叫 service、render 結果。核心 API 包含：
34	
35	- `Reconcile/List/Resolve/ResolveOrCreate/Touch`
36	- `Deprecate/Reactivate/Archive/Restore/Graduate`
37	- request/result types 明確描述 dry-run plan、move、catalog transition 與需要重新載入的 inventory。
38	
39	Reconcile/backfill 規則：
40	
41	1. 掃描 `TriesRoot` 第一層並跳過隱藏目錄（含 `.dev`）；首次看到既有目錄時配置 ID，不搬、不改名、不寫 repo sidecar。
42	2. 日期前綴只用來回填 `CreatedAt`；不再把 directory mtime 當 last-used。Open 成功後 `Touch`，列表 activity 取 `max(LastOpenedAt, last Git commit)`，都未知就顯示 unknown。
43	3. Resolve 順序為 exact ID、完整 basename、去日期後完整名稱、唯一 substring；多個 substring 必須回 ambiguity，不再靜默挑最新。
44	4. Clone 預設採 `owner-repo` slug；同日碰撞以 `-2/-3` versioning，不覆寫也不誤開另一個 Try。
45	5. 外部手動搬移且無唯一身份時，以 `dev tries attach <id> <path>` 明確重新連結。
46	
47	Lifecycle filesystem 行為：
48	
49	- `deprecate/reactivate` 只改 phase，不搬檔。
50	- `archive` 搬到 `<tries_root>/.dev/archive/<id>/<basename>`，記住 restore path；`restore` 拒絕覆蓋已存在目的地。
51	- `graduate` 保留 ID/tags/note/Experiment history，將 kind 改為 repository、更新 location；normal directory 用 `os.Rename`，linked worktree 新增並使用 `gitx.MoveWorktree`（`git worktree move`）。MVP 對跨 filesystem move 明確拒絕。
52	- Non-Git Try 的 Git init/initial commit 在搬移前完成，失敗時仍留在原處；remote create/push 在本機 graduation 成功後才做，失敗不謊稱 remote 成功，也不回滾已完成的本機 graduation。
53	- Archive/graduate 先寫 `MoveIntent`、執行 move、再 finalize；`Reconcile` 根據 from/to 實際存在性修復中斷狀態。Catalog finalize 失敗時嘗試搬回並回報。
54	- Evicted tombstone 保留最後 path、phase、tags、remote/recovery receipt 與時間；首版不自動 GC/forget catalog history。

80	## 4. 實作一致的容量模型
81	
82	新增 `internal/diskusage`；在 `gitx.Repo` 的同一次 `rev-parse` 補取 checkout-specific `GitDir`，搭配既有 `GitCommonDir/Key/MainRoot/IsLinkedWorktree` 判斷 ownership。
83	
84	`Usage` 至少包含：
85	
86	- `checkout_bytes`：checkout root 內 logical `Lstat.Size()`，跳過 root `.git` entry；不 follow symlink，symlink 只算自身，sparse file 以 logical length 計。
87	- `private_git_bytes`：只屬於此 checkout、刪除此 checkout 可回收的 Git admin data。
88	- `shared_git_bytes`：shared common-dir 的非重疊 logical bytes，只供 detail/context，不歸到每個 worktree。
89	- `owned_bytes = checkout + private_git`：TRY/REPOS `SIZE` 欄的預設值。
90	- `total_bytes`：僅在 standalone ownership 完整、沒有 shared ambiguity 時提供。
91	- `complete/unreadable_entries/measured_at/cached`；partial 顯示為 `≥N`，不可包裝成精確值。
92	
93	Ownership 規則：standalone clone 且 common-dir 位於目標內時，`.git` 算 private；linked worktree 只算自己的 checkout 與可唯一歸屬的 gitdir，common objects/refs 算 shared；main checkout 仍有 linked worktrees或 external git-dir 時，common-dir 不算其 reclaimable bytes。各欄位不得重複計數。
94	
95	效能與快取：
96	
97	- Portable Go walker、context cancellation、最多 2 個背景 scanner；列表/TUI startup 不同步遞迴所有 repo。
98	- `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/sizes-v1.json` 使用 versioned key（canonical checkout/git/common dirs）與原子 `0600` 寫入，TTL 10 分鐘；nested 變更主要依 TTL，不假裝 root mtime 能完整 invalidation。
99	- Create/clone/archive/restore/graduate/evict、外部 TUI tool 返回後精準 invalidate；`r` 強制重測當前 local view。
100	- TUI 先套 fresh cache，再以 `loadID + sizeMsg` 流式逐列更新；切 view/reload 時 cancel 舊 batch，晚到訊息因 load ID 不符而忽略。每個 `sizeMsg` 後排下一個 channel receive command，避免阻塞 Tea loop。
101	
102	## 5. 安全 backup／reclaim／evict
103	
104	新增 `internal/reclaim`，將 inspect/plan、backup、evict、restore 與 finding codes 放在 domain；CLI/TUI 只呈現 plan 並收集明確意圖。`Apply` 必須在真正 move/remove 前重新 inspect，不能信任幾秒前的畫面。
105	
106	Git preflight 除了重用 `gitx.StatusOf/Discover/Worktrees`，新增 `gitx.RecoverySnapshot` 檢查：
107	
108	- staged/unstaged/untracked/conflicted 與 merge/rebase/cherry-pick/bisect 等進行中狀態；
109	- ignored files（尤其 `.env`、dependencies/build artifacts）及 unreadable content；
110	- local heads/tags/notes、stash，以及指定 remote 的實際 refs/OIDs；
111	- linked/locked/prunable worktrees、shared common-dir ownership；
112	- submodule、nested Git repo、Git LFS；首版無法完整證明時直接阻擋 safe eviction；
113	- catalog `keep`、未完成 task、live runtime、目前 cwd 位於 target、alias/symlink containment。
114	
115	操作語意：
116	
117	- `backup --push` 明確推送選定 heads/tags/notes，再以 `ls-remote` 驗證並寫 receipt；stash 不自動藏到特殊 ref。`forge.CreateRepo(...Push:true)` 不能單獨當完整 backup proof。
118	- Standalone Git 只有在 worktree clean、ignored 已處理、所有受保護 refs 已由指定 remote 驗證且無 blocker 時可 safe-evict。
119	- Linked worktree 若 clean 且 branch/commit 仍由可用 shared common-dir 保留，使用 `git worktree remove`；永不刪 branch/common-dir。Main clone 仍有 linked worktree 時阻擋整個 clone eviction。
120	- Non-Git 預設只能 archive；要永久丟棄須明示 `--discard-without-backup`。Dirty/untracked/ignored/keep 各自使用名稱精確的 `--discard-dirty`、`--discard-ignored`、`--override-keep`，不提供含糊 `--force`，`--yes` 也不能代替 data-loss flags。
121	- 普通 directory eviction 先寫 intent、rename 至同 parent staging name、再 remove；這提供可 reconcile 的 metadata，不宣稱未備份資料在中途刪除後可復原。Safe eviction 已有 remote receipt；unsafe discard 明確顯示不可恢復。
122	- 批次操作預設 report-only；apply 前顯示每筆 canonical path、owned bytes、recovery source、blockers/warnings，要求完全大寫 `YES`。只有命令列明確列出 refs 時 `--yes` 可略過互動，廣泛 filter 不可靜默批次刪除。
123	
124	首版刻意不做：跨 filesystem copy-verify-delete、non-Git/dirty 自動 tar/object-store backup、LFS/submodule/nested-repo 完整備份、allocated blocks/APFS clone/hardlink dedup、daemon/watch/automatic GC、remote repo deletion或 forge archive。
125
```

The implementation will use three domain layers inside `internal/experiment`:

1. **Inventory:** reconcile only immediate visible directories, probe Git with a bounded worker pool, persist/refresh stable Try entries by canonical path or common-dir, and return readable items plus per-record/probe diagnostics.
2. **Selection and creation:** deterministic exact-to-substring resolution with typed errors, clone-aware owner/repo naming and collision versioning, catalog-accurate create results, and explicit post-handoff `Touch`.
3. **Graduation:** plan and revalidate destination safety, initialize/commit before moving, preserve existing repositories unchanged, rename only on one filesystem, finalize the same catalog ID, and roll back the move if finalization fails.

The CLI files will retain only Cobra parsing, rendering, forge remote creation, and `openOrCD`; all path/Git/lifecycle decisions move into the service.

```go
// Package experiment owns discovery, creation, selection and graduation policy
// for the dated scratch directories managed by dev. It deliberately has no
// terminal or runtime dependencies; callers decide how to render and open the
// paths returned here.
package experiment

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/catalog"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
)

var (
	// ErrNotFound identifies a Try reference that matched no eligible item.
	ErrNotFound = errors.New("try not found")
	// ErrAmbiguous identifies a reference that needs a more specific name or ID.
	ErrAmbiguous = errors.New("ambiguous try reference")
)

// Diagnostic is one non-fatal inventory failure. Other valid Tries remain in
// the result when a catalog record, directory, or Git probe cannot be read.
type Diagnostic struct {
	Path      string
	Operation string
	Err       error
}

func (d Diagnostic) Error() string {
	operation := d.Operation
	if operation == "" {
		operation = "inspect"
	}
	if d.Path == "" {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s: %v", operation, d.Err)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s: %v", operation, d.Path, d.Err)
}

func (d Diagnostic) Unwrap() error { return d.Err }

// Candidate is the deterministic, human-readable part of an ambiguous match.
type Candidate struct {
	ID       string
	Name     string
	Basename string
	Path     string
}

// NotFoundError describes an unsuccessful reference lookup.
type NotFoundError struct {
	Ref  string
	Root string
}

func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("no try matching %q under %s", e.Ref, e.Root)
}

func (e *NotFoundError) Unwrap() error { return ErrNotFound }

// AmbiguousError lists every candidate rather than silently picking whichever
// directory happened to have the newest mtime.
type AmbiguousError struct {
	Ref        string
	Candidates []Candidate
}

func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
	labels := make([]string, 0, len(e.Candidates))
	for _, candidate := range e.Candidates {
		label := candidate.Basename
		if label == "" {
			label = candidate.Name
		}
		if candidate.ID != "" {
			label += " (" + candidate.ID + ")"
		}
		labels = append(labels, label)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("try reference %q is ambiguous: %s", e.Ref, strings.Join(labels, ", "))
}

func (e *AmbiguousError) Unwrap() error { return ErrAmbiguous }

// AmbiguousMatchError is retained as a descriptive alias for callers that use
// the same naming as catalog matching.
type AmbiguousMatchError = AmbiguousError

// LiveFacts are observations, never persisted status. DiscoverError is kept
// separate from StatusError and LastCommitError so one failed probe does not
// erase the facts gathered by the others.
type LiveFacts struct {
	Present     bool
	CurrentPath string
	RealPath    string

	Repo   *gitx.Repo
	Status *gitx.Status

	LastCommit        time.Time
	LastCommitSubject string

	DiscoverError   error
	StatusError     error
	LastCommitError error
}

// Item joins durable catalog identity with the current host's live facts.
// Entry is a deep copy and may be nil when a live directory could not be
// cataloged; CatalogError then explains why it is untracked.
type Item struct {
	Entry *catalog.Entry

	ID       string
	Name     string
	Basename string
	Slug     string
	Phase    catalog.ExperimentPhase

	Created    time.Time
	Started    time.Time
	LastOpened time.Time

	OriginURL     string
	RemoteIdentity string

	Live         LiveFacts
	CatalogError error
}

// CurrentPath returns the host-local navigation path, if one is known.
func (i Item) CurrentPath() string { return i.Live.CurrentPath }

// IsRepo reports whether Git discovery identified this Try as a repository.
func (i Item) IsRepo() bool { return i.Live.Repo != nil }

// Activity is the newest explicit dev open or Git commit. A zero time means
// activity is unknown; directory mtime is deliberately not a substitute.
func (i Item) Activity() time.Time {
	activity := i.LastOpened
	if i.Live.LastCommit.After(activity) {
		activity = i.Live.LastCommit
	}
	return activity
}

// DisplayName is the stable directory label used by legacy CLI output.
func (i Item) DisplayName() string {
	if i.Basename != "" {
		return i.Basename
	}
	if i.Name != "" {
		return i.Name
	}
	return i.ID
}

// SearchText contains the identity and path terms useful to CLI/TUI filters.
func (i Item) SearchText() string {
	return strings.Join([]string{i.ID, i.Name, i.Basename, i.Slug, i.OriginURL, i.RemoteIdentity, i.Live.CurrentPath}, " ")
}

// OpenTarget contains everything a caller needs for runtime handoff without
// introducing a runtime dependency into this package.
type OpenTarget struct {
	CatalogID string
	Path      string
	Label     string
}

// OpenTarget returns the selected directory and presentation label.
func (i Item) OpenTarget() OpenTarget {
	return OpenTarget{CatalogID: i.ID, Path: i.Live.CurrentPath, Label: i.DisplayName()}
}

// ListOptions controls durable-history visibility and optional live work.
type ListOptions struct {
	IncludeGraduated  bool
	IncludeNonPresent bool
	SkipEnrichment    bool
	Query             string
}

// CreateRequest describes either a new empty Try or a local Git clone.
type CreateRequest struct {
	Name  string
	Clone string
	NoGit bool
}

// CreateResult distinguishes filesystem success from catalog success. A
// catalog error is returned alongside a result with Created and Path set.
type CreateResult struct {
	Item        Item
	Path        string
	Created     bool
	Existing    bool
	Cloned      bool
	Tracked     bool
	InitWarning error
	Diagnostics []Diagnostic
}

// OpenTarget returns the selected or newly created Try for caller handoff.
func (r CreateResult) OpenTarget() OpenTarget {
	if r.Item.Live.CurrentPath != "" {
		return r.Item.OpenTarget()
	}
	return OpenTarget{CatalogID: r.Item.ID, Path: r.Path, Label: filepath.Base(r.Path)}
}

// TouchResult records the explicit activity written after a successful caller
// handoff.
type TouchResult struct {
	Item      Item
	TouchedAt time.Time
}

// GraduateRequest selects a Try and its safe project destination. CurrentDir is
// optional; an empty Ref falls back to CurrentDir and then the injected getwd.
type GraduateRequest struct {
	Ref        string
	Category   string
	Name       string
	CurrentDir string
	DryRun     bool
}

// GraduatePlan is read-only and can be rendered before an apply. Apply always
// plans again so a destination created after preview cannot be overwritten.
type GraduatePlan struct {
	Item Item

	Source      string
	Destination string
	Category    string
	Name        string

	NeedsGitInit       bool
	NeedsInitialCommit bool
	DryRun             bool
	Diagnostics        []Diagnostic
}

// GraduateResult reports local work only. Remote creation and push remain an
// explicit caller step after this result succeeds.
type GraduateResult struct {
	Plan GraduatePlan
	Item Item

	Moved              bool
	GitInitialized     bool
	InitialCommitMade  bool
	RolledBack         bool
	RollbackError      error
	Diagnostics        []Diagnostic
}

// GitRunFunc and the other hook types are narrow seams used to make destructive
// failure paths deterministic in tests.
type GitRunFunc func(context.Context, string, ...string) (string, error)
type GitDiscoverFunc func(context.Context, string) (gitx.Repo, error)
type GitStatusFunc func(context.Context, string) (gitx.Status, error)
type GitLastCommitFunc func(context.Context, string) (int64, string, error)
type RenameFunc func(string, string) error
type SameFilesystemFunc func(string, string) (bool, error)
type CatalogCreateFunc func(*catalog.Entry) error
type CatalogUpdateFunc func(string, func(*catalog.Entry) error) (*catalog.Entry, error)

// Hooks replaces only the supplied operations; zero fields use production
// implementations. It is intentionally small and operation-shaped rather than
// exposing the Service's internals.
type Hooks struct {
	GitRun        GitRunFunc
	GitDiscover   GitDiscoverFunc
	GitStatus     GitStatusFunc
	GitLastCommit GitLastCommitFunc

	Rename        RenameFunc
	SameFilesystem SameFilesystemFunc
	Getwd         func() (string, error)

	CatalogCreate CatalogCreateFunc
	CatalogUpdate CatalogUpdateFunc
}

// ServiceConfig injects the catalog and host-specific roots. Registry and Store
// must refer to the same durable catalog; either may be omitted when the other
// is sufficient to derive it.
type ServiceConfig struct {
	Registry *catalog.Registry
	Store    *catalog.Store

	TriesRoot   string
	ProjectRoot string
	Host        string
	Clock       func() time.Time

	MaxEnrichment int
	Hooks         Hooks
}

// Service owns all Try policy while delegating persistence and Git porcelain to
// their focused packages.
type Service struct {
	registry *catalog.Registry
	store    *catalog.Store

	triesRoot   string
	projectRoot string
	host        string
	clock       func() time.Time
	workers     int

	gitRun        GitRunFunc
	gitDiscover   GitDiscoverFunc
	gitStatus     GitStatusFunc
	gitLastCommit GitLastCommitFunc
	rename        RenameFunc
	sameFilesystem SameFilesystemFunc
	getwd         func() (string, error)
	catalogCreate CatalogCreateFunc
	catalogUpdate CatalogUpdateFunc
}

// NewService validates and normalizes the injected service dependencies.
func NewService(config ServiceConfig) (*Service, error) {
	store := config.Store
	registry := config.Registry
	if store == nil && registry != nil {
		store = registry.Store()
	}
	if registry == nil && store != nil {
		registry = catalog.NewRegistry(store)
	}
	if store == nil || registry == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("experiment service requires a catalog registry and store")
	}
	if registry.Store() != store {
		return nil, errors.New("experiment service registry and store do not share a catalog")
	}

	triesRoot, err := absoluteRoot(config.TriesRoot, "tries root")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	projectRoot, err := absoluteRoot(config.ProjectRoot, "project root")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	host := strings.TrimSpace(config.Host)
	if host == "" || host != config.Host || strings.ContainsRune(host, '\x00') {
		return nil, errors.New("experiment service host is required and must be normalized")
	}
	clock := config.Clock
	if clock == nil {
		clock = time.Now
	}
	workers := config.MaxEnrichment
	if workers <= 0 {
		workers = 4
	}

	s := &Service{
		registry: registry, store: store,
		triesRoot: triesRoot, projectRoot: projectRoot, host: host,
		clock: clock, workers: workers,
		gitRun: gitx.Run, gitDiscover: gitx.Discover,
		gitStatus: gitx.StatusOf, gitLastCommit: gitx.LastCommit,
		rename: os.Rename, sameFilesystem: sameFilesystem,
		getwd: os.Getwd,
	}
	s.catalogCreate = store.Create
	s.catalogUpdate = registry.Update
	applyHooks(s, config.Hooks)
	return s, nil
}

func applyHooks(service *Service, hooks Hooks) {
	if hooks.GitRun != nil {
		service.gitRun = hooks.GitRun
	}
	if hooks.GitDiscover != nil {
		service.gitDiscover = hooks.GitDiscover
	}
	if hooks.GitStatus != nil {
		service.gitStatus = hooks.GitStatus
	}
	if hooks.GitLastCommit != nil {
		service.gitLastCommit = hooks.GitLastCommit
	}
	if hooks.Rename != nil {
		service.rename = hooks.Rename
	}
	if hooks.SameFilesystem != nil {
		service.sameFilesystem = hooks.SameFilesystem
	}
	if hooks.Getwd != nil {
		service.getwd = hooks.Getwd
	}
	if hooks.CatalogCreate != nil {
		service.catalogCreate = hooks.CatalogCreate
	}
	if hooks.CatalogUpdate != nil {
		service.catalogUpdate = hooks.CatalogUpdate
	}
}

func absoluteRoot(root, label string) (string, error) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(root) == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("experiment service %s is required", label)
	}
	absolute, err := filepath.Abs(root)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("make %s absolute: %w", label, err)
	}
	return filepath.Clean(absolute), nil
}

func (s *Service) now() time.Time { return s.clock().UTC() }

func (s *Service) ensureTriesRoot() error {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(s.triesRoot, 0o755); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create tries root %s: %w", s.triesRoot, err)
	}
	return nil
}

func candidatesOf(items []Item) []Candidate {
	candidates := make([]Candidate, len(items))
	for index, item := range items {
		candidates[index] = Candidate{
			ID: item.ID, Name: item.Name, Basename: item.Basename, Path: item.Live.CurrentPath,
		}
	}
	sort.Slice(candidates, func(i, j int) bool {
		left, right := strings.ToLower(candidates[i].Basename), strings.ToLower(candidates[j].Basename)
		if left != right {
			return left < right
		}
		if candidates[i].Basename != candidates[j].Basename {
			return candidates[i].Basename < candidates[j].Basename
		}
		return candidates[i].ID < candidates[j].ID
	})
	return candidates
}

func itemFromEntry(entry *catalog.Entry, live LiveFacts) Item {
	if entry == nil {
		return Item{Live: live}
	}
	copy := entry.Clone()
	item := Item{
		Entry: copy,
		ID: copy.ID, Name: copy.Name,
		Created: copy.Created, LastOpened: copy.LastOpened,
		RemoteIdentity: copy.RemoteIdentity,
		Live: live,
	}
	if copy.Experiment != nil {
		item.Slug = copy.Experiment.Slug
		item.Phase = copy.Experiment.Phase
		item.Started = copy.Experiment.Started
		item.OriginURL = copy.Experiment.OriginURL
	}
	if item.Live.CurrentPath == "" {
		if location, ok := copy.LocationFor(""); ok {
			item.Live.CurrentPath = location.CurrentPath
		}
	}
	if item.Live.CurrentPath != "" {
		item.Basename = filepath.Base(item.Live.CurrentPath)
	} else if copy.Experiment != nil && copy.Experiment.OriginalPath != "" {
		item.Basename = filepath.Base(copy.Experiment.OriginalPath)
	}
	return item
}

func catalogDiagnostics(diagnostics []catalog.Diagnostic) []Diagnostic {
	out := make([]Diagnostic, len(diagnostics))
	for index, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
		out[index] = Diagnostic{Path: diagnostic.Path, Operation: "read catalog record", Err: diagnostic.Err}
	}
	return out
}

func directoryExists(path string) (bool, error) {
	info, err := os.Stat(path)
	if err == nil {
		return info.IsDir(), nil
	}
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return false, nil
	}
	return false, err
}
```
