530	// externalTools resolves the configured tool bindings.
531	//
532	// Configurable rather than fixed because which program you reach for is
533	// personal, and because the useful ones are often your own scripts and
534	// aliases, not just the well-known tools.
535	func externalTools(app *App) []tui.Tool {
536		var out []tui.Tool
537		for _, t := range app.Cfg.EffectiveTools() {
538			run := t.Run
539			name := t.Name
540			if name == "" {
541				name = firstWord(run)
542			}
543			command := []string{shellPath(), "-c", run}
544			if t.Interactive {
545				// The command string passed to shell -lic is parsed before some
546				// shells finish loading aliases. Parse only eval "$1" up front,
547				// then evaluate the configured command after rc loading, so both
548				// aliases (vibe) and functions (claude-plans-here) work.
549				command = []string{shellPath(), "-lic", `eval "$1"`, "dev-tui-tool", run}
550			}
551			out = append(out, tui.Tool{
552				Key: t.Key, Name: name, Command: command,
553				Available: commandRunnable(run, t.Interactive),
554			})
555		}
556		return out
557	}

559	// commandRunnable resolves the command's first word on PATH, expanding a
560	// leading environment variable so "$EDITOR ." checks the editor itself.
561	func commandRunnable(run string, interactive bool) func() bool {
562		// Availability is stable for the lifetime of one dashboard. In particular,
563		// probing an interactive alias starts a login shell; doing that on every
564		// render would turn a 60fps UI into a shell-launch benchmark.
565		var once sync.Once
566		available := false
567		return func() bool {
568			once.Do(func() { available = checkCommandRunnable(run, interactive) })
569			return available
570		}
571	}
572	
573	func checkCommandRunnable(run string, interactive bool) bool {
574		word := firstWord(run)
575		if strings.HasPrefix(word, "$") {
576			word = os.Getenv(strings.TrimPrefix(word, "$"))
577			if word == "" {
578				return false
579			}
580			word = firstWord(word)
581		}
582		if word == "" {
583			return false
584		}
585		if interactive {
586			// Ask the configured shell after it loads its rc files; LookPath
587			// cannot see aliases or functions.
588			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
589			defer cancel()
590			probe := exec.CommandContext(ctx, shellPath(), "-lic",
591				`command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1`, "dev-tool-probe", word)
592			return probe.Run() == nil
593		}
594		if filepath.IsAbs(word) {
595			_, err := os.Stat(word)
596			return err == nil
597		}
598		_, err := exec.LookPath(word)
599		return err == nil
600	}

679	// collectRemotes aggregates gh and glab, caches the normalised response, then
680	// marks remotes that already have a checkout under the configured scan roots.
681	// Calls run concurrently so one slow forge does not serialise the other.
682	func collectRemotes(ctx context.Context, app *App, limit int) ([]tui.RemoteRow, error) {
683		if limit <= 0 {
684			limit = app.Cfg.Forge.RemoteLimit
685		}
686		type result struct {
687			repos []forge.RemoteRepo
688			err   error
689		}
690		ch := make(chan result, len(forge.All()))
691		var wg sync.WaitGroup
692		available := 0
693		for _, f := range forge.All() {
694			if !f.Available() {
695				continue
696			}
697			available++
698			wg.Add(1)
699			go func(f forge.Forge) {
700				defer wg.Done()
701				r, err := f.ListRepos(ctx, limit)
702				ch <- result{repos: r, err: err}
703			}(f)
704		}
705		wg.Wait()
706		close(ch)
707		if available == 0 {
708			return nil, fmt.Errorf("neither gh nor glab is installed")
709		}
710	
711		var (
712			remoteRepos []forge.RemoteRepo
713			errs        []error
714		)
715		for res := range ch {
716			if res.err != nil {
717				errs = append(errs, res.err)
718			}
719			remoteRepos = append(remoteRepos, res.repos...)
720		}
721		// Cache partial results too. They are exactly what was observed, and a
722		// partial list is more useful on the next switch than another six-second
723		// wait merely to rediscover the same provider failure.
724		if len(remoteRepos) > 0 && limit >= app.Cfg.Forge.RemoteLimit {
725			_ = forge.SaveCache(remoteCachePath(), remoteRepos)
726		}
727		return matchRemoteLocals(ctx, app, remoteRepos), errors.Join(errs...)
728	}

735			assets = make([]*catalog.Entry, len(locals))

739			asset      *catalog.Entry
740		}
741		localByRemote := map[string]localMatch{}

745			}
746			kind, name := forge.IdentityFromURL(gitx.RemoteFromConfig(r.CommonDir, "origin"))

772	func applyCatalogRemoteMatches(app *App, rows []tui.RemoteRow) {
773		if app == nil || app.Catalog == nil || len(rows) == 0 {
774			return
775		}
776		entries, diagnostics, err := app.Catalog.ListWithDiagnostics()
777		if err != nil {
778			app.warnf("could not read catalog for remote matching: %v", err)
779			return
780		}
781		for _, diagnostic := range diagnostics {
782			app.warnf("%s", diagnostic.Error())
783		}
784		if len(diagnostics) > 0 {
785			return
786		}
787		host := config.Hostname()
788		byIdentity := make(map[string][]*catalog.Entry)
789		for _, entry := range entries {
790			location, ok := entry.LocationFor(host)
791			if !ok || location.State != catalog.LocationPresent || entry.RemoteIdentity == "" ||
792				liveCatalogLocationPath(location) == "" {
793				continue
794			}
795			byIdentity[entry.RemoteIdentity] = append(byIdentity[entry.RemoteIdentity], entry)
796		}
797		for index := range rows {
798			identity := catalog.NormalizeRemoteIdentity(rows[index].Repo.CloneURL)
799			matches := byIdentity[identity]
800			if identity == "" || len(matches) != 1 {
801				continue
802			}
803			location, _ := matches[0].LocationFor(host)
804			rows[index].LocalPath = liveCatalogLocationPath(location)
805			rows[index].LocalName = matches[0].Name
806			rows[index].LocalKind = matches[0].Kind
807		}
808	}
809	
810	func liveCatalogLocationPath(location catalog.Location) string {

814			}
815			if info, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
816				return candidate
817			}
818		}
819		return ""
820	}

Also, while passing `remoteIdentity` to `Registry.EnsureRepository`, I need to be cautious about how raw `gitx.RemoteFromConfig` is normalized. I'll keep track of potential issues in TUI as well. 

**Identifying catalog bugs**

If a `try` is deleted or archived, the catalog still shows it as archived. Upon reload, cached remote rows might retain `LocalKind try` from an earlier model, which doesn't match with the current state, thus preserving outdated local markers. The `applyCatalogRemoteMatches` function only works on the initial cache and doesn't affect the model match. This leads to correctness bugs, as current local tries data needs to be updated on each reload. I might consider changing the reload message to ensure local mapping is included afterward. The user wants suppressions now, but there might be better ways to handle it later. 

**Exploring reload options**

I'm considering whether the `reloadRepos` in `runTUI` could activate `IncludeTries` while still using the model's `visibleRepos` filters. This means `m.repos` would include Try rows, but `visibleRepos` can suppress them. However, right now, `collectRepos` has default filters. I could adjust TUI actions for `reloadRepos` to include Try rows, although the model currently lacks flexibility. It might be worth adding a field or maintaining two separate slices to manage this better. Task 4 will introduce a Try view, so I need to plan ahead!

164	func (s *Service) List(ctx context.Context, options ListOptions) ([]Item, []Diagnostic, error) {
165		visible, diagnostics, err := s.Reconcile(ctx)

196

200			}
201			if location, ok := entry.LocationFor(s.host); ok {
202				if _, pathSeen := seenPaths[pathKey(location.CurrentPath)]; pathSeen {
203					continue

205			}
206			graduated := entry.Kind == catalog.KindRepository && entry.Experiment != nil &&
207				entry.Experiment.Phase == catalog.PhaseGraduated
208			if graduated {
209				if !options.All && !options.IncludeGraduated {
210					continue
211				}
212			} else if entry.Kind != catalog.KindTry || entry.Experiment == nil ||
213				!includeExperimentPhase(entry.Experiment.Phase, options) {
214				continue
215			}
216	
217			location, located := entry.LocationFor(s.host)
218			if !located {
219				if !options.All && !options.IncludeNonPresent {
220					continue
221				}

223				continue

225			present := located && location.State == catalog.LocationPresent && !s.hiddenStorage(location.CurrentPath)
226			if present && !graduated && s.validateVisibleTryPath(location.CurrentPath) != nil {
227				present = false
228			}
229			if present {
230				isDirectory, statErr := directoryExists(location.CurrentPath)
231				if statErr != nil {
232					diagnostics = append(diagnostics, Diagnostic{

234					})
235					present = false

238				}
239			}
240			if location.State == catalog.LocationPresent && !present &&
241				!options.All && !options.IncludeNonPresent {
242				continue
243			}
244	
245			live := LiveFacts{Present: present}
246			if located {
247				live.CurrentPath = location.CurrentPath
248				live.RealPath = location.RealPath
249			}
250			if present {

252				if probe.diagnostic != nil {

254				}
255				if probe.valid {

261

263			filtered := items[:0]

280	func includeExperimentPhase(phase catalog.ExperimentPhase, options ListOptions) bool {
281		switch phase {

284		case catalog.PhaseDeprecated:
285			return options.All || options.IncludeDeprecated
286		case catalog.PhaseGraduated:

299		case catalog.LocationEvicted:

390	func compareRepos(a, b RepoRow, sortBy string) int {
391		nameCmp := strings.Compare(strings.ToLower(a.Repo.Display()), strings.ToLower(b.Repo.Display()))
392		descInt := func(x, y int) int {
393			switch {
394			case x > y:
395				return -1
396			case x < y:
397				return 1
398			default:
399				return 0
400			}
401		}
402		descBool := func(x, y bool) int {
403			if x == y {
404				return 0
405			}
406			if x {
407				return -1
408			}
409			return 1
410		}
411		latest := func() int {
412			if a.LastActivity.Equal(b.LastActivity) {
413				return 0
414			}
415			if a.LastActivity.After(b.LastActivity) {
416				return -1
417			}
418			return 1
419		}
420	
421		switch sortBy {
422		case "name":
423			return nameCmp
424		case "latest":
425			if c := latest(); c != 0 {
426				return c
427			}
428		case "git":
429			if c := descBool(a.Status.Dirty(), b.Status.Dirty()); c != 0 {
430				return c
431			}
432			if c := descInt(a.Status.Changed, b.Status.Changed); c != 0 {
433				return c
434			}
435		case "tasks":
436			if c := descInt(a.HotTasks(), b.HotTasks()); c != 0 {
437				return c
438			}
439			if c := descInt(len(a.Tasks), len(b.Tasks)); c != 0 {
440				return c
441			}
442		default: // activity
443			if c := descInt(a.HotTasks(), b.HotTasks()); c != 0 {
444				return c
445			}
446			if c := descBool(a.Live, b.Live); c != 0 {
447				return c
448			}
449			if c := descBool(a.Status.Dirty(), b.Status.Dirty()); c != 0 {
450				return c
451			}
452			if c := descInt(len(a.Tasks), len(b.Tasks)); c != 0 {
453				return c
454			}
455			if c := latest(); c != 0 {
456				return c
457			}
458		}
459		return nameCmp

343	// visibleRepos applies the text query, and sorts repositories with work in
344	// flight to the top — that is what someone opening the dashboard is looking
345	// for, not alphabetical order.
346	func (m Model) visibleRepos() []RepoRow {
347		var out []RepoRow
348		for _, r := range m.repos {
349			if !matches(r.searchText(), m.filter) {
350				continue
351			}
352			out = append(out, r)
353		}
354		sortBy := m.actions.RepoSort
355		if sortBy == "" {
356			sortBy = "activity"
357		}
358		sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool {
359			cmp := compareRepos(out[i], out[j], sortBy)
360			if m.actions.RepoReverse {
361				return cmp > 0
362			}
363			return cmp < 0
364		})
365		return out
366	}
367	
368	// visibleRemotes filters the combined gh/glab inventory. Local clones sort
369	// first, then recently updated repositories.
370	func (m Model) visibleRemotes() []RemoteRow {
371		var out []RemoteRow
372		for _, r := range m.remotes {
373			if matches(r.searchText(), m.filter) {
374				out = append(out, r)
375			}
376		}
377		sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool {
378			if out[i].Cloned() != out[j].Cloned() {
379				return out[i].Cloned()
380			}
381			if !out[i].Repo.UpdatedAt.Equal(out[j].Repo.UpdatedAt) {
382				return out[i].Repo.UpdatedAt.After(out[j].Repo.UpdatedAt)
383			}
384			return out[i].Repo.Label() < out[j].Repo.Label()
385		})
386		return out
387	}

552	// matchRemoteLocals fills cached remote rows from the freshly loaded local
553	// inventory without another scan.
554	func (m *Model) matchRemoteLocals() {
555		byRemote := map[string]RepoRow{}
556		ambiguous := map[string]bool{}
557		for _, r := range m.repos {
558			if r.RemoteName == "" {
559				continue
560			}
561			key := string(r.RemoteForge) + "/" + strings.ToLower(r.RemoteName)
562			if ambiguous[key] {
563				continue
564			}
565			if _, exists := byRemote[key]; exists {
566				delete(byRemote, key)
567				ambiguous[key] = true
568				continue
569			}
570			byRemote[key] = r
571		}
572		for i := range m.remotes {
573			key := string(m.remotes[i].Repo.Forge) + "/" + strings.ToLower(m.remotes[i].Repo.FullName)
574			if local, ok := byRemote[key]; ok {
575				m.remotes[i].LocalPath = local.Repo.Path
576				m.remotes[i].LocalName = local.Repo.Display()
577				m.remotes[i].LocalKind = catalog.KindRepository
578				if local.Asset != nil {
579					m.remotes[i].LocalKind = local.Asset.Kind
580				}
581			} else {
582				m.remotes[i].LocalPath, m.remotes[i].LocalName, m.remotes[i].LocalKind = "", "", ""
583			}
584		}
585	}

598		}
599		if r, ok := m.currentRemote(); ok {

601		}
602		return ""
603	}

673				m.stats = &msg.panel
674			}
675			m.status = ""

678		case actionMsg:
679			if msg.err != nil {
680				m.err = msg.err
681				return m, nil
682			}
683			m.err, m.status = nil, msg.status
684			if msg.remoteName != "" && msg.localPath != "" {
685				for i := range m.remotes {
686					if m.remotes[i].Repo.FullName == msg.remoteName {
687						m.remotes[i].LocalPath = msg.localPath
688						break
689					}
690				}
691			}
692			if msg.cd != "" {

695				// screen torn down first.
696				m.chosen, m.quitting = msg.cd, true
697				return m, tea.Quit
698			}
699			if m.view == ViewRemote {
700				// Clone already updated the selected row; only local repo/task
701				// state needs a refresh. A network round-trip here would make a
702				// successful clone feel hung for several seconds.
703				return m, m.reload()
704			}
705			return m, m.reload()

711			switch m.mode {
712			case modeFilter:

714			case modeEditNext, modeConfirmPark, modeStartTask, modeStartDirect, modeConfirmClone:
715				return m.updatePrompt(msg)
716			}
717			return m.updateList(msg)
718		}
719		return m, nil

722	func (m Model) updateList(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
723		n := m.count()
724		page := m.listHeight() / 2
725		if page < 1 {
726			page = 1
727		}
728	
729		switch msg.String() {
730		case "q", "ctrl+c":
731			m.quitting = true
732			return m, tea.Quit
733		case "esc":
734			// One escape clears whatever narrowing is in effect before quitting
735			// becomes the meaning of the key.
736			if m.filter != "" || len(m.states) > 0 {
737				m.filter, m.states = "", nil
738				m.setAt(0)
739				return m, nil
740			}
741			m.quitting = true
742			return m, tea.Quit
743	
744		// Vim-style movement, with the arrow equivalents alongside.
745		case "j", "down", "ctrl+n":
746			m.setAt(m.at() + 1)
747		case "k", "up", "ctrl+p":
748			m.setAt(m.at() - 1)
749		case "ctrl+d", "pgdown":
750			m.setAt(m.at() + page)
751		case "ctrl+u", "pgup":
752			m.setAt(m.at() - page)
753		case "g", "home":
754			m.setAt(0)
755		case "G", "end":
756			m.setAt(n - 1)
757	
758		// View switching. h/l double as left/right between views, since a list has
759		// no horizontal axis of its own.
760		case "tab", "l", "right":
761			m.view = Views[(int(m.view)+1)%len(Views)]
762			return m.afterViewSwitch()
763		case "shift+tab", "h", "left":
764			m.view = Views[(int(m.view)+len(Views)-1)%len(Views)]
765			return m.afterViewSwitch()
766	
767		case "/":
768			m.mode = modeFilter
769			m.input.SetValue(m.filter)
770			m.input.Placeholder = "filter"
771			m.input.CursorEnd()
772			m.input.Focus()
773			return m, textinput.Blink
774	
775		case "r":
776			m.status = "reloading config + data…"
777			if m.view == ViewRemote {
778				m.remotesLoading = true
779			}
780			return m, m.reloadConfig(m.view == ViewRemote)
781	
782		case "1":
783			m.states, m.showDone = []task.State{task.Hot}, false
784			m.view = ViewTasks
785			m.setAt(0)
786		case "2":
787			m.states, m.showDone = []task.State{task.Warm}, false
788			m.view = ViewTasks
789			m.setAt(0)
790		case "3":
791			m.states, m.showDone = []task.State{task.Cold}, false
792			m.view = ViewTasks
793			m.setAt(0)
794		case "0":
795			m.states, m.filter = nil, ""
796			m.setAt(0)
797		case "a":
798			m.showDone, m.states = !m.showDone, nil
799			m.setAt(0)
800	
801		case "enter", "o":
802			return m, m.openSelected()
803	
804		case "p":
805			if _, ok := m.currentTask(); !ok {
806				return m, nil
807			}
808			return m.prompt(modeConfirmPark, "", "what to do when you come back")
809	
810		case "c":
811			if row, ok := m.currentTask(); ok {
812				return m.prompt(modeEditNext, row.Task.Next, "next action")
813			}
814			if row, ok := m.currentRemote(); ok && !row.Cloned() {
815				return m.prompt(modeConfirmClone, row.Repo.FullName,
816					"enter to clone; esc to cancel")

818			return m, nil
819	
820		case "s":
821			if _, ok := m.currentRepo(); !ok {
822				return m, nil
823			}
824			return m.prompt(modeStartTask, "", "name for the new worktree task")
825	
826		case "d":
827			if _, ok := m.currentRepo(); !ok {
828				return m, nil
829			}
830			return m.prompt(modeStartDirect, "", "name for direct work on current branch")
831	
832		case "e":
833			if m.actions.EditConfig == nil {
834				return m, nil
835			}
836			proc, err := m.actions.EditConfig()
837			if err != nil {
838				m.err = err
839				return m, nil
840			}
841			m.status = "editing config…"
842			return m, tea.ExecProcess(proc, func(err error) tea.Msg {
843				return configEditedMsg{err: err}

845	
846		case "O":
847			if m.view != ViewRepos {
848				return m, nil
849			}
850			orders := []string{"activity", "latest", "name", "git", "tasks"}
851			current := 0
852			for i, order := range orders {
853				if order == m.actions.RepoSort {
854					current = i

857			}

863		case "R":

971	func (m Model) updateFilter(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {

976			m.filter = ""

1012		switch md {
1013		case modeEditNext:
1014			row, ok := m.currentTask()
1015			if !ok {
1016				return nil
1017			}
1018			t := row.Task
1019			return func() tea.Msg {
1020				if err := m.actions.SetNext(context.Background(), t, value); err != nil {
1021					return actionMsg{err: err}
1022				}
1023				return actionMsg{status: "next action recorded for " + t.Title()}
1024			}
1025	
1026		case modeConfirmPark:
1027			row, ok := m.currentTask()
1028			if !ok {
1029				return nil
1030			}
1031			t := row.Task
1032			return func() tea.Msg {
1033				status, err := m.actions.Park(context.Background(), t, value)
1034				return actionMsg{status: status, err: err}
1035			}
1036	
1037		case modeStartTask:
1038			r, ok := m.currentRepo()
1039			if !ok {
1040				return nil
1041			}
1042			if value == "" {
1043				return func() tea.Msg { return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("a task needs a name")} }
1044			}
1045			return func() tea.Msg {
1046				status, err := m.actions.Start(context.Background(), r, value)
1047				return actionMsg{status: status, err: err}
1048			}
1049	
1050		case modeStartDirect:
1051			r, ok := m.currentRepo()
1052			if !ok {
1053				return nil
1054			}
1055			if value == "" {
1056				return func() tea.Msg { return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("a task needs a name")} }
1057			}
1058			return func() tea.Msg {
1059				status, err := m.actions.StartDirect(context.Background(), r, value)

1066				return nil

1069				status, path, err := m.actions.CloneRemote(context.Background(), r)

1078	func (m Model) openSelected() tea.Cmd {
1079		cdWanted := m.actions.Runtime != nil && m.actions.Runtime.Name() == "none"
1080	
1081		if row, ok := m.currentTask(); ok {
1082			t := row.Task
1083			dir := row.Checkout
1084			return func() tea.Msg {
1085				status, err := m.actions.Open(context.Background(), t)
1086				cd := ""
1087				if err == nil && cdWanted {
1088					cd = dir
1089				}
1090				return actionMsg{status: status, cd: cd, err: err}
1091			}
1092		}
1093		if r, ok := m.currentRepo(); ok {
1094			dir := r.Repo.Path
1095			return func() tea.Msg {
1096				status, err := m.actions.OpenRepo(context.Background(), r)
1097				cd := ""
1098				if err == nil && cdWanted {
1099					cd = dir
1100				}
1101				return actionMsg{status: status, cd: cd, err: err}
1102			}
1103		}
1104		if r, ok := m.currentRemote(); ok {
1105			if !r.Cloned() {
1106				return nil // c is the explicit clone action
1107			}
1108			dir := r.LocalPath
1109			return func() tea.Msg {
1110				status, err := m.actions.OpenRemote(context.Background(), r)
1111				cd := ""
1112				if err == nil && cdWanted {
1113					cd = dir
1114				}
1115				return actionMsg{status: status, cd: cd, err: err}
1116			}
1117		}
1118		return nil
1119	}

1121	// launchTool hands the terminal to an external program running in the selected
1122	// row's checkout, then reloads — the tool may well have changed the git state
1123	// the dashboard is displaying.
1124	func (m Model) launchTool(key string) tea.Cmd {
1125		for _, t := range m.actions.Tools {
1126			if t.Key != key {
1127				continue
1128			}
1129			if t.Available != nil && !t.Available() {
1130				return func() tea.Msg {
1131					return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("%s is not installed", t.Command[0])}
1132				}
1133			}
1134			dir := m.currentDir()
1135			if dir == "" {
1136				return func() tea.Msg {
1137					return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("nothing selected with a checkout on disk")}
1138				}
1139			}
1140			c := exec.Command(t.Command[0], t.Command[1:]...)
1141			c.Dir = dir
1142			return tea.ExecProcess(c, func(err error) tea.Msg {
1143				if err != nil {
1144					return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", t.Name, err)}
1145				}
1146				return actionMsg{status: "back from " + t.Name}
1147			})
1148		}
1149		return nil
1150	}
1151	
1152	// Tools lists the external programs available on this machine, so the footer
1153	// only advertises bindings that will actually work.
1154	func (m Model) Tools() []Tool {
1155		var out []Tool
1156		for _, t := range m.actions.Tools {
1157			if t.Available == nil || t.Available() {
1158				out = append(out, t)
1159			}

14	// listHeight budgets rows from what the current detail and footer actually

18	func (m Model) listHeight() int {
19		// Header + its blank line, table header, blank before detail, blank before
20		// footer. Detail and footer can each wrap/change by view and terminal width.
21		fixed := 2 + 1 + 1 + lineCount(m.renderDetail()) + 1 + lineCount(m.renderFooter())
22		h := m.height - fixed
23		if h < 3 {
24			return 3
25		}
26		// A long list adds the "… x–y of n" scroll note.
27		if m.count() > h && h > 3 {
28			h--
29		}
30		return h
31	}

93	func humanSeconds(seconds int) string {

97		}
98		return fmt.Sprintf("%dh %dm", int(d.Hours()), int(d.Minutes())%60)

149		from, to := m.window(len(rows))
150		for i := from; i < to; i++ {
151			r := rows[i]
152			line := fmt.Sprintf("%-*s  %-6s  %-*s  %-16s  %-5s  %s",
153				nameW, pad(r.Task.Title(), nameW),
154				r.Task.State.Label(),
155				branchW, pad(r.Task.Branch, branchW),
156				pad(gitColumn(r), 16),
157				pad(shortAge(r), 5),
158				pad(nextColumn(r), nextW),
159			)
160			b.WriteString(m.renderLine(i, line, colourState(r.Task.State, line)))
161		}
162		b.WriteString(m.scrollNote(len(rows), from, to))
163		return b.String()
164	}

166	func (m Model) renderRepos() string {
167		repos := m.visibleRepos()
168		if len(repos) == 0 {
169			if m.loadingLocal {
170				return "  " + styleDim.Render("Loading local repositories…") + "\n"
171			}
172			return "  " + styleDim.Render("No repositories found. Check paths.scan_roots in your config,"+
173				" or run `dev config init`.\n")
174		}
175		columns := m.repoColumns()
176	
177		var b strings.Builder
178		var headers []string
179		for _, c := range columns {
180			headers = append(headers, fitCell(c.header, c.width))
181		}
182		b.WriteString(styleHeader.Render("  "+strings.Join(headers, "  ")) + "\n")
183	
184		from, to := m.window(len(repos))
185		for i := from; i < to; i++ {
186			r := repos[i]
187			cells := make([]string, 0, len(columns))
188			for _, c := range columns {
189				cells = append(cells, fitCell(repoColumnValue(r, c.name), c.width))
190			}
191			line := strings.Join(cells, "  ")
192			styled := line
193			if r.Status.Dirty() {
194				styled = styleDirty.Render(line)
195			} else if len(r.Tasks) == 0 && !r.Live {
196				styled = styleClean.Render(line)
197			}
198			b.WriteString(m.renderLine(i, line, styled))
199		}
200		b.WriteString(m.scrollNote(len(repos), from, to))
201		return b.String()
202	}

204	type repoColumnSpec struct {
205		name, header string
206		width, min   int
207	}
208	
209	func (m Model) repoColumns() []repoColumnSpec {
210		names := m.actions.RepoColumns
211		if len(names) == 0 {
212			names = []string{"repo", "branch", "git", "live", "latest", "worktrees", "tasks"}
213		}
214		defaults := map[string]repoColumnSpec{
215			"repo":      {"repo", "REPO", 28, 12},
216			"branch":    {"branch", "BRANCH", 22, 10},
217			"git":       {"git", "GIT", 16, 8},
218			"live":      {"live", "LIVE", 15, 7},
219			"latest":    {"latest", "LATEST", 8, 6},
220			"worktrees": {"worktrees", "WT", 3, 2},
221			"tasks":     {"tasks", "TASKS", 18, 8},
222			"category":  {"category", "CATEGORY", 14, 8},
223			"path":      {"path", "PATH", 30, 12},
224		}
225		columns := make([]repoColumnSpec, 0, len(names))
226		for _, name := range names {
227			if c, ok := defaults[name]; ok {
228				columns = append(columns, c)
229			}
230		}
231		// Shrink flexible columns to fit. Configuration controls what exists and in
232		// what order; width adapts to the current pane.
233		total := 2 + 2*(len(columns)-1)
234		for _, c := range columns {
235			total += c.width
236		}
237		for _, preferred := range []string{"path", "tasks", "repo", "branch", "live", "git"} {
238			for i := range columns {
239				if columns[i].name != preferred {
240					continue
241				}
242				// Exhaust the least-important flexible column before touching
243				// the next. Round-robin shrinking made LIVE unreadable while REPO
244				// and TASKS still had plenty of space.
245				for total > m.width && columns[i].width > columns[i].min {
246					columns[i].width--
247					total--
248				}
249			}
250			if total <= m.width {
251				break
252			}
253		}
254		return columns
255	}

257	func repoColumnValue(r RepoRow, name string) string {
258		switch name {
259		case "repo":
260			return r.Repo.Display()
261		case "branch":
262			if r.Repo.Bare {
263				return "(bare)"
264			}
265			return r.Status.Branch
266		case "git":
267			if r.Repo.Bare {
268				return "—"
269			}
270			return r.Status.Summary()
271		case "live":
272			if !r.Live {
273				return "—"
274			}
275			if r.RuntimeStatus != "" {
276				return r.Runtime + ":" + r.RuntimeStatus
277			}
278			return r.Runtime
279		case "latest":
280			return latestAge(r.LastActivity)
281		case "worktrees":
282			if r.Worktrees > 0 {
283				return fmt.Sprintf("%d", r.Worktrees)
284			}
285			return "—"
286		case "tasks":
287			if tasks := r.StateSummary(); tasks != "" {
288				return tasks
289			}
290			return "—"
291		case "category":
292			if r.Repo.Category != "" {
293				return r.Repo.Category
294			}
295			return "—"
296		case "path":
297			return contract(r.Repo.Path)
298		}
299		return ""
300	}

302	func latestAge(at time.Time) string {
303		if at.IsZero() {
304			return "—"
305		}
306		d := time.Since(at)
307		switch {
308		case d < time.Hour:
309			return fmt.Sprintf("%dm", int(d.Minutes()))
310		case d < 24*time.Hour:
311			return fmt.Sprintf("%dh", int(d.Hours()))
312		case d < 14*24*time.Hour:
313			return fmt.Sprintf("%dd", int(d.Hours()/24))
314		case d < 60*24*time.Hour:
315			return fmt.Sprintf("%dw", int(d.Hours()/24/7))
316		default:
317			return fmt.Sprintf("%dmo", int(d.Hours()/24/30))
318		}
319	}

325		}
326		return s

608	// wrapBindings lays the key hints out over as many lines as the width needs,
609	// rather than truncating them — a hint you cannot read is not a hint.
610	func wrapBindings(items []string, width int) string {
611		if width < 20 {
612			width = 20
613		}
614		var lines []string
615		cur := ""
616		for _, it := range items {
617			candidate := it
618			if cur != "" {
619				candidate = cur + " · " + it
620			}
621			if lipgloss.Width(candidate) > width && cur != "" {
622				lines = append(lines, cur)
623				cur = it
624				continue
625			}
626			cur = candidate
627		}
628		if cur != "" {
629			lines = append(lines, cur)
630		}
631		return strings.Join(lines, "\n  ")
632	}

681	// pad truncates to n display columns, measuring the way lipgloss renders so
682	// CJK repo and task names do not shift the table.
683	func pad(s string, n int) string {
684		if lipgloss.Width(s) <= n {
685			return s
686		}
687		var b strings.Builder
688		used := 0
689		for _, r := range s {
690			w := lipgloss.Width(string(r))
691			if used+w > n-1 {
692				break
693			}
694			b.WriteRune(r)
695			used += w
696		}
697		return b.String() + "…"
698	}

16	// RepoRow is one repository as the dashboard shows it: what it is, plus how
17	// much of it is currently in flight.
18	//
19	// The repository view exists because the task list alone answers only half the
20	// question. On a machine with forty repositories and no tasks recorded yet,
21	// a task-only dashboard is empty — and the honest answer to "what do I have
22	// here?" has to come before "what am I working on?"
23	type RepoRow struct {
24		Repo   repo.Repo
25		Status gitx.Status
26		// Asset is catalog metadata joined without persisting an otherwise
27		// unobserved repository. A Try asset lets callers suppress or label it.
28		Asset *catalog.Entry
29		// LastActivity is the newest commit time in this checkout. It is a durable,
30		// cheap approximation of "when was this repo last touched" and is sortable.
31		LastActivity time.Time
32		// Worktrees is the number of linked worktrees, excluding the main checkout.
33		Worktrees int
34		// Tasks are the recorded tasks belonging to this repository.
35		Tasks []*task.Task
36		// Live reports a runtime session sitting in this repository.
37		Live          bool
38		Runtime       string
39		RuntimeHandle string
40		RuntimeStatus string
41		// RemoteForge / RemoteName identify origin for matching the REMOTE view to
42		// this local checkout without rescanning every repo when a cache opens.
43		RemoteForge forge.Kind
44		RemoteName  string
45	}
46	
47	// HotTasks counts the repository's tasks that are currently hot.
48	// IsTry reports an ungraduated Try that should live in the dedicated TRY view,
49	// while remaining in the model's local snapshot for REMOTE matching.
50	func (r RepoRow) IsTry() bool {
51		return r.Asset != nil && r.Asset.Kind == catalog.KindTry && r.Asset.Experiment != nil &&
52			(r.Asset.Experiment.Phase == catalog.PhaseActive || r.Asset.Experiment.Phase == catalog.PhaseDeprecated)
53	}
54	
55	func (r RepoRow) HotTasks() int {
56		n := 0
57		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
58			if t.State == task.Hot {
59				n++
60			}
61		}
62		return n
63	}
64	
65	// StateSummary renders the repository's tasks as a compact per-state tally,
66	// which is what makes the list scannable at forty repositories.
67	func (r RepoRow) StateSummary() string {
68		if len(r.Tasks) == 0 {
69			return ""
70		}
71		counts := map[task.State]int{}
72		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
73			counts[t.State]++
74		}
75		var parts []string
76		for _, s := range task.States {
77			if counts[s] > 0 {
78				parts = append(parts, s.Icon()+strconv.Itoa(counts[s]))
79			}
80		}
81		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
82	}
83	
84	// searchText is what a filter query matches against.
85	func (r RepoRow) searchText() string {
86		var b strings.Builder
87		b.WriteString(r.Repo.Display())
88		b.WriteString(" ")
89		b.WriteString(r.Status.Branch)
90		if r.Asset != nil {
91			b.WriteString(" ")
92			b.WriteString(string(r.Asset.Kind))
93			b.WriteString(" ")
94			b.WriteString(r.Asset.Note)
95			b.WriteString(" ")
96			b.WriteString(strings.Join(r.Asset.Tags, " "))
97		}
98		for _, t := range r.Tasks {
99			b.WriteString(" ")
100			b.WriteString(t.Title())
101			b.WriteString(" ")
102			b.WriteString(t.Branch)
103		}
104		return strings.ToLower(b.String())
105	}
106	
107	// taskSearchText is what a filter query matches a task row against.
108	func taskSearchText(r inventory.Row) string {
109		t := r.Task
110		return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
111			t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, t.Next, t.Note, string(t.State),
112		}, " "))
113	}
114	
115	// matches reports whether every whitespace-separated term of the query appears
116	// in the haystack.
117	//
118	// Term-wise rather than substring so "auth api" finds a task named "api token
119	// auth" — the order words come to mind in is rarely the order they appear in.
120	func matches(haystack, query string) bool {
121		query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
122		if query == "" {
123			return true
124		}
125		for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
126			if !strings.Contains(haystack, term) {
127				return false
128			}
129		}
130		return true
131	}
132	
133	// RemoteRow is one repository known to GitHub or GitLab, optionally matched to
134	// a local checkout. The REMOTE view is the bridge between "what exists on the
135	// forge" and "what is already on this machine".
136	type RemoteRow struct {
137		Repo forge.RemoteRepo `json:"repo"`
138		// LocalPath is the checkout under the configured scan roots, empty when the
139		// remote has not been cloned here.
140		LocalPath string `json:"local_path,omitempty"`
141		// LocalName is the discovered repo's display name.
142		LocalName string `json:"local_name,omitempty"`
143		// LocalKind distinguishes a cataloged Try from an ordinary repository.
144		LocalKind catalog.Kind `json:"local_kind,omitempty"`
145	}
146	
147	// Cloned reports whether this remote already has a local checkout.
148	func (r RemoteRow) Cloned() bool { return r.LocalPath != "" }
149	
150	func (r RemoteRow) searchText() string {
151		return strings.ToLower(strings.Join([]string{
152			string(r.Repo.Forge), r.Repo.Name, r.Repo.FullName, r.Repo.Description,
153			r.Repo.Visibility, r.Repo.DefaultBranch, r.LocalName, string(r.LocalKind),
154		}, " "))
155	}

162		ActiveDays int
163		Since      time.Time
164		Until      time.Time
165	}

86	// send feeds a sequence of key presses through Update, running any command the
87	// model returns so the action callbacks actually fire — that is what makes
88	// these tests exercise the real key bindings rather than the model's fields.
89	func send(m tui.Model, msgs ...tea.Msg) tui.Model {
90		var cur tea.Model = m
91		for _, msg := range msgs {
92			var cmd tea.Cmd
93			cur, cmd = cur.Update(msg)
94			// Follow the command chain, so an action's resulting message (and the
95			// reload it triggers) is applied too. Commands that do not return
96			// promptly are the cursor's blink timers; running those would make the
97			// suite sleep for half a second per keystroke.
98			for i := 0; cmd != nil && i < 8; i++ {
99				out, ok := runQuickly(cmd)
100				if !ok || out == nil {
101					break
102				}
103				if _, isBatch := out.(tea.BatchMsg); isBatch {
104					break
105				}
106				cur, cmd = cur.Update(out)
107			}
108		}
109		return cur.(tui.Model)
110	}
111	
112	// runQuickly executes a command, giving up on anything that blocks — which in
113	// practice means the cursor blink timers.
114	func runQuickly(cmd tea.Cmd) (tea.Msg, bool) {
115		done := make(chan tea.Msg, 1)
116		go func() { done <- cmd() }()
117		select {
118		case msg := <-done:
119			return msg, true
120		case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
121			return nil, false
122		}
123	}
124	
125	func key(s string) tea.KeyMsg {
126		switch s {
127		case "enter":
128			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEnter}
129		case "esc":
130			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEsc}
131		case "down":
132			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyDown}
133		case "up":
134			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyUp}
135		}
136		return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune(s)}
137	}
138	
139	func typeText(s string) []tea.KeyMsg {
140		out := make([]tea.KeyMsg, 0, len(s))
141		for _, r := range s {
142			out = append(out, tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune{r}})
143		}
144		return out
145	}

423			rows = append(rows, row(fmt.Sprintf("t%02d", i), fmt.Sprintf("task %02d", i), task.Hot, ""))
424		}
425		m := tui.New(newActions(&recorder{}, rows), rows, nil)
426		m = send(m, tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: 120, Height: 40})
427	
428		m = send(m, key("G"))
429		if !strings.Contains(m.View(), "▸") {
430			t.Fatal("G should leave the cursor somewhere visible")
431		}
432		m = send(m, key("g"))
433		// After g the first row must be selected, so it carries the marker.
434		lines := strings.Split(m.View(), "\n")
435		var markerLine string
436		for _, l := range lines {
437			if strings.Contains(l, "▸") {
438				markerLine = l
439				break
440			}
441		}
442		if !strings.Contains(markerLine, "task 00") {
443			t.Errorf("g should jump to the top, cursor is on %q", markerLine)
444		}
445	
446		// ctrl+d moves further than a single j.
447		oneDown := send(m, key("j"))
448		halfPage := send(m, tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyCtrlD})
449		if oneDown.View() == halfPage.View() {
450			t.Error("ctrl+d should move further than j")
451		}
452	}

557	func remoteRow(provider forge.Kind, fullName, local string) tui.RemoteRow {
558		name := fullName
559		if i := strings.LastIndexByte(name, '/'); i >= 0 {
560			name = name[i+1:]
561		}
562		return tui.RemoteRow{
563			Repo: forge.RemoteRepo{
564				Forge: provider, Name: name, FullName: fullName,
565				Description:   "description for " + name,
566				URL:           "https://example.com/" + fullName,
567				CloneURL:      "https://example.com/" + fullName + ".git",
568				DefaultBranch: "main", Visibility: "private",
569				UpdatedAt: time.Now().Add(-24 * time.Hour),
570			},
571			LocalPath: local,
572		}
573	}

113		// each on its own key. When empty, DefaultTools applies.
114		//
115		// Configurable rather than fixed because which program you reach for is
116		// personal — nvim or helix, lazygit or gitui, and whatever aliases and
117		// scripts you have built up around your own workflow.
118		Tools []Tool `toml:"tools"`
119	}
120	
121	// RepoTable configures columns and ordering in the TUI REPOS view.
122	type RepoTable struct {
123		// Columns may contain repo, branch, git, live, latest, worktrees, tasks,
124		// category, or path, in the exact display order wanted.
125		Columns []string `toml:"columns"`
126		// Sort is activity, latest, name, git, or tasks.
127		Sort string `toml:"sort"`
128		// Reverse flips the selected order.
129		Reverse bool `toml:"reverse"`
130	}
131	
132	// DefaultRepoColumns is the useful full local inventory without paths (detail
133	// shows the selected path).
134	func DefaultRepoColumns() []string {
135		return []string{"repo", "branch", "git", "live", "latest", "worktrees", "tasks"}
136	}
137	
138	// EffectiveRepoColumns returns configured columns or the defaults.
139	func (c Config) EffectiveRepoColumns() []string {
140		if len(c.TUI.Repos.Columns) == 0 {
141			return DefaultRepoColumns()
142		}
143		return c.TUI.Repos.Columns
144	}
145	
146	// EffectiveRepoSort returns the configured ordering or activity-first.
147	func (c Config) EffectiveRepoSort() string {
148		if c.TUI.Repos.Sort == "" {
149			return "activity"
150		}
151		return c.TUI.Repos.Sort
152	}
153	
154	// Tool is one external program bound to a key in the dashboard.
155	type Tool struct {
156		// Key launches it. A single character, and not one of the dashboard's own
157		// bindings — dev reports a clash rather than silently shadowing.
158		Key string `toml:"key"`
159		// Name is shown in the footer.
160		Name string `toml:"name"`
161		// Run is a shell command, executed in the selected row's checkout.
162		Run string `toml:"run"`
163		// Interactive runs through $SHELL -lic, loading the user's rc file so a
164		// shell alias or function can be used. Off by default: startup files can
165		// print output and alter environment in ways an ordinary command should
166		// not inherit accidentally.
167		Interactive bool `toml:"interactive"`
168	}
169	
170	// reservedKeys are the dashboard's own bindings. A tool cannot take one,
171	// because losing the ability to quit or move is not a trade anyone wants.
172	var reservedKeys = map[string]string{
173		"q": "quit", "j": "down", "k": "up", "g": "top", "G": "bottom",
174		"h": "previous view", "l": "next view", "tab": "next view",
175		"/": "filter", "r": "refresh", "o": "open", "p": "park",
176		"c": "edit next action", "s": "start a worktree task", "d": "start a direct task", "a": "include done",
177		"0": "clear filters", "1": "hot", "2": "warm", "3": "cold",
178		"?": "help", "H": "repo activity heatmap", "e": "edit config",
179		"O": "cycle repo sort", "R": "reverse repo sort",
180	}
181	
182	// ReservedKey reports the dashboard binding a key would collide with.
183	func ReservedKey(key string) (string, bool) {
184		name, ok := reservedKeys[key]
185		return name, ok
186	}

```text
1	# TUI navigation
2	
3	Bare `dev` opens the dashboard when stdin/stdout are terminals; `dev tui`
4	opens it explicitly. When piped, bare `dev` prints `dev ls` instead, so shell
5	composition stays predictable.
6	
7	## Three views
8	
9	Switch with `tab`, `l`/`h`, or right/left:
10	
11	| View | Answers | Data source |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| TASKS | What am I working on? | task registry + live Git/runtime state |
14	| REPOS | What repositories exist here? | recursive configured scan roots |
15	| REMOTE | What can I open or clone? | authenticated `gh` + `glab` inventories |
16	
17	REPOS shows branch, dirty state, linked-worktree count and HOT/WARM/COLD task
18	tallies. Repos with active work sort first; untracked clean repos remain
19	visible below them. On a first run with no tasks, switch to REPOS and press `s`
20	to start one, or run `dev adopt` to import work already in flight.
21	
22	REMOTE loads lazily, so dashboard startup never waits on the network. A
23	private XDG cache makes later switches instant; `r` refreshes explicitly. It
24	marks remotes already cloned under `scan_roots`. Enter opens a local clone; `c`
25	asks before cloning an absent repo into `project_root`.
26	
27	## Vim-style movement
28	
29	```
30	j / k                next / previous
31	ctrl+d / ctrl+u      half page down / up
32	g / G                top / bottom
33	h / l, shift-tab/tab previous / next view
34	/                    filter as you type
35	esc                  clear prompt/filter; when clear, quit
36	q                    quit
37	```
38	
39	The `/` query applies to the current view and matches whitespace-separated
40	terms independently. `gitlab auth` finds a GitLab repo whose name/description
41	also contains auth, regardless of word order.
42	
43	## Actions
44	
45	TASKS:
46	
47	```
48	enter / o  open in the selected runtime
49	p          park warm, prompting for the next action
50	c          edit the next action
51	1 / 2 / 3  show HOT / WARM / COLD
52	0          clear filters
53	a          include DONE
54	```
55	
56	REPOS:
57	
58	```
59	enter / o  ad-hoc open: no task, branch or worktree
60	d          track direct work on the current branch (usually main)
61	s          isolated task: branch + worktree + provisioning + runtime + entry
62	```
63	
64	The LIVE column makes runtime state explicit (`herdr:working`, `herdr:idle`);
65	the detail pane includes the workspace handle. LATEST is the newest dirty-file
66	mtime, commit time, or task update.
67	
68	Columns and ordering are configured under `[tui.repos]`. In the view, `O`
69	cycles activity/latest/name/git/tasks and `R` reverses the current sort.
70	
71	REMOTE:
72	
73	```
74	enter / o  open an existing local clone
75	c          confirm and clone an absent repo into project_root
76	r          refresh gh + glab, replacing the cache
77	```
78	
79	## Heatmap and live config
80	
81	```
82	H   open the selected repository's one-year activity heatmap
83	    b backfills only that repo; r rereads stats; H / esc returns
84	
85	e   edit the effective config in VISUAL/EDITOR
86	r   reparse config and reload local/remote data and tool bindings
87	```
88	
89	An empty heatmap is actionable: press `b` to derive only the selected repo's
90	history into stats.db and automatically redraw. `r` does not manufacture data;
91	it rereads what collectors/backfill have stored.
92	
93	Returning from `e` live-reloads the config. Changes to scan roots, worktree
94	policy, forge cache settings and `[[tui.tools]]` take effect immediately. A
95	runtime backend change needs a restart because existing callbacks and sessions
96	belong to the backend the TUI opened with; the status line says so rather than
97	pretending to switch underneath a live workspace.
98	
99	## External tools are explicit configuration
100	
101	```bash
102	dev tui tools
103	```
104	
105	shows every binding, the exact command, its source, and whether it can run on
106	this machine. `dev config init` writes the defaults out in full:
107	
108	```toml
109	[[tui.tools]]
110	key  = "L"
111	name = "lazygit"
112	run  = "lazygit"
113	
114	[[tui.tools]]
115	key  = "Y"
116	name = "yazi"
117	run  = "yazi"
118	
119	[[tui.tools]]
120	key  = "V"
121	name = "nvim"
122	run  = "nvim ."
123	
124	[[tui.tools]]
125	key  = "B"
126	name = "vibe"
127	run  = "vibe"
128	interactive = true
129	
130	[[tui.tools]]
131	key  = "P"
132	name = "plans here"
133	run  = "claude-plans-here"
134	interactive = true
135	```
136	
137	A configured list replaces the defaults entirely. Commands run through
138	`$SHELL` in the selected row's checkout, so arguments, environment variables
139	and executable scripts work. `interactive = true` runs through `$SHELL -lic`
140	and deliberately evaluates the command *after* rc loading, so this machine's
141	`vibe` alias and `claude-plans-here` function work. Prefer a real script on PATH
142	when the binding should be portable to machines with different shell configs.
143	
144	Keys are case-sensitive. A tool cannot take one the dashboard owns; config
145	loading reports the collision instead of silently shadowing movement or quit.
146
```

```go
package tui

import (
	"context"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/catalog"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/experiment"
)

// TryRow is one durable experiment plus the live runtime facts the dashboard
// adds to experiment.Service's filesystem and Git inventory.
type TryRow struct {
	Item experiment.Item

	Live          bool
	Runtime       string
	RuntimeHandle string
	RuntimeStatus string
}

// Present reports whether this host has an openable checkout for the Try.
func (r TryRow) Present() bool { return r.Item.Live.Present && r.Item.Live.CurrentPath != "" }

// LocationState returns this host's durable disposition, or an empty value when
// the catalog has no location for it.
func (r TryRow) LocationState() catalog.LocationState {
	if r.Item.Entry == nil {
		return ""
	}
	for _, location := range r.Item.Entry.Locations {
		if location.CurrentPath == r.Item.Live.CurrentPath && location.State == catalog.LocationPresent {
			return location.State
		}
	}
	// Item has already selected the current host's live facts, but archived and
	// evicted rows have no host field of their own. There is at most one location
	// whose current path is the Item path in the host-scoped inventory.
	for _, location := range r.Item.Entry.Locations {
		if location.CurrentPath == r.Item.Live.CurrentPath && r.Item.Live.CurrentPath != "" {
			return location.State
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// Where renders the host-local lifecycle state used in rows and structured
// filters. Missing is distinct from evicted: it means metadata expected a path
// that the live probe could not find.
func (r TryRow) Where() string {
	if state := r.LocationState(); state != "" {
		if state == catalog.LocationPresent && !r.Item.Live.Present {
			return "missing"
		}
		return string(state)
	}
	if r.Item.Live.Present {
		return string(catalog.LocationPresent)
	}
	return "other-host"
}

// Mark is the compact intent column shared with the future reclaim view.
func (r TryRow) Mark() string {
	switch {
	case r.Item.Entry != nil && r.Item.Entry.HasTag("important"):
		return "!"
	case r.Item.Entry != nil && r.Item.Entry.HasTag("keep"):
		return "◆"
	default:
		return "·"
	}
}

func (r TryRow) searchText() string {
	values := []string{
		r.Item.SearchText(), r.Where(), r.Runtime, r.RuntimeStatus,
	}
	return strings.ToLower(strings.Join(values, " "))
}

func (r TryRow) matches(query string) bool {
	query = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(query))
	if query == "" {
		return true
	}
	for _, term := range strings.Fields(query) {
		key, value, structured := strings.Cut(term, ":")
		if structured {
			switch key {
			case "tag":
				if r.Item.Entry == nil || !r.Item.Entry.HasTag(value) {
					return false
				}
				continue
			case "phase":
				if string(r.Item.Phase) != value {
					return false
				}
				continue
			case "where":
				if r.Where() != value {
					return false
				}
				continue
			case "git":
				if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(tryGitSummary(r)), value) {
					return false
				}
				continue
			}
		}
		if !strings.Contains(r.searchText(), term) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func tryGitSummary(row TryRow) string {
	switch {
	case row.Item.Live.DiscoverError != nil:
		return "error"
	case row.Item.Live.Repo == nil:
		return "—"
	case row.Item.Live.StatusError != nil || row.Item.Live.Status == nil:
		return "repo ?"
	default:
		return row.Item.Live.Status.Summary()
	}
}

func tryActivityAge(row TryRow) string {
	return latestAge(row.Item.Activity())
}

// TryAction is an operation requested by a dashboard form. Domain validation
// remains in experiment.Service; these names only describe user intent.
type TryAction string

const (
	TryOpen       TryAction = "open"
	TryCreate     TryAction = "create"
	TryMark       TryAction = "mark"
	TryDeprecate  TryAction = "deprecate"
	TryReactivate TryAction = "reactivate"
	TryArchive    TryAction = "archive"
	TryRestore    TryAction = "restore"
	TryGraduate   TryAction = "graduate"
)

// TryRequest is the normalized payload produced by a TUI overlay.
type TryRequest struct {
	Action TryAction
	ID     string

	Name     string
	Clone    string
	NoGit    bool
	Tags     []string
	Note     string
	Category string
	To       string
}

// TryActionResult tells the model what local snapshots need refreshing. CD is
// honored after Bubble Tea leaves the alternate screen.
type TryActionResult struct {
	Status       string
	CD           string
	RefreshRepos bool
}

// TryActions groups Try-specific callbacks instead of continuously widening the
// dashboard's top-level Actions surface.
type TryActions struct {
	Reload func(ctx context.Context, includeAll bool) ([]TryRow, error)
	Apply  func(ctx context.Context, request TryRequest) (TryActionResult, error)
}

func sortTryRows(rows []TryRow, sortBy string, reverse bool) {
	sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
		left, right := rows[i], rows[j]
		cmp := 0
		switch sortBy {
		case "name":
			cmp = strings.Compare(strings.ToLower(left.Item.DisplayName()), strings.ToLower(right.Item.DisplayName()))
		case "phase":
			leftKey := string(left.Item.Phase) + "/" + left.Where()
			rightKey := string(right.Item.Phase) + "/" + right.Where()
			cmp = strings.Compare(leftKey, rightKey)
		default: // activity
			leftActivity, rightActivity := left.Item.Activity(), right.Item.Activity()
			switch {
			case left.Item.Entry != nil && left.Item.Entry.HasTag("important") &&
				(right.Item.Entry == nil || !right.Item.Entry.HasTag("important")):
				cmp = -1
			case right.Item.Entry != nil && right.Item.Entry.HasTag("important") &&
				(left.Item.Entry == nil || !left.Item.Entry.HasTag("important")):
				cmp = 1
			case leftActivity.After(rightActivity):
				cmp = -1
			case rightActivity.After(leftActivity):
				cmp = 1
			}
		}
		if cmp == 0 {
			cmp = strings.Compare(strings.ToLower(left.Item.DisplayName()), strings.ToLower(right.Item.DisplayName()))
		}
		if cmp == 0 {
			cmp = strings.Compare(left.Item.ID, right.Item.ID)
		}
		if reverse {
			return cmp > 0
		}
		return cmp < 0
	})
}

func splitTagInput(value string) []string {
	return catalog.NormalizeTags(strings.FieldsFunc(value, func(r rune) bool {
		return r == ',' || r == ';' || r == '\n' || r == '\t' || r == ' '
	}))
}

func parseBoolInput(value string, fallback bool) (bool, bool) {
	value = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(value))
	if value == "" {
		return fallback, true
	}
	if parsed, err := strconv.ParseBool(value); err == nil {
		return parsed, true
	}
	switch value {
	case "yes", "y", "on":
		return true, true
	case "no", "n", "off":
		return false, true
	default:
		return false, false
	}
}

```

_**Agent (gpt-5.6-sol 2026-08-27 14:12:05Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```go
package tui

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/textinput"
	tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/catalog"
)

type overlayKind int

const (
	overlayNone overlayKind = iota
	overlayHelp
	overlayTryMenu
	overlayTryForm
	overlayTryConfirm
)

type formField struct {
	key   string
	label string
	input textinput.Model
}

// overlayState uses fixed arrays so copying Model also copies the mutable form
// and menu state. A slice or pointer would violate Bubble Tea's value semantics.
type overlayState struct {
	kind   overlayKind
	title  string
	target TryRow
	action TryAction

	options     [8]TryAction
	optionLabels [8]string
	optionCount int
	optionIndex int

	fields     [4]formField
	fieldCount int
	fieldIndex int
}

func (m Model) openHelpOverlay() Model {
	m.overlay = overlayState{kind: overlayHelp, title: "keyboard help"}
	m.err = nil
	return m
}

func (m Model) openTryMenu(row TryRow) Model {
	overlay := overlayState{kind: overlayTryMenu, title: "Try actions", target: row}
	overlay.addOption(TryMark, "edit tags and note")
	switch row.Item.Phase {
	case catalog.PhaseActive:
		overlay.addOption(TryDeprecate, "deprecate (metadata only)")
	case catalog.PhaseDeprecated:
		overlay.addOption(TryReactivate, "reactivate")
	}
	switch row.LocationState() {
	case catalog.LocationPresent:
		overlay.addOption(TryArchive, "archive locally (reversible move)")
		overlay.addOption(TryGraduate, "graduate into a project")
	case catalog.LocationArchived:
		overlay.addOption(TryRestore, "restore from local archive")
		overlay.addOption(TryGraduate, "graduate archived Try")
	}
	m.overlay = overlay
	m.err = nil
	return m
}

func (o *overlayState) addOption(action TryAction, label string) {
	if o.optionCount >= len(o.options) {
		return
	}
	o.options[o.optionCount] = action
	o.optionLabels[o.optionCount] = label
	o.optionCount++
}

func (m Model) openTryForm(action TryAction, row TryRow) (Model, tea.Cmd) {
	overlay := overlayState{kind: overlayTryForm, action: action, target: row}
	switch action {
	case TryCreate:
		overlay.title = "new Try"
		overlay.addField("name", "name", "experiment name", "")
		overlay.addField("clone", "clone", "optional repository URL/ref", "")
		overlay.addField("git", "git init", "yes or no", "yes")
	case TryMark:
		overlay.title = "mark " + row.Item.DisplayName()
		overlay.addField("tags", "tags", "comma or space separated", strings.Join(row.Item.Tags, ", "))
		overlay.addField("note", "note", "optional note", row.Item.Note)
	case TryRestore:
		overlay.title = "restore " + row.Item.DisplayName()
		overlay.addField("to", "to", "optional basename/path under tries_root", "")
	case TryGraduate:
		overlay.title = "graduate " + row.Item.DisplayName()
		overlay.addField("category", "category", "optional project category", "")
		overlay.addField("name", "name", "optional project name", "")
	default:
		m.err = fmt.Errorf("Try action %q has no form", action)
		return m, nil
	}
	m.overlay = overlay
	m.err = nil
	return m.focusOverlayField(0)
}

func (m Model) openTryConfirmation(action TryAction, row TryRow) (Model, tea.Cmd) {
	overlay := overlayState{
		kind: overlayTryConfirm, title: "confirm " + string(action),
		target: row, action: action,
	}
	overlay.addField("confirm", "confirm", "type YES exactly", "")
	m.overlay = overlay
	m.err = nil
	return m.focusOverlayField(0)
}

func (o *overlayState) addField(key, label, placeholder, value string) {
	if o.fieldCount >= len(o.fields) {
		return
	}
	input := textinput.New()
	input.CharLimit = 300
	input.Placeholder = placeholder
	input.SetValue(value)
	input.CursorEnd()
	o.fields[o.fieldCount] = formField{key: key, label: label, input: input}
	o.fieldCount++
}

func (m Model) focusOverlayField(index int) (Model, tea.Cmd) {
	if m.overlay.fieldCount == 0 {
		return m, nil
	}
	if index < 0 {
		index = m.overlay.fieldCount - 1
	}
	if index >= m.overlay.fieldCount {
		index = 0
	}
	for fieldIndex := 0; fieldIndex < m.overlay.fieldCount; fieldIndex++ {
		m.overlay.fields[fieldIndex].input.Blur()
	}
	m.overlay.fieldIndex = index
	return m, m.overlay.fields[index].input.Focus()
}

func (m Model) updateOverlay(message tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	switch m.overlay.kind {
	case overlayHelp:
		switch message.String() {
		case "esc", "?", "q":
			m.overlay = overlayState{}
		}
		return m, nil

	case overlayTryMenu:
		switch message.String() {
		case "esc", "q":
			m.overlay = overlayState{}
			return m, nil
		case "j", "down":
			if m.overlay.optionCount > 0 {
				m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + 1) % m.overlay.optionCount
			}
			return m, nil
		case "k", "up":
			if m.overlay.optionCount > 0 {
				m.overlay.optionIndex = (m.overlay.optionIndex + m.overlay.optionCount - 1) % m.overlay.optionCount
			}
			return m, nil
		case "enter":
			if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 {
				return m, nil
			}
			action := m.overlay.options[m.overlay.optionIndex]
			row := m.overlay.target
			switch action {
			case TryMark, TryRestore, TryGraduate:
				return m.openTryForm(action, row)
			case TryArchive:
				return m.openTryConfirmation(action, row)
			case TryDeprecate, TryReactivate:
				m.overlay = overlayState{}
				m.status = string(action) + " in progress…"
				return m, m.applyTry(TryRequest{Action: action, ID: row.Item.ID})
			}
		}
		return m, nil

	case overlayTryForm, overlayTryConfirm:
		switch message.String() {
		case "esc":
			m.overlay = overlayState{}
			m.err = nil
			return m, nil
		case "tab", "down":
			return m.focusOverlayField(m.overlay.fieldIndex + 1)
		case "shift+tab", "up":
			return m.focusOverlayField(m.overlay.fieldIndex - 1)
		case "enter":
			return m.submitTryOverlay()
		}
		index := m.overlay.fieldIndex
		input, command := m.overlay.fields[index].input.Update(message)
		m.overlay.fields[index].input = input
		return m, command
	}
	return m, nil
}

func (m Model) submitTryOverlay() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
	value := func(key string) string {
		for index := 0; index < m.overlay.fieldCount; index++ {
			if m.overlay.fields[index].key == key {
				return strings.TrimSpace(m.overlay.fields[index].input.Value())
			}
		}
		return ""
	}
	request := TryRequest{Action: m.overlay.action, ID: m.overlay.target.Item.ID}
	switch m.overlay.action {
	case TryCreate:
		request.Name, request.Clone = value("name"), value("clone")
		if request.Name == "" && request.Clone == "" {
			m.err = fmt.Errorf("a new Try needs a name or clone reference")
			return m, nil
		}
		gitInit, ok := parseBoolInput(value("git"), true)
		if !ok {
			m.err = fmt.Errorf("git init must be yes or no")
			return m, nil
		}
		request.NoGit = !gitInit
	case TryMark:
		request.Tags = splitTagInput(value("tags"))
		request.Note = value("note")
	case TryRestore:
		request.To = value("to")
	case TryGraduate:
		request.Category, request.Name = value("category"), value("name")
	case TryArchive:
		if value("confirm") != "YES" {
			m.err = fmt.Errorf("confirmation must be exactly YES")
			return m, nil
		}
	default:
		m.err = fmt.Errorf("unsupported Try form action %q", m.overlay.action)
		return m, nil
	}
	m.overlay = overlayState{}
	m.err = nil
	m.status = string(request.Action) + " in progress…"
	return m, m.applyTry(request)
}

func (m Model) renderOverlay() string {
	var builder strings.Builder
	builder.WriteString(styleTitle.Render("dev  "+strings.ToUpper(m.overlay.title)) + "\n\n")
	switch m.overlay.kind {
	case overlayHelp:
		builder.WriteString("  navigation\n")
		builder.WriteString("    j/k, arrows move · ctrl+d/u page · g/G first/last · tab/h/l switch view\n")
		builder.WriteString("    / filter · 0 clear · r reload · esc close/clear/quit · q quit\n\n")
		builder.WriteString("  TASKS   enter open · p park · c next · 1/2/3 state · a done\n")
		builder.WriteString("  REPOS   enter open · s worktree task · d direct task · O/R sort\n")
		builder.WriteString("  TRY     enter open · n create · space actions · a history · O/R sort\n")
		builder.WriteString("  REMOTE  enter open local · c clone\n\n")
		builder.WriteString("  " + styleHelp.Render("? / esc / q close help"))

	case overlayTryMenu:
		builder.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  %s\n  %s\n\n", m.overlay.target.Item.DisplayName(), contract(m.overlay.target.Item.Live.CurrentPath)))
		for index := 0; index < m.overlay.optionCount; index++ {
			prefix := "  "
			line := fmt.Sprintf("%-12s %s", m.overlay.options[index], m.overlay.optionLabels[index])
			if index == m.overlay.optionIndex {
				prefix = "▸ "
				line = styleSelected.Render(line)
			}
			builder.WriteString(prefix + line + "\n")
		}
		builder.WriteString("\n  " + styleHelp.Render("j/k choose · enter continue · esc cancel"))

	case overlayTryForm, overlayTryConfirm:
		if m.overlay.target.Item.ID != "" {
			builder.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  %s\n  %s\n\n", m.overlay.target.Item.DisplayName(), contract(m.overlay.target.Item.Live.CurrentPath)))
		}
		for index := 0; index < m.overlay.fieldCount; index++ {
			marker := "  "
			if index == m.overlay.fieldIndex {
				marker = "▸ "
			}
			builder.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("%s%-10s %s\n", marker, m.overlay.fields[index].label+":", m.overlay.fields[index].input.View()))
		}
		if m.err != nil {
			builder.WriteString("\n  " + styleErr.Render("✗ "+m.err.Error()))
		}
		builder.WriteString("\n\n  " + styleHelp.Render("tab field · enter submit · esc cancel"))
	}
	return builder.String()
}

package gitx

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"
)

// Remote describes every configured fetch/push location for one Git remote.
// Multiple URLs are preserved because Git can fetch from one place and push to
// several destinations.
type RemoteInfo struct {
	Name      string   `json:"name"`
	FetchURLs []string `json:"fetch_urls,omitempty"`
	PushURLs  []string `json:"push_urls,omitempty"`
}

// BranchUpstream is one local branch and the tracking ref configured for it.
type BranchUpstream struct {
	Branch   string `json:"branch"`
	OID      string `json:"oid"`
	Upstream string `json:"upstream,omitempty"`
	Remote   string `json:"remote,omitempty"`
}

// RecoveryTopology is repository-wide publication structure. It deliberately
// does not claim that matching names mean the commits are backed up; reclaim
// performs remote-ref containment checks against this inventory later.
type RecoveryTopology struct {
	Remotes  []RemoteInfo    `json:"remotes"`
	Branches []BranchUpstream `json:"branches"`

	LocalOnlyBranches []string `json:"local_only_branches,omitempty"`
	UpstreamRemotes   []string `json:"upstream_remotes,omitempty"`
}

// HasRemote reports whether any remote is configured.
func (t RecoveryTopology) HasRemote() bool { return len(t.Remotes) > 0 }

// MultipleRemotes distinguishes several configured remotes from branches that
// merely use different upstreams.
func (t RecoveryTopology) MultipleRemotes() bool { return len(t.Remotes) > 1 }

// MultipleUpstreams reports local branches tracking more than one remote.
func (t RecoveryTopology) MultipleUpstreams() bool { return len(t.UpstreamRemotes) > 1 }

// Summary is the compact CLI/TUI form. Local-only branches remain visible even
// when a repository has one or more remotes.
func (t RecoveryTopology) Summary() string {
	if len(t.Remotes) == 0 {
		if len(t.LocalOnlyBranches) > 0 {
			return fmt.Sprintf("none · local:%d", len(t.LocalOnlyBranches))
		}
		return "none"
	}
	names := make([]string, len(t.Remotes))
	for index, remote := range t.Remotes {
		names[index] = remote.Name
	}
	summary := strings.Join(names, ",")
	if len(t.LocalOnlyBranches) > 0 {
		summary += fmt.Sprintf(" · local:%d", len(t.LocalOnlyBranches))
	}
	return summary
}

// RecoveryTopologyOf reads all configured remotes and every local branch's
// upstream. Two Git processes cover the repository regardless of branch count.
func RecoveryTopologyOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (RecoveryTopology, error) {
	remoteOutput, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "-v")
	if err != nil {
		return RecoveryTopology{}, err
	}
	branchOutput, err := run(ctx, dir, "for-each-ref",
		"--format=%(refname:short)%00%(objectname)%00%(upstream:short)%00%(upstream:remotename)",
		"refs/heads")
	if err != nil {
		return RecoveryTopology{}, err
	}

	topology := RecoveryTopology{Remotes: parseRemoteInventory(remoteOutput)}
	configured := make(map[string]struct{}, len(topology.Remotes))
	for _, remote := range topology.Remotes {
		configured[remote.Name] = struct{}{}
	}
	upstreamRemotes := map[string]struct{}{}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(branchOutput, "\n") {
		if line == "" {
			continue
		}
		fields := strings.Split(line, "\x00")
		if len(fields) != 4 {
			return RecoveryTopology{}, fmt.Errorf("parse branch upstream record %q", line)
		}
		branch := BranchUpstream{
			Branch: fields[0], OID: fields[1], Upstream: fields[2], Remote: fields[3],
		}
		topology.Branches = append(topology.Branches, branch)
		_, remoteConfigured := configured[branch.Remote]
		if branch.Upstream == "" || branch.Remote == "" || branch.Remote == "." || !remoteConfigured {
			topology.LocalOnlyBranches = append(topology.LocalOnlyBranches, branch.Branch)
			continue
		}
		upstreamRemotes[branch.Remote] = struct{}{}
	}
	for remote := range upstreamRemotes {
		topology.UpstreamRemotes = append(topology.UpstreamRemotes, remote)
	}
	sort.Strings(topology.UpstreamRemotes)
	sort.Strings(topology.LocalOnlyBranches)
	sort.Slice(topology.Branches, func(i, j int) bool { return topology.Branches[i].Branch < topology.Branches[j].Branch })
	return topology, nil
}

func parseRemoteInventory(output string) []RemoteInfo {
	byName := map[string]*RemoteInfo{}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(output, "\n") {
		name, rest, ok := strings.Cut(line, "\t")
		if !ok || name == "" {
			continue
		}
		kind := ""
		switch {
		case strings.HasSuffix(rest, " (fetch)"):
			kind = "fetch"
			rest = strings.TrimSuffix(rest, " (fetch)")
		case strings.HasSuffix(rest, " (push)"):
			kind = "push"
			rest = strings.TrimSuffix(rest, " (push)")
		default:
			continue
		}
		remote := byName[name]
		if remote == nil {
			remote = &RemoteInfo{Name: name}
			byName[name] = remote
		}
		switch kind {
		case "fetch":
			remote.FetchURLs = appendUnique(remote.FetchURLs, rest)
		case "push":
			remote.PushURLs = appendUnique(remote.PushURLs, rest)
		}
	}
	names := make([]string, 0, len(byName))
	for name := range byName {
		names = append(names, name)
	}
	sort.Strings(names)
	remotes := make([]RemoteInfo, 0, len(names))
	for _, name := range names {
		remote := *byName[name]
		sort.Strings(remote.FetchURLs)
		sort.Strings(remote.PushURLs)
		remotes = append(remotes, remote)
	}
	return remotes
}

func appendUnique(values []string, value string) []string {
	for _, current := range values {
		if current == value {
			return values
		}
	}
	return append(values, value)
}

1	// Package gittest builds throwaway git repositories for tests. It is a test

14	// Repo is a scratch repository under t.TempDir().
15	type Repo struct {
16		T    *testing.T
17		Root string
18	}
19	
20	// New initialises a repository with one commit on branch "main".
21	func New(t *testing.T) *Repo {
22		t.Helper()
23		root := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "repo")
24		if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
25			t.Fatal(err)
26		}
27		r := &Repo{T: t, Root: root}
28		r.Git("init", "--initial-branch=main")
29		// Identity and signing are configured locally so the test never depends on
30		// (or is broken by) the developer's global git config.
31		r.Git("config", "user.email", "dev@example.test")
32		r.Git("config", "user.name", "dev test")
33		r.Git("config", "commit.gpgsign", "false")
34		r.Write("README.md", "# test repo\n")
35		r.Git("add", "README.md")
36		r.Git("commit", "-m", "chore: initial commit")
37		return r
38	}
39	
40	// Git runs a git command in the repo root and fails the test on error.
41	func (r *Repo) Git(args ...string) string {
42		r.T.Helper()
43		return r.GitIn(r.Root, args...)
44	}
45	
46	// GitIn runs a git command in an arbitrary directory (e.g. a linked worktree).
47	func (r *Repo) GitIn(dir string, args ...string) string {
48		r.T.Helper()
49		cmd := exec.Command("git", args...)
50		cmd.Dir = dir
51		cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
52			"GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null", // ignore the developer's ~/.gitconfig
53			"GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null",
54			"GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
55			"GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
56		)
57		out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
58		if err != nil {
59			r.T.Fatalf("git %s in %s: %v\n%s", strings.Join(args, " "), dir, err, out)
60		}
61		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
62	}

package gitx_test

import (
	"context"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"testing"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx/gittest"
)

func TestRecoveryTopologyReportsRepositoryWithoutRemote(t *testing.T) {
	repository := gittest.New(t)
	topology, err := gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(context.Background(), repository.Root)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if topology.HasRemote() || len(topology.Remotes) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected remotes: %+v", topology.Remotes)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(topology.LocalOnlyBranches, []string{"main"}) {
		t.Fatalf("local-only branches = %v", topology.LocalOnlyBranches)
	}
	if got := topology.Summary(); got != "none · local:1" {
		t.Errorf("Summary = %q", got)
	}
}

func TestRecoveryTopologySeparatesMultipleRemotesAndBranchUpstreams(t *testing.T) {
	repository := gittest.New(t)
	origin := repository.WithRemote()
	upstream := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(repository.Root), "upstream.git")
	repository.GitIn(filepath.Dir(repository.Root), "init", "--bare", "--initial-branch=main", upstream)
	repository.Git("remote", "add", "upstream", upstream)

	repository.Git("switch", "-c", "feature/local", "main")
	repository.Git("switch", "-c", "release", "main")
	repository.Git("push", "-u", "upstream", "release")

	topology, err := gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(context.Background(), repository.Root)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !topology.MultipleRemotes() || !topology.MultipleUpstreams() {
		t.Fatalf("multiple topology not detected: %+v", topology)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(topology.UpstreamRemotes, []string{"origin", "upstream"}) {
		t.Errorf("upstream remotes = %v", topology.UpstreamRemotes)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(topology.LocalOnlyBranches, []string{"feature/local"}) {
		t.Errorf("local-only branches = %v", topology.LocalOnlyBranches)
	}
	if got := topology.Summary(); got != "origin,upstream · local:1" {
		t.Errorf("Summary = %q", got)
	}
	if len(topology.Remotes) != 2 || topology.Remotes[0].Name != "origin" || topology.Remotes[1].Name != "upstream" {
		t.Fatalf("remote ordering = %+v", topology.Remotes)
	}
	if !slices.Contains(topology.Remotes[0].FetchURLs, origin) || !slices.Contains(topology.Remotes[0].PushURLs, origin) {
		t.Errorf("origin URLs = %+v", topology.Remotes[0])
	}
}

func TestRecoveryTopologyTreatsLocalBranchTrackingAsLocalOnly(t *testing.T) {
	repository := gittest.New(t)
	repository.Branch("child")
	repository.Git("branch", "--set-upstream-to=main", "child")
	topology, err := gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(context.Background(), repository.Root)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !slices.Contains(topology.LocalOnlyBranches, "child") || !slices.Contains(topology.LocalOnlyBranches, "main") {
		t.Fatalf("local branch upstream was treated as remote recovery: %+v", topology)
	}
	for _, branch := range topology.Branches {
		if branch.Branch == "child" && branch.Remote != "." {
			t.Errorf("local upstream remote = %q, want .", branch.Remote)
		}
	}
}

func TestRecoveryTopologyHonorsCancellation(t *testing.T) {
	repository := gittest.New(t)
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	cancel()
	if _, err := gitx.RecoveryTopologyOf(ctx, repository.Root); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("cancelled topology probe succeeded")
	}
}

15		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every

25		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
26		Bare bool

29	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
30	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
31	
32	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
33	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
34		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
35		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
36		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
37			"rev-parse",
38			"--path-format=absolute",
39			"--show-toplevel",
40			"--git-common-dir",
41			"--is-bare-repository",
42		)
43		if err != nil {
44			return Repo{}, err
45		}
46		f := lines(out)
47		r := Repo{}
48		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
49		switch len(f) {
50		case 3:
51			r.Root = f[0]
52			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
53			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
54		case 2:
55			r.GitCommonDir = f[0]
56			r.Bare = f[1] == "true"
57		default:
58			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
59		}
60	
61		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
62		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
63		if r.Bare {
64			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
65		} else {
66			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
67		}
68		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.Root != r.MainRoot
69		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
70		if r.Bare {
71			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
72			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
73			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
74				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
75			}
76		}
77		return r, nil
78	}
79	
80	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
81	// a full Discover.
82	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
83		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
84		return err == nil
85	}
86	
87	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
88	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
89	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
90	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
91	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
92		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
93			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
94				return b
